right: Return of the mutual insurance mechanism contribution (cross-reference)
description: Where DEP grants use the Horizon Europe mutual insurance mechanism, beneficiaries' contribution to it is returned at payment of the balance.
exercise: Applies via Art. 37 of Regulation (EU) 2021/695 (contribution offset against pre-financing and returned at payment of the balance, Art. 37(3)-(4)).
quote: Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2021/695 shall apply.
notes: Cross-reference to Horizon Europe Regulation Art. 37(4); 'legal entity' includes natural persons (Art. 2(2)).
tl_reason: Return of funding contribution at payment of balance; financial entitlement, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Access to European Digital Innovation Hub services
rightholder: Union industry, in particular SMEs, start-ups and mid-caps
description: Businesses (especially SMEs, start-ups and mid-caps) can use EDIH services: digital-transformation expertise, testing and experimentation facilities, thematic AI/HPC/cybersecurity services and matching with hubs in other regions.
exercise: Approach a designated EDIH; hubs may specialise and need not offer all thematic services to all categories of entities (Art. 16(6), second subpara.).
quote: raising awareness and providing or ensuring access to digital transformation expertise, knowhow and services, including testing and experimentation facilities
notes: Programme service delivered by funded hubs rather than an individually enforceable claim; public-sector users also served but are outside the catalogue's person scope.
tl_reason: Advisory and testing services of innovation hubs for businesses; programme service, nothing technical required to exercise. Test: yes.

right: Right to consent to sharing of application and evaluation data (Seal of Excellence)
description: Information on an application and its evaluation may be shared with other interested financing authorities only with the applicant's prior authorisation.
exercise: Prior authorisation from the applicant; sharing subject to confidentiality agreements.
quote: With prior authorisation from the applicant, information concerning the application and the evaluation may be shared with interested financing authorities
tl_reason: Prior authorisation to share application data, given by plain consent. Test: yes.

right: Contractor's ownership of IP in pre-commercial procurement results
rightholder: contractor generating results in pre-commercial procurement
description: The contractor owns at least the IP rights in results it generates in pre-commercial procurement; contracting authorities get royalty-free use and licensing rights, and can require transfer of ownership only after consulting the contractor on non-exploitation.
exercise: Contract terms; transfer may be required if results are not commercially exploited within the period set in the contract, after consultation of the contractor.
quote: The contractor generating results in pre-commercial procurement shall own at least the intellectual property rights attached to those results.
tl_reason: IP ownership in procurement results; exclusive right set by contract, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to feedback on evaluation and reasons for rejection
description: Applicants receive feedback at all stages of the evaluation and, if the proposal is rejected, the reasons for rejection.
exercise: Communicated with evaluation results (Art. 200(7) Financial Regulation).
quote: applicants shall receive feedback at all stages of the evaluation and, where the proposal is rejected, the reasons for rejection
notes: 'Legal entity' includes natural persons (Art. 2).
tl_reason: Evaluation feedback and rejection reasons in plain language; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a record of participation (widening)
rightholder: legal entities established in low R&I performing countries that participated successfully in 'widening participation and spreading excellence'
description: Successful widening participants can obtain a record of their participation, which they may attach to proposals they coordinate in collaborative parts of the Programme.
exercise: On request.
quote: shall receive, upon request, a record of their participation, that may accompany proposals to the collaborative parts of the Programme that they coordinate
tl_reason: Record of participation issued on request; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to request an evaluation review
addressee: Commission or relevant funding body (evaluation review committee)
description: An applicant who considers that the evaluation procedure was not correctly applied to its proposal can request an evaluation review, which may lead to a re-evaluation by different evaluators.
exercise: Request per specific proposal within 30 days of communication of evaluation results; procedural aspects only, not the merits (Art. 30(2)-(3)); review committee of staff not involved recommends re-evaluation or confirmation; does not delay other selections (Art. 30(4)).
quote: An applicant may request an evaluation review if it considers that the applicable evaluation procedure has not been correctly applied to its proposal
tl_reason: Procedural review request in funding evaluation; letter works, plain result. Test: yes.

right: Right to make enquiries and complaints about involvement in the Programme
description: Participants can make direct enquiries and complaints about their involvement in Horizon Europe through a Commission procedure.
exercise: Via the Commission's enquiry/complaint procedure; information on how to register is published online.
quote: The Commission shall ensure the existence of a procedure for participants to make direct enquiries and complaints about their involvement in the Programme.
tl_reason: Enquiry and complaint procedure for funding participants; ordinary means suffice. Test: yes.

right: Right to timely evaluation outcome and grant signature (time-to-grant)
description: Applicants must be informed of the outcome of the evaluation within five months, and grant agreements signed within eight months, of the submission deadline.
exercise: Maximum periods from the final submission date; work programme may set shorter periods (Art. 31(2)); may be exceeded for ERC actions, missions and actions under ethics assessment or security scrutiny (Art. 31(3)).
quote: for informing all applicants of the outcome of the evaluation of their application, a maximum period of five months from the final date for submission of complete proposals
tl_reason: Time limits for evaluation outcome and grant signature; procedural, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of the coordinator to a prior procedure before termination of an action
description: Before terminating an action because its expected results have lost relevance, the Commission must conduct a procedure with the action coordinator.
exercise: Procedure under Art. 133 Financial Regulation, where appropriate with independent external experts.
quote: The Commission shall undergo a procedure with the action coordinator and, if appropriate, with independent external experts, before deciding to terminate an action
tl_reason: Procedure before termination of a funded action; procedural right. Test: yes.

right: Right to return of the mutual insurance mechanism contribution
description: The beneficiaries' contribution (normally 5 % of Union funding) to the Mutual Insurance Mechanism is returned to them at payment of the balance.
exercise: Contribution offset against initial pre-financing (Art. 37(3)) and returned at payment of the balance.
quote: The contribution of the beneficiaries shall be returned at the payment of the balance.
tl_reason: Return of mutual insurance contribution; financial entitlement, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Ownership of results
addressee: other beneficiaries; Commission or funding body
description: Beneficiaries own the results they generate; jointly generated, inseparable results are jointly owned under a written joint-ownership agreement.
exercise: Joint owners agree in writing on allocation and terms of exercise, or on another regime; employees' and others' rights must be exercisable compatibly with grant obligations.
quote: Beneficiaries shall own the results they generate.
tl_reason: Ownership of research results; IP right, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of a joint owner to grant non-exclusive licences to third parties
description: Unless otherwise agreed, each joint owner can grant non-exclusive licences (without sub-licensing) to third parties to exploit jointly owned results.
exercise: Default rule unless the consortium or joint-ownership agreement provides otherwise; requires advance notice and fair and reasonable compensation to the other joint owners.
quote: each joint owner may grant non-exclusive licences to third parties to exploit the jointly-owned results (without any right to sub-license), if the other joint owners are given advance notice
tl_reason: Licensing of jointly owned results; contractual IP right. Test: yes.

right: Right of joint owners to advance notice and fair compensation for licences
description: Where a joint owner licenses jointly owned results to a third party, the other joint owners are entitled to advance notice and fair and reasonable compensation.
exercise: Default rule unless otherwise agreed in the consortium or joint-ownership agreement.
quote: if the other joint owners are given advance notice and fair and reasonable compensation
tl_reason: Advance notice and compensation for licences; contractual IP remuneration. Test: yes.

right: Right to request waiver of the obligation to use an exploitation platform
description: A beneficiary whose results remain unexploited can ask to be relieved, if justified, of the obligation to seek interested parties through the designated online platform.
exercise: Request to the granting authority; waiver only if justified.
quote: That obligation may be waived at the request of the beneficiary if justified.
tl_reason: Plain request to funder to waive the exploitation-platform obligation. Test: yes.

right: Open access to scientific publications from funded research
rightholder: any person (readers and re-users of publications)
description: Scientific publications resulting from Horizon Europe funding must be made openly accessible, with beneficiaries or authors retaining sufficient IP rights to allow this.
exercise: Terms and conditions set in the grant agreement (see also Art. 14(1)(a)); open-access costs are eligible (Art. 36(7)).
quote: Beneficiaries shall ensure that open access to scientific publications applies under the terms and conditions laid down in the grant agreement.
notes: Derived from beneficiaries' obligation; enforced by the granting authority, not directly by members of the public.
tl_reason: Publications made openly accessible online, but reading them needs no technical ability and a printout works; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Open access to research data ('as open as possible, as closed as necessary')
description: Research data generated in funded actions are, as a general rule, openly accessible, subject to exceptions for legitimate interests, data protection, confidentiality, trade secrets, security or IP.
exercise: Terms and conditions set in the grant agreement; FAIR data management and Data Management Plan (Art. 39(4)).
quote: Open access to research data shall be the general rule under the terms and conditions laid down in the grant agreement
notes: Derived from beneficiaries' obligation; exceptions allowed; enforced by the granting authority.
tl_reason: Object is research datasets needing technical handling, but right derives from beneficiaries' grant obligation, with no mechanism owed to the holder. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to advance notice of and to object to dissemination of results
description: Beneficiaries must be notified in advance of planned dissemination and can object where it would significantly harm their legitimate interests in their results or background.
exercise: Objection must show significant harm; results are then not disseminated unless appropriate safeguards are taken.
quote: Any other beneficiary may object if it can show that dissemination of the results would significantly harm its legitimate interests in relation to its results or background.
tl_reason: Objection to dissemination among consortium partners by plain notice. Test: yes.

right: Right to transfer ownership of and license results
addressee: other beneficiaries; Commission or funding body
description: Beneficiaries can transfer ownership of their results and grant licences, including exclusive licences (Art. 40(3)), provided their obligations are passed on and complied with.
exercise: Obligations follow the results to the new owner; subject to other beneficiaries' notice/objection (Art. 40(2)), consent for exclusive licences (Art. 40(3)) and any Commission right to object (Art. 40(4)).
quote: Beneficiaries may transfer ownership of their results.
tl_reason: Transfer of ownership and licensing of results; IP and contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to advance notice of and to object to transfer of ownership of results
rightholder: beneficiary that still has access rights to the results
description: Beneficiaries with access rights must be told in advance (with enough information on the new owner) of an intended transfer of results and can object if it would adversely affect their access rights.
exercise: Unless otherwise agreed in writing for identified third parties; on objection, no transfer until agreement is reached; time limits set in the grant agreement.
quote: a beneficiary may object to the transfer of ownership of results by another beneficiary if it can show that the transfer would adversely affect its access rights
tl_reason: Notice of and objection to ownership transfer; contractual, plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to withhold consent to exclusive licences over results
rightholder: other beneficiaries concerned (holders of access rights)
description: An exclusive licence to results can only be granted if all other beneficiaries concerned consent to waive their access rights to those results.
exercise: Consent and waiver of access rights in writing (Art. 41(1)).
quote: Exclusive licences for results may be granted subject to consent by all the other beneficiaries concerned that they will waive their access rights thereto.
tl_reason: Consent to exclusive licences given in writing; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of restrictions on access to background
description: Before acceding to the grant agreement, each beneficiary must be informed by the others of any restrictions on granting access to their background.
exercise: Before accession to the grant agreement.
quote: Before acceding to the grant agreement the beneficiaries shall inform each other of any restrictions to granting access to their background.
tl_reason: Information on background restrictions between partners; plain. Test: yes.

right: Access rights to other beneficiaries' results to implement own tasks
description: A beneficiary can obtain royalty-free access to other beneficiaries' results that it needs to carry out its own tasks in the action.
exercise: Written request (Art. 41(1)); no sub-licensing unless agreed (Art. 41(2)); continues if the granting beneficiary leaves the action (Art. 41(4)); may be withdrawn from a defaulting beneficiary by agreement (Art. 41(5)).
quote: their results on a royalty-free basis to any other beneficiary in the action that needs them to implement its own tasks
tl_reason: Access rights to partners' results by written request; IP licence, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Access rights to other beneficiaries' background to implement own tasks
description: A beneficiary can obtain access to other beneficiaries' background needed for its own tasks, royalty-free unless agreed otherwise before accession.
exercise: Written request (Art. 41(1)); subject to restrictions notified under Art. 41(3); no sub-licensing unless agreed.
quote: their background to any other beneficiary in the action that needs it to implement its own tasks, subject to any restrictions referred to in paragraph 3
tl_reason: Access rights to partners' background by written request; IP licence, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Access rights to results and background to exploit own results
description: A beneficiary can obtain access to other beneficiaries' results and background that it needs to exploit its own results, on fair and reasonable conditions.
exercise: Written request up to one year after the end of the action unless otherwise agreed (Art. 41(8)); conditions to be agreed; subject to background restrictions (Art. 41(3)).
quote: their results and, subject to any restrictions referred to in paragraph 3, to their background to any other beneficiary in the action that needs them to exploit its own results
tl_reason: Access to results and background for exploitation on fair conditions; contractual IP licence. Test: yes.

right: Access rights of affiliated entities for exploitation
rightholder: legal entity established in a Member State or associated country that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a beneficiary
description: Affiliated entities of a beneficiary can obtain access to other beneficiaries' results and background needed to exploit that beneficiary's results, on fair and reasonable conditions.
exercise: Unless otherwise agreed by the beneficiaries; written request within one year after the end of the action unless otherwise agreed (Art. 41(8)).
quote: they shall also grant access to their results and, subject to any restrictions referred to in paragraph 3, to their background to a legal entity that:
tl_reason: Affiliated entities' access rights to results; contractual IP licence. Test: yes.

right: Right of independent external experts to remuneration
description: Independent experts who evaluate proposals or advise are paid under standard conditions, exceptionally above standard rates for high-level experts.
exercise: Standard conditions under Art. 237(2)-(3) Financial Regulation.
quote: the independent external experts shall be remunerated based on standard conditions
tl_reason: Remuneration of independent experts; financial entitlement. Test: yes.

right: Access to consortium-building matchmaking services
description: Entities interested in forming consortia can use the Commission's evidence-based matchmaking services and events, with particular attention to entities from low R&I performing countries.
quote: Evidence-based matchmaking services informed by analytics and network affinities shall be provided to interested entities in order to form consortia for collaborative projects
notes: Programme service; no individually enforceable entitlement stated.
tl_reason: Consortium matchmaking services; programme service, no technical condition. Test: yes.

right: Informed consent and risk information for persons admitted to deal on a DLT MTF
rightholder: natural or legal person admitted as member/participant dealing on own account
description: Where an exemption lets a DLT MTF admit natural and legal persons as members, they must give informed consent and be told of the risks; the authority may impose extra protections for natural persons.
exercise: Only where the competent authority has granted the exemption at the operator's request.
quote: they have given informed consent to trading on the DLT MTF as members or participants and have been informed by the DLT MTF of the potential risks of using its systems
notes: Conditional on exemption
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Informed consent to trade on a DLT platform plus risk notice; plain declaration and notice suffice, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Informed consent of persons admitted as participants in a DLT SS
rightholder: natural or legal person admitted as participant
description: Natural and legal persons may be admitted as DLT SS participants only if they have given informed consent and are adequately informed of the pilot regime's experimental nature and risks.
exercise: Only where the competent authority has granted the exemption.
quote: have given informed consent to be included in the pilot regime provided for in this Regulation and are adequately informed of its experimental nature and the potential risks associated with it
notes: Conditional on exemption
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Consent to join the DLT pilot and risk information; plain declaration and notice suffice, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Fair and open access to DLT settlement systems
description: Where exempted from CSDR access rules, the DLT SS must publish transparent, objective and non-discriminatory participation criteria allowing fair and open access for all would-be participants.
quote: the DLT SS publicly discloses criteria for participation that allow fair and open access for all persons that intend to become participants
notes: Compensatory measure where exemption granted
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Fair, non-discriminatory participation criteria for a DLT settlement system; market-access right, no technical mechanism for the holder.

right: Access for other DLT market infrastructures to an exempted DLT SS
rightholder: operators of DLT SSs or DLT TSSs
description: A CSD exempted from CSDR links/access obligations must nonetheless give other DLT SS/TSS operators access to its DLT SS, unless the authority prohibits it for stability reasons.
quote: it shall give other operators of DLT SSs or other operators of DLT TSSs access to its DLT SS
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Access between DLT settlement systems is a technical interconnection (test: no), but holders are peer infrastructure operators, not governed users. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Information on how a DLT market infrastructure functions
addressee: operator of a DLT market infrastructure
description: Users must receive clear information on how the operator carries out its functions and how these differ from non-DLT infrastructures, including the type of DLT used; legal terms on rights, liabilities, governing law, dispute settlement and jurisdiction must be published (Art. 7(1)).
exercise: On the operator's website.
quote: Operators of DLT market infrastructures shall provide their members, participants, issuers and clients with clear and unambiguous information on their website
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Plain-language information published on the operator's website; website is only the channel, content usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Consent before use of safekept assets for the operator's own account
addressee: operator of a DLT market infrastructure
description: Operators safekeeping users' funds, collateral or DLT financial instruments may not use them for their own account without the user's prior express written consent; assets must be segregated.
exercise: Prior express written consent, may be electronic.
quote: to prevent the use of those assets on the operator’s own account without the prior express written consent of the member, participant, issuer, or client concerned
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Prior express written consent, which may be given electronically; paper consent works and nothing technical is required. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for lost funds, collateral or DLT financial instruments
addressee: operator of a DLT market infrastructure
description: The operator is liable for loss of funds, collateral or DLT financial instruments up to the market value of the asset lost, unless caused by an unavoidable external event beyond its control.
exercise: Claim against the operator.
quote: the operator of a DLT market infrastructure that lost the funds, collateral or DLT financial instrument shall be liable for the loss, up to the market value of the asset lost
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Liability for lost funds or instruments; ordinary compensation claim, no technical mechanism.

right: Access to complaint handling and compensation/redress procedures
addressee: operator of a DLT market infrastructure
description: Operators must have mechanisms for handling client complaints and procedures for compensation or redress for investor losses, including on cessation of business.
quote: shall establish mechanisms for handling client complaints and procedures for compensation or redress in cases of investor loss
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Complaint and redress procedures with a DLT operator; complaint by letter works, outcome plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of DLT operators to a timely, non-discriminatory response to takeover requests
rightholder: operator of a DLT SS or DLT TSS
addressee: CSD operating a securities settlement system
description: A CSD asked to take over operations of a DLT infrastructure must respond within three months, conclude arrangements non-discriminatorily for a reasonable cost-based fee, and give written reasons for any refusal (not on market-share grounds).
exercise: Request to the CSD; response within three months.
quote: If it denies a request, it shall inform the operator of the DLT market infrastructure that made the request of its reasons in writing.
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Takeover arrangement request between infrastructures; written reasons on refusal, no technical mechanism.

right: Right to apply for a specific permission (and exemptions) to operate a DLT MTF
rightholder: investment firm or market operator (legal person)
description: Authorised investment firms and market operators may apply for a specific permission, with requested exemptions; the authority must check completeness within 30 working days and decide within 90 working days; permission is valid EU-wide for up to six years.
exercise: Application with the information in Art. 8(4).
quote: authorised to operate a regulated market, under Directive 2014/65/EU may apply for a specific permission to operate a DLT MTF under this Regulation
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Application for regulatory permission; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to apply for a specific permission (and exemptions) to operate a DLT SS
description: Authorised CSDs may apply for a specific permission to operate a DLT settlement system, with requested exemptions; completeness check within 30 working days and decision within 90 working days.
exercise: Application with the information in Art. 9(4).
quote: A legal person who is authorised as a CSD under Regulation (EU) No 909/2014 may apply for a specific permission to operate a DLT SS under this Regulation.
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Application for regulatory permission; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to apply for a specific permission (and exemptions) to operate a DLT TSS
rightholder: investment firm, market operator or CSD (legal person)
description: Authorised investment firms, market operators and CSDs may apply for a specific permission to operate a DLT trading and settlement system; completeness check within 30 working days, decision within 90 working days.
exercise: Application with the information in Art. 10(4)-(5).
quote: may apply for a specific permission to operate a DLT TSS under this Regulation
table_entry: Regulation on a pilot regime for market infrastructures based on DLT
tl_reason: Application for regulatory permission; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Access to InvestEU Advisory Hub support
rightholder: public and private project promoters, including SMEs and start-ups; financial and non-financial intermediaries
addressee: Commission / InvestEU Advisory Hub (EIB Group and advisory partners)
description: Project promoters, including SMEs and start-ups, can obtain advisory support to identify, prepare, structure and implement investment projects, including IP advice for start-ups.
exercise: Through the central entry point (Art. 25(2)(a)); fees may be charged, but capped at one third of cost for SMEs and free for public promoters/non-profits where justified (Art. 25(4)).
quote: The InvestEU Advisory Hub shall be available to public and private project promoters, including SMEs and start-ups
notes: Public authorities and national promotional banks also covered but outside the catalogue's person scope.
tl_reason: Advisory support for project promoters; programme service. Test: yes.

right: Right to list projects on the InvestEU Portal
description: Project promoters seeking finance can list projects on the InvestEU Portal to make them visible to investors; compatible projects are passed to implementing partners for examination.
exercise: Only projects compatible with Union law and policies are listed; listing does not prejudge selection (Art. 26(2)); implementing partners examine projects in their scope (Art. 26(3)-(4)).
quote: The InvestEU Portal shall provide a channel for project promoters to make projects for which they are seeking finance visible to investors.
tl_reason: Law makes an online portal the channel for listing projects, but the listing and its result are non-technical. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right of final recipients to be informed of InvestEU support
addressee: implementing partners, advisory partners and financial intermediaries
description: Final recipients must be told that their financing benefits from InvestEU support.
exercise: Information made clearly visible in the agreement providing support.
quote: The implementing partners and advisory partners shall inform the final recipients, including SMEs, of the existence of support under the InvestEU Programme
tl_reason: Plain information that financing benefits from InvestEU support. Test: yes.

right: Entitlement to pre-financing of at least 20 % (military mobility actions)
rightholder: beneficiaries of transport actions on the EU Priority Military Mobility Corridors
description: Military-mobility transport actions financed with resources transferred at mid-term review are entitled to pre-financing of at least 20 % of the grant amount.
exercise: Applies only if resources are transferred to the CEF in the mid-term review; actions must lie on the four priority corridors and meet Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1328 requirements.
quote: actions are entitled to a pre-financing payment representing at least 20 % of the amount allocated in the grant agreement
notes: Natural persons are not eligible under CEF (Art. 11(3)); Member State beneficiaries outside person scope.
tl_reason: Pre-financing entitlement; funding right. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit observations before grant reduction or termination
description: Before a grant is reduced or terminated (e.g. for late start or major delays), beneficiaries can submit their observations after a comprehensive examination of the case.
exercise: Within a reasonable time-frame set by the Commission.
quote: the beneficiaries concerned shall be given the possibility to submit their observations within a reasonable time-frame
notes: Natural persons are not eligible under CEF (Art. 11(3)).
tl_reason: Observations before grant reduction or termination; procedural right. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of changes to grant amounts and final amounts paid
description: Beneficiaries are informed by the Commission of changes to their grant amounts and of the final amounts paid during implementation.
quote: the beneficiaries and the Member States concerned shall be informed by the Commission regarding changes to the grant amounts and the final amounts paid
tl_reason: Information on grant amounts paid; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of legal entities to apply for Private Membership
rightholder: legal entity established in a Member State that supports research and innovation
addressee: Governing Board of the Joint Undertaking
description: A legal entity that contributes to the JU's financing and accepts the Statutes can apply to become a Private Member.
exercise: Application to the Governing Board, which assesses relevance and added value and decides (Statutes Art. 3(4)).
quote: is established in a Member State that directly or indirectly supports research and innovation in a Member State may apply to become a Private Member of the Joint Undertaking
notes: Governance right of organisations.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Application for private membership; governance right. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate membership
rightholder: member of the Joint Undertaking (Private Members)
description: A member can withdraw from the Joint Undertaking and is then discharged from obligations not approved or incurred before notification.
exercise: Notification to the Executive Director; effective and irrevocable six months later.
quote: Any member may terminate its membership in the Joint Undertaking.
notes: Counted only for Private Members (legal entities); the Union and Participating States are outside person scope.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Withdrawal from membership by notification; governance right. Test: yes.

right: One-stop shop for users of AI-optimised supercomputers (AI factories)
rightholder: users, including start-ups, SMEs and scientific users
description: Hosting entities of AI-optimised supercomputers must offer users a one-stop shop giving access to their support services.
quote: the hosting entity shall create a one-stop shop for users, including startups, small and medium-sized enterprises and scientific users, to facilitate access to its support services
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: One-stop shop for support services; advisory access, nothing technical required to exercise. Test: yes.

right: Access to Union access time on AI gigafactories
rightholder: users residing, established or located in a Member State or a country associated to DEP, Horizon Europe or CEF
addressee: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (Governing Board) / AI gigafactory
description: Eligible users can access the Union's share of AI gigafactory time, free of charge for public-law entities, publicly funded R&I and SME/scale-up innovation, with reserved priority capacity for Union-funded projects.
exercise: Under access conditions set by the Governing Board (Art. 12b(14)); detailed user conditions in the AI gigafactory Hosting Agreement (Art. 12b(17)(f)).
quote: is granted to users residing, established or located in a Member State or in a third country associated to the Digital Europe Programme, to Horizon Europe or to the Connecting Europe Facility
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Access time on AI gigafactories; object is compute, usable only by running own software on the system. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Equal security and quality of service within each user category
description: All users in the same category receive the same security and quality of service.
exercise: Quality of service set out in the hosting agreement's service level agreement (Art. 10(2)(c)).
quote: The security and quality of service shall be the same for all users within each user category
notes: Exception: industrial-grade supercomputers follow industrial requirements.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Equal-treatment guarantee on security and service quality; nothing the holder exercises through a mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Dedicated access for start-ups and SMEs to AI-optimised supercomputers
rightholder: start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises
description: Special access conditions for AI-optimised supercomputers must include dedicated access for start-ups and SMEs.
exercise: Under special access conditions adopted by the Governing Board; only proposals for trustworthy and ethical AI in line with Union values are eligible.
quote: Those shall include dedicated access to startups and small and medium-sized enterprises.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Dedicated access to AI supercomputers for start-ups and SMEs; compute usable only by running own workloads. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of eligible users to access the Union's share of EuroHPC supercomputer time
rightholder: users residing, established or located in a Member State or a country associated to Digital Europe or Horizon Europe
description: Public and private users from Member States and associated countries are granted access to the Union's share of access time on EuroHPC supercomputers acquired after 2020.
exercise: Under general and specific access conditions defined by the Governing Board (Arts 16(2), 17(5)); the Executive Director monitors compliance with access rights of academic and industrial users (Statutes Art. 9).
quote: Users residing, established or located in a Member State or in a third country associated to the Digital Europe Programme or to Horizon Europe shall be granted the Union’s share of access time
notes: Art. 16(3) gives the same for machines acquired under Reg (EU) 2018/1488 (Horizon 2020 associated countries); use open to public and private sectors (Art. 16(1)).
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Access time on EuroHPC supercomputers; object is compute, usable only through the system with own software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Free-of-charge access time allocated by fair and transparent peer review
rightholder: public-sector users; industrial users in Horizon Europe/DEP-funded R&I or with a Seal of Excellence; SMEs for private innovation
description: Eligible public, research and SME users can use the Union's share of access time free of charge, allocated through a fair and transparent peer-review process.
exercise: Apply to continuously open calls for expression of interest; peer review defined by the Governing Board; non-SME users must follow open science rules (Art. 17(7)).
quote: Use of the Union’s share of access time to the EuroHPC supercomputers shall be free of charge for the users from the public sector referred to in Article 16(4).
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Free-of-charge allocation through peer review; concerns pricing and allocation procedure, not a mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Access to Union access time for commercial use (pay-per-use)
description: Industry can buy access time on the Union's share for commercial purposes on a pay-per-use basis at market prices, with equal quality for all commercial users.
exercise: Fee set by the Governing Board; capped at 20 % of Union access time per machine (Art. 18(3)); same quality for all users (Art. 18(4)).
quote: This service for commercial use shall be a pay-per-use service, based on market prices.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Pay-per-use commercial access to supercomputer time; compute usable only through the system with own software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by Joint Undertaking staff
description: Persons harmed by EuroHPC JU staff in the performance of their duties can obtain compensation under non-contractual liability.
exercise: Action before the Court of Justice (Art. 25(1)(b)); general principles common to the laws of the Member States; JU not liable for hosting entities' operation of supercomputers (Art. 23(5)).
quote: the Joint Undertaking shall, in accordance with the general principles common to the laws of the Member States, make good any damage caused by its staff in the performance of their duties
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Non-contractual compensation through court action. Test: yes.

right: Judicial remedy for Joint Undertaking staff before the Court of Justice
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Staff can bring disputes with the Joint Undertaking before the Court of Justice.
exercise: Within the limits and conditions of the Staff Regulations and Conditions of Employment, which apply to JU staff (Art. 20(1)).
quote: in any dispute between the Joint Undertaking and its staff within the limits and under the conditions laid down in the Staff Regulations or the Conditions of Employment.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Staff judicial remedy before the Court of Justice. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to the European Ombudsman
rightholder: any person entitled under Art. 228 TFEU
description: Decisions of the EuroHPC JU can be challenged by a complaint to the European Ombudsman.
exercise: In accordance with Art. 228 TFEU.
quote: Decisions taken by the Joint Undertaking in implementing this Regulation may form the subject of a complaint to the Ombudsman in accordance with Article 228 TFEU.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Complaint to the Ombudsman by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right of public access to Joint Undertaking documents
rightholder: any citizen of the Union and any natural or legal person residing or registered in a Member State
description: Persons can request access to documents held by the EuroHPC JU.
exercise: Under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 (application, deadlines, confirmatory application).
quote: shall apply to documents held by the Joint Undertaking.
notes: Cross-reference to Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Access to documents under Reg. 1049/2001; letter request, plain documents. Test: yes.

right: Applicant and participant rights under the Horizon Europe rules for participation (cross-reference)
rightholder: applicants and beneficiaries in indirect actions funded by the Joint Undertaking
addressee: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (as funding body); other beneficiaries
description: Horizon Europe rules apply to JU-funded indirect actions, so applicants and beneficiaries enjoy the feedback, evaluation-review, complaint, ownership, objection and access rights of Reg (EU) 2021/695.
exercise: As under Reg (EU) 2021/695 Arts 29-31 and 38-41, with the JU acting as funding body.
quote: Regulation (EU) 2021/695 shall apply to the indirect actions funded by the Joint Undertaking under Horizon Europe.
notes: Cross-reference; Arts 35-36 likewise apply CEF and DEP rules to activities funded under those programmes.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Cross-reference to funding participation rights; procedural and IP rights. Test: yes.

right: Continuation of rights and employment contracts of predecessor JU staff
description: Staff of the previous EuroHPC JU keep their rights and obligations; their employment contracts continue under this Regulation.
exercise: Automatic; contracts continue under the Staff Regulations and Conditions of Employment.
quote: This Regulation shall not affect the rights and obligations of staff engaged under Regulation (EU) 2018/1488.
notes: Transitional provision.
table_entry: Regulation on the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
tl_reason: Continuation of staff employment contracts. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to apply for associated membership of a joint undertaking
rightholder: legal entity established in a Member State or associated country
description: Legal entities can apply, in response to an open call for expression of interest, to become associated members and have their application assessed and decided.
exercise: Respond to the open call (mandatory for JUs with founding members in Annexes I-III); assessed by the executive director with independent experts; governing board approves or rejects (Art. 7(2)-(3)).
quote: The governing board shall assess and approve or reject applications for membership.
notes: Governance right of organisations; international organisations outside person scope.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Application for associated membership; governance right. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to terminate membership of a joint undertaking
rightholder: member of a joint undertaking (private and associated members)
description: A member can withdraw from a joint undertaking and is then discharged from obligations not approved or incurred before termination.
exercise: Notification to the executive director; effective and irrevocable six months later.
quote: Any member of a joint undertaking may terminate its membership of that joint undertaking.
notes: Counted only for private/associated members that are legal entities; the Union and participating states are outside person scope.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Withdrawal from membership by notification; governance right. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to apply to become a contributing partner
rightholder: candidate contributing partner (legal entity other than a member)
addressee: governing board of the joint undertaking
description: A legal entity supporting a JU's objectives can apply, by letter of endorsement, to become a contributing partner and obtain a decision on its application.
exercise: Letter of endorsement specifying scope, activities, duration and contribution; governing board approves or rejects (Art. 9(2)); no voting rights (Art. 9(3)).
quote: The governing board shall assess the letter of endorsement and shall approve or reject the application.
notes: Countries and international organisations can also apply but are outside person scope.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Application as contributing partner by letter of endorsement. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Applicant and participant rights under the Horizon Europe rules for participation (cross-reference)
rightholder: applicants and beneficiaries in indirect actions funded by the joint undertakings
addressee: joint undertaking (as funding body); other beneficiaries
description: Horizon Europe rules apply to JU-funded actions, so applicants and beneficiaries enjoy the feedback, evaluation-review, complaint, ownership, objection and access rights of Reg (EU) 2021/695.
exercise: As under Reg (EU) 2021/695 Arts 29-31 and 38-41, subject to JU-specific provisions in Part Two (Art. 24(2)).
quote: The Horizon Europe Regulation shall apply to the actions funded by the joint undertakings under Horizon Europe.
notes: Cross-reference. Art. 24(3) extends the funding body's right to object to transfers (HE Reg Art. 40(4)) and is not counted.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Cross-reference to funding participation rights; procedural and IP rights. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right of public access to joint undertaking documents
rightholder: any citizen of the Union and any natural or legal person residing or registered in a Member State
description: Persons can request access to documents held by any of the joint undertakings.
exercise: Under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
quote: shall apply to documents held by a joint undertaking.
notes: Cross-reference to Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Access to documents under Reg. 1049/2001; letter request, plain documents. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to compensation for damage caused by joint undertaking staff
description: Persons harmed by JU staff in the performance of their duties can obtain compensation under non-contractual liability.
exercise: Action before the Court of Justice (Art. 43(1)(b)); general principles common to the laws of the Member States.
quote: a joint undertaking shall, in accordance with the general principles common to the laws of the Member States, make good any damage caused by its staff in the performance of their duties
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Non-contractual compensation through court action. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Judicial remedy for joint undertaking staff before the Court of Justice
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Staff can bring disputes with their joint undertaking before the Court of Justice.
exercise: Within the limits of the Staff Regulations and CEOS, which apply to JU staff (Art. 37(1)).
quote: in any dispute between the joint undertaking and its staff within the limits and under the conditions laid down in the Staff Regulations and the CEOS.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Staff judicial remedy before the Court of Justice. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to complain to the European Ombudsman
rightholder: any person entitled under Art. 228 TFEU
description: Decisions of the joint undertakings can be challenged by a complaint to the European Ombudsman.
exercise: In accordance with Art. 228 TFEU.
quote: Decisions taken by a joint undertaking in the implementation of this Regulation may form the subject of a complaint to the Ombudsman in accordance with Article 228 of the TFEU.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Complaint to the Ombudsman by ordinary means. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to request EASA advice on individual projects (Clean Aviation JU)
description: Applicants and beneficiaries in the Clean Aviation JU can invite EASA to advise on their projects regarding aviation safety, interoperability and environmental standards.
exercise: Certification activities and services subject to fees and charges under Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (Art. 71(2)).
quote: The EASA may be invited by applicants, beneficiaries or the Executive Director to advise on individual projects and demonstration activities
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Inviting EASA advice on projects; plain request. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Open and non-discriminatory access to Chips JU capacities
description: Capacities built by the Chips JU (e.g. design platform, pilot lines) are open to a wide range of users on a transparent and non-discriminatory basis.
exercise: Access granted in proportion to the Union's financial contribution to the activities' total costs.
quote: Access to capacities resulting from the implementation by the Chips Joint Undertaking of operational objectives 1 to 4 shall be open to a wide range of users across the Union
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Chips JU capacities mix a digital design platform with physical pilot lines; programme access. Digital-object criterion holds only partly.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Right to request EASA advice on individual projects (SESAR 3 JU)
description: Applicants and participants in the SESAR 3 JU can invite EASA to advise on their projects regarding aviation safety, interoperability and environmental standards.
exercise: Certification activities and services subject to fees and charges under Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (Art. 156(2)).
quote: The EASA may be invited by applicants, participants or the Executive Director to advise on individual projects and demonstration activities
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Inviting EASA advice on projects; plain request. Test: yes.

act: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe Regulation (EU) 2021/2085
right: Continuation of rights and employment contracts of predecessor JU staff
rightholder: staff engaged under the repealed joint undertaking Regulations
description: Staff of the predecessor joint undertakings keep their rights and obligations; the new JUs succeed to their employment contracts.
exercise: Automatic; successor JUs are universal successors to employment contracts (Art. 174(3)-(9)).
quote: This Regulation does not affect the rights and obligations of staff engaged under the Regulations referred to in paragraph 1.
notes: Transitional provision.
table_entry: Regulation on Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
entry_current_status: In force; Chips JU amendment adopted as Council Regulation (EU) 2023/1782
tl_reason: Continuation of staff employment contracts. Test: yes.

right: Right of undertakings to be informed before their data are passed to the Commission
rightholder: undertakings that previously provided data at the request of a Member State
description: Where a Member State gives the Commission information containing data earlier supplied by undertakings at its request, those undertakings are informed before the data are transmitted.
quote: such undertakings shall be informed thereof before Member States provide the data to the Commission.
table_entry: Decision on the Digital Decade Policy Programme 2030
tl_reason: Undertakings informed before authorities pass their data on; administrative notice, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to existing physical infrastructure
addressee: network operators and public sector bodies owning or controlling physical infrastructure
description: Obtain access to ducts, poles, masts, buildings and other physical infrastructure of network operators and public sector bodies on fair and reasonable terms, including price, to deploy very high capacity network (VHCN) elements; public sector bodies must also apply non-discriminatory terms.
exercise: Written request specifying the infrastructure elements and time frame; refusal only on Art. 3(5)-(6) grounds; dispute settlement if refused or no agreement within one month (Art. 13(1)(a)).
quote: Network operators and public sector bodies owning or controlling physical infrastructure shall meet, upon written request of an operator, all reasonable requests for access
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Written request for physical infrastructure access between operators; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to good-faith negotiation of access to land
addressee: legal persons primarily active as tenants of land or holders of rights over land (other than property rights), or managing lease contracts for landowners
description: Have tenants and holders of land rights negotiate in good faith, including on a market-reflecting price, access to land on which VHCN facilities are planned or installed.
exercise: Request to the land-rights holder; national contract law applies; concluded agreements and price must be reported to the NRA.
quote: Upon request of an operator, legal persons who are primarily active as tenants of land, or as holders of rights over land, other than property rights
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Negotiation of land access by request; contract law. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request access to private commercial buildings in rural or remote areas
addressee: owners of private commercial buildings not owned or controlled by a network operator
description: Where the Member State so provides, obtain access to private commercial buildings, including rooftops, to install VHCN elements on fair and reasonable terms at a market price.
exercise: Written request; only in rural/remote areas with no VHCN of the same type available or planned and no suitable infrastructure of network operators or public bodies; exempt building categories may be listed.
quote: owners of private commercial buildings which are not owned or controlled by a network operator are to meet, upon the written request of an operator, reasonable requests for access to those buildings
notes: Member-State option
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Written request for building access; physical infrastructure only. Test: yes.

right: Right to a written, reasoned refusal of access
addressee: network operator or public sector body owning or controlling physical infrastructure
description: Receive in writing the specific and detailed reasons for any refusal of access to physical infrastructure.
exercise: No later than one month from receipt of the complete request; detailed reasons not required for national critical infrastructure; refusal can be taken to dispute settlement (Art. 13).
quote: shall communicate to the access seeker, in writing, the specific and detailed reasons for such refusal no later than one month from the date of the receipt of the complete request for access
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Written reasoned refusal; plain document. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to offer access to physical infrastructure for other networks
description: Offer access to their physical infrastructure for deploying networks other than electronic communications networks.
quote: Operators shall have the right to offer access to their physical infrastructure for the purpose of deploying networks other than electronic communications networks or associated facilities.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Business freedom to offer infrastructure access; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to minimum information on existing physical infrastructure
addressee: single information point (fed by network operators and public sector bodies)
description: Obtain georeferenced location and route, type and current use, and a contact point for existing physical infrastructure, in electronic format.
exercise: Request via the single information point specifying the deployment area; information within 10 working days (extendable once by 5); may be limited for security, critical infrastructure or business-secret reasons; information must be kept confidential (Art. 4(8)); disputes under Art. 13(1)(b).
quote: an operator shall have the right to access, upon request, the following minimum information on existing physical infrastructure, in electronic format via a single information point
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Law requires electronic format via single information point, but plain infrastructure information on paper would serve; holder a business access seeker. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to on-site surveys of physical infrastructure
addressee: network operators and public sector bodies
description: Have reasonable requests for on-site surveys of specific elements of physical infrastructure granted.
exercise: Specific written request identifying the elements; granted within one month on proportionate, non-discriminatory and transparent terms; same limitations as Art. 4(1).
quote: Network operators and public sector bodies shall meet reasonable requests for on-site surveys of specific elements of their physical infrastructure upon specific written request of an operator.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: On-site physical survey on written request. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to negotiate agreements on coordination of civil works
rightholder: public sector bodies owning or controlling physical infrastructure and network operators
description: Negotiate agreements with operators on the coordination of civil works, including cost apportioning, for VHCN deployment.
quote: shall have the right to negotiate agreements on the coordination of civil works, including on the apportioning of costs, with operators with a view to deploying elements of VHCNs
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Contract negotiation on civil works. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request coordination of publicly financed civil works
addressee: network operators and public sector bodies performing civil works fully or partially financed by public means
description: Have reasonable requests to coordinate publicly financed civil works met on transparent and non-discriminatory terms in order to deploy VHCN elements.
exercise: Written request as soon as possible and at least one month before the final project is submitted for permits; no unrecoverable extra costs, initiator keeps control; may be deemed unreasonable under Art. 5(3)-(4); dispute settlement if no agreement within one month (Art. 13(1)(c)).
quote: shall meet any reasonable written request to coordinate those civil works under transparent and non-discriminatory terms made by operators with a view to deploying elements of VHCNs
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Written request to coordinate civil works. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to equal retail prices for domestic and intra-EU communications
addressee: providers of number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Pay the same retail price for calls and SMS to another Member State (intra-EU communications) as for domestic communications.
exercise: Applies from 1 January 2029 provided technical rules on safeguards (fair use, anti-fraud) are adopted by implementing act; providers may apply it voluntarily earlier (Art. 5a(8)).
quote: From 1 January 2029, providers shall not apply different retail prices to consumers for domestic communications and intra-EU communications
notes: Conditional on implementing act on safeguards
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Retail price parity for intra-EU calls/SMS; pricing rule, nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to minimum information on planned civil works
addressee: single information point (fed by network operators and public sector bodies)
description: Obtain location and type of works, infrastructure elements involved, estimated dates and a contact point for planned civil works.
exercise: Reasoned request via the single information point specifying the deployment area; information within 10 working days (extendable once by 5); may be limited for security or business-secret reasons.
quote: Operators shall have the right to access the minimum information referred to in the first subparagraph in electronic format, upon reasoned request, via a single information point
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Electronic format via single information point required, but plain civil-works information usable without technical means. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to apply electronically for permits and rights of way and track their status
description: Submit applications for all permits, renewals and rights of way electronically via the single information point and retrieve information on the status of the application.
exercise: Via the single information point in electronic format; Member States may specify detailed procedures.
quote: Any operator shall have the right to submit, via a single information point in electronic format, applications for all necessary permits or renewals thereof, or rights of way
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Law requires electronic submission and status tracking via single information point, but the permit request and result are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to a timely and reasoned decision on permit applications
description: Have permits (other than rights of way) granted or refused within four months of a complete application, be invited to supply missing information within 20 working days, and receive a duly substantiated refusal.
exercise: Extensions only on pre-published grounds, as short as possible and max. four months; refusal must rest on objective, transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate criteria.
quote: The competent authorities shall grant or refuse permits, other than rights of way, within 4 months of the date of receipt of a complete permit application.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Administrative deadline for permit decisions. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to timely grant of rights of way
description: Where rights of way are needed in addition to permits, have them granted within four months (or a shorter national deadline) of a complete application.
exercise: Not applicable to expropriation; owner's prior authorisation or national law required for private property.
quote: competent authorities shall grant such rights of way within the four-month period or the deadline set by national law, whichever is shorter, from the date of receipt of the complete application
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Administrative deadline for rights of way. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Tacit approval of permits
description: If the competent authority does not decide within the Art. 7(5) deadline, the permit (other than rights of way) is deemed granted.
exercise: Member States may derogate where compensation or a court/supervisory remedy is available (Art. 8(2)).
quote: In the absence of a decision from the competent authority within the applicable deadline referred to in Article 7(5), the permit shall be deemed to be granted upon expiry of that deadline.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Tacit approval of permits; administrative law. Test: yes.

right: Right to written confirmation of a tacitly granted permit
rightholder: the operator or any affected party
description: Obtain written confirmation from the competent authority that a permit has been implicitly granted.
exercise: On request.
quote: Upon request, the operator or any affected party shall be entitled to receive written confirmation from the competent authority that, where applicable, the permit has been implicitly granted.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Written confirmation of tacit permit on request; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right of affected third parties to intervene in the permit procedure and challenge the permit
addressee: Member States / competent authorities and courts
description: Intervene in the administrative permit-granting procedure and challenge the decision granting the permit, including a tacit permit.
exercise: Under national procedural law.
quote: Member States shall ensure that any third party affected has the right to intervene in the administrative procedure and to challenge the decision granting the permit.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Procedural right to intervene and challenge a permit. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for missed permit deadlines
description: Claim compensation for damage caused by the competent authority's failure to meet the permit deadline.
exercise: In accordance with national law; available where the Member State derogates from tacit approval.
quote: the operator which suffered damage as a result of non-compliance by the competent authority with the applicable deadline set out in accordance with Article 7(5) is entitled to claim compensation
notes: Member-State option (alternative to tacit approval)
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Compensation claim against authority. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to refer a missed permit deadline to a court or supervising authority
description: Refer the competent authority's failure to decide on time to a court or a supervising authority.
exercise: Available where the Member State derogates from tacit approval; can be used immediately on expiry of the deadline (Art. 8(3)).
quote: the operator may refer the case to a court or to a supervising authority.
notes: Member-State option (alternative to tacit approval)
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Referral to court or supervising authority. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a facilitation meeting on a delayed permit
addressee: competent authority or other body designated by the Member State
description: After the permit deadline expires, request a meeting to facilitate a decision and receive a written account indicating the date by which a decision will be issued.
exercise: Applies where the Member State derogated from tacit approval; meeting within two months of the request; written account without undue delay.
quote: shall invite the applicant, without undue delay, upon request of the operator, or on its own motion, to a meeting to facilitate the adoption of a decision on the permit application
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Facilitation meeting and written account; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to roll out the network up to the building access point
rightholder: any provider of public electronic communications networks
addressee: building owners and holders of rights / Member States
description: Roll out its network at its own cost up to the access point of a building.
exercise: Subject to Art. 11(3) and without prejudice to property rights.
quote: any provider of public electronic communications networks shall have the right to roll out its network at its own costs up to the access point.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Physical network rollout right; no mechanism for a governed party. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to existing in-building physical infrastructure
rightholder: any provider of public electronic communications networks
addressee: holders of a right to use the in-building physical infrastructure
description: Access existing in-building physical infrastructure to deploy VHCN elements where duplication is technically impossible or economically inefficient.
exercise: Reasonable written request (Art. 11(3)); dispute settlement if no agreement within one month (Art. 13(1)(d)); without prejudice to property rights.
quote: any provider of public electronic communications networks shall have the right to access any existing in-building physical infrastructure with a view to deploying elements of VHCNs
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Access to in-building physical infrastructure by written request. Test: yes.

right: Right to FRAND access to the building access point and in-building infrastructure
rightholder: providers of public electronic communications networks
addressee: any holder of a right to use the access point and in-building physical infrastructure
description: Have reasonable written requests for access to the access point and in-building physical infrastructure met on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms, including price where appropriate.
exercise: Written request; dispute settlement if no agreement within one month (Art. 13(1)(d)).
quote: Any holder of a right to use the access point and the in-building physical infrastructure shall meet all reasonable written requests for access
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: FRAND access to physical access point by written request. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the network at the subscriber's premises
rightholder: any provider of public electronic communications networks
description: Where no fibre-ready in-building infrastructure exists, terminate its network at the subscriber's premises using existing in-building infrastructure.
exercise: Subject to the agreement of the owner and/or subscriber under national law; must minimise impact on third-party property.
quote: any provider of public electronic communications networks shall have the right to terminate its network at the premises of the subscriber, subject to the agreement of the owner and/or the subscriber
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Physical network termination at premises; contract/property law. Test: yes.

right: Right to refer disputes to the national dispute settlement body
rightholder: any party (access seekers, network operators, public sector bodies, holders of in-building rights)
description: Refer disputes on infrastructure access, information and surveys, coordination of civil works or in-building access to an independent dispute settlement body for a binding decision.
exercise: Where access is refused or no agreement within one month; binding decision within four months (access) or one month (other disputes), which may set FRAND terms and price; without prejudice to court action.
quote: Without prejudice to the possibility to refer a case to a court, any party shall be entitled to refer to the competent national dispute settlement body established pursuant to Article 14 a dispute
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Referral to dispute settlement body. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of competent bodies
rightholder: parties affected by a decision of a competent body
description: Appeal any decision of a dispute settlement body or single information point body to a fully independent appeal body, and bring the dispute before the competent national court.
exercise: In accordance with national law; Art. 31 EECC applies mutatis mutandis.
quote: Any decision taken by a competent body shall be subject to an appeal, in accordance with national law, before a fully independent appeal body, including a body of judicial character.
entry_current_status: Directive 2014/61/EU replaced by the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1309
tl_reason: Appeal to independent body/court. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to open internet access
description: End-users may access and distribute information and content, use and provide applications and services, and use terminal equipment of their choice via their internet access service, irrespective of location, origin or destination; contracts and commercial practices may not limit these rights (Art. 3(2)).
exercise: Complaint to the provider (Art. 4(2)); enforcement by NRA (Art. 5).
quote: End-users shall have the right to access and distribute information and content, use and provide applications and services, and use terminal equipment of their choice
notes: Without prejudice to law on lawfulness of content
tl_reason: Provider must permit apps, content and terminal equipment of choice; holder operates devices and services online. Nothing remains without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to equal, non-discriminatory treatment of internet traffic
description: Providers must treat all traffic equally and may not block, slow down, alter, restrict, degrade or discriminate between specific content, applications or services, except reasonable, transparent, non-commercial traffic management or where necessary to comply with law, protect network security or manage exceptional congestion.
quote: Providers of internet access services shall treat all traffic equally, when providing internet access services, without discrimination, restriction or interference
tl_reason: Object is network traffic handling; duty fulfilled only technically, using it means using the internet and checking throttling needs measurement. Test: no.

right: Freedom to offer specialised (optimised) services
rightholder: providers of electronic communications to the public and providers of content, applications and services
description: Providers may offer services other than internet access that are optimised for specific content, applications or services where optimisation is objectively necessary, provided network capacity suffices and internet access quality is not degraded.
