quote: shall be free to offer services other than internet access services which are optimised for specific content, applications or services, or a combination thereof
tl_reason: Business freedom of providers to offer optimised services; market access, no user-side mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to contractual information on traffic management, speeds and remedies
description: Contracts including internet access must explain the impact of traffic management, volume limits and specialised services, the minimum, normally available, maximum and advertised speeds (fixed) or estimated maximum and advertised speeds (mobile), and the consumer's remedies for discrepancies; providers must also publish this information.
quote: Providers of internet access services shall ensure that any contract which includes internet access services specifies at least the following:
tl_reason: Contract and published information on speeds and remedies; plain text usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to an internal complaint procedure on open internet rights
description: Providers must have transparent, simple and efficient procedures to handle end-users' complaints about open internet rights and contractual transparency obligations.
exercise: Complaint to the provider.
quote: Providers of internet access services shall put in place transparent, simple and efficient procedures to address complaints of end-users
tl_reason: Complaint to the provider through a simple procedure; letter works and reply is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to consumer remedies for persistent internet speed/quality discrepancies
description: A significant continuous or regularly recurring gap between actual and contractually indicated speed or quality, established by an NRA-certified monitoring mechanism, is deemed non-conformity triggering the consumer's national-law remedies.
exercise: Evidence via NRA-certified monitoring mechanism; remedies under national law.
quote: be deemed to constitute non-conformity of performance for the purposes of triggering the remedies available to the consumer in accordance with national law.
notes: Only contracts concluded or renewed from 29 November 2015
tl_reason: Remedy is contractual, but non-conformity is proven with an NRA-certified speed-monitoring tool. Conflict: technical evidence mechanism, plain result.

right: Right to capped retail prices for intra-EU calls and SMS
description: Retail prices for calls and SMS from the home Member State to numbers in another Member State may not exceed EUR 0.19 per minute and EUR 0.06 per SMS (excl. VAT); consumers who did not choose another tariff are automatically put on the capped tariff (Art. 5a(3)).
quote: any retail price (excluding VAT) charged to consumers for regulated intra-EU communications shall not exceed EUR 0,19 per minute for calls and EUR 0,06 per SMS message.
notes: Inserted by EECC (M2); Art. 5a expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 10(5)); NRA derogations possible (Art. 5a(6))
tl_reason: Retail price cap for intra-EU calls and SMS; no mechanism or technical ability. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose an alternative international tariff, after being informed of lost advantages
description: Consumers may expressly choose a different international tariff instead of the regulated cap, after the provider informs them of the advantages they would lose.
exercise: Express choice; prior information by the provider.
quote: providers of regulated intra-EU communications may additionally offer, and consumers may expressly choose, a tariff for international communications
notes: Art. 5a expires 30 June 2032
tl_reason: Express choice of another tariff; ordinary contractual choice. Test: yes.

right: Right to switch to or from the regulated intra-EU tariff free of charge
description: Consumers can switch from or back to the capped intra-EU tariff free of charge, without conditions on other subscription elements.
exercise: Request to the provider; switch within one working day of receipt.
quote: Consumers may switch from or back to the tariffs laid down in paragraph 1 within one working day of receipt of the request by the provider, free of charge
notes: Art. 5a expires 30 June 2032
tl_reason: Tariff switch on request; ordinary contractual request, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of a provider to request a derogation from the intra-EU price cap
description: A provider facing specific and exceptional circumstances that make the cap unsustainable for its domestic pricing can apply to the NRA for a derogation for a renewable one-year period.
exercise: Application to the NRA carrying the evidentiary burden.
quote: a national regulatory authority may, upon that provider’s request, grant a derogation from paragraph 1 only to the extent necessary and for a renewable period of one year.
notes: Art. 5a expires 30 June 2032
tl_reason: Provider's application for a regulatory derogation; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to pay domestic prices for intra-EU communications
addressee: providers of number-based interpersonal communications services
description: From 2029 providers may not charge consumers different retail prices for domestic and intra-EU calls/SMS, once Commission technical rules on sustainability, fair use and anti-fraud are adopted; providers may apply this voluntarily from 2025 (Art. 5a(8)).
quote: From 1 January 2029, providers shall not apply different retail prices to consumers for domestic communications and intra-EU communications
notes: Inserted by Reg (EU) 2024/1309 (M3); conditional on adoption of implementing rules
tl_reason: Price parity for intra-EU communications; pricing rule without technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to start providing networks or services upon notification, without prior authorisation decision
rightholder: undertaking (natural or legal person) subject to the general authorisation
description: An undertaking may start providing electronic communications networks or services once it has notified the authority (where notification is required); no explicit decision or other administrative act may be required first.
exercise: Submit the minimal notification listed in Art. 12(4) (name, legal status, address, contact, description, Member States, start date); only Art. 52(1) TFEU grounds can limit the freedom to provide (Art. 12(1)).
quote: Upon notification, when required, an undertaking may start the activity, where necessary subject to the provisions on the rights of use under this Directive.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Market entry upon notification; administrative freedom of undertakings. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a standardised declaration confirming general-authorisation rights
rightholder: undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services under the general authorisation
description: On request, the undertaking obtains a standardised declaration confirming its notification and detailing its rights to apply for rights to install facilities, negotiate interconnection and obtain access, to facilitate exercise of those rights vis-a-vis other authorities or undertakings.
exercise: Request to the competent authority; issued within one week (may be an automatic reply to the notification).
quote: Competent authorities shall, within one week of the request of an undertaking, issue standardised declarations confirming, where applicable, that the undertaking has submitted a notification
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Standardised declaration issued by the authority on request; administrative document. Test: yes.

right: Minimum rights derived from the general authorisation
rightholder: undertaking subject to the general authorisation
description: Authorised undertakings have the right to provide electronic communications networks and services, to use radio spectrum (subject to Arts 13, 46, 55) and to have their applications for rights to install facilities (Art. 43) and for numbering resources (Art. 94) considered.
exercise: Applications to the competent authorities under Arts 43, 48 and 94.
quote: Undertakings subject to the general authorisation pursuant to Article 12, shall have the right to:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Authorisation rights of undertakings (market access, applications); no user-side mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to negotiate interconnection and obtain access or interconnection
rightholder: undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services to the public under the general authorisation
addressee: other providers of public networks / publicly available services
description: Public providers may negotiate interconnection with, and where applicable obtain access to or interconnection from, other authorised providers anywhere in the Union.
exercise: Commercial negotiation with other providers; disputes may be referred to the NRA (Arts 26-27).
quote: negotiate interconnection with and, where applicable, obtain access to, or interconnection from, other providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Interconnection is technical, but the right is commercial negotiation between peer operators, not a governed party. Conflict: holder and non-technical exercise.

right: Right to be given an opportunity to be designated as universal service provider
rightholder: undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services to the public under the general authorisation
description: Public providers must be given the opportunity to be designated to provide elements of the universal service or to cover parts of the national territory.
exercise: Through the efficient, objective, transparent and non-discriminatory designation mechanism of Art. 86(4), in which no undertaking is a priori excluded.
quote: be given an opportunity to be designated to provide different elements of the universal service or to cover different parts of the national territory in accordance with Article 86 or 87.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Opportunity to be designated universal service provider; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment on proposed amendments to rights, conditions and procedures
rightholder: interested parties, including users and consumers; holders of rights
description: Before rights, conditions or procedures concerning general authorisations, rights of use or rights to install facilities are amended, interested parties must be notified and allowed time to express their views; minor amendments need the holder's agreement.
exercise: Comment period of at least four weeks (save exceptional circumstances); amendments and reasons are published.
quote: Interested parties, including users and consumers, shall be allowed a sufficient period of time to express their views on the proposed amendments.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Comment in a regulatory consultation; ordinary written submission. Test: yes.

right: Compensation for restriction or withdrawal of radio spectrum rights of use
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum
description: Where rights of use for radio spectrum are restricted or withdrawn before expiry under pre-established procedures, the holder may be compensated appropriately.
exercise: Under national compensation provisions; withdrawal without consent requires prior consultation of interested parties (Art. 19(4)).
quote: In such cases, the holders of the rights may, where appropriate and in accordance with Union law and relevant national provisions, be compensated appropriately.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; compensation 'where appropriate'
tl_reason: Compensation for restricted spectrum rights; monetary claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed when information supplied to the authority is passed to the Commission
rightholder: undertakings that previously supplied information at the request of the authority
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authority
description: Where an authority passes to the Commission information that undertakings had earlier provided to it, those undertakings are informed.
quote: Where the information provided refers to information previously provided by undertakings at the request of the authority, such undertakings shall be informed thereof.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Information that data were passed to the Commission; administrative notice. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told the specific purpose of an information request
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authority
description: When an authority requires information relating to the general authorisation, rights of use or specific obligations, it must tell the undertaking the specific purpose for which the information will be used.
exercise: Requests must also be proportionate and objectively justified (Art. 21(1)).
quote: they shall inform them of the specific purpose for which this information is to be used.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Told the purpose of an information request; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of NGA coverage of a designated area
rightholder: undertaking expressing interest in a designated area
addressee: national regulatory and/or other competent authority
description: An undertaking that expresses interest in a designated 'white' area is told whether that area is or is likely to be covered by a next-generation access network below 100 Mbps.
exercise: Express interest to the authority following an invitation under Art. 22(3).
quote: It shall also inform any undertaking or public authority expressing its interest whether the designated area is covered or likely to be covered by a next-generation access network
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Information on network coverage of an area; plain administrative answer. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment on draft regulatory measures
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authority
description: Interested parties may comment on draft measures of national regulatory or other competent authorities that have a significant impact on the relevant market.
exercise: Consultation period of at least 30 days except in exceptional circumstances; consultations accessible through a single information point (Art. 23(3)).
quote: they give interested parties the opportunity to comment on the draft measure within a reasonable period
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Comment on draft regulatory measures; consultation by ordinary submission. Test: yes.

right: Right of end-users and consumers to have their views taken into account on end-user rights issues
rightholder: end-users, in particular consumers and end-users with disabilities
description: Competent authorities must take account of the views of end-users, consumers and end-users with disabilities on end-user and consumer rights issues, through a consultation mechanism accessible to persons with disabilities.
exercise: Via the national consultation mechanism.
quote: establish a consultation mechanism, accessible for end-users with disabilities, ensuring that in their decisions on issues related to end-user and consumer rights
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Views considered through a consultation mechanism; procedural participation, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to out-of-court dispute resolution with providers
rightholder: consumer (Member States may extend to other end-users, notably micro and small enterprises)
addressee: Member State / NRA or independent ADR body
description: Consumers can bring contract-performance disputes with providers arising under the Code to an ADR entity listed under the ADR Directive (NRA, competent authority or independent body expert in Arts 102-107 and 115).
exercise: Complaint to the designated ADR entity; cross-border disputes coordinated between Member States (Art. 25(2)).
quote: is listed as an alternative dispute resolution entity in accordance with Article 20(2) of Directive 2013/11/EU with a view to resolving disputes between providers and consumers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option to extend to other end-users
tl_reason: Out-of-court dispute resolution via an ADR entity; ordinary complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right to binding NRA dispute resolution between undertakings
rightholder: providers of electronic communications networks or services, undertakings benefiting from access/interconnection obligations, providers of associated facilities
description: Either party to a dispute about obligations under the Code can ask the NRA for a binding decision, with a full statement of reasons; court action remains open.
exercise: Request by either party; decision within four months save exceptional circumstances (Art. 26(1)); NRA may decline where mediation etc. is better, but must decide after four months on request (Art. 26(2)); reasons given (Art. 26(4)); courts not precluded (Art. 26(5)).
quote: the national regulatory authority concerned shall, at the request of either party, and without prejudice to paragraph 2, issue a binding decision to resolve the dispute
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: NRA dispute resolution between undertakings; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to refer a cross-border dispute to the national regulatory authorities
rightholder: any party to a dispute between undertakings in different Member States
description: A party to a cross-border dispute under the Code may refer it to the NRAs concerned; where trade between Member States is affected BEREC gives an opinion and NRAs then resolve the dispute.
exercise: Referral to NRA(s); BEREC opinion within four months; NRA obligations within one month of the opinion; interim measures possible on request (Art. 27(4)); courts not precluded (Art. 27(6)).
quote: Any party may refer the dispute to the national regulatory authority or authorities concerned.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Referral of a cross-border dispute to NRAs; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified of findings of non-compliance and to state views
rightholder: undertaking found not to comply with authorisation conditions, rights of use or specific obligations
description: Before enforcement measures, the undertaking is notified of the findings and can state its views; measures and their reasons are then communicated with a reasonable compliance period (Art. 30(3)).
exercise: Within the reasonable time limit set by the authority.
quote: it shall notify the undertaking of those findings and give the undertaking the opportunity to state its views, within a reasonable time limit.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Right to be heard before enforcement; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard on urgent interim measures
rightholder: undertaking subject to urgent interim measures
description: Where an authority takes urgent interim measures for serious breaches, the undertaking concerned must be given a reasonable opportunity to state its views and propose remedies.
exercise: Interim measures valid max. three months, extendable by up to three months.
quote: The competent authority shall give the undertaking concerned a reasonable opportunity to state its views and propose any remedies.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Right to be heard on interim measures; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal enforcement measures
description: Undertakings may appeal against compliance and enforcement measures taken under Art. 30 (penalties, cease orders, suspension or withdrawal of rights).
exercise: Appeal procedure of Art. 31.
quote: Undertakings shall have the right to appeal against measures taken under this Article in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 31.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Appeal against enforcement measures; legal remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right of appeal against decisions of a competent authority
rightholder: any user or undertaking providing electronic communications networks, services or associated facilities who is affected by a decision
description: Any affected user or undertaking can appeal a competent authority's decision to an independent appeal body that duly considers the merits; non-judicial bodies must give written reasons and their decisions are reviewable by a court (Art. 31(2)).
exercise: Appeal to the national appeal body; decision stands pending appeal unless interim measures are granted under national law.
quote: any user or undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services or associated facilities who is affected by a decision of a competent authority has the right of appeal
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Appeal against authority decisions; legal remedy without technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of market participants to reasons when Member States do not run a joint spectrum authorisation
rightholder: market participants that expressed interest in a joint authorisation process
description: Where market participants have expressed interest in a joint authorisation process for spectrum but Member States do not act jointly, the participants are informed of the reasons.
quote: Where, in spite of the interest expressed by market participants, Member States do not act jointly, they shall inform those market participants of the reasons explaining their decision.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Reasons for not running a joint spectrum authorisation; administrative information. Test: yes.

right: Right to a timely, transparent decision on applications for rights of way
rightholder: undertaking authorised to provide (public) electronic communications networks
description: Applications for rights to install facilities on, over or under public or private property must be handled through simple, transparent, non-discriminatory procedures, with conditions attached transparently and non-discriminatorily.
exercise: Decision within six months of the application, except in case of expropriation.
quote: acts on the basis of simple, efficient, transparent and publicly available procedures, applied without discrimination and without delay, and in any event makes its decision within six months
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Timely decision on rights-of-way applications; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of an alternative-use decision for harmonised spectrum
rightholder: prospective user of a harmonised band
description: A prospective user can obtain prompt review of a decision allowing exceptional alternative use of a harmonised spectrum band where it wants to use the band in line with the technical implementing measure.
exercise: Duly justified request to the competent authority.
quote: shall in any event be reviewed promptly upon a duly justified request by a prospective user to the competent authority for use of the band in accordance with the technical implementing measure
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Request review of an alternative-use spectrum decision; administrative request. Test: yes.

right: Right to be granted individual rights of use for radio spectrum upon request
rightholder: undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services under the general authorisation
description: Where individual rights of use are needed, they are granted on request to any authorised undertaking through open, objective, transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate procedures (Art. 48(2)).
exercise: Application to the competent authority; decision as soon as possible and within six weeks for spectrum declared available in the national frequency plan (Art. 48(6)); up to eight months for competitive/comparative procedures (Art. 55(7)).
quote: Member States shall grant such rights, upon request, to any undertaking for the provision of electronic communications networks or services under the general authorisation referred to in Article 12
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Grant of spectrum rights on application; administrative licensing. Test: yes.

right: Right to a reasoned decision when a spectrum applicant is found unable to meet conditions
rightholder: applicant for individual rights of use for radio spectrum
description: If the authority concludes that an applicant lacks the ability to comply with the conditions, it must issue a duly reasoned decision; eligibility criteria must be set out in advance.
quote: Where the competent authority concludes that an applicant does not possess the required ability, it shall provide a duly reasoned decision to that effect.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Reasoned decision for a rejected spectrum applicant; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to minimum duration and extension of wireless broadband spectrum rights
rightholder: holders of individual rights of use for harmonised wireless broadband spectrum
description: Holders benefit from at least 20 years of regulatory predictability: rights valid for at least 15 years plus adequate extension, which must be granted unless general criteria (efficient use, competition) are not met; the holder is notified of the outcome.
exercise: Authority assesses at the latest two years before expiry and notifies the holder; interested parties may comment on draft measures for at least three months. Derogations in Art. 49(3).
quote: Member States shall ensure that such rights are valid for a duration of at least 15 years and include, where necessary to comply with the first subparagraph, an adequate extension thereof
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Minimum duration and extension of spectrum licences; regulatory predictability, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to request assessment of renewal of harmonised spectrum rights
rightholder: holder of individual rights of use for harmonised radio spectrum
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authority
description: The holder can ask the authority to assess renewal of its rights; the authority must decide in a timely manner before expiry unless renewal was excluded at assignment.
exercise: Request not earlier than five years before expiry; open procedure with public consultation where rights are limited in number (Art. 50(3)).
quote: those authorities shall assess the need for such renewal at their own initiative or upon request by the holder of the right, in the latter case not earlier than five years prior to expiry
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Request a renewal assessment of spectrum rights; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to transfer or lease individual rights of use for radio spectrum
rightholder: undertakings holding individual rights of use for radio spectrum
description: Holders may transfer or lease spectrum rights to other undertakings; transfers/leases keeping original conditions must be allowed under the least onerous procedure, and leases cannot be refused where the lessor remains liable (Art. 51(3)).
exercise: Notify intention and effective transfer to the competent authority (Art. 51(2)); requests to adapt conditions must be considered in a timely manner.
quote: Member States shall ensure that undertakings may transfer or lease to other undertakings individual rights of use for radio spectrum.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may exclude rights granted free of charge or for broadcasting
tl_reason: Transfer or lease of spectrum rights; licence transaction. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of a limitation on the number of spectrum rights
description: Where the number of spectrum rights of use is limited, affected undertakings can request that the limitation be reviewed; interested parties including users and consumers can comment via public consultation (Art. 55(1)(b)).
exercise: Reasonable request to the authority.
quote: review, as appropriate, the limitation at regular intervals or at the reasonable request of affected undertakings;
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Request review of a limit on spectrum rights; administrative request. Test: yes.

right: Right to provide RLAN (Wi-Fi) access without general authorisation
rightholder: undertaking, public authority or end-user providing RLAN access on a non-economic or ancillary basis
description: Persons who provide access to a public network through RLANs where this is not part of, or is ancillary to, an economic activity are not subject to the general authorisation, end-user-rights obligations or interconnection obligations.
quote: any undertaking, public authority or end-user providing such access shall not be subject to any general authorisation for the provision of electronic communications networks or services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Exemption from authorisation for non-commercial Wi-Fi provision; regulatory freedom, no duty-bearer mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to give prior informed agreement before a provider opens an RLAN at the end-user's premises to the public
addressee: provider of public electronic communications networks or services
description: A provider may allow public access through an RLAN located at an end-user's premises only with the end-user's prior informed agreement.
quote: subject to compliance with the applicable general authorisation conditions and the prior informed agreement of the end-user.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is the end-user's router opened as a public RLAN, but agreement can be given or refused by any means. Conflict: digital object, non-technical consent.

right: Right to access third-party RLANs and to share one's own RLAN
addressee: providers of public electronic communications networks or services; competent authorities
description: Providers may not unilaterally restrict end-users from accessing RLANs of their choice provided by third parties or from sharing access reciprocally, including via aggregation initiatives; authorities may not limit end-users sharing their RLANs (Art. 56(5)).
quote: providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services do not unilaterally restrict or prevent end-users from:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Provider must not block third-party Wi-Fi or sharing; holder connects devices across networks. Unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to deploy small-area wireless access points without individual permits
rightholder: persons deploying small-area wireless access points (operators)
description: Deployment of small cells complying with the Commission's characteristics cannot be subject to individual town-planning or other prior permits (save protected buildings/sites or public safety), nor to fees beyond administrative charges (Art. 57(5)).
quote: competent authorities shall not subject the deployment of small-area wireless access points complying with the characteristics laid down pursuant to paragraph 2 to any individual town planning permit
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Deploying small cells without individual permits; planning freedom for operators. Test: yes.

right: Right of operators to access public physical infrastructure to host small cells
addressee: national, regional or local public authorities
description: Operators may access physical infrastructure controlled by public authorities (street furniture, light poles, bus stops etc.) that is suitable to host or connect small-area wireless access points.
exercise: Reasonable request; authorities must meet it on fair, reasonable, transparent and non-discriminatory terms published at a single information point.
quote: ensure that operators have the right to access any physical infrastructure controlled by national, regional or local public authorities, which is technically suitable to host
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Access to public physical infrastructure for small cells; property access. Test: yes.

right: Freedom to negotiate access and interconnection agreements, including without local authorisation
description: Undertakings can freely negotiate technical and commercial access/interconnection arrangements; a requester that does not provide services or operate a network in a Member State need not be authorised there.
quote: The undertaking requesting access or interconnection does not need to be authorised to operate in the Member State where access or interconnection is requested
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Free negotiation of technical access/interconnection without local authorisation; object technical but right commercial and regulatory. Conflict: holder and non-technical exercise.

right: Right of network operators to negotiate interconnection
rightholder: operators of public electronic communications networks
description: Public network operators have a right (and, when requested by other authorised undertakings, an obligation) to negotiate interconnection to ensure provision and interoperability of services.
exercise: Request to negotiate; NRA-imposed conditions under Arts 61, 62, 68 apply; disputes under Arts 26-27.
quote: Operators of public electronic communications networks shall have a right and, when requested by other undertakings so authorised in accordance with Article 15, an obligation to negotiate
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Negotiating interconnection between operators; object technical but exercised by commercial negotiation among peers. Conflict: holder and non-technical exercise.

right: Right to confidentiality of information supplied in access/interconnection negotiations
rightholder: undertaking supplying information in access or interconnection negotiations
description: Information obtained from another undertaking before, during or after access or interconnection negotiations may be used only for the purpose supplied and must be kept confidential, not passed to departments, subsidiaries or partners.
quote: use that information solely for the purpose for which it was supplied and respect at all times the confidentiality of information transmitted or stored.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Confidentiality of negotiation information; legal protection. Test: yes.

right: Right of broadcasters to conditional access services on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms
description: Conditional access providers on which broadcasters depend must offer all broadcasters, on FRAND terms, technical services enabling their digital services to be received by authorised viewers or listeners (Annex II, Part I(a)).
quote: offer to all broadcasters, on a fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory basis compatible with Union competition law, technical services enabling the broadcasters’ digitally-transmitted services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; content in Annex II Part I
tl_reason: Conditional-access provider must offer technical services enabling digital reception; usable only technically. Business holder. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of consumer-equipment manufacturers to FRAND licences for conditional access technology
addressee: holders of industrial property rights in conditional access products and systems
description: Licences for conditional access products/systems must be granted to equipment manufacturers on FRAND terms and may not prohibit or discourage including a common interface or means specific to another access system (Annex II, Part I(b)).
quote: holders of industrial property rights to conditional access products and systems are to ensure that this is done on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; content in Annex II Part I
tl_reason: FRAND licence is a contract right, but its point is building interoperable equipment with a common interface. Conflict: legal exercise vs technical use; manufacturer holder.

right: Right of SMP undertakings to offer commitments
rightholder: undertakings designated as having significant market power
description: SMP undertakings may offer commitments on access and/or co-investment (incl. very high capacity networks, Art. 76, and voluntary separation, Art. 78), receive the NRA's preliminary conclusions after a market test and revise their offer; the NRA may make them binding.
exercise: Sufficiently detailed offer to the NRA; market test by public consultation (Art. 79(2)).
quote: Undertakings designated as having significant market power may offer to the national regulatory authority commitments regarding conditions for access, co-investment, or both
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: SMP undertaking offers commitments to the NRA; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of potential co-investors and access seekers to comment on offered commitments
rightholder: potential co-investors or access seekers (third parties directly affected)
description: In the NRA's market test of SMP commitments, directly affected third parties may give views on compliance with the conditions and propose changes.
exercise: Public consultation run by the NRA.
quote: Potential co-investors or access seekers may provide views on the compliance of the commitments offered with the conditions provided
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Comment on offered commitments in a market test; consultation. Test: yes.

right: Right to affordable adequate broadband internet access and voice services at a fixed location
rightholder: consumer (Member States may extend to SMEs and not-for-profit organisations, Art. 84(5))
description: All consumers must have access at an affordable price to an available adequate broadband internet access service (supporting at least the Annex V services) and voice communications, including the underlying connection, at a fixed location.
exercise: Implemented through Arts 85-86 measures (support, social tariffs, designation).
quote: all consumers in their territories have access at an affordable price, in light of specific national conditions, to an available adequate broadband internet access service
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; universal service; Member States may extend to mobile services (Art. 84(2))
tl_reason: Object is a broadband connection usable only technically, but the right is affordability obtained by ordinary contract. Conflict: digital object, social-price entitlement.

right: Right to request a universal service connection limited to voice
description: A consumer may ask that the universal service connection be limited to supporting voice communications services.
exercise: Request to the provider.
quote: When a consumer so requests, the connection referred to in paragraph 1 and, where applicable, in paragraph 2 may be limited to support voice communications services.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Request a voice-only connection; ordinary contractual request. Test: yes.

right: Right of low-income consumers to affordability support or social tariffs
rightholder: consumers with a low income or special social needs
addressee: Member State; providers of broadband and voice services
description: Where retail prices are unaffordable, consumers with a low income or special social needs receive support for communication purposes and/or special tariff options or packages for adequate broadband and voice services at least at a fixed location, with a choice of undertakings where providers are designated.
exercise: As organised nationally (direct support or provider tariff obligations).
quote: Member States may ensure that support is provided to such consumers for communication purposes or require providers of such services to offer to those consumers tariff options or packages
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may extend to SMEs and not-for-profits (Art. 85(6))
tl_reason: Social tariffs or financial support; price and funding right. Test: yes.

right: Right to conclude a contract for social tariff options, keep one's number and avoid unwarranted disconnection
rightholder: consumers entitled to social tariff options or packages
description: Entitled consumers can conclude a contract with a provider or designated undertaking; their number must remain available for an adequate period and unwarranted disconnection must be avoided.
quote: consumers entitled to such tariff options or packages have a right to conclude a contract either with a provider of the services referred to in Article 84(1), or with an undertaking designated
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Contract for social tariff, number retention, no unwarranted disconnection; contract rights. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumers with disabilities to support for equivalent access
description: Consumers with disabilities receive support as appropriate, and measures ensure that related terminal equipment and specific equipment and services enhancing equivalent access (incl. total conversation and relay services) are available and affordable.
quote: Member States shall ensure, in light of national conditions, that support is provided, as appropriate, to consumers with disabilities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Support may cover assistive terminal equipment and relay services used technically, but the entitlement is support and affordability. Conflict: digital object, social right.

right: Right to have reasonable requests for a fixed broadband/voice connection met under a universal service obligation
description: Where availability cannot be ensured commercially, Member States may impose universal service obligations requiring designated undertakings to meet all reasonable end-user requests for access to adequate broadband and voice at a fixed location.
exercise: Request to the designated undertaking.
quote: it may impose appropriate universal service obligations to meet all reasonable requests by end-users for accessing those services in the relevant parts of its territory.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option
tl_reason: Reasonable request for a fixed broadband connection is plain, but the result is a connection usable only technically. Conflict: plain exercise, technical result.

right: Right not to pay for unnecessary facilities or services in universal service offers
addressee: providers of universal service broadband and voice
description: Terms of universal service providers must not oblige end-users to pay for facilities or services not necessary or not required for the requested service.
quote: establish terms and conditions in such a way that the end-user is not obliged to pay for facilities or services which are not necessary or not required for the service requested.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for unnecessary facilities; contract term rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to expenditure-control facilities and protection against unwarranted disconnection (universal service)
rightholder: consumers benefiting from affordable universal service under Art. 85
description: Consumers get the Annex VI Part A facilities to monitor and control spending (itemised billing, free selective barring, pre-payment, phased connection payments, warning before disconnection for non-payment, tariff advice, cost control, deactivation of third-party billing) and a system avoiding unwarranted disconnection.
exercise: Competent authority may waive where facilities are widely available (Art. 88(3)).
quote: offer the specific facilities and services set out in Part A of Annex VI as applicable, in order that consumers can monitor and control expenditure.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may extend to SMEs and not-for-profits
tl_reason: Mandated facilities mix technical settings (selective barring, third-party billing deactivation) with plain ones (itemised bills, instalments). Conflict: mechanism only partly technical.

right: Right of universal service providers to compensation or cost-sharing for an unfair net-cost burden
rightholder: universal service provider found to bear an unfair burden
description: A universal service provider that requests compensation has its net cost calculated (Art. 89) and, if the burden is unfair, is compensated from public funds and/or through a sharing mechanism among providers.
exercise: Request by the provider; transparent net-cost calculation and audit (Arts 89, 91).
quote: Member States shall, upon request from the provider concerned, decide to do one or both of the following:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Compensation for universal service net cost; funding. Test: yes.

right: Right to be granted rights of use for numbering resources upon request
rightholder: undertakings providing electronic communications networks or services (and other undertakings eligible under Art. 93(2))
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authority
description: Where individual rights of use for numbers are needed, they are granted on request through open, objective, transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate procedures, without unnecessary limits on their number.
exercise: Decision as soon as possible and within three weeks for numbers allocated for specific purposes (Art. 94(3)), extendable by three weeks for numbers of exceptional economic value (Art. 94(4)).
quote: national regulatory or other competent authorities shall grant such rights, upon request, to any undertaking for the provision of electronic communications networks or services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Grant of numbering rights; administrative licensing. Test: yes.

right: Right to free access to the 116000 missing-children hotline
description: End-users can call the hotline for reporting missing children on 116000 free of charge; end-users with disabilities must be able to access it to the greatest extent possible.
quote: Member States shall ensure that end-users have access free of charge to a service operating a hotline to report cases of missing children.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Free call to the 116000 hotline; a phone call is ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to access all numbers in the Union, including non-geographic numbers
addressee: national regulatory or other competent authorities; providers
description: Where economically feasible, end-users must be able to access and use services using non-geographic numbers within the Union and to access all numbers provided in the Union, including UIFN, regardless of technology.
exercise: Unless the called end-user has chosen for commercial reasons to limit access from certain areas; blocking possible for fraud or misuse (Art. 97(2)).
quote: access all numbers provided in the Union, regardless of the technology and devices used by the operator
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Reaching all EU numbers; routing duty is technical but exercise is an ordinary phone call. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed that a microenterprise provider is exempt from end-user rights
addressee: Member State / microenterprise provider of number-independent interpersonal communications services
description: Before concluding a contract with a microenterprise providing number-independent interpersonal communications services that benefits from the exemption from Title III, end-users must be informed of the exemption.
exercise: Before contract conclusion.
quote: Member States shall ensure that end-users are informed of an exemption under the first paragraph before concluding a contract with a microenterprise benefitting from such an exemption.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-contract notice of a microenterprise exemption; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to non-discrimination based on nationality, residence or establishment
addressee: providers of electronic communications networks or services
description: Providers may not apply different requirements or general conditions of access or use to end-users because of their nationality, place of residence or place of establishment, unless objectively justified.
quote: Providers of electronic communications networks or services shall not apply any different requirements or general conditions of access to, or use of, networks or services to end-users
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; also applies to exempt microenterprises (Art. 98)
tl_reason: Non-discrimination by nationality or residence; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a prior fair procedure, to be heard and to an effective remedy before access to services is restricted
rightholder: person(s) concerned by a measure restricting access to or use of services and applications
description: National measures limiting end-users' access to or use of services and applications via electronic communications networks must respect the Charter; a prior, fair and impartial procedure, including the right to be heard, presumption of innocence, privacy and an effective remedy, must be guaranteed.
exercise: Subject to adapted arrangements in duly substantiated urgent cases.
quote: A prior, fair and impartial procedure shall be guaranteed, including the right to be heard of the person or persons concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Fair procedure and remedy before access restrictions; procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive, Art. 102(2))
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (except M2M transmission)
description: Before being bound, the consumer receives the information required by Arts 5-6 of the Consumer Rights Directive plus Annex VIII (service characteristics, prices, duration, termination, compensation, etc.), clearly, on a durable medium or in an easily downloadable document.
exercise: Before conclusion of the contract or offer.
quote: Before a consumer is bound by a contract or any corresponding offer, providers of publicly available electronic communications services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on durable medium or downloadable document; plain content usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive contractual information in an accessible format
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services
description: End-users with disabilities can obtain the pre-contractual information in an accessible format.
exercise: On request.
quote: The information shall, upon request, be provided in an accessible format for end-users with disabilities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Contract information in an accessible format on request; plain request and usable result. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free contract summary before conclusion of the contract
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive)
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (except M2M transmission)
description: Consumers receive free of charge a concise contract summary on the Commission template (provider contacts, main characteristics, prices, duration, renewal/termination, accessibility, internet speeds and remedies); if it cannot be provided beforehand, the contract only becomes effective after the consumer confirms agreement upon receipt.
exercise: Before conclusion, including distance contracts.
quote: provide the contract summary free of charge to consumers, prior to the conclusion of the contract, including distance contracts.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Contract summary on a template, often delivered electronically; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right that pre-contractual information and summary form binding contract terms
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services
description: The pre-contractual information and contract summary become an integral part of the contract and cannot be altered unless both parties expressly agree.
quote: The information referred to in paragraphs 1 and 3 shall become an integral part of the contract and shall not be altered unless the contracting parties expressly agree otherwise.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-contract information becomes binding contract terms; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to monitor and control usage and be alerted before consumption limits are reached
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive)
addressee: providers of internet access or interpersonal communications services billed on time or volume
description: Consumers get a facility giving timely information on consumption of services in their tariff plan, a notification before any consumption limit is reached and when an included service is fully consumed.
quote: their providers shall offer consumers the facility to monitor and control the usage of each of those services.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may add usage caps (Art. 102(6))
tl_reason: Law mandates a usage-monitoring facility and alerts, but consumption figures are plain and obtainable by asking. Conflict: technical facility required, plain result.

right: Right to free access to an independent comparison tool
description: End-users have free access to at least one independent tool comparing prices, tariffs and quality of internet access and interpersonal communications services; the tool must offer a procedure to report incorrect information (Art. 103(3)(g)).
quote: ensure that end-users have access free of charge to at least one independent comparison tool which enables them to compare and evaluate different internet access services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Right is to an online comparison tool, but its output is a plain price and quality comparison. Conflict: electronic tool required, non-technical result.

right: Right of comparison-tool providers to certification
rightholder: provider of a comparison tool meeting the Art. 103(3)(a)-(h) criteria
description: A comparison tool that fulfils the independence, transparency and accuracy requirements is certified by the competent authority at its provider's request.
exercise: Request to the competent authority.
quote: Comparison tools fulfilling the requirements in points (a) to (h) shall, upon request by the provider of the tool, be certified by competent authorities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Certification of a comparison tool on request; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of third parties to reuse providers' published information for comparison tools
addressee: providers of internet access or interpersonal communications services
description: Third parties may use, free of charge and in open data formats, the information published by providers of internet access or interpersonal communications services in order to build independent comparison tools.
quote: Third parties shall have a right to use, free of charge and in open data formats, the information published by providers of internet access services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Reuse of providers' published information in open data formats to build comparison tools; requires software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to a maximum 24-month contractual commitment period
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive, Art. 105(2))
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (except NI-ICS and M2M transmission)
description: Contracts may not impose a commitment period longer than 24 months, and termination conditions must not deter switching; separate instalment contracts for deploying a physical connection are excepted.
quote: do not mandate a commitment period longer than 24 months.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may set shorter maxima
tl_reason: Maximum commitment period; contract term rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate an automatically prolonged contract at any time
addressee: providers of electronic communications services (except NI-ICS and M2M transmission)
description: After automatic prolongation of a fixed-term contract, the end-user may terminate at any time without costs other than charges for service during the notice period.
exercise: Notice period of at most one month, set by Member States.
quote: end-users are entitled to terminate the contract at any time with a maximum one-month notice period, as determined by Member States, and without incurring any costs
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Terminate a prolonged contract with notice; ordinary termination. Test: yes.

right: Right to notice before automatic prolongation and to best-tariff advice
addressee: providers of electronic communications services (except NI-ICS and M2M transmission)
description: Before automatic prolongation, end-users must be told prominently, in good time and on a durable medium of the end of the commitment and how to terminate, together with best-tariff advice; best-tariff information must be given at least annually.
quote: Before the contract is automatically prolonged, providers shall inform end-users, in a prominent and timely manner and on a durable medium, of the end of the contractual commitment
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Notice before prolongation and best-tariff advice on a durable medium; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate without cost upon unilateral changes to contractual conditions
rightholder: end-users (for M2M only consumers, micro/small enterprises, not-for-profits, Art. 105(7))
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (except NI-ICS)
description: End-users may terminate without further costs when the provider proposes changes to contractual conditions, unless the changes are exclusively beneficial, purely administrative with no negative effect, or imposed by law; providers must notify changes and the termination right at least one month in advance.
exercise: Exercise within one month of the notification (Member States may extend by up to three months); notification on a durable medium.
quote: End-users shall have the right to terminate their contract without incurring any further costs upon notice of changes in the contractual conditions proposed by the provider
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Termination on unilateral contract changes; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to remedies, including free termination, for persistent performance discrepancies
addressee: providers of electronic communications services other than IAS and NI-ICS
description: A significant continued or frequently recurring discrepancy between actual and contractual performance triggers the consumer's national-law remedies, including free termination.
exercise: Under national law.
quote: shall be considered to be a basis for triggering the remedies available to the consumer in accordance with national law, including the right to terminate the contract free of cost.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; for internet access services see Art. 4(4) Open Internet Regulation
tl_reason: Remedies for performance discrepancies under national law; contract remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right to early termination without compensation other than for retained subsidised equipment
rightholder: end-users with a right to terminate early (for M2M only consumers, micro/small enterprises, not-for-profits)
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (except NI-ICS)
description: Where an end-user lawfully terminates before the end of the term, no compensation is due except for retained subsidised terminal equipment, capped at its pro rata value or the remaining service fees, whichever is smaller.
quote: no compensation shall be due by the end-user other than for retained subsidised terminal equipment.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No compensation on early termination beyond subsidised equipment; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to have retained terminal equipment unlocked free of charge
rightholder: end-users retaining bundled terminal equipment after early termination
description: The provider must lift any condition (e.g. SIM lock) on the use of the terminal equipment on other networks free of charge.
exercise: At a time set by Member States and at the latest upon payment of the compensation.
quote: The provider shall lift any condition on the use of that terminal equipment on other networks free of charge
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Provider must lift the SIM/network lock on the device; result is using it on other networks. Impossible without technical unlocking. Test: no.

right: Right to a smooth internet-access switching process with continuity of service
addressee: receiving and transferring internet access service providers
description: When switching internet access provider, the end-user receives adequate information before and during the process, continuity of service (old provider continues on same terms), activation on the agreed date, and loss of service of at most one working day.
exercise: Process led by the receiving provider (Art. 106(6)).
quote: The receiving provider shall ensure that the activation of the internet access service occurs within the shortest possible time on the date and within the timeframe expressly agreed with the end-user.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Provider-led technical switching with service continuity; holder only requests and receives information. Conflict: technical object, no technical ability required.

right: Right to number portability
rightholder: end-users with numbers from the national numbering plan
description: End-users can keep their numbers when changing provider (geographic numbers at a specific location, non-geographic at any location; not between fixed and mobile, Annex VI Part C), with no direct charges to the end-user (Art. 106(4)).
exercise: Request to the receiving provider, which leads the process.
quote: Member States shall ensure that all end-users with numbers from the national numbering plan have the right to retain their numbers, upon request, independently of the undertaking providing the service
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Porting is a technical process run by providers; holder requests by any means and keeps phoning on the number. Conflict: technical object, plain exercise.

right: Right to port a number for at least one month after contract termination
description: After terminating a contract, the end-user keeps the right to port the number to another provider for at least one month, unless renounced.
quote: the end-user can retain the right to port a number from the national numbering plan to another provider for a minimum of one month after the date of termination
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Port a number within a month after termination; technical porting by providers, plain request. Conflict: technical object, plain exercise.

right: Right to number activation within one working day and to reactivation if porting fails
rightholder: end-users who have agreed to port a number
addressee: receiving and transferring providers; access network operators
description: Ported numbers must be activated within one working day of the agreed date; if porting fails the transferring provider reactivates the number and services; service loss may not exceed one working day.
quote: end-users who have concluded an agreement to port a number to a new provider shall have that number activated within one working day from the date agreed with the end-user.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Activation of a ported number within one working day and reactivation; technical duties of providers, holder passive. Conflict: technical object, no holder ability.

right: Right not to be switched or have a number ported without explicit consent
description: Providers may not delay or abuse switching and porting, nor switch end-users or port numbers without their explicit consent; the old contract ends automatically once switching is completed.
quote: nor shall they port numbers or switch end-users without the end-users’ explicit consent.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Explicit consent before switching or porting; consent by any means protects against slamming. Test: yes.

right: Right to refund of remaining pre-paid credit on switching
description: On switching, consumers can obtain a refund of remaining pre-paid credit; any fee must be provided for in the contract and be proportionate to actual costs.
exercise: Request to the transferring provider.
quote: Transferring providers shall refund, upon request, any remaining credit to the consumers using pre-paid services.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Refund of prepaid credit on request; monetary claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for failed, delayed or abused switching/porting and missed appointments
description: End-users are compensated by their providers, easily and promptly, where providers fail to comply with switching and porting obligations, delay or abuse porting/switching, or miss service and installation appointments; end-users must be informed of these compensation rights (Art. 106(9)).
exercise: Under national compensation rules.
quote: Member States shall lay down rules on the compensation of end-users by their providers in an easy and timely manner in the case of the failure of a provider to comply with the obligations
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Compensation for failed switching or porting; monetary claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to end-user protections across all elements of a bundle
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive, Art. 107(4))
description: Where a bundle includes internet access or number-based interpersonal communications, the contract summary, transparency, duration/termination and switching rules apply to all bundle elements, including terminal equipment and other services.
quote: Article 102(3), Article 103(1), Article 105 and Article 106(1) shall apply to all elements of the bundle
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Consumer protections extend to all bundle elements; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the whole bundle where one element may be terminated
description: If the consumer may terminate any element of a bundle early for lack of conformity or failure to supply, the consumer may terminate the contract for all elements of the bundle.
quote: Member States shall provide that the consumer has the right to terminate the contract with respect to all elements of the bundle.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Terminate the whole bundle; contract termination. Test: yes.

right: Right that add-on subscriptions do not extend the contract duration
rightholder: consumer (and micro/small enterprises and not-for-profits unless they waive)
addressee: provider of internet access or number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Subscribing to additional services or terminal equipment from the same provider does not extend the original contract duration unless the consumer expressly agrees.
quote: shall not extend the original duration of the contract to which such services or terminal equipment are added, unless the consumer expressly agrees otherwise
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Add-ons do not extend contract duration; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to free access to emergency services via 112
rightholder: end-users, including users of public pay telephones
addressee: providers of number-based interpersonal communications services; Member States
description: End-users can reach emergency services free of charge, without any means of payment, by calling 112 and national emergency numbers; calls are routed to the most appropriate PSAP and caller location is transmitted free of charge (Art. 109(6)).
exercise: Dial 112.
quote: are able to access the emergency services through emergency communications free of charge and without having to use any means of payment, by using the single European emergency number ‘112’
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Free emergency calls to 112 with automatic location; a phone call is ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right of end-users with disabilities to equivalent access to emergency services
description: End-users with disabilities have access to emergency services equivalent to other end-users, including when travelling in another Member State, where feasible without pre-registration.
quote: Member States shall ensure that access for end-users with disabilities to emergency services is available through emergency communications and is equivalent to that enjoyed by other end-users
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Equivalent emergency access for persons with disabilities relies on text, video or app channels, but no specific mechanism is mandated. Conflict: technical channels, equivalence standard.

right: Right to receive public warnings
addressee: providers of mobile number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Where public warning systems exist, warnings on imminent or developing major emergencies and disasters are transmitted to end-users concerned (or via an equivalent channel such as a mobile app, Art. 110(2)).
quote: public warnings are transmitted by providers of mobile number-based interpersonal communications services to the end-users concerned.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Warnings arrive only via mobile network or app; nothing to request and content is plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right of end-users with disabilities to equivalent access and choice
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services
description: End-users with disabilities must have access to electronic communications services and related contractual information equivalent to the majority, and benefit from the same choice of undertakings and services.
exercise: Per requirements specified by competent authorities.
quote: have access to electronic communications services, including the related contractual information provided pursuant to Article 102, equivalent to that enjoyed by the majority of end-users; and
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Equivalent access needs accessible technical service design, but the right is equivalence obtained by ordinary subscription. Conflict: digital object, non-technical exercise.

right: Right of directory providers to obtain subscriber information on fair, cost-oriented terms
rightholder: providers of publicly available directory enquiry services and directories
addressee: providers of number-based interpersonal communications services attributing numbers
description: Number-assigning providers must meet all reasonable requests to make relevant subscriber information available for directory enquiry services and directories, in an agreed format and on fair, objective, cost-oriented and non-discriminatory terms.
exercise: Reasonable request; subject to data protection and Art. 12 ePrivacy Directive (Art. 112(4)).
quote: meet all reasonable requests to make available, for the purposes of the provision of publicly available directory enquiry services and directories, the relevant information in an agreed format
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Subscriber data in an agreed format on cost-oriented terms; dataset object, but format not prescribed and terms commercial. Conflict: mechanism not mandated.

right: Right to access directory enquiry services in other Member States
description: End-users in one Member State can directly access directory enquiry services in another Member State by voice call or SMS.
quote: Member States shall not maintain any regulatory restrictions which prevent end-users in one Member State from accessing directly the directory enquiry service in another Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Access directory enquiry services abroad by voice call or SMS; ordinary call. Test: yes.

right: Right to return digital television equipment free of charge on contract termination
description: On termination, end-users can return the provider's digital television equipment through a free and easy process, unless the provider shows it is fully interoperable with other providers' services.
quote: upon termination of their contract, end-users have the possibility to return the digital television equipment through a free and easy process
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Return TV equipment free of charge; physical return. Test: yes.

right: Right to additional expenditure-control facilities (Annex VI Part A)
rightholder: end-users as determined by Member States (some points consumers only)
addressee: providers of internet access or number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Where required by the competent authority, providers make available free of charge facilities such as itemised billing, free selective barring of outgoing/premium calls and SMS, pre-payment, phased connection payments, tariff advice on request, cost-control alerts and deactivation of third-party billing.
exercise: Request to the provider (e.g. barring, tariff advice) once the facility is mandated; Member States may waive or go further (Art. 115(2)-(3)).
quote: are able to require all providers of internet access services or publicly available number-based interpersonal communications services to make available free of charge
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; only where the competent authority requires it
tl_reason: Facilities mix technical settings (barring, cost-control alerts, third-party billing deactivation) with plain ones (itemised billing, tariff advice). Conflict: mechanism only partly technical.

right: Right to calling-line identification and e-mail forwarding/access after leaving an internet provider (Annex VI Part B)
addressee: providers of internet access or number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Where required by the competent authority, end-users get calling-line identification and, on request and free of charge after terminating an internet access contract, continued access to e-mails at the former provider's address or forwarding to a new address for a set period.
exercise: Request to the former internet access provider; period set by the NRA.
quote: This facility shall, on request and free-of-charge, enable end-users who terminate their contract with a provider of an internet access service to either access their e-mails
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; only where the competent authority requires it; content in Annex VI Part B
tl_reason: Continued e-mail access or forwarding after leaving the provider; result is a mailbox usable only technically. Test: no.

right: Right to wholesale roaming access
rightholder: undertakings requesting wholesale roaming access (roaming providers)
description: Mobile network operators must meet all reasonable requests for wholesale roaming access covering all network elements, technologies and generations, refusing only on objective grounds (not commercial ones), and must supply the reference offer and a draft agreement within one month and grant access within three months (Art. 3(5)).
exercise: Request to the MNO; good-faith negotiation; disputes to NRA (Art. 18).
quote: Mobile network operators shall meet all reasonable requests for wholesale roaming access
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: MNO must grant wholesale access to network elements and technologies; result usable only technically. Business holder. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Protection against unilateral termination of a wholesale roaming agreement without NRA authorisation
description: A visited network operator may terminate a wholesale roaming agreement for permanent roaming or abusive use only as a last resort and only after prior authorisation from its NRA, which decides within three months after consulting the home NRA.
quote: may terminate the wholesale roaming agreement unilaterally on grounds of permanent roaming or anomalous or abusive use of wholesale roaming access only upon prior authorisation
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Protection against termination of a wholesale roaming agreement; contractual and regulatory. Test: yes.

right: Right to a timely response to requests for commercial negotiation of components outside the reference offer
description: An access seeker wanting to negotiate components not in the reference offer must receive a response within a reasonable period not exceeding two months.
exercise: Request to the MNO.
quote: the mobile network operators shall respond to such a request within a reasonable period of time not exceeding two months from its initial receipt.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Timely response to a negotiation request; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to roam like at home (no roaming surcharges)
