description: Roaming customers pay no surcharge over the domestic retail price for regulated roaming calls, SMS and data in the EU, nor any general charge to use their device abroad, subject to fair use (Art. 5), which must still allow consumption consistent with the tariff plan, and authorised sustainability surcharges (Art. 6).
exercise: Disputes: out-of-court resolution (Art. 18(2)).
quote: Roaming providers shall not levy any surcharge in addition to the domestic retail price on roaming customers in any Member State for any regulated roaming calls made or received
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: No roaming surcharges; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to the same roaming quality of service as at home
description: Roaming services may not be offered on less advantageous terms than domestically, in particular as to quality of service, where the same network generation and technology is available on the visited network; unreasonable handover delays at borders must be avoided.
quote: Roaming providers shall not offer regulated retail roaming services under conditions that are less advantageous than those offered domestically
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Network quality abroad is technical behaviour, but the right also covers contractual conditions and calls usable non-technically. Conflict: object only partly technical.

right: Right of a roaming provider to apply for authorisation of a sustainability surcharge
description: A roaming provider unable to recover roaming costs from revenues may apply for authorisation to apply a surcharge; the NRA must authorise within one month unless the application is manifestly unfounded or incomplete, and must hear the provider before a final decision.
exercise: Application to the NRA with required information, updated every 12 months; decision within one month, or a further two months after hearing the provider (Art. 6(4)).
quote: that roaming provider may apply for authorisation to apply a surcharge.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Application for surcharge authorisation; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to capped surcharges and per-second/per-kilobyte billing beyond fair use
description: Surcharges for consumption beyond fair-use limits may not exceed the maximum wholesale charges (calls received: the EU mobile termination rate); no surcharge for SMS or voicemail received; calls billed per second (max. 30-second initial period) and data per kilobyte.
quote: any surcharge applied for regulated roaming calls made, regulated roaming SMS messages sent and regulated data roaming services shall not exceed the maximum wholesale charges
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Capped surcharges and billing units; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose an alternative roaming tariff, after a reminder of lost advantages
description: Customers may deliberately choose a roaming tariff other than the regulated one; the provider must remind them of the roaming advantages lost. The regulated tariff applies automatically otherwise.
quote: Roaming providers may offer, and roaming customers may deliberately choose, a roaming tariff other than one set in accordance with Articles 4, 5, 6 and paragraph 1 of this Article
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Choose an alternative roaming tariff; contractual choice. Test: yes.

right: Right to switch to or from the regulated roaming tariff at any time, free of charge
description: Customers can request at any time to switch to or back from the regulated roaming tariff; the switch is free, made within one working day and cannot impose conditions on other subscription elements.
exercise: Request to the provider; provider may require the previous tariff to have run up to two months.
quote: Any roaming customer may, at any time, request to switch to or from a tariff set in accordance with Articles 4, 5, 6 and paragraph 1 of this Article.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Switch tariff on request; contractual request. Test: yes.

right: Right to contractual information on roaming conditions
description: Retail contracts must specify the roaming tariff plans and volumes, quantified fair-use restrictions, conditions and quality of roaming, and the types of services (e.g. value-added services) that may cost more when roaming (Art. 8(4)); providers must also publish this information (Art. 8(5)).
quote: roaming providers shall ensure that a retail contract which includes any type of regulated retail roaming service specifies the characteristics of that regulated retail roaming service provided
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Contractual and published roaming information; plain text. Test: yes.

right: Right to an automatic free roaming price message on entering another Member State
description: On entering another Member State, customers automatically receive free basic personalised pricing information for calls and SMS (incl. fair use and surcharges) and a warning on value-added service costs with a link to a webpage; they can opt out and later require the service again free of charge.
exercise: Automatic; opt-out/re-activation free of charge on each message.
quote: by means of an automatic message, without undue delay and free of charge, when they enter a Member State other than that of their domestic provider, with basic personalised pricing information
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24); value-added-services database information applies from 1 June 2023 (Art. 24); also applies to non-terrestrial networks and travel outside the EU
tl_reason: Law requires an automatic location-triggered message with opt-out, but content is plain pricing information. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right of customers with disabilities to roaming price information by voice call
description: Customers with disabilities can request to receive the basic personalised roaming pricing information automatically by voice call, free of charge.
exercise: Request to the roaming provider.
quote: provide customers with disabilities with the basic personalised pricing information referred to in the first subparagraph automatically, by voice call, free of charge, if they so request.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Pricing information by voice call on request; ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to request detailed roaming pricing information free of charge
description: Customers can request and receive free detailed personalised pricing information on voice and SMS roaming charges and on transparency measures, wherever they are in the Union.
exercise: Voice call or SMS to the free number designated by the provider.
quote: customers shall have the right to request and receive, free of charge, and irrespective of their location within the Union, more detailed personalised pricing information on the roaming charges
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Detailed pricing information via free call or SMS; plain request and answer. Test: yes.

right: Right to notification when the voice/SMS fair-use volume is exhausted
description: Customers are notified when the fair-use volume for voice or SMS roaming is used up or a sustainability threshold is reached, with the surcharge that will apply; they can stop and later reinstate these notifications free of charge.
quote: The roaming provider shall send a notification to the roaming customer when the applicable fair use volume of regulated voice, or SMS, roaming services is fully consumed
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Automatic notification triggered by network metering; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to full information on roaming charges at subscription and on changes
description: Customers receive full information on applicable roaming charges when subscribing and updates without undue delay whenever charges change; customers on alternative tariffs get periodic reminders.
quote: Roaming providers shall provide all customers with full information on applicable roaming charges, when subscriptions are taken out.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Full roaming charge information at subscription and on changes; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to protection against inadvertent roaming charges in border regions
description: Providers must inform customers how to avoid inadvertent roaming in border regions and take all reasonable steps so they do not pay roaming charges for roaming inadvertently accessed while in their home Member State (also for data, Art. 14(6)).
quote: Roaming providers shall take all reasonable steps to protect their customers from paying roaming charges for inadvertently accessed roaming services while situated in their home Member State.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Provider must take technical network steps against inadvertent roaming, but holder's result is financial and a refund claim works. Conflict: technical duty, plain result.

right: Right to opt out of non-terrestrial networks (voice and SMS)
description: Where an opt-out mechanism from non-terrestrial (ship/aircraft) networks is offered, customers may opt out at any time, easily and free of charge, and request reinstatement; providers must take reasonable steps against charges from inadvertent connection.
quote: the roaming customer shall have the right to opt out from the use of non-terrestrial networks at any time, easily and free of charge and to request the reinstatement of the connection
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Opt-out from ship/aircraft networks presupposes a mechanism with technical effect, but a phone request works and the result needs no technical use. Conflict: exercise.

right: Right to information on data roaming charges and how to switch off automatic data roaming
description: Customers are kept informed before and after contracting about data roaming charges so they can monitor spending, about the risk of automatic data roaming, and, free of charge, how to switch off automatic data roaming connections.
quote: roaming providers shall notify to their customers, free of charge and in a clear and easily understandable manner, how to switch off those automatic data roaming connections
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Information on data roaming charges and how to switch off data roaming; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to an automatic free data roaming tariff message
description: When first using data roaming in another Member State, customers receive free basic personalised tariff information (incl. fair use and surcharges); they can opt out and later require it again free of charge.
quote: An automatic message from the roaming provider shall inform the roaming customer that the latter is using regulated data roaming services, and provide basic personalised tariff information
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24); does not apply to M2M devices (Art. 14(5))
tl_reason: Automatic data-roaming tariff message required; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to notification when the data fair-use volume is exhausted
description: Customers are notified when the data fair-use volume is used up or a sustainability threshold is reached, with the surcharge for further use; they can stop and later reinstate these notifications free of charge.
quote: The roaming provider shall send a notification when the applicable fair use volume of regulated data roaming service is fully consumed
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Automatic notification when data fair use is exhausted; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to a data roaming spending cap with alerts and cut-off
description: Customers get free access to a facility showing accumulated data roaming consumption and guaranteeing that spending does not exceed a chosen limit (default about EUR 50 per month) without explicit consent; alerts at 80 % and when the limit would be exceeded, after which service stops unless the customer asks to continue.
exercise: Choose another limit or opt out by notifying the provider; removal or reinstatement within one working day, free of charge.
quote: Each roaming provider shall grant to all their roaming customers free of charge access to a facility which provides in a timely manner information on the accumulated consumption
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24); not for M2M devices; outside the EU only where real-time monitoring is possible (Art. 14(8))
tl_reason: Provider must offer a facility tracking consumption and cutting off data at a chosen limit; a real-time cap cannot work without it. Test: no.

right: Right to opt out of non-terrestrial networks (data)
description: Where an opt-out from non-terrestrial networks is offered, customers may opt out of using them for data at any time, easily and free of charge, and request reinstatement.
quote: the customer shall have the right to opt out from the use of non-terrestrial networks at any time, easily and free of charge, and to request the reinstatement of the connection to such networks.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Opt-out from non-terrestrial networks for data has technical effect, but a request by any means works. Conflict: technical object, plain exercise.

right: Right to information on access to emergency services when roaming
description: On entering another Member State, customers receive a free automatic message that they can call 112 free of charge, with a link to an accessible webpage on alternative means of emergency access and, where available, public warning apps.
exercise: Automatic SMS on entering another Member State.
quote: inform the roaming customer, by means of an automatic message, that the latter may access emergency services free of charge by calling the single European emergency number ‘112’.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24); database-related information applies from 1 June 2023 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Automatic message on 112 access with a webpage link; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to NRA dispute resolution between undertakings on roaming obligations
rightholder: undertakings providing electronic communications networks or services (incl. visited network operators and other operators)
description: Disputes between undertakings about obligations under the Regulation, including rates for wholesale roaming inputs, can be referred to the NRA under EECC Arts 26-27; cross-border disputes are notified to BEREC.
exercise: Referral to the competent NRA(s).
quote: the dispute resolution procedures laid down in Articles 26 and 27 of Directive (EU) 2018/1972 shall apply.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: NRA dispute resolution between undertakings; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to out-of-court dispute resolution for roaming disputes
addressee: Member States / ADR entity under EECC Art. 25
description: Consumers and end-users with unresolved disputes on matters covered by the Regulation can use the out-of-court procedures of EECC Art. 25.
exercise: Complaint to the national ADR entity.
quote: the Member States shall ensure that the out-of-court dispute resolution procedures laid down in Article 25 of Directive (EU) 2018/1972 are available.
notes: Regulation expires 30 June 2032 (Art. 24)
tl_reason: Out-of-court dispute resolution; ordinary complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right to register .eu domain names
rightholder: Union citizens (wherever resident), non-EU residents of a Member State, undertakings and organisations established in the Union
description: Eligible persons may request registration of one or more .eu domain names; names are allocated first-come, first-served to the eligible party whose technically correct request is received first (Art. 4(1)), and the Registry must perform the registration (Art. 10(e)).
exercise: Request through an accredited Registrar; names transferable only to eligible parties (Art. 4(6)).
quote: Registration of one or more domain names under the .eu TLD can be requested by any of the following:
tl_reason: Registration via registrar systems of a domain name, a digital resource usable only through DNS and hosting. Test: no.

right: Right to seek revocation or transfer of a speculative or abusive .eu domain name
rightholder: holder of a right in a name recognised by Union or national law
description: A person with a right in a name can have an identical or confusingly similar .eu domain revoked and, where necessary, transferred, if it was registered without rights or legitimate interest or registered or used in bad faith.
exercise: ADR procedure under the .eu ADR policy (Art. 11(a)) or judicial procedure.
quote: A domain name may also be revoked, and where necessary subsequently transferred to another party, following an appropriate ADR or judicial procedure
tl_reason: ADR or court claim is non-technical; result may be transfer of a domain name usable only technically. Conflict: plain exercise, sometimes digital result.

right: Right to register .eu domain names in all official EU language scripts
description: Registration is available in all characters of the official languages of the Union institutions, as allowed by Internationalised Domain Name protocols.
quote: The registration of domain names shall be carried out in all the characters of the official languages of the Union institutions
tl_reason: Registry must support internationalised domain names; result is a domain usable only technically. Test: no.

right: Right to a Member State governing law and an EU-based dispute forum in registration contracts
description: Contracts between the Registry and Registrars and between Registrars and registrants may not choose non-Member-State law or a court, arbitration or other dispute body outside the Union.
quote: nor shall they designate a court, arbitration court or other body located outside the Union as the relevant dispute resolution body.
notes: Without prejudice to Reg (EU) 1215/2012
tl_reason: Governing-law and forum rule in registration contracts; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right of Registrars to fair accreditation and equal treatment
rightholder: Registrars (natural or legal persons providing registration services)
description: Registrars are accredited under reasonable, transparent, non-discriminatory, publicly available procedures approved by the Commission, and receive equivalent conditions, services and information as the Registry's own equivalent services.
exercise: Application for accreditation to the Registry.
quote: The Registry shall accredit Registrars in accordance with reasonable, transparent and non-discriminatory accreditation procedures which have been approved in advance by the Commission.
tl_reason: Registrar accreditation; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to ADR for contractual disputes with the Registry
description: Registrars and registrants can resolve contractual disputes with the Registry through alternative dispute resolution with adequate procedural guarantees, without prejudice to court proceedings.
quote: the possibility for Registrars and registrants to resolve any contractual dispute with the Registry by means of ADR;
tl_reason: ADR for contractual disputes with the Registry; ordinary dispute resolution. Test: yes.

right: Right of existing holders to retain .eu domain names registered under the old rules
rightholder: domain name holders registered under Art. 4(2)(b) Reg (EC) 733/2002
description: Holders of domain names registered under the previous eligibility rules keep their rights in those names.
quote: shall retain their rights in relation to the existing registered domain names.
notes: Transitional provision
tl_reason: Transitional guarantee needs no act or mechanism, but its object, a domain name, is usable only technically. Conflict: no exercise, digital object.

right: Right to withdraw consent
description: Withdraw consent to processing at any time; withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent and does not affect prior lawful processing.
exercise: Any time, by means as easy as those used to give consent; data subject must be told of this right before consenting.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.
tl_reason: Withdrawal must be as easy as consent, so a click where consent was clicked; but a letter or email still withdraws validly. Conflict: mechanism vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right of the holder of parental responsibility to give or authorise a child's consent
rightholder: holder of parental responsibility over a child below 16 (or lower national age, min. 13)
description: For information society services offered directly to a child under the age threshold, processing based on consent is lawful only if a parent or guardian gives or authorises consent.
exercise: Controller must make reasonable efforts to verify parental consent (Art. 8(2)).
quote: such processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child
notes: Member-State option to lower age to not below 13.
tl_reason: Consent to a child's ISS processing, verified with available technology, often online; a signed parental declaration still works. Conflict: digital object vs plain act. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise data subject rights by providing additional identifying information
description: Where the controller cannot identify the data subject, it must inform them if possible, and the data subject can still exercise Arts 15-20 by supplying information enabling identification.
exercise: Provide additional information to the controller; controller may not refuse to act unless it shows it cannot identify the data subject (Art. 12(2)).
quote: Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject, for the purpose of exercising his or her rights under those articles, provides additional information
tl_reason: Identifying info may be a technical identifier (cookie or device ID) for pseudonymous data, but plain details often suffice. Conflict: ability sometimes needed. Test: mostly yes.

right: Right to a response to a data subject request within one month
description: Receive information on action taken on requests under Arts 15-22 without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two months with reasons); free of charge as a rule.
exercise: Response within 1 month of receipt (+2 months for complex cases, notified within 1 month); electronic reply to electronic requests; free of charge unless manifestly unfounded/excessive (Art. 12(5)); oral information on request (Art. 12(1)).
quote: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.
tl_reason: Electronic reply to electronic requests, but the reply is plain information; a letter request still works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of reasons for not acting on a request and of remedies
description: If the controller does not act on a request, the data subject must be told why and informed of the possibility to complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.
exercise: Without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons for not taking action
tl_reason: Plain-language reasons and remedies, delivered by any means including electronic. No mechanism needed. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data are collected from the data subject
description: Receive, at the time of collection, the controller's identity, purposes, legal basis, recipients, transfers, retention period, existence of rights, automated decision-making logic, and information before any further processing for a new purpose.
exercise: At time of collection; before further processing for another purpose (Art. 13(3)); not required where data subject already has the information.
quote: the controller shall, at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information
tl_reason: Privacy notice information, usually online but usable on paper in plain language. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
description: Receive information about processing of data obtained from third parties, including categories of data and their source, plus the same core information as under Art. 13.
exercise: Within a reasonable period, at the latest one month after obtaining the data, or at first communication or first disclosure; exceptions in Art. 14(5).
quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the following information
tl_reason: Plain-language information on data sources and processing; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of access
description: Obtain confirmation whether personal data are processed and access to the data plus information on purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, source and automated decision-making.
exercise: Request to the controller; free of charge; reply within 1 month (Art. 12).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed
tl_reason: Object is the personal dataset, but a letter request works and access plus information can be given in plain form. Conflict: digital object vs plain result.

right: Right to be informed of safeguards for third-country transfers
description: Be informed of the appropriate safeguards (Art. 46) applied when personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation.
exercise: Part of an access request to the controller.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards pursuant to Article 46 relating to the transfer
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer safeguards, part of an access reply. No mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a copy of personal data
description: Obtain a copy of the personal data undergoing processing, in a commonly used electronic form where the request is made electronically.
exercise: First copy free; reasonable fee for further copies; must not adversely affect rights of others (Art. 15(4)).
quote: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing.
tl_reason: Copy of processed data delivered in commonly used electronic form (data archive); holder must open and interpret files. Test: no.

right: Right to rectification
description: Obtain without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data and completion of incomplete data, including by a supplementary statement.
exercise: Request to the controller; free of charge; reply within 1 month (Art. 12).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.
tl_reason: Object is the stored dataset and correction is technical for the controller, but a letter request works; holder only checks the result. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
description: Obtain erasure of personal data without undue delay where e.g. data are no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, an objection succeeds, processing is unlawful, or data were collected from a child for ISS.
exercise: Request to the controller; exceptions in Art. 17(3) (free expression, legal obligation, public health, archiving/research, legal claims).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay
tl_reason: Erasure of a dataset is done technically by the controller, but a plain request works and the result needs only checking. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to have other controllers informed of an erasure request for published data
description: Where the controller made the data public and must erase them, it must take reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing the data that the data subject requests erasure of links, copies or replications.
exercise: Follows from a successful erasure request; reasonable steps taking account of technology and cost.
quote: shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data that the data subject has requested the erasure
tl_reason: Object is published links, copies, replications; controller uses technical measures, but holder only makes a plain erasure request. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to restriction of processing
description: Obtain restriction of processing while accuracy is contested, where processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, where data are needed for legal claims, or pending verification of an objection.
exercise: Request to the controller; restricted data may then only be stored or processed with consent or on limited grounds (Art. 18(2)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies
tl_reason: Restriction is marking data in the controller's systems; a plain request works and the holder only checks. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed before a restriction is lifted
description: A data subject who obtained restriction must be informed by the controller before the restriction is lifted.
quote: A data subject who has obtained restriction of processing pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted.
tl_reason: Plain notice before a restriction is lifted; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to have recipients notified of rectification, erasure or restriction and to be told who they are
description: Controller must pass on rectifications, erasures and restrictions to each recipient, and on request tell the data subject who those recipients are.
exercise: On request of the data subject; notification to recipients unless impossible or disproportionate.
quote: The controller shall inform the data subject about those recipients if the data subject requests it.
tl_reason: Plain list of recipients on request; controller-to-recipient notification needs nothing from holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to data portability
description: Receive personal data provided to a controller in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit them to another controller without hindrance.
exercise: Only for automated processing based on consent or contract; not for public-interest tasks (Art. 20(3)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to receive the personal data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
tl_reason: Data in structured machine-readable format to be taken to another controller; holder must handle and transfer files. Test: no.

right: Right to direct controller-to-controller transmission
description: Have personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another when exercising portability, where technically feasible.
exercise: Where technically feasible.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible
tl_reason: Direct technical transmission between controllers; holder operates across two services. Without the transfer mechanism the right cannot be used. Test: no.

right: Right to object to processing based on public interest or legitimate interests
description: Object at any time, on grounds relating to one's particular situation, to processing based on Art. 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling; controller must stop unless it shows compelling legitimate grounds.
exercise: At any time; right must be explicitly brought to the data subject's attention at the latest at first communication (Art. 21(4)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her
tl_reason: Object is processing incl. profiling, but objection on personal grounds works by letter; nothing comes back. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to object to direct marketing
description: Object at any time to processing for direct marketing, including related profiling; data must then no longer be processed for that purpose (Art. 21(3)).
exercise: At any time; unconditional; must be presented clearly and separately (Art. 21(4)).
quote: the data subject shall have the right to object at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her for such marketing
tl_reason: Opt-out of marketing processing and profiling is often a click, but no mechanism is required and a letter works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to object by automated means
description: In the context of information society services, exercise the right to object through automated means using technical specifications (e.g. browser signals).
exercise: Via technical specifications in the context of information society services.
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her right to object by automated means using technical specifications
tl_reason: Objection expressed by automated means using technical specifications (e.g. browser signal); holder must find and configure software. Without it, no automated objection. Test: no.

right: Right to object to processing for research or statistical purposes
description: Object, on grounds relating to one's particular situation, to processing for scientific or historical research or statistics, unless necessary for a public-interest task.
quote: the data subject, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, shall have the right to object to processing of personal data concerning him or her
tl_reason: Objection to research processing of data; plain reasoned request works, nothing returned. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
description: Not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects.
exercise: Exceptions for contract necessity, authorisation by law, or explicit consent (Art. 22(2)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling
tl_reason: Object is software behaviour (solely automated decision), but it is a prohibition invoked by plain request; no mechanism to operate. Conflict: digital object vs no mechanism.

right: Right to human intervention, to express one's view and to contest an automated decision
description: Where automated decisions are allowed on contract or consent grounds, obtain human intervention by the controller, express one's point of view and contest the decision.
exercise: Applies in the cases of Art. 22(2)(a) and (c).
quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision
tl_reason: Contesting an automated decision concerns software behaviour, but human review is requested and delivered in plain terms. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed about a restriction of data subject rights
addressee: controller (per Union or Member State legislative measure)
description: Legislative measures restricting GDPR rights must, where relevant, provide for the data subject's right to be informed of the restriction unless prejudicial to its purpose.
exercise: Depends on the restricting Union or national law.
quote: the right of data subjects to be informed about the restriction, unless that may be prejudicial to the purpose of the restriction
notes: Must be provided for in the Union/Member State law that restricts rights.
tl_reason: Plain information about a legislative restriction of rights, per national law; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to the essence of the joint controller arrangement
description: Have the essence of the arrangement between joint controllers (who handles which obligations and rights) made available.
quote: The essence of the arrangement shall be made available to the data subject.
tl_reason: Essence of joint-controller arrangement made available, typically in a privacy notice; plain text. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise rights against each joint controller
description: Exercise GDPR rights in respect of and against any of the joint controllers, regardless of their internal arrangement.
exercise: Against any joint controller; arrangement may designate a contact point (Art. 26(1)).
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers
tl_reason: Choice of addressee among joint controllers; purely legal, no technical element.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach
description: Be informed without undue delay, in clear and plain language, of a personal data breach likely to result in a high risk, including likely consequences, measures taken and DPO contact.
exercise: Not required if data were encrypted, risk mitigated, or disproportionate effort (then public communication); supervisory authority may order notification (Art. 34(4)).
quote: the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay
tl_reason: Breach notice in clear and plain language; any channel works. Test: yes.

right: Protection of the data protection officer against dismissal or penalty
description: The DPO may not be dismissed or penalised for performing their tasks and receives no instructions on how to exercise them.
quote: He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the controller or the processor for performing his tasks.
tl_reason: Employment-type protection of the DPO; no technical element.

right: Right to contact the data protection officer
description: Contact the controller's or processor's DPO about any issue related to the processing of one's data and the exercise of GDPR rights.
exercise: Where a DPO has been designated; contact details published (Art. 37(7)) and given in Arts 13/14.
quote: Data subjects may contact the data protection officer with regard to all issues related to processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under this Regulation.
tl_reason: Contact with the DPO via published details, often email, but a letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to a code of conduct monitoring body
description: Lodge a complaint about infringements of an approved code of conduct with the accredited monitoring body, whose complaint procedures must be transparent to data subjects.
exercise: Only where an approved code with an accredited monitoring body applies; not for public authorities (Art. 41(6)).
quote: established procedures and structures to handle complaints about infringements of the code or the manner in which the code has been, or is being, implemented by a controller or processor
tl_reason: Complaint to a code-of-conduct monitoring body by ordinary means; no mechanism.

right: Right to enforce binding corporate rules as a data subject
addressee: group of undertakings bound by BCRs
description: BCRs must confer enforceable rights on data subjects, including complaint, court action and redress and compensation for breaches of the BCRs.
exercise: Against the EU-established member accepting liability (Art. 47(2)(f)); complaint to SA or courts under Art. 79.
quote: the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority and before the competent courts of the Member States in accordance with Article 79, and to obtain redress
tl_reason: Enforcing BCRs through complaint, courts and compensation; no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of a transfer based on compelling legitimate interests
description: Where a one-off transfer relies on the controller's compelling legitimate interests, the data subject must be informed of the transfer and of those interests.
exercise: In addition to Arts 13/14 information.
quote: inform the data subject of the transfer and on the compelling legitimate interests pursued
notes: Second subparagraph of Art. 49(1).
tl_reason: Plain information on a transfer and the interests pursued; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of risks before consenting to a third-country transfer
description: A transfer based on consent without adequacy or safeguards requires explicit consent after being informed of the possible risks.
exercise: Before consenting; not applicable to public authorities exercising public powers (Art. 49(3)).
quote: the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed transfer, after having been informed of the possible risks of such transfers
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer risks before consenting; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to information from the supervisory authority on exercising rights
description: Ask a supervisory authority for information about how to exercise data subject rights.
exercise: On request; free of charge (Art. 57(3)) unless manifestly unfounded or excessive (Art. 57(4)).
quote: upon request, provide information to any data subject concerning the exercise of their rights under this Regulation
tl_reason: Information from a supervisory authority on request by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to due process and judicial remedy against supervisory authority measures
rightholder: controller, processor or other person subject to the supervisory authority's powers
description: The exercise of investigative and corrective powers, including fines (Art. 83(8)), is subject to safeguards including effective judicial remedy and due process.
exercise: Under Union and Member State procedural law.
quote: shall be subject to appropriate safeguards, including effective judicial remedy and due process, set out in Union and Member State law in accordance with the Charter
notes: See also Art. 83(8) for fines.
tl_reason: Due process and judicial remedy against authority measures; no technical element.

right: Right of a complainant to receive the decision on a dismissed or rejected complaint from the local authority
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: In cross-border cases, a complainant is informed of the decision by the authority where they complained, and a dismissal or rejection is adopted and notified to them by that authority (enabling a local challenge).
exercise: Notification by the local supervisory authority; partial dismissals handled under Art. 60(9).
quote: the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall adopt the decision and notify it to the complainant
tl_reason: Procedural notification of a complaint decision by the authority; no technical element.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
description: Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of habitual residence, workplace or alleged infringement, if processing infringes the GDPR.
exercise: Free of charge (Art. 57(3)); authority must facilitate e.g. with an electronic complaint form (Art. 57(2)).
quote: every data subject shall have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
tl_reason: Authority must offer a complaint form that can also be completed electronically, without excluding other means. Letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the progress and outcome of a complaint
description: Be informed by the supervisory authority of the progress and outcome of the complaint, including the possibility of a judicial remedy.
quote: The supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant on the progress and the outcome of the complaint
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint progress from the authority; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a binding decision of a supervisory authority
rightholder: any natural or legal person concerned
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Challenge in court a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority that concerns the person.
exercise: Before the courts of the Member State where the authority is established (Art. 78(3)).
quote: each natural or legal person shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them
tl_reason: Judicial remedy before courts; no technical element.

right: Right to a judicial remedy against supervisory authority inaction
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Go to court where the competent supervisory authority does not handle a complaint or does not inform the data subject within three months of progress or outcome.
exercise: After three months without handling/information.
quote: where the supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Articles 55 and 56 does not handle a complaint or does not inform the data subject within three months
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against authority inaction; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor
description: Bring court proceedings against a controller or processor where rights under the GDPR have been infringed by non-compliant processing.
exercise: Courts where the controller/processor has an establishment, or where the data subject habitually resides (Art. 79(2)), unless the defendant is a public authority exercising public powers.
quote: each data subject shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy where he or she considers that his or her rights under this Regulation have been infringed
tl_reason: Court action against controller or processor; no technical element.

right: Right to mandate a not-for-profit body to act on one's behalf
description: Mandate a qualifying not-for-profit body to lodge complaints, bring judicial remedies and (where national law allows) claim compensation on one's behalf.
exercise: Body must be properly constituted, have public-interest objectives and be active in data protection.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association
tl_reason: Mandate covers only complaints, court actions and compensation; signed by ordinary means, no mechanism. Test: yes. Differs from Table A DELEGATE.

right: Right of qualified bodies to complain and sue without a mandate
description: Where a Member State so provides, a qualified body may lodge complaints and seek judicial remedies independently of any data subject's mandate.
exercise: Only in Member States that opt in.
quote: has the right to lodge, in that Member State, a complaint with the supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Article 77
notes: Member-State option.
tl_reason: Standing of qualified bodies to complain and sue; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation
rightholder: any person who has suffered damage
description: Receive compensation for material or non-material damage resulting from an infringement of the GDPR; joint controllers/processors are each liable for the entire damage (Art. 82(4)).
exercise: Court proceedings in courts competent under Art. 79(2) (Art. 82(6)); exemption only if not in any way responsible (Art. 82(3)).
quote: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right of recourse between controllers and processors
rightholder: controller or processor that paid full compensation
addressee: other controllers or processors involved in the same processing
description: A controller or processor that paid full compensation may claim back from co-responsible controllers or processors their share of the compensation.
exercise: In proportion to responsibility under the conditions of Art. 82(2).
quote: that controller or processor shall be entitled to claim back from the other controllers or processors involved in the same processing
tl_reason: Recourse between liable controllers and processors; contractual-type claim, no technical element.

right: Right to withdraw consent
description: Withdraw consent at any time; withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent.
exercise: Any time; informed of this before consenting.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Withdrawal as easy as consent, a click where consent was clicked, but a letter still withdraws validly. Conflict: mechanism vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right of the holder of parental responsibility to give or authorise a child's consent
rightholder: holder of parental responsibility over a child below 13
description: For information society services offered directly to a child under 13, consent-based processing is lawful only if given or authorised by the parent or guardian.
exercise: Controller must make reasonable efforts to verify (Art. 8(2)).
quote: such processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Parental consent to a child's ISS processing, verified with available means; a signed declaration works. Conflict: digital object vs plain act. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise data subject rights by providing additional identifying information
description: Where the controller cannot identify the data subject, it must inform them if possible, and the data subject can still exercise Arts 17-22 by supplying identifying information.
exercise: Provide additional information to the controller (see also Art. 14(2)).
quote: Articles 17 to 22 shall not apply except where the data subject, for the purpose of exercising his or her rights under those articles, provides additional information
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Identifying info may be a technical identifier for pseudonymous data, but plain details often suffice. Conflict: ability sometimes needed. Test: mostly yes.

right: Right to a response to a data subject request within one month
description: Receive information on action taken on requests under Arts 17-24 without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two months); free of charge.
exercise: 1 month (+2 months with reasons); free of charge (Art. 14(5)); oral information on request (Art. 14(1)).
quote: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 17 to 24 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain reply on action taken, electronic where requested electronically; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of reasons for not acting on a request and of remedies
description: If the controller does not act, the data subject must be told why and of the possibility to complain to the EDPS and seek a judicial remedy.
exercise: Within one month of receipt of the request.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons for not taking action
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain-language reasons for inaction and remedies; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data are collected from the data subject
description: Receive at collection the controller's identity, DPO contact, purposes, legal basis, recipients, transfers, retention, rights, right to complain to the EDPS and automated decision-making information.
exercise: At time of collection; before further processing for another purpose (Art. 15(3)).
quote: the controller shall, at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain notice information at collection; usable on paper. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
description: Receive information about processing of data obtained from other sources, including categories of data and their source.
exercise: Within a reasonable period (max. 1 month), or at first communication or disclosure; exceptions in Art. 16(5).
quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the following information
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain information on data obtained elsewhere; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of access
description: Obtain confirmation whether personal data are processed and access to them plus information on purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, source and automated decision-making.
exercise: Request to the controller; free of charge; 1 month (Art. 14).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Object is the personal dataset, but a letter request works and access can be plain. Conflict: digital object vs plain result.

right: Right to be informed of safeguards for third-country transfers
description: Be informed of the appropriate safeguards (Art. 48) relating to transfers to third countries or international organisations.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards pursuant to Article 48 relating to the transfer
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer safeguards. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a copy of personal data
description: Obtain a copy of the personal data undergoing processing, electronically where requested electronically.
exercise: Free of charge; must not adversely affect rights of others (Art. 17(4)).
quote: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Copy of processed data, electronic when requested electronically (data archive); holder must open and interpret it. Test: no.

right: Right to rectification
description: Obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data and completion of incomplete data without undue delay.
exercise: Request to the controller.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Correction of a stored dataset; plain request works, holder only checks result. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
description: Obtain erasure without undue delay where data are no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, an objection succeeds, processing is unlawful, a legal obligation requires it, or data were collected from a child for ISS.
exercise: Exceptions in Art. 19(3).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Erasure of a dataset is technical for the controller, but plain request works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to have other controllers informed of an erasure request for published data
description: Where the controller made the data public and must erase them, it must take reasonable steps to inform other controllers that erasure of links and copies is requested.
quote: shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers, or controllers other than Union institutions and bodies, which are processing the personal data
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Object is published links and copies; controller uses technical measures, holder only requests erasure. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to restriction of processing
description: Obtain restriction of processing while accuracy (including completeness) is contested, where processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, for legal claims, or pending an objection.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Restriction marks data in systems; plain request works, holder only checks. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed before a restriction is lifted
description: A data subject who obtained restriction must be informed before it is lifted.
quote: A data subject who has obtained restriction of processing pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain notice before lifting a restriction. Test: yes.

right: Right to have recipients notified of rectification, erasure or restriction and to be told who they are
description: Controller must pass on rectifications, erasures and restrictions to recipients and on request tell the data subject who they are.
exercise: On request.
quote: The controller shall inform the data subject about those recipients if the data subject requests it.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain list of recipients on request. Test: yes.

right: Right to data portability
description: Receive personal data provided to the controller in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit them to another controller.
exercise: Only for automated processing based on consent or contract; not for public-interest tasks (Art. 22(3)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to receive the personal data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Machine-readable data to be transmitted to another controller; holder must handle and move files. Test: no.

right: Right to direct controller-to-controller transmission
description: Have the data transmitted directly to another controller, including controllers other than Union institutions and bodies, where technically feasible.
exercise: Where technically feasible.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Direct technical transmission between controllers; holder operates across services. Test: no.

right: Right to object
description: Object at any time, on grounds relating to one's particular situation, to processing for a public-interest task (Art. 5(1)(a)), including profiling.
exercise: Must be brought explicitly to the data subject's attention at first communication (Art. 23(2)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Objection to processing incl. profiling; plain reasoned request works, nothing returned. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to object by automated means
description: In the context of information society services, exercise the right to object through automated means using technical specifications.
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her right to object by automated means using technical specifications
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Objection by automated means using technical specifications; holder must find and configure a signal. Test: no.

right: Right to object to processing for research or statistical purposes
description: Object to processing for scientific or historical research or statistics on grounds relating to one's particular situation, unless necessary for a public-interest task.
quote: the data subject, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, shall have the right to object to processing of personal data concerning him or her
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Objection to research processing; plain reasoned request works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
description: Not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with legal or similarly significant effects.
exercise: Exceptions in Art. 24(2).
quote: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Object is software behaviour (automated decision), but a prohibition invoked by plain request; nothing to operate. Conflict: digital object vs no mechanism.

right: Right to human intervention, to express one's view and to contest an automated decision
description: Where automated decisions are allowed on contract or consent grounds, obtain human intervention, express one's view and contest the decision.
quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Contesting an automated decision; human review requested and given in plain terms. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the reasons for a restriction of rights
description: Where rights are restricted by a legal act or internal rule, be informed of the principal reasons and of the right to complain to the EDPS.
exercise: May be deferred, omitted or denied if it would cancel the restriction's effect (Art. 25(8)); in access cases EDPS informs whether data were processed correctly (Art. 25(7)).
quote: the data subject shall be informed in accordance with Union law of the principal reasons on which the application of the restriction is based
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain information on reasons for a restriction of rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to the essence of the joint controller arrangement
description: Have the essence of the joint controllers' arrangement made available.
quote: The essence of the arrangement shall be made available to the data subject.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Essence of joint-controller arrangement made available in plain text. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise rights against each joint controller
description: Exercise rights against any of the joint controllers irrespective of their arrangement.
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Choice of addressee among joint controllers; no technical element.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach
description: Be informed without undue delay of a personal data breach likely to result in a high risk, in clear and plain language.
exercise: Exceptions in Art. 35(3); EDPS may require notification (Art. 35(4)).
quote: the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Breach notice in clear and plain language; any channel. Test: yes.

right: Protection of the data protection officer against dismissal or penalty
description: The DPO may not be dismissed or penalised for performing their tasks; dismissal only if conditions no longer met and with EDPS consent (Art. 44(8)).
quote: He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the controller or the processor for performing his or her tasks.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Employment-type protection of the DPO; no technical element.

right: Right to contact the data protection officer
description: Contact the DPO about any issue relating to processing of one's data and the exercise of rights.
quote: Data subjects may contact the data protection officer with regard to all issues related to processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under this Regulation.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Contacting the DPO, typically by email; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to consult the DPO directly and protection from prejudice for reporting breaches
description: Consult the DPO on any matter of interpretation or application without going through official channels, and suffer no prejudice for reporting an alleged breach.
exercise: Direct consultation, bypassing official channels.
quote: No one shall suffer prejudice on account of a matter brought to the attention of the competent data protection officer alleging that a breach of the provisions of this Regulation has taken place.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Direct consultation of the DPO and protection from prejudice; ordinary channels work. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a DPO investigation
description: Ask the DPO to investigate matters and occurrences relating to the DPO's tasks, and receive a report back.
exercise: Request to the DPO; DPO reports back to the person who commissioned the investigation.
quote: at the request of the controller or the processor, the staff committee concerned or any individual, investigate matters and occurrences directly relating to his or her tasks
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Request for a DPO investigation and plain report back; internal complaint, channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of risks before consenting to a third-country transfer
description: A transfer based on consent without adequacy or safeguards requires explicit consent after being informed of the risks.
exercise: Not applicable to activities in the exercise of public powers (Art. 50(2)).
quote: the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed transfer, after having been informed of the possible risks of such transfers
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer risks before consent. Test: yes.

right: Right to information from the EDPS on exercising rights
description: Ask the EDPS for information and advice on the exercise of data subject rights (see also Art. 58(3)(a)).
exercise: On request; free of charge (Art. 57(3)).
quote: upon request, provide information to any data subject concerning the exercise of their rights under this Regulation
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Information from the EDPS on request; no technical element.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor
description: Lodge a complaint with the EDPS if processing by an EU institution or body infringes the Regulation.
exercise: Free of charge; electronic complaint form (Art. 57(2)-(3)).
quote: every data subject shall have the right to lodge a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Complaint form that can also be completed electronically, other means not excluded. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the progress and outcome of a complaint
description: Be informed of the progress and outcome of the complaint and of the possibility of a judicial remedy; silence for three months counts as a negative decision (Art. 63(3)).
quote: The European Data Protection Supervisor shall inform the complainant of the progress and the outcome of the complaint
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint progress; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy before the Court of Justice
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Bring disputes under the Regulation, including damages claims and actions against EDPS decisions (including deemed negative decisions), before the Court of Justice.
exercise: Actions before the CJEU; deemed negative decision after 3 months of EDPS inaction (Art. 63(3)).
quote: Actions against decisions of the European Data Protection Supervisor, including decisions under Article 63(3), shall be brought before the Court of Justice.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Judicial remedy before the CJEU; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation
rightholder: any person who has suffered damage
description: Receive compensation from the EU institution or body for material or non-material damage caused by an infringement of the Regulation.
exercise: Subject to Treaty conditions (non-contractual liability, CJEU).
quote: shall have the right to receive compensation from the Union institution or body for the damage suffered
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right of complainants to be closely associated with fine proceedings
description: Complainants must be closely associated with EDPS proceedings that may lead to administrative fines.
quote: Complainants shall be associated closely with the proceedings.
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Procedural association with fine proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to mandate a not-for-profit body to act on one's behalf
description: Mandate a qualifying not-for-profit body to lodge a complaint with the EDPS, bring judicial actions and claim compensation on one's behalf.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Mandate covers complaints, court actions, compensation; ordinary legal act, no mechanism. Test: yes. Differs from Table A DELEGATE.

right: Right of EU staff to complain to the EDPS without official channels
rightholder: person employed by a Union institution or body
description: EU staff may lodge a complaint with the EDPS about an alleged infringement without going through official channels and may not suffer prejudice for doing so.
exercise: Direct complaint to the EDPS.
quote: Any person employed by a Union institution or body may lodge a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor regarding an alleged infringement
notes: Applies to processing by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Staff complaint to the EDPS by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to human intervention in automated decisions on operational data
description: Solely automated decisions with adverse legal or significant effects are prohibited unless authorised by Union law providing safeguards, at least human intervention.
quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Human intervention in an automated decision on operational data; plain request and plain review. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed of follow-up to a request within three months
description: Be informed in writing about the follow-up to a request without undue delay and at the latest within three months; free of charge (Art. 78(4)).
quote: The controller shall inform the data subject in writing about the follow-up to his or her request without undue delay and in any case at the latest within three months
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Written plain information on follow-up to a request. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on processing of operational personal data
description: Have available the controller's identity, DPO contact, purposes, right to complain to the EDPS and existence of rights; in specific cases also legal basis, retention, recipients.
exercise: Further information may be delayed, restricted or omitted on law-enforcement grounds (Art. 79(3)).
quote: The controller shall make available to the data subject at least the following information
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain information made available on processing. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to operational personal data
description: Obtain confirmation of processing and access to operational personal data with information on purposes, legal basis, recipients, retention, rights and origin.
exercise: Subject to limitations under Art. 81.
