quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not operational personal data concerning him or her are processed
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Object is operational dataset, but plain request works and access can be plain. Conflict: digital object vs plain result.

right: Right to be informed of refusal or restriction of access
description: Be informed in writing of any refusal or restriction of access and its reasons, and of the possibility to complain to the EDPS or go to the Court of Justice.
exercise: Reasons may be omitted where they would undermine the restriction's purpose.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject, without undue delay, in writing of any refusal or restriction of access and of the reasons for the refusal or the restriction
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Written plain information on refusal and remedies. Test: yes.

right: Right to rectification of operational personal data
description: Obtain rectification of inaccurate and completion of incomplete operational personal data without undue delay.
quote: Any data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate operational personal data relating to him or her.
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Correction of stored operational data; plain request works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to erasure of operational personal data
description: Obtain erasure where processing infringes Arts 71, 72(1) or 76 or erasure is legally required.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of operational personal data concerning him or her without undue delay
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Erasure of operational data, technical for controller; plain request works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to restriction instead of erasure and to be informed before lifting
description: Processing is restricted instead of erased where accuracy is contested and cannot be ascertained or data are needed as evidence; data subject informed before a restriction is lifted.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject before lifting the restriction of processing
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Restriction marking in place of erasure plus notice before lifting; nothing to operate. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed of refusal of rectification, erasure or restriction
description: Be informed in writing of any refusal and its reasons, and of the possibility to complain to the EDPS or seek a remedy before the Court of Justice.
exercise: Information may be restricted on law-enforcement grounds.
quote: The controller shall inform the data subject in writing of any refusal of rectification or erasure of operational personal data or restrict processing and of the reasons for the refusal.
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Written plain information on refusal. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise rights indirectly through the EDPS
description: Where information, access or rectification is restricted, exercise rights through the EDPS, which verifies the processing and informs the data subject that verification took place and of the right to a judicial remedy.
exercise: Controller must inform the data subject of this possibility (Art. 84(2)).
quote: the rights of the data subject may also be exercised through the European Data Protection Supervisor
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Indirect exercise through the EDPS, which only confirms verification; ordinary procedure, no mechanism.

right: Right to exercise rights against each joint controller (operational data)
description: Exercise rights against any joint controller of operational personal data; essence of the arrangement made available (Art. 86(2)).
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Choice of addressee among joint controllers; no technical element.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach (operational data)
description: Be informed without undue delay of a breach of operational personal data likely to result in a high risk.
exercise: Exceptions in Art. 93(3); may be delayed/omitted on Art. 79(3) grounds (Art. 93(5)).
quote: the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay
notes: Chapter IX: operational personal data processed by EU bodies in police and judicial cooperation (e.g. Eurojust).
table_entry: Regulation on personal data processed by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
tl_reason: Plain breach notice. Test: yes.

act: Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation
right: Freedom to store and process non-personal data anywhere in the EU
rightholder: users and service providers processing non-personal data
description: Unjustified national data localisation requirements are prohibited, so persons can choose where in the EU their non-personal data are stored and processed and can rely on this against national rules.
exercise: Invoke before national authorities or courts (directly applicable Regulation).
quote: Data localisation requirements shall be prohibited, unless they are justified on grounds of public security in compliance with the principle of proportionality.
notes: Only public-security justifications allowed; no individual procedure.
table_entry: Regulation on the free flow of non-personal data
tl_reason: Prohibition of data localisation invoked against Member States; market freedom, no mechanism. Test: yes.

act: Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation
right: Right to general information from national single points of contact
addressee: Member State single point of contact
description: Obtain general information on the Regulation, including codes of conduct on porting data and switching providers, from the national single point of contact.
quote: The single points of contact shall provide users with general information on this Regulation, including on the codes of conduct.
table_entry: Regulation on the free flow of non-personal data
tl_reason: General information from national single point of contact; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to re-use public sector documents
addressee: Member States / public sector bodies and public undertakings
description: Re-use documents held by public sector bodies (and, where re-use is allowed, public undertakings and memory institutions, Art. 3(2)) for commercial or non-commercial purposes, in open, machine-readable formats where possible (Art. 5).
exercise: Subject to national access regimes and exclusions (Art. 1(2)-(3)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that documents to which this Directive applies in accordance with Article 1 shall be re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Re-use of public documents in any medium; machine-readable formats only where possible. Request by letter works, result only sometimes a dataset. Result criterion conflicts.

right: Right to have re-use requests processed within set time limits
description: Have a re-use request processed and documents delivered (or a licence offer finalised) within the national access-to-documents deadline or, failing that, within 20 working days.
exercise: Extension by 20 working days for complex requests, notified within three weeks with reasons; electronic processing where possible (Art. 4(1)); not applicable to public undertakings and research bodies (Art. 4(6)).
quote: finalise the licence offer to the applicant as soon as possible, and in any event within 20 working days of receipt
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Deadline for processing re-use requests; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to be given the grounds for refusal of a re-use request
description: Receive the grounds for a negative decision, including (for third-party IP) a reference to the rightholder or licensor where known.
quote: In the event of a negative decision, the public sector bodies shall communicate the grounds for refusal to the applicant
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Grounds for refusal communicated in plain language. Test: yes.

right: Right of redress against re-use decisions
addressee: Member State (impartial review body or court)
description: Challenge decisions on re-use before an impartial review body whose decisions bind the public body; every decision must state the means of redress, and applicants must be informed of redress for decisions or practices affecting them (Art. 7(3)).
quote: The means of redress shall include the possibility of review by an impartial review body with the appropriate expertise
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Redress before an impartial review body. Test: yes.

right: Right to re-use documents free of charge or at marginal cost
description: Re-use is free of charge or limited to marginal costs; high-value datasets and publicly funded research data are free of charge for the user (Art. 6(6)).
exercise: Exceptions for revenue-generating bodies, libraries/museums/archives and public undertakings (Art. 6(2)).
quote: The re-use of documents shall be free of charge.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Free-of-charge or marginal-cost re-use; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to an explanation of how re-use charges were calculated
addressee: holder of the documents (public sector body or public undertaking)
description: On request, learn how non-standard charges were calculated for a specific re-use request.
exercise: On request.
quote: Upon request, the holder of the documents in question shall also indicate the way in which such charges have been calculated in relation to a specific re-use request.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Explanation of charge calculation in plain language. Test: yes.

right: Right to re-use publicly funded research data
addressee: researchers, research performing and research funding organisations
description: Re-use publicly funded research data already made public in a repository, for commercial or non-commercial purposes, free of charge (Art. 6(6)(b)).
quote: research data shall be re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes in accordance with Chapters III and IV, insofar as they are publicly funded
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Legal permission to re-use research data already in repositories; object is a dataset needing technical handling, but no mechanism is owed. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to non-discriminatory re-use conditions
description: Re-use conditions must be non-discriminatory for comparable categories of re-use, including cross-border, and objective, proportionate and justified (Art. 8(1)); the same terms apply when public bodies re-use for commercial activities (Art. 11(2)).
quote: Any applicable conditions for the re-use of documents shall be non-discriminatory for comparable categories of re-use, including for cross-border re-use.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: Non-discriminatory re-use conditions; equal-treatment rule. Test: yes.

right: Right of all market actors to re-use (no exclusive arrangements)
description: Re-use is open to all potential market actors; contracts may not grant exclusive rights except where necessary for a public-interest service, subject to review and publication.
quote: The re-use of documents shall be open to all potential actors in the market, even if one or more market actors already exploit added-value products based on those documents.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (deadline 17 July 2021).
tl_reason: No exclusive re-use arrangements; market access for all actors. Test: yes.

right: Right to a comprehensible and transparent decision prohibiting the use of results
description: Where a public body prohibits the use of re-use results that jeopardise third-party rights (secure processing environment), the re-user must receive a comprehensible and transparent decision.
quote: The decision to prohibit the use of the results shall be comprehensible and transparent to the re-user.
tl_reason: Comprehensible decision prohibiting use of results; plain decision. Test: yes.

right: Right of affected legal persons to be informed of unauthorised re-use of non-personal data
rightholder: legal persons whose rights and interests may be affected
addressee: re-user (with assistance of the public sector body)
description: Be informed without delay by the re-user when non-personal data concerning them has been re-used without authorisation.
quote: the re-user shall, without delay, where appropriate with the assistance of the public sector body, inform the legal persons whose rights and interests may be affected
tl_reason: Notification of unauthorised re-use to affected legal persons; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of potential re-users to assistance in seeking consent or permission
addressee: public sector body (assisted by competent body)
description: Where re-use cannot be allowed with anonymisation or secure environments, obtain the public body's best-efforts help in seeking data subjects' consent or data holders' permission.
exercise: Only where feasible without disproportionate burden on the public body.
quote: the public sector body shall make best efforts, in accordance with Union and national law, to provide assistance to potential re-users in seeking consent of the data subjects
notes: Best-efforts duty.
tl_reason: Best-efforts assistance in seeking consent or permission; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of affected legal persons to be informed of and to permit third-country transfer
rightholder: legal person whose rights and interests may be affected by re-use
description: For re-use based on consent/permission (Art. 5(6)), be informed of a re-user's intention to transfer non-personal data to a third country, its purpose and safeguards, and decide whether to permit the transfer.
exercise: Re-use is not allowed unless the legal person gives permission.
quote: The public sector body shall not allow the re-use unless the legal person gives permission for the transfer.
tl_reason: Permission for third-country transfer given by plain consent. Test: yes.

right: Right to transparent, non-discriminatory fees payable online cross-border
description: Fees for re-use must be transparent, non-discriminatory, proportionate and cost-based (Art. 6(2), (5)) and payable online via widely available cross-border payment services without discrimination.
quote: Public sector bodies shall ensure that any fees can also be paid online through widely available cross-border payment services
tl_reason: Fees must also be payable online; online payment is an option, not a condition. Test: yes.

right: Right to a decision on a request to re-use protected public-sector data
rightholder: applicant for re-use (any natural or legal person)
description: Request re-use of public-sector data protected by commercial or statistical confidentiality, third-party IP or data protection, and obtain a decision within two months.
exercise: Request via the national single information point (Art. 8(2)); decision within 2 months, extendable by up to 30 days for complex requests with notice and reasons; re-use conditions must be non-discriminatory, transparent and proportionate (Art. 5(2)).
quote: shall adopt a decision on the request for the re-use of the categories of data referred to in Article 3(1) within two months of the date of receipt of the request
notes: The DGA does not oblige public bodies to allow re-use (Art. 1(2)); the right is to a timely decision under published conditions.
tl_reason: Decision on a re-use request within two months; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of redress against decisions on re-use requests
rightholder: any natural or legal person directly affected by a re-use decision
addressee: Member State (impartial review body or court)
description: Challenge a decision on a re-use request before an impartial body (e.g. competition authority, access-to-documents authority, DPA or court) whose decisions bind the public body.
exercise: In the Member State where the deciding body is located; procedure laid down in national law.
quote: Any natural or legal person directly affected by a decision as referred to in paragraph 1 shall have an effective right of redress in the Member State where the relevant body is located.
tl_reason: Redress before an impartial body or court. Test: yes.

right: Right to address the EU legal representative of a non-EU data intermediation services provider
addressee: legal representative of a non-EU data intermediation services provider
description: Address all issues concerning a non-EU data intermediation service to its designated EU legal representative instead of or in addition to the provider.
quote: to be addressed in addition to or instead of it by competent authorities for data intermediation services or data subjects and data holders
notes: Contact point usable by persons.
tl_reason: Contacting the EU legal representative by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to provide data intermediation services in all Member States upon notification
description: After submitting a notification, start activity (Art. 11(4)) and provide data intermediation services throughout the EU.
exercise: Notification to the competent authority for data intermediation services with the information in Art. 11(6); possible proportionate fee (Art. 11(11)).
quote: The notification referred to in paragraph 1 shall entitle the data intermediation services provider to provide data intermediation services in all Member States.
tl_reason: Notification-based market access for intermediation providers. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a standardised declaration confirming notification
addressee: competent authority for data intermediation services
description: Obtain, on request, a standardised declaration confirming that a complete notification has been submitted.
exercise: Issued within one week of a duly and fully completed notification.
quote: the competent authority for data intermediation services shall, within one week of a duly and fully completed notification, issue a standardised declaration
tl_reason: Declaration confirming notification; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to request confirmation of compliance and use of the 'recognised in the Union' label
addressee: competent authority for data intermediation services
description: Request confirmation of compliance with Arts 11-12 and then use the label 'data intermediation services provider recognised in the Union' and the common logo.
quote: At the request of the data intermediation services provider, the competent authority for data intermediation services shall confirm that the data intermediation services provider complies
tl_reason: Compliance confirmation and label; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to obtain the data collected about their activity on the service
description: Obtain on request the data (e.g. date, time, geolocation, duration, connections) the intermediary collected about their activity in using the service.
exercise: On request.
quote: which may entail the use of data for the detection of fraud or cybersecurity, and shall be made available to the data holders upon request
tl_reason: Activity data the intermediary logged (time, geolocation, connections) delivered as data to interpret. Test: no.

right: Right to opt out of data format conversions
description: Opt out of the intermediary converting their data into other formats, unless the conversion is mandated by Union law.
quote: shall offer an opt-out possibility regarding those conversions to data subjects or data holders, unless the conversion is mandated by Union law
tl_reason: Provider must offer an opt-out from data format conversions; object is software processing. Test: no.

right: Right to decide on use of additional tools (storage, curation, anonymisation etc.)
description: Additional tools such as temporary storage, curation, conversion, anonymisation or pseudonymisation may be used only at their explicit request or approval.
quote: such tools being used only at the explicit request or approval of the data holder or data subject
tl_reason: Object is technical processing tools, but explicit request or approval can be given by plain message; no mechanism prescribed. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to fair, transparent and non-discriminatory access to data intermediation services
rightholder: data subjects, data holders and data users
description: Access the intermediation service under a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory procedure, including prices and terms; commercial terms may not be tied to use of other services (Art. 12(b)).
quote: shall ensure that the procedure for access to its service is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory for both data subjects and data holders, as well as for data users
tl_reason: Fair, non-discriminatory access procedure and prices; equal-treatment rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to access, transfer or retrieve data in the event of the intermediary's insolvency
rightholder: data holders, data users and data subjects
description: If the intermediary becomes insolvent, obtain access to, transfer or retrieve stored data, and data subjects can continue to exercise their rights.
quote: shall have mechanisms in place to allow data holders and data users to obtain access to, to transfer or to retrieve their data
tl_reason: Provider must have mechanisms to access, transfer or retrieve stored data on insolvency; data must be moved elsewhere. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of unauthorised transfer, access or use of shared non-personal data (intermediaries)
description: Be informed without delay of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of non-personal data the intermediary has shared.
quote: the data intermediation services provider shall without delay inform data holders in the event of an unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data that it has shared
tl_reason: Notification by the intermediary of unauthorised transfer or use; plain information within a digital service. Test: yes.

right: Right of data subjects to information and advice before consenting
addressee: data intermediation services provider offering services to data subjects
description: Receive concise, transparent information and, where appropriate, advice on intended data uses and standard terms before consenting; the intermediary must act in the data subject's best interest.
quote: informing and, where appropriate, advising data subjects in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible manner about intended data uses by data users
tl_reason: Plain-language information and advice before consenting, delivered by the intermediation service. Test: yes.

right: Right to tools to give and withdraw consent or permission (intermediaries)
addressee: data intermediation services provider providing consent/permission tools
description: Use tools to both give and withdraw consent (personal data) or permission (non-personal data), and be told the third-country jurisdiction of intended use.
quote: provide data subjects with tools to both give and withdraw consent and data holders with tools to both give and withdraw permissions to process data
tl_reason: Intermediary must provide tools to give and withdraw consent or permission; exercised in its interface. Test: no.

right: Right to be heard before enforcement measures (data intermediation services providers)
addressee: competent authority for data intermediation services
description: Be notified of findings of non-compliance and state views before measures are taken; receive notice of measures with reasons and a compliance period of up to 30 days (Art. 14(6)).
exercise: Within 30 days of receipt of the notification.
quote: it shall notify that data intermediation services provider of those findings and give it the opportunity to state its views, within 30 days of the receipt of the notification
tl_reason: Right to be heard before enforcement; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for registration as a recognised data altruism organisation
rightholder: entity meeting the Art. 18 requirements (not-for-profit legal person)
addressee: competent authority for the registration of data altruism organisations
description: Apply for entry in the public national register; once registered (within 12 weeks, valid EU-wide) use the label 'data altruism organisation recognised in the Union' (Art. 17(2)).
exercise: Application in the Member State of establishment or main establishment (Art. 19(1)-(2)); registration within 12 weeks (Art. 19(5)).
quote: An entity which meets the requirements of Article 18 may submit an application for registration in the public national register of recognised data altruism organisations
tl_reason: Registration application for data altruism organisations. Test: yes.

right: Right to address the EU legal representative of a non-EU data altruism organisation
addressee: legal representative of a non-EU recognised data altruism organisation
description: Address all issues relating to a non-EU recognised data altruism organisation to its designated EU legal representative.
quote: to be addressed in addition to or instead of it by competent authorities for the registration of data altruism organisations or data subjects and data holders
notes: Contact point usable by persons.
tl_reason: Contacting the EU legal representative by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to information before processing (data altruism)
description: Be informed, before any processing, of the general-interest objectives and specific purposes, and of the location and objectives of any third-country processing (and third-country jurisdiction of third-party use, Art. 21(6)).
quote: A recognised data altruism organisation shall inform data subjects or data holders prior to any processing of their data in a clear and easily comprehensible manner of
tl_reason: Plain information before processing, delivered by the data altruism organisation. Test: yes.

right: Right to tools to give and easily withdraw consent or permission (data altruism)
description: Give consent or permission through tools provided by the organisation and withdraw it easily.
quote: The recognised data altruism organisation shall also provide tools for easy withdrawal of such consent or permission.
tl_reason: Organisation must provide tools to give and easily withdraw consent or permission; exercised in its interface. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of unauthorised transfer, access or use of shared non-personal data (data altruism)
description: Be informed without delay of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of non-personal data the organisation has shared.
quote: The recognised data altruism organisation shall, without delay, inform data holders in the event of any unauthorised transfer, access or use of the non-personal data that it has shared.
tl_reason: Notification by the data altruism organisation of unauthorised use; plain information within a digital service. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before enforcement measures (recognised data altruism organisations)
addressee: competent authority for the registration of data altruism organisations
description: Be notified of findings of non-compliance and state views before the authority requires cessation or removes the organisation from the register.
exercise: Within 30 days of receipt of the notification.
quote: give it the opportunity to state its views within 30 days of the receipt of the notification
tl_reason: Right to be heard before enforcement; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a competent authority
addressee: competent authority for data intermediation services / for registration of data altruism organisations
description: Complain about any matter within the DGA's scope against a data intermediation services provider or a recognised data altruism organisation.
exercise: Individually or collectively; the authority must inform the complainant of progress, the decision and available judicial remedies (Art. 27(2)). Persons may also request compliance monitoring (Arts 14(1), 24(1)).
quote: Natural and legal persons shall have the right to lodge a complaint in relation to any matter falling within the scope of this Regulation, individually or, where relevant, collectively
tl_reason: Complaint to a competent authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against binding decisions of competent authorities
rightholder: any affected natural and legal persons
addressee: courts of the Member State of the competent authority
description: Challenge legally binding decisions of the competent authorities on data intermediation services (Art. 14) or data altruism organisations (Arts 19, 24) in court.
exercise: Before the courts of the authority's Member State, individually or collectively through representatives (Art. 28(2)).
quote: any affected natural and legal persons shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy with regard to legally binding decisions referred to in Article 14
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against authority decisions. Test: yes.

right: Right to a remedy where a competent authority fails to act on a complaint
rightholder: any affected natural and legal persons
addressee: Member State (courts or impartial review body)
description: Obtain a judicial remedy or review by an impartial expert body if the competent authority fails to act on a complaint.
exercise: In accordance with national law.
quote: fails to act on a complaint, any affected natural and legal persons shall, in accordance with national law, either have the right to an effective judicial remedy or access to review
tl_reason: Remedy for authority inaction. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to be informed of third-country authority access requests
addressee: public sector body, re-user, data intermediation services provider or recognised data altruism organisation
description: Be informed of a third-country administrative authority's request to access its non-personal data before the request is complied with.
exercise: Except where the request serves law enforcement purposes, for as long as necessary.
quote: shall inform the data holder about the existence of a request of a third-country administrative authority to access its data before complying with that request
tl_reason: Notification of a third-country access request; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Exclusive right of the database author (copyright)
description: Authorise or prohibit reproduction, translation/adaptation, distribution and communication to the public of a database whose selection or arrangement is the author's own intellectual creation.
exercise: Enforced through national remedies (Art. 12); first sale of a copy in the EU by or with consent of the rightholder exhausts the resale right.
quote: the author of a database shall have the exclusive right to carry out or to authorize:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Author may be a legal person where national law so permits (Art. 4(1)).
tl_reason: Exclusive copyright in a database, enforced through national remedies; no technical mechanism or holder ability required. Test: yes.

right: Lawful user's right to perform acts needed for access to and normal use of a database
description: Perform any restricted act (e.g. reproduction) necessary to access and normally use the contents of a copyright-protected database without the author's authorisation.
exercise: No authorisation needed; limited to the part the user is authorised to use; contractual provisions to the contrary are null and void (Art. 15).
quote: which is necessary for the purposes of access to the contents of the databases and normal use of the contents by the lawful user shall not require the authorization of the author of the database
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof user right.
tl_reason: Copyright exception immunising acts needed for normal use of any database, electronic or not; no mechanism the author must provide. Test: yes.

right: Sui generis right of the database maker
description: Prevent extraction and/or re-utilisation of all or a substantial part of a database's contents where the maker made a substantial investment in obtaining, verifying or presenting them; also covers repeated systematic extraction of insubstantial parts (Art. 7(5)).
exercise: 15-year term, renewable by substantial new investment (Art. 10); transferable and licensable (Art. 7(3)); beneficiaries: EU nationals/residents and EU companies (Art. 11); remedies under Art. 12.
quote: Member States shall provide for a right for the maker of a database which shows that there has been qualitatively and/or quantitatively a substantial investment
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Sui generis exclusive right of the database maker against extraction; legal entitlement enforced in court, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Lawful user's right to extract and re-utilise insubstantial parts of a database
rightholder: lawful user of a database made available to the public
description: Extract and/or re-utilise insubstantial parts of a publicly available database's contents for any purpose, without the maker being able to prevent it.
exercise: Limited to the part the user is authorised to use; must not conflict with normal exploitation (Art. 8(2)-(3)); contractual provisions to the contrary are null and void (Art. 15).
quote: may not prevent a lawful user of the database from extracting and/or re-utilizing insubstantial parts of its contents, evaluated qualitatively and/or quantitatively, for any purposes whatsoever
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof user right.
tl_reason: Mandatory exception for insubstantial extraction from any public database; a legal immunity, no mechanism or technical ability required. Test: yes.

right: Right to remedies for infringement of database rights
rightholder: author or maker of a database (rightholder)
description: Obtain appropriate remedies under national law against infringements of the database copyright or sui generis right.
exercise: National court proceedings; see also IPR Enforcement Directive 2004/48/EC.
quote: Member States shall provide appropriate remedies in respect of infringements of the rights provided for in this Directive.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Judicial remedies for database infringement before national courts; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to the EU design
rightholder: designer or successor in title (employer for designs made by employees, Art. 14(3))
description: The entitlement to the EU design (and to register it) belongs to the designer or successor in title; jointly developed designs vest jointly.
exercise: File an application at the EUIPO (Art. 35) or disclose the design for unregistered protection; enforce entitlement under Art. 15.
quote: shall vest in the designer or his successor in title.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Entitlement to a design, realised by filing at EUIPO or disclosure; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to claim recognition as legitimate holder of an EU design
rightholder: person entitled under Art. 14 (incl. joint holder, Art. 15(2))
addressee: competent court or authority of the Member State; EUIPO
description: Where a non-entitled person disclosed, applied for or registered the design, claim recognition as its legitimate (joint) holder and have the change of ownership registered.
exercise: Claim before national court/authority, barred 3 years after publication/disclosure unless bad faith (Art. 15(3)); then request change of ownership at the EUIPO with the final decision (Art. 15(4)).
quote: claim before the competent court or authority of the Member State concerned recognition as the legitimate holder of the EU design
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Entitlement claim before a court or authority; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of prior holder or licensee to a non-exclusive licence after change of ownership
rightholder: former holder or licensee who exploited or prepared to exploit the design in good faith
addressee: new holder of the registered EU design
description: After ownership changes following an entitlement claim, continue exploiting the design by obtaining a non-exclusive licence from the new holder on reasonable terms.
exercise: Request within 3 months of the entry of the new holder in the Register; licence for reasonable period on reasonable terms; excluded for bad faith (Art. 16(3)).
quote: may continue such exploitation provided that they request, within a period of three months of the date of the entry in the Register of the new holder, a non-exclusive licence from the new holder
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request for a non-exclusive licence from the new holder; contractual, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the designer to be cited
description: Be named as the designer before the EUIPO and in the Register, including having a change of the designer's name entered.
exercise: Citation in the application or later entry; the designer may waive it (Art. 36(3)(e)).
quote: The designer shall have the right, in the same way as the applicant for or the holder of a registered EU design, to be cited as such before the Office and in the Register.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Designer named in application and Register; administrative entry, no mechanism or ability required. Test: yes.

right: Exclusive right conferred by a registered EU design
rightholder: holder of a registered EU design
description: Use the design exclusively and prevent unauthorised third parties from using it, incl. making, marketing, importing/exporting, stocking and creating or sharing files (e.g. 3D-printing files) enabling the product (Art. 19(2)).
exercise: Infringement action before EU design courts (Art. 81); subject to limitations (Art. 20), repair clause (Art. 20a) and exhaustion (Art. 21); 5-year terms renewable up to 25 years (Art. 12).
quote: A registered EU design shall confer on its holder the exclusive right to use it and to prevent any third party not having the consent of the holder from using it.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Exclusive design right (covers 3D-printing files as a topic) enforced by infringement action; no mechanism for the holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to stop infringing goods in transit from third countries
rightholder: holder of a registered EU design
addressee: third parties bringing goods into the Union; customs authorities
description: Prevent third parties from bringing into the Union, in the course of trade, goods not released for free circulation that bear an identical or essentially indistinguishable design.
exercise: Via customs proceedings under Reg (EU) 608/2013; lapses if the declarant/holder of the goods proves the right holder cannot prohibit marketing in the country of final destination.
quote: The holder of a registered EU design shall be entitled to prevent all third parties from bringing products, in the course of trade, from third countries into the Union
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822. Introduced by Reg 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Stopping infringing goods in transit via customs proceedings; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the unregistered EU design holder to prevent copying
rightholder: holder of an unregistered EU design
description: Prevent the acts covered by Art. 19(1)-(2) but only where the contested use results from copying the protected design.
exercise: Protection for 3 years from first disclosure in the Union (Art. 11); independent creation is not copying; also applies to registered designs under deferred publication (Art. 19(5)).
quote: The holder of an unregistered EU design shall be entitled to prevent acts referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 only if the contested use results from copying the protected design.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Anti-copying right of unregistered design holder enforced in court; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Repair clause: freedom to use component-part designs to repair complex products
rightholder: any person (makers, sellers and users of spare parts, repairers)
description: Use a design of a component part of a complex product (e.g. a car body panel) solely to repair that product and restore its original appearance without infringing the EU design.
exercise: Can be invoked by manufacturers/sellers only if they duly inform consumers of the part's commercial origin and manufacturer (Art. 20a(2)); no duty to guarantee end use (Art. 20a(3)).
quote: Protection shall not be conferred on an EU design which constitutes a component part of a complex product upon whose appearance the design of the component part is dependent
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822. Introduced by Reg 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Repair clause is an IP limitation for physical spare parts; no digital mechanism or software lock involved. Test: yes.

right: Consumer right to information on the origin of spare parts used for repair
addressee: manufacturer or seller of the component part
description: Be informed, by a clear and visible indication on the product or in another appropriate form, of the commercial origin and manufacturer of a repair part, so as to choose between competing parts.
exercise: Framed as a condition for relying on the repair clause; no separate sanction stated.
quote: who failed to duly inform consumers, through a clear and visible indication on the product or in another appropriate form, about the commercial origin, and the identity of the manufacturer
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Origin information on the product or in another appropriate form; no technical mechanism or ability required. Test: yes.

right: Right of prior use
rightholder: third person who in good faith commenced use or made serious preparations before the filing/priority date
addressee: holder of the registered EU design
description: Continue to exploit an independently created design that falls within a later registered EU design for the purposes for which use had begun or been prepared.
exercise: Must establish good-faith use/preparations within the Union before filing/priority date and no copying; cannot license it; transferable only with the relevant part of the business (Art. 22(3)-(4)).
quote: A right of prior use shall exist for any third person who can establish that before the date of filing of the application
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Prior-use defence against a later design; legal entitlement, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of any person to seek invalidity of an EU design on absolute grounds
rightholder: any natural or legal person; groups representing manufacturers, producers, service suppliers, traders or consumers
description: Apply for a declaration of invalidity where the design is not a 'design' or lacks novelty, individual character or otherwise fails Arts 4-9.
exercise: Application to the EUIPO for registered designs (Art. 52: written reasoned statement + fee) or action/counterclaim before an EU design court (Arts 24, 81, 84); possible after lapse/surrender if legitimate interest (Art. 24(2)).
quote: The grounds for invalidity provided for in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b), may be invoked by the following:
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Invalidity application to EUIPO or design court by written statement and fee; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the entitled person to seek invalidity of a design held by a non-entitled person
rightholder: person entitled to the EU design under Art. 14
description: Have an EU design declared invalid where a court/authority has decided the registered holder is not entitled to it.
exercise: Application to EUIPO (Art. 52) or action/counterclaim before an EU design court (Art. 84(2)).
quote: The ground for invalidity provided for in paragraph 1, point (c), of this Article, may be invoked solely by the person who is entitled to the EU design under Article 14.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Invalidity application by the entitled person; administrative/judicial procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of holders of earlier rights to seek invalidity of a conflicting EU design
rightholder: applicant for or holder of an earlier design, distinctive sign or copyright; persons entitled to exercise it; authorised licensee
description: Have an EU design declared invalid where it conflicts with an earlier protected design, uses an earlier distinctive sign, or makes unauthorised use of a copyright work.
exercise: Application to EUIPO or counterclaim; barred if holder expressly consented (Art. 25(7)); all earlier rights must be invoked in the first application (Art. 25(8)).
quote: The grounds for invalidity provided for in paragraph 1, points (d), (e) and (f), may be invoked solely by the following:
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Invalidity application based on earlier rights; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Claim to repayment of sums paid under contracts after invalidity
rightholder: party who paid under a contract concerning the invalidated design (e.g. licensee)
addressee: holder of the invalidated EU design / contracting party
description: Where an EU design is declared invalid, claim repayment, on grounds of equity and to the extent justified, of sums paid under a contract performed before the invalidity decision.
exercise: Subject to national rules on compensation for negligence/bad faith or unjust enrichment.
quote: repayment, to an extent justified by the circumstances, of sums paid under the relevant contract may be claimed on grounds of equity.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Equitable repayment claim under a contract after invalidity; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to have transfers, licences and rights in rem entered in the Register
rightholder: party to a transfer, licence or right in rem
description: Have a transfer of a registered EU design entered in the Register and published; the same applies to rights in rem, levies of execution and licences.
exercise: Application with documents establishing the transfer (Art. 28(3)); successor cannot invoke the rights before entry (Art. 28(6)); see Arts 29(2), 30(3), 32a; cancellation/modification on application (Art. 33a).
quote: At the request of one of the parties, a transfer of a registered EU design shall be entered in the Register and published.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Registration of transfers and licences on request with documents; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Licensee's right to bring infringement proceedings
description: Sue for infringement with the holder's consent (unless the contract provides otherwise); an exclusive licensee may sue alone if the holder does not act after formal notice.
exercise: Formal notice to the holder, then infringement action before an EU design court.
quote: However, the holder of an exclusive licence may bring such proceedings if the holder of the EU design, after a formal notice, does not bring infringement proceedings within an appropriate period.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Licensee's standing to sue for infringement; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Licensee's right to intervene to obtain compensation
description: Intervene in infringement proceedings brought by the holder in order to obtain compensation for the licensee's own damage.
exercise: Intervention in the pending infringement action.
quote: A licensee shall, for the purpose of obtaining compensation for damage suffered, be entitled to intervene in infringement proceedings brought by the holder of the EU design.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Intervention in infringement proceedings for compensation; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of priority
rightholder: person who duly filed a design or utility model application in a Paris Convention/WTO State, or successors in title
description: Claim the earlier filing date for an EU design application on the same design filed within 6 months.
exercise: Declaration of priority with the application or within 2 months; file number and documents within 3 months (Art. 42).
quote: a right of priority for a period of six months from the date of filing of the first application.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Priority claim by declaration in the application; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Exhibition priority
rightholder: applicant who disclosed the products at an officially recognised international exhibition
description: Claim priority from the date of first disclosure at a recognised international exhibition if the application is filed within 6 months.
exercise: Declaration of priority with the application or within 2 months; evidence of disclosure within 3 months (Art. 44(2)).
quote: the applicant may, if the application is filed within a period of six months from the date of the first disclosure of such products, claim a right of priority from that date.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Exhibition priority claimed by declaration and evidence; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Applicant's right to be heard before refusal for non-registrability
rightholder: applicant for a registered EU design
description: On notification of a ground for non-registrability, submit observations, withdraw the application or objected views, or submit an amended representation before any refusal.
exercise: Within the period set in the notification; refusal is appealable (Art. 55).
quote: the Office shall specify a period within which the applicant may submit observations, withdraw the application or the objected views or submit an amended representation of the design
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Right to be heard before refusal; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request deferment of publication
rightholder: applicant for a registered EU design
description: Keep the registered design unpublished for up to 30 months from filing/priority.
exercise: Request when filing plus deferment fee (Art. 36(4)); holder may ask for earlier publication (Art. 50(4)) or prevent publication by surrender at least 3 months before expiry (Art. 50(5)).
quote: The applicant for a registered EU design may request, when filing the application, that the publication of the registered EU design be deferred for a period of up to 30 months
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request for deferred publication with fee; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of a person sued during deferment to receive register and file information
rightholder: person against whom an action based on a deferred registered EU design is brought
addressee: holder of the registered EU design (claimant)
description: Before being sued on a design whose publication is deferred, receive the information in the Register and the application file.
exercise: Condition for instituting legal proceedings during the deferment period.
quote: shall be subject to the condition that the information contained in the Register and in the file relating to the application has been communicated to the person against whom the action is brought.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Register and file information communicated before suit; procedural condition, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to a registration certificate and copies
rightholder: holder of the registered EU design
description: Receive a certificate of registration after publication and obtain certified or uncertified copies on request.
exercise: Issued electronically.
quote: the Office shall issue to the holder a certificate of registration. The Office shall provide certified or uncertified copies of the certificate, upon request.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Law requires certificates and copies issued by electronic means, but the request and the certificate are non-technical; holder is a design holder, not governed party.

right: Right to renew the registration
rightholder: holder of the registered EU design or person expressly authorised
description: Renew the registration for further 5-year periods (up to 25 years) on request and payment of the fee.
exercise: Within 6 months before expiry, or 6 months after with a surcharge (Art. 50d(3)); fees refunded if not renewed (Art. 50d(8)).
quote: Registration of the EU design shall be renewed at the request of the right holder of the registered EU design or of any person expressly authorised by the right holder to request the renewal
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Renewal on request and fee payment; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of upcoming expiry of the registration
rightholder: holder and any person with a registered right in the EU design
description: Be informed of the expiry of the registration at least 6 months beforehand.
exercise: Automatic notice by EUIPO; failure to notify does not engage EUIPO liability or affect expiry.
quote: any person having a registered right in respect of the EU design of the expiry of the registration at least six months before the date of such expiry.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: EUIPO notice of upcoming expiry; plain information, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Consent and information rights of registered right holders and licensees on surrender
rightholder: proprietor of a right entered in the Register; registered licensee; entitlement claimant (Art. 51(4))
addressee: EUIPO; holder of the registered EU design
description: Surrender of a registered EU design is entered only with the consent of proprietors of registered rights; registered licensees must be informed and surrender takes effect only after 3 months or their consent; an entitlement claimant's agreement is needed while Art. 15 proceedings are pending.
exercise: Holder must prove consent/notice to the EUIPO.
quote: A surrender shall be registered only with the agreement of the proprietor of a right entered in the Register.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Consent of registered right holders to surrender; administrative/legal consent, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Holder's right to require proof of genuine use of an earlier trade mark
rightholder: holder of the registered EU design
addressee: applicant for a declaration of invalidity; EUIPO
description: In invalidity proceedings based on an earlier trade mark, require the applicant to prove genuine use of that mark.
exercise: Request in the invalidity proceedings; Art. 64(2)-(3) EUTMR applies.
quote: If the holder of the registered EU design so requests, an applicant for a declaration of invalidity invoking an earlier EU or national trade mark as a distinctive sign
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request for proof of use in invalidity proceedings; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Alleged infringer's right to join invalidity proceedings
rightholder: third party sued for infringement, or who sought a declaration of non-infringement after a cease request
description: Be joined as a party to pending EUIPO invalidity proceedings concerning the same design.

notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Joining EUIPO invalidity proceedings by reasoned request and fee; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of appeal against EUIPO decisions
rightholder: party to proceedings adversely affected by a decision of examiners, Register department or Invalidity Division
description: Appeal decisions of the EUIPO's first-instance bodies to the Boards of Appeal.
exercise: Notice of appeal in writing within 2 months of notification (Art. 62(3)); Arts 66-72 EUTMR apply, incl. further action before the General Court.
quote: An appeal shall lie from the decisions of the Office referred to in Article 102, points (a), (b) and (c).
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Written appeal to the Boards of Appeal; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a reasoned decision and to comment before an EUIPO decision
rightholder: parties to proceedings before the EUIPO
description: Receive decisions stating reasons, based only on reasons or evidence on which the party had an opportunity to comment.
quote: They shall be based only on reasons or evidence on which the parties concerned have had an opportunity to present their comments.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Reasoned decisions and right to comment; procedural guarantee, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request oral proceedings
rightholder: party to proceedings before the EUIPO
description: Request oral proceedings before the EUIPO.
exercise: Held where the EUIPO considers them expedient; public before Invalidity Divisions and Boards of Appeal (Art. 64(3)).
quote: If the Office considers that oral proceedings would be expedient, they shall be held either at the instance of the Office or at the request of any party to the proceedings.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request for oral proceedings; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to attend and question witnesses and experts
rightholder: parties to proceedings before the EUIPO
description: Be informed of hearings of witnesses or experts and attend them and put questions.

table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Attendance and questioning at hearings of witnesses; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a decision on a finding of loss of rights
rightholder: persons concerned by an EUIPO finding that rights were lost
description: Contest an EUIPO communication finding a loss of rights by applying for a formal (appealable) decision.
exercise: Application within 2 months of notification of the communication.
quote: The persons concerned may apply for a decision on the matter within two months of notification of the communication, if they consider that the finding of the Office is incorrect.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

right: Right to request correction of errors
rightholder: party to proceedings; holder of the EU design
description: Request correction of linguistic or transcription errors and manifest oversights in EUIPO decisions, registrations or publications.
exercise: Corrections are published (Art. 66g(3)).
quote: errors in registering an EU design or errors in publishing the registration, of its own motion or at the request of a party.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
