right: Right to request cancellation of erroneous entries or revocation of erroneous decisions
rightholder: party to proceedings before the EUIPO
description: Request cancellation of a Register entry or revocation of a decision containing an obvious error attributable to the EUIPO.
exercise: Within one year of the entry/decision; appeal fee reimbursed if a pending appeal becomes devoid of purpose (Art. 66h(3)).
quote: shall be determined, of its own motion or at the request of one of the parties to the proceedings, by the department which made the entry or took the decision.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request to cancel erroneous entries or revoke erroneous decisions; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Restitutio in integrum (re-establishment of rights)
rightholder: applicant for or holder of a registered EU design, or any other party
description: Have rights re-established after missing a time limit despite all due care, where the omission caused a loss of rights or means of redress.
exercise: Written application within 2 months of removal of the cause and within 1 year of the missed time limit, completing the omitted act; fee refunded if granted (Art. 67(2)-(3)).
quote: was unable to observe a time limit vis-à-vis the Office shall, upon application, have his rights re-established
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Written application for re-establishment of rights; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Third-party proceedings against re-establishment of rights
rightholder: third party who in good faith marketed products while the rights were lost
description: A third party who in good faith marketed products during the loss-of-rights period cannot be sued for that (Art. 67(6)) and may challenge the decision re-establishing the rights.
exercise: Within 2 months of publication of the mention of re-establishment.
quote: may bring third party proceedings against the decision re-establishing the rights of the applicant for or holder of the registered
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Third-party proceedings against re-establishment; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Continuation of proceedings after a missed time limit
rightholder: applicant for or holder of a registered EU design, or any other party
description: Obtain continuation of proceedings despite a missed time limit by carrying out the omitted act.
exercise: Request within 2 months of expiry of the missed time limit plus fee; excluded for certain time limits (Art. 67a(2)); fee refunded if rejected.
quote: who has not observed a time limit vis-à-vis the Office may, upon request, obtain the continuation of proceedings, provided that at the time the request is made the omitted act has been carried out.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Request for continuation of proceedings with fee; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to recover fees and costs from the losing party
rightholder: successful party in invalidity or appeal proceedings
description: Recover the invalidity/appeal fees paid and essential costs (travel, subsistence, representation within maximum rates) from the losing party.
exercise: Costs fixed by the Invalidity Division/Board or on request within 2 months (Art. 70(6)); review on request within 1 month (Art. 70(7)); enforceable under national civil procedure (Art. 71).
quote: The losing party in proceedings for a declaration of invalidity of a registered EU design or appeal proceedings shall bear the fees paid by the other party
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Recovery of fees and costs from losing party; compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the holder to be notified of changes in the Register
rightholder: holder of a registered EU design
description: Be notified of any change made in the Register concerning the design.
quote: The holder of a registered EU design shall be notified of any change in the Register.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Notification of register changes to the holder; plain information, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain extracts from the Register
description: Obtain certified or uncertified extracts from the Register of EU designs.
exercise: Electronic request; restricted for designs under deferred publication (Art. 74(5)).
quote: The Office shall, where access to the Register is not restricted pursuant to Article 74(5), provide, by electronic means, certified or uncertified extracts from the Register upon request.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Law requires register extracts be provided by electronic means, but the request and the extract are non-technical documents. Conflict: mandated electronic channel versus test yes.

right: Consent required before personal data in the EUIPO database are made public
rightholder: party whose personal data are held in the EUIPO design database
description: Personal data held in the database beyond the Register entries are not made public unless the party expressly consents.
quote: Access to the personal data referred to in paragraph 2 shall be restricted and such data shall not be made publicly available unless the party concerned has expressly consented.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Object is publication of personal data in EUIPO's electronic database (digital), but protection is default and consent is a plain statement; no mechanism required.

right: Right to removal of personal data from the EUIPO database
rightholder: party whose personal data are held in the database
description: Request deletion of personal data from the database after the design expires or inter partes proceedings close.
exercise: Request after 18 months from expiry of the design or closure of the procedure.
quote: the party concerned may request the removal of any personal data from the database after 18 months from the expiry of the registered EU design or the closure of the relevant inter partes procedure.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Object is personal data in an electronic database (digital), but removal is requested plainly and no mechanism is required. Conflict: digital object versus test yes.

right: Right to correction of inaccurate data in the EUIPO database
description: Obtain correction of inaccurate or erroneous data held in the database at any time.
quote: The party concerned shall have the right to obtain the correction of inaccurate or erroneous data at any time.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Correction of data in EUIPO's electronic database: object digital, but a plain request works and the result needs only checking. Conflict: digital object versus test yes.

right: Right to removal of personal data from published EUIPO decisions
rightholder: party to the proceedings that led to the decision
description: Request removal of personal data included in EUIPO decisions published online.
quote: Any party to the proceedings that led to the adoption of the decision may request the removal of any personal data included in the decision.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Removal of personal data from decisions published online: object digital, but request is plain and no mechanism required. Conflict: digital object versus test yes.

right: Right to inspect unpublished files on showing a legitimate interest
rightholder: any person with a legitimate interest (in particular one against whom the holder has invoked the design)
description: Inspect files of unpublished, deferred or surrendered designs without the applicant's/holder's consent.
exercise: Request with evidence of legitimate interest (Art. 74a(2)); confidential parts excluded (Art. 74(4)).
quote: Any person who can establish a legitimate interest may inspect a file without the consent of the applicant for or holder of the registered
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Inspection of unpublished files on showing legitimate interest; electronic copies only optional, plain request and documents. Test: yes.

right: Right to inspect the file after publication
description: Inspect the file of a published registered EU design and obtain electronic or certified copies.
exercise: Online inspection; electronic copies and certified copies on request (Art. 74a(1),(3)); internal documents and confidential parts excluded (Art. 74(4)).
quote: the file may be inspected on request.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Law requires file inspection to take place online (Art. 74a), but the request and the documents are non-technical. Conflict: mandated electronic channel versus plain result.

right: Right to keep parts of the file confidential
description: Have parts of the file excluded from public inspection if a special interest in confidentiality was shown before the inspection request.
exercise: Show special interest before any inspection request; overridable by overriding legitimate interests of the requester.
quote: parts of the file which the party concerned showed a special interest in keeping confidential before the request for inspection of the files was made
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Confidentiality of file parts on showing special interest; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to act before the EUIPO without a representative
rightholder: natural or legal persons domiciled or established in the EEA
description: Act in person before the EUIPO without compulsory representation; EEA persons may be represented by an employee.
exercise: Non-EEA persons must use a professional representative except for filing an application (Art. 77(2)).
quote: Subject to paragraph 2, no person shall be compelled to be represented before the Office.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

right: Right to be entered on the list of professional representatives in design matters

description: Be entered on the EUIPO's special list of professional representatives in design matters and thereby represent others before the EUIPO.
exercise: Request with certificate from the Benelux/national IP office (Art. 78(5)); removal at own request (Art. 78(7)).
quote: Any natural person who fulfils all the following conditions may be entered on that list:
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.

entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

quote: for actions for declaration of non-infringement of

entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

description: Where a counterclaim for invalidity is raised in an action to which the holder is not a party, be informed and join the action.
exercise: Under the procedural law of the court's Member State.
quote: he shall be informed thereof and may be joined as a party to the action in accordance with the conditions set out in the law of the Member State where the court is situated.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

right: Right to an injunction against infringement
rightholder: holder of the EU design (and licensees under Art. 32(3))
description: Obtain a court order prohibiting the defendant from continuing infringing acts, plus measures to ensure compliance and other remedies under applicable national law.
exercise: Infringement action before an EU design court with exclusive jurisdiction (Art. 81(a)); jurisdiction per Art. 82; other orders under Art. 89(2).
quote: issue an order prohibiting the defendant from proceeding with the acts which infringed or would infringe the EU design.
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

rightholder: holder of the EU design or other interested party
description: Apply to national courts for provisional, including protective, measures in respect of an EU design, even if another court has jurisdiction on the merits.
exercise: Measures available under national law for national designs; courts with Art. 82(1)-(4) jurisdiction can grant EU-wide measures (Art. 90(3)).
quote: Application may be made to the courts of a Member State, including
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822

addressee: EU design courts of second instance
description: Appeal first-instance EU design court judgments in infringement and validity actions; further appeal under national rules.

entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Appeal to second-instance design courts; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: International registration holder's right to respond to a provisional refusal
rightholder: holder of an international registration designating the Union
description: After notification of refusal, renounce or limit the international registration for the Union or submit observations within a time limit; refusal confirmed only if observations do not satisfy the Office.
exercise: Within the time limit set by EUIPO; confirmed refusals are appealable (Art. 106e(5)).
quote: The Office shall specify a time limit by which the holder of the international registration may renounce the international registration in respect of the Union
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.
table_entry: Community Design Regulation (listed in the table as a Directive)
entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Response to provisional refusal of an international registration; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of earlier right holders in new Member States to oppose use of an extended EU design
rightholder: applicant for or holder of an earlier right acquired in good faith in a new Member State before accession
addressee: user/holder of the EU design; national courts
description: Oppose use of an EU design (extended to the new Member State on accession) within the territory where the earlier right is protected.
exercise: Applies to earlier designs, distinctive signs and copyright (Art. 25(1)(d)-(f)); also to unregistered EU designs (Art. 110a(5)).
quote: The applicant or the holder of an earlier right in a new Member State may oppose the use of a
notes: Consolidated text as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/2822.

entry_current_status: In force as the EU Design Regulation, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2822
tl_reason: Opposing use of an extended EU design on the basis of earlier rights; IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Standing to seek IP enforcement measures and remedies
rightholder: IP rightholders; licensees and other authorised users; collective rights-management bodies; professional defence bodies
description: Apply for the enforcement measures, procedures and remedies of the Directive (evidence, information, injunctions, damages etc.).
exercise: Licensees and representative bodies only as permitted by applicable law.
quote: Member States shall recognise as persons entitled to seek application of the measures, procedures and remedies referred to in this chapter:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Standing to seek IP enforcement remedies in court; judicial, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Presumption of authorship enabling infringement proceedings
rightholder: author of a literary or artistic work; holders of related rights
description: Be presumed the author (and entitled to sue) where one's name appears on the work in the usual manner, absent proof to the contrary.
quote: to be entitled to institute infringement proceedings, it shall be sufficient for his/her name to appear on the work in the usual manner
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Presumption of authorship from name on the work; evidentiary rule, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request an order for production of evidence
rightholder: party to IP proceedings that has presented reasonably available evidence
description: Ask the court to order the opposing party to present specified evidence under its control.
exercise: Subject to protection of confidential information; a reasonable sample may constitute reasonable evidence.
quote: on application by a party which has presented reasonably available evidence sufficient to support its claims
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court order for production of evidence; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request production of banking, financial or commercial documents
rightholder: party to IP proceedings concerning commercial-scale infringement
description: In commercial-scale cases, ask the court to order communication of the opposing party's banking, financial or commercial documents.
exercise: Same conditions as Art. 6(1); confidentiality protected.
quote: on application by a party, the communication of banking, financial or commercial documents under the control of the opposing party
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court order for banking or commercial documents; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to provisional measures to preserve evidence
rightholder: applicant claiming that its IP right is or is about to be infringed
description: Obtain, even before proceedings on the merits and if needed without hearing the other party, measures such as detailed description, sampling or seizure of infringing goods, materials and documents.
exercise: Application with reasonably available evidence; may require security (Art. 7(2)).
quote: order prompt and effective provisional measures to preserve relevant evidence in respect of the alleged infringement, subject to the protection of confidential information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Provisional evidence-preservation measures from a court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to notice and review of ex parte evidence-preservation measures
rightholder: parties affected by evidence-preservation measures taken without hearing them
description: Be notified without delay after execution and obtain a review, including a hearing, on whether the measures are modified, revoked or confirmed.
exercise: Request for review within a reasonable period after notification.
quote: A review, including a right to be heard, shall take place upon request of the parties affected
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Notice and review of ex parte measures; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to revocation of evidence measures if no action on the merits
description: Have evidence-preservation measures revoked if the applicant does not start merits proceedings in time.
exercise: Period set by the court or, failing that, 20 working days / 31 calendar days, whichever is longer.
quote: are revoked or otherwise cease to have effect, upon request of the defendant
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Revocation of evidence measures on defendant's request; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to compensation for unjustified evidence measures
description: Obtain appropriate compensation for injury caused by evidence measures that are revoked, lapse through the applicant's fault, or prove unjustified.
exercise: Request to the court; may be secured by applicant's security (Art. 7(2)).
quote: to order the applicant, upon request of the defendant, to provide the defendant appropriate compensation for any injury caused by those measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Compensation for unjustified evidence measures; compensation via court, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of information on origin and distribution networks
addressee: infringer and third parties (commercial-scale possessors, users, service providers); court
description: Obtain a court order requiring the infringer or certain third parties to disclose names/addresses of producers and distributors and quantities and prices of infringing goods or services.
exercise: Justified and proportionate request in proceedings; subject to privilege, confidentiality and data-protection rules (Art. 8(3)).
quote: in response to a justified and proportionate request of the claimant, the competent judicial authorities may order that information on the origin and distribution networks of the goods or services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court-ordered disclosure of origin and distribution networks; judicial information right, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to interlocutory injunctions and seizure of suspected goods
description: Obtain interlocutory injunctions against imminent or continuing infringement (also against intermediaries) and seizure or delivery up of suspected goods.
exercise: Application with evidence of title and infringement (Art. 9(3)); possibly ex parte (Art. 9(4)); may require security (Art. 9(6)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that the judicial authorities may, at the request of the applicant:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Interlocutory injunctions and seizure via court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to precautionary seizure of the infringer's assets
description: Obtain precautionary seizure of the alleged infringer's movable and immovable property, including blocking bank accounts, where recovery of damages is endangered.
exercise: Must show circumstances likely to endanger recovery of damages.
quote: the judicial authorities may order the precautionary seizure of the movable and immovable property of the alleged infringer, including the blocking of his/her bank accounts and other assets
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Precautionary seizure of assets via court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to review of ex parte provisional measures
description: Be informed without delay after execution and obtain a review, including a hearing, of provisional measures taken without hearing the defendant.
exercise: Request within a reasonable time after notification.
quote: A review, including a right to be heard, shall take place upon request of the defendant
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Review of ex parte provisional measures; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to revocation of provisional measures if no action on the merits
description: Have provisional measures revoked if the applicant does not start merits proceedings in time.
exercise: Period set by court or 20 working days / 31 calendar days, whichever is longer.
quote: are revoked or otherwise cease to have effect, upon request of the defendant, if the applicant does not institute, within a reasonable period, proceedings leading to a decision on the merits
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Revocation of provisional measures absent merits action; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Defendant's right to compensation for unjustified provisional measures
description: Obtain compensation for injury caused by provisional measures that are revoked, lapse, or prove unjustified.
exercise: Request to the court.
quote: the judicial authorities shall have the authority to order the applicant, upon request of the defendant, to provide the defendant appropriate compensation for any injury caused by those measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Compensation for unjustified provisional measures; compensation via court, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to corrective measures (recall, removal, destruction)
description: Obtain recall, definitive removal from commerce or destruction of infringing goods and principal production materials, at the infringer's expense.
exercise: After a finding of infringement; proportionality and third-party interests considered (Art. 10(3)).
quote: the competent judicial authorities may order, at the request of the applicant, that appropriate measures be taken with regard to goods that they have found to be infringing
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Recall, removal or destruction of infringing goods ordered by court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a permanent injunction against the infringer
description: After a finding of infringement, obtain an injunction prohibiting its continuation, backed by penalty payments where national law provides.
quote: the judicial authorities may issue against the infringer an injunction aimed at prohibiting the continuation of the infringement
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Permanent injunction after infringement finding; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for an injunction against intermediaries
addressee: court; intermediaries whose services are used to infringe
description: Apply for an injunction against intermediaries (e.g. platforms, ISPs) whose services are used by third parties to infringe.
exercise: Copyright/related rights cases covered by Art. 8(3) InfoSoc Directive.
quote: rightholders are in a position to apply for an injunction against intermediaries whose services are used by a third party to infringe an intellectual property right
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court injunction against intermediaries such as platforms; digital topic only, holder needs no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Innocent infringer's right to request pecuniary compensation instead of measures
rightholder: person liable to corrective measures or injunctions who acted unintentionally and without negligence
description: Ask the court to order pecuniary compensation to the injured party instead of corrective measures/injunctions where those would cause disproportionate harm.
exercise: Conditions: no intent or negligence, disproportionate harm, compensation reasonably satisfactory.
quote: at the request of the person liable to be subject to the measures provided for in this section, the competent judicial authorities may order pecuniary compensation to be paid to the injured party
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
tl_reason: Request for pecuniary compensation instead of measures; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to damages for IP infringement
description: Obtain damages appropriate to the actual prejudice from a knowing infringer, including lost profits, unfair profits and moral prejudice, or a lump sum based at least on hypothetical royalties.
exercise: Application to the court; for non-knowing infringers Member States may allow recovery of profits or pre-established damages (Art. 13(2)).
quote: on application of the injured party, order the infringer who knowingly, or with reasonable grounds to know, engaged in an infringing activity, to pay the rightholder damages
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Damages for IP infringement ordered by court; compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the successful party to recover legal costs
description: Have reasonable and proportionate legal costs and expenses borne by the unsuccessful party as a general rule.
exercise: Unless equity does not allow this.
quote: reasonable and proportionate legal costs and other expenses incurred by the successful party shall, as a general rule, be borne by the unsuccessful party
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Recovery of legal costs from unsuccessful party; compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to publication of the judicial decision
description: Obtain an order for dissemination of the decision (display, full or partial publication) at the infringer's expense.
quote: the judicial authorities may order, at the request of the applicant and at the expense of the infringer, appropriate measures for the dissemination of the information concerning the decision
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court-ordered publication of decision; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Trade secret holder's right to apply for measures and remedies
rightholder: trade secret holder (natural or legal person lawfully controlling a trade secret)
description: Apply for the Directive's civil measures, procedures and remedies to prevent or obtain redress for unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure of the trade secret.
exercise: Limitation period up to 6 years (Art. 8).
quote: Member States shall ensure that trade secret holders are entitled to apply for the measures, procedures and remedies provided for in this Directive in order to prevent, or obtain redress for
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Trade secret holder's standing to seek civil remedies; judicial, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Respondent's right to dismissal for freedom of expression, whistleblowing or worker representation
rightholder: respondent (journalists, whistleblowers, workers and their representatives, any person acting for a protected purpose)
description: Have a trade-secret claim dismissed where the acquisition, use or disclosure was for freedom of expression/information, revealing misconduct in the public interest, disclosure to worker representatives, or another legitimate interest recognised by law.
exercise: Raised as a defence in the proceedings.
quote: Member States shall ensure that an application for the measures, procedures and remedies provided for in this Directive is dismissed where the alleged acquisition, use or disclosure
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Defence for expression, whistleblowing or worker representation raised in proceedings; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Respondent's right to measures against abusive trade-secret litigation
description: Request measures, such as damages, sanctions or publication of the decision, where a manifestly unfounded application was brought abusively or in bad faith.
exercise: May be dealt with in separate proceedings.
quote: competent judicial authorities may, upon the request of the respondent, apply appropriate measures as provided for in national law, where an application concerning the unlawful acquisition
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Measures against abusive litigation via court; procedural/compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to have information identified as confidential in proceedings
description: Have a (alleged) trade secret identified as confidential so that parties, lawyers, witnesses and others may not use or disclose it, also after proceedings end.
exercise: Duly reasoned application.
quote: in response to a duly reasoned application by an interested party, identified as confidential
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Court identification of information as confidential; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to specific confidentiality measures in proceedings
description: Obtain measures such as restricting access to documents and hearings to a limited circle and publishing only redacted decisions, while each party keeps access for at least one natural person and its lawyers.
exercise: Duly reasoned application; proportionality assessment (Art. 9(3)).
quote: the competent judicial authorities may, on a duly reasoned application by a party, take specific measures necessary to preserve the confidentiality of any trade secret or alleged trade secret
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Confidentiality measures in proceedings; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to provisional and precautionary measures
description: Obtain provisional cessation/prohibition of use or disclosure, prohibition of dealing in infringing goods, or seizure of suspected infringing goods.
exercise: Evidence requirements and proportionality (Art. 11(1)-(2)); alternative: guarantees for continued use (Art. 10(2)).
quote: the competent judicial authorities may, at the request of the trade secret holder, order any of the following provisional and precautionary measures against the alleged infringer:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Provisional and precautionary measures via court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Respondent's right to revocation of provisional measures
description: Have provisional measures revoked if no merits proceedings are started in time or the information ceases to be a trade secret for reasons not attributable to the respondent.
exercise: Period set by court or 20 working days / 31 calendar days.
quote: are revoked or otherwise cease to have effect, upon the request of the respondent, if:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Revocation of provisional measures on respondent's request; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for unjustified provisional measures
description: Obtain compensation for injury caused by provisional measures that are revoked, lapse, or turn out to be unjustified.
exercise: May be dealt with in separate proceedings.
quote: upon the request of the respondent or of an injured third party, to provide the respondent, or the injured third party, appropriate compensation for any injury caused by those measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Compensation for unjustified provisional measures; compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to injunctions and corrective measures after a merits decision
description: Obtain cessation/prohibition of use or disclosure, prohibition of dealing in infringing goods, corrective measures (recall, destruction) and destruction or delivery up of documents and files embodying the secret.
exercise: At the infringer's expense (Art. 12(4)); Member States may allow delivery of goods to the holder or charities (Art. 12(3)); proportionality factors (Art. 13(1)).
quote: the competent judicial authorities may, at the request of the applicant, order one or more of the following measures against the infringer:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Injunctions and corrective measures after merits decision (incl. destroying files); judicial remedy, no mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Respondent's right to revocation of injunctions when the information is no longer secret
description: Have injunctions under Art. 12(1)(a)-(b) revoked when the information no longer qualifies as a trade secret for reasons not attributable to the respondent.
quote: upon the request of the respondent, if the information in question no longer meets the requirements of point (1) of Article 2
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Revocation of injunctions once information no longer secret; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Good-faith user's right to request pecuniary compensation instead of injunctions
rightholder: person liable to Art. 12 measures who did not know the secret was unlawfully obtained
description: Ask the court to order pecuniary compensation to the injured party instead of injunctions/corrective measures where these would cause disproportionate harm.
exercise: Compensation capped at the royalties that would have been due for the period of prohibition.
quote: at the request of the person liable to be subject to the measures provided for in Article 12, the competent judicial authority may order pecuniary compensation to be paid to the injured party
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Request for pecuniary compensation instead of injunctions; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to damages for trade secret misappropriation
description: Obtain damages appropriate to the actual prejudice from an infringer who knew or ought to have known, including lost profits, unfair profits, moral prejudice or a royalty-based lump sum.
exercise: Member States may limit employees' liability towards employers absent intent.
quote: the competent judicial authorities, upon the request of the injured party, order an infringer who knew or ought to have known
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Damages for trade secret misappropriation; compensation, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to publication of the judicial decision
description: Obtain dissemination of the decision at the infringer's expense, with trade secrets preserved.
exercise: Proportionality and privacy of natural persons considered (Art. 15(3)).
quote: the competent judicial authorities may order, at the request of the applicant and at the expense of the infringer, appropriate measures for the dissemination of the information concerning the decision
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on the protection of trade secrets
tl_reason: Court-ordered publication of decision; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request confidential treatment of information provided to ENISA
rightholder: any third party providing information to ENISA
description: A person submitting information to ENISA can make a reasoned request that it be treated confidentially, and ENISA must then not divulge it to third parties.
exercise: Reasoned request for confidential treatment to ENISA; subject to Art. 28 (access to documents).
quote: ENISA shall not divulge to third parties information that it processes or receives in relation to which a reasoned request for confidential treatment has been made
tl_reason: Reasoned request for confidential treatment; administrative, no technical element.

right: Right of access to ENISA documents
rightholder: any natural or legal person (per Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001)
description: Public access to documents held by ENISA under the conditions of Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
exercise: Application to ENISA under Regulation 1049/2001 and ENISA's implementing arrangements (Art. 28(2)).
quote: Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 shall apply to documents held by ENISA.
notes: Right granted by reference to Regulation 1049/2001
tl_reason: Access to documents under Reg. 1049/2001; ordinary application.

right: Right to complain to the European Ombudsman or bring an action before the CJEU against ENISA access-to-documents decisions
addressee: European Ombudsman / Court of Justice of the European Union
description: ENISA decisions on (confirmatory) access-to-documents applications can be challenged by a complaint to the European Ombudsman or an annulment action before the CJEU.
exercise: Complaint under Art. 228 TFEU or action under Art. 263 TFEU against decisions taken under Art. 8 of Regulation 1049/2001.
quote: Decisions taken by ENISA pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 may be the subject of a complaint to the European Ombudsman under Article 228 TFEU
tl_reason: Ombudsman complaint or CJEU action; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by ENISA or its staff
description: ENISA must make good any damage caused by it or its staff in the performance of their duties (non-contractual liability).
exercise: Claim against ENISA; the CJEU has jurisdiction over compensation disputes (Art. 39(4)); general principles common to Member State laws apply.
quote: In the case of non-contractual liability, ENISA shall make good any damage caused by it or its staff in the performance of their duties
tl_reason: Non-contractual compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right to issue an EU statement of conformity (conformity self-assessment) recognised in all Member States
rightholder: manufacturer or provider of ICT products, ICT services, ICT processes or managed security services
addressee: Member States / national cybersecurity certification authorities
description: Where a scheme allows self-assessment (assurance level 'basic' only), the manufacturer or provider may itself issue an EU statement of conformity, which must be recognised in all Member States (Art. 53(5)).
exercise: Only under schemes permitting self-assessment; voluntary unless Union or national law requires it (Art. 53(4)); copy to the national certification authority and ENISA (Art. 53(3)).
quote: may issue an EU statement of conformity stating that the fulfilment of the requirements set out in the scheme has been demonstrated
tl_reason: Market-access right to self-declare conformity; no mechanism for a governed user.

right: Right of end users to supplementary cybersecurity information on certified ICT products, services and processes
addressee: manufacturer or provider of certified (or self-declared) ICT products, services or processes
description: End users can obtain guidance on secure configuration and operation, the period of security support (including security updates), and references to repositories of disclosed vulnerabilities and advisories.
exercise: Information must be publicly available in electronic form and kept updated at least until the certificate or EU statement of conformity expires (Art. 55(2)).
quote: the period during which security support will be offered to end users, in particular as regards the availability of cybersecurity related updates
notes: Public (non-individualised) information; only for certified products or those with an EU statement of conformity
tl_reason: Law requires public electronic-form information; using it (secure configuration, updates) needs technical ability, but it is generic published guidance. Conflict: plain info vs technical use.

right: Right to report vulnerabilities to the manufacturer or provider through a published contact point
addressee: manufacturer or provider of certified (or self-declared) ICT products, services or processes
description: Manufacturers and providers must publish contact information and accepted methods for receiving vulnerability information, which end users and security researchers can use to report vulnerabilities.
exercise: Via the published contact details/methods; available electronically until expiry of the certificate or statement (Art. 55(2)).
quote: contact information of the manufacturer or provider and accepted methods for receiving vulnerability information from end users and security researchers
notes: Only for certified products or those with an EU statement of conformity
tl_reason: Report via published contact methods; the vulnerability is a digital topic, but the report is a message. Test: yes.

right: Right to renewal of a European cybersecurity certificate
rightholder: holder of a European cybersecurity certificate
addressee: issuing conformity assessment body or national cybersecurity certification authority
description: A European cybersecurity certificate may be renewed at the end of its validity period provided the relevant requirements continue to be met.
exercise: Application to the issuing body under the conditions of the relevant scheme (Art. 54(1)(k)); refusal can be challenged under Arts 63-64.
quote: A European cybersecurity certificate shall be issued for the period provided for in the European cybersecurity certification scheme and may be renewed
tl_reason: Certificate renewal by application; no technical element.

right: Right to Union-wide recognition of a European cybersecurity certificate
rightholder: holder of a European cybersecurity certificate
description: A certificate issued under a European scheme must be recognised in all Member States, so the holder can rely on it throughout the Union.
exercise: Invocable before any Member State authority; certified products are presumed to comply with the scheme (Art. 56(1)).
quote: A European cybersecurity certificate issued pursuant to this Article shall be recognised in all Member States.
tl_reason: Union-wide recognition of a certificate; market-access right.

right: Right to complain to the national cybersecurity certification authority about certificates and EU statements of conformity
description: Persons can complain about certificates issued by national authorities or by conformity assessment bodies under Art. 56(6), or about EU statements of conformity; the authority must investigate and inform the complainant of progress and outcome.
exercise: Complaint to the national cybersecurity certification authority; investigation to the extent appropriate; information on progress and outcome within a reasonable period.
quote: handle complaints by natural or legal persons in relation to European cybersecurity certificates issued by national cybersecurity certification authorities
notes: Overlaps Art. 63 but also covers EU statements of conformity (self-assessment)
tl_reason: Complaint to certification authority by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to lodge a complaint concerning a European cybersecurity certificate
addressee: issuer of the certificate (conformity assessment body or national cybersecurity certification authority)
description: Any natural or legal person can lodge a complaint with the issuer of a European cybersecurity certificate, or with the national authority where a conformity assessment body issued a high-assurance certificate under Art. 56(6).
exercise: Complaint to the issuer, or to the relevant national cybersecurity certification authority for certificates issued under Art. 56(6).
quote: Natural and legal persons shall have the right to lodge a complaint with the issuer of a European cybersecurity certificate
notes: The issuer may be a private conformity assessment body
tl_reason: Complaint to certificate issuer by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right of complainants to be informed of progress, decision and judicial remedy
addressee: authority or body with which the complaint was lodged
description: The complainant must be informed of the progress of the proceedings, of the decision taken and of the right to an effective judicial remedy under Art. 64.
exercise: Automatic once a complaint under Art. 63(1) is lodged.
quote: shall inform the complainant of the progress of the proceedings and of the decision taken, and shall inform the complainant of the right to an effective judicial remedy referred to in Article 64
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint progress; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy
addressee: courts of the Member State where the authority or body is located
description: Persons can go to court against decisions of the certificate issuer or national authority (including improper issuing, failure to issue or recognition of a certificate they hold) and against failure to act on a complaint.
exercise: Before the courts of the Member State where the authority or body is located (Art. 64(2)); available notwithstanding administrative or non-judicial remedies.
quote: Notwithstanding any administrative or other non-judicial remedies, natural and legal persons shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy with regard to:
tl_reason: Judicial remedy; no technical element.

right: Right to request registration as a member of the Cybersecurity Competence Community
rightholder: entities established in the Member States (industry, academic and research organisations, civil society associations, etc.)
addressee: European Cybersecurity Competence Centre / national coordination centre
description: Entities with cybersecurity expertise meeting the Art. 8(3) criteria can ask to be registered as Community members; registration is not time-limited and a revocation on security grounds must be proportional and reasoned.
exercise: Request to the Competence Centre after assessment by the national coordination centre of the Member State of establishment (Art. 7(1)(i)); criteria in Art. 8(3).
quote: The Competence Centre shall register entities, at their request, as members of the Community after an assessment made by the national coordination centre
notes: Only entities established in the Member States
table_entry: Regulation establishing the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
tl_reason: Registration as community member; market-access type, no technical element.

right: Right of access to documents of the Competence Centre
rightholder: any natural or legal person (per Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001)
description: Public access to documents held by the Competence Centre under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
exercise: Application under Regulation 1049/2001 and the Governing Board's implementing arrangements (Art. 37(2)).
quote: Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 shall apply to documents held by the Competence Centre.
notes: Right granted by reference to Regulation 1049/2001
table_entry: Regulation establishing the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
tl_reason: Access to documents under Reg. 1049/2001; ordinary application.

right: Right to complain to the Ombudsman or bring an action before the CJEU against access-to-documents decisions
addressee: European Ombudsman / Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Competence Centre decisions on access-to-documents applications can be challenged by a complaint to the Ombudsman or an annulment action before the CJEU.
exercise: Complaint under Art. 228 TFEU or action under Art. 263 TFEU against decisions taken under Art. 8 of Regulation 1049/2001.
quote: Decisions taken by the Competence Centre pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 may be the subject of a complaint to the Ombudsman under Article 228 TFEU
table_entry: Regulation establishing the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
tl_reason: Ombudsman complaint or CJEU action; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by Competence Centre staff
description: The Competence Centre must make good damage caused by its staff in the performance of their duties (non-contractual liability).
exercise: Claim against the Competence Centre; the CJEU has jurisdiction over such compensation disputes (Art. 41(1)(b)).
quote: In the case of non-contractual liability, the Competence Centre shall make good any damage caused by its staff in the performance of their duties
table_entry: Regulation establishing the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
tl_reason: Non-contractual compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right to request CSIRT assistance with real-time monitoring
description: Essential and important entities can ask the national CSIRT for assistance with real-time or near real-time monitoring of their network and information systems.
exercise: Request to the competent CSIRT; CSIRTs may prioritise tasks on a risk basis (Art. 11(3), last subpara.).
quote: upon request, providing assistance to essential and important entities concerned regarding real-time or near real-time monitoring of their network and information systems
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Monitoring assistance is inherently technical (test: no), but the holder is a regulated entity asking a CSIRT, not a governed party. Conflict: holder.

right: Right to request proactive vulnerability scanning by the CSIRT
description: An essential or important entity can ask the CSIRT to proactively scan its network and information systems to detect vulnerabilities with potentially significant impact.
exercise: Request to the competent CSIRT; subject to risk-based prioritisation.
quote: providing, upon the request of an essential or important entity, a proactive scanning of the network and information systems of the entity concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Vulnerability scan and report are technical (test: no), but the holder is a regulated entity, not a governed party. Conflict: holder.

right: Right to report a vulnerability, anonymously if requested, to the CSIRT acting as coordinator
addressee: CSIRT designated as coordinator for coordinated vulnerability disclosure
description: Anyone can report a vulnerability to the designated CSIRT coordinator, anonymously on request; the CSIRT must ensure diligent follow-up and protect the reporter's anonymity.
exercise: Report to the national CSIRT designated as CVD coordinator; anonymity on request.
quote: Member States shall ensure that natural or legal persons are able to report, anonymously where they so request, a vulnerability to the CSIRT designated as coordinator.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Vulnerability report to the CSIRT by message; digital topic, technology incidental to the channel. Test: yes.

right: Right to request CSIRT intermediation and assistance in coordinated vulnerability disclosure
rightholder: natural or legal person reporting a vulnerability; manufacturer or provider of the affected ICT product or service
addressee: CSIRT designated as coordinator for coordinated vulnerability disclosure
description: Either the reporter of a vulnerability or the manufacturer/provider can ask the CSIRT coordinator to act as trusted intermediary, including contacting the entities concerned, assisting the reporter and negotiating disclosure timelines.
exercise: Request by either party to the CSIRT coordinator.
quote: shall act as a trusted intermediary, facilitating, where necessary, the interaction between the natural or legal person reporting a vulnerability and the manufacturer or provider
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Request for CSIRT intermediation in disclosure; human coordination through ordinary channels. Test: yes.

right: Right to access, and voluntarily register vulnerabilities in, the European vulnerability database
rightholder: all stakeholders; entities and their suppliers (for registration)
description: All stakeholders get access to the vulnerability information in ENISA's European vulnerability database (description, affected products, severity, patches or mitigation guidance), and entities and their suppliers can voluntarily disclose and register publicly known vulnerabilities in it.
exercise: Via the database maintained by ENISA; registration voluntary and open to entities regardless of whether they fall within NIS2 scope.
quote: All stakeholders shall be provided access to the information about the vulnerabilities contained in the European vulnerability database.
notes: Obligation directly on ENISA
tl_reason: Access is to an online vulnerability database; records (severity, patches) need technical interpretation. Without the database, no right. Test: no.

right: Right of service recipients to be notified of significant incidents
rightholder: recipients of the services of essential and important entities
description: Recipients of services are to be notified without undue delay of significant incidents likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.
exercise: Notification by the entity 'where appropriate', without undue delay.
quote: Where appropriate, entities concerned shall notify, without undue delay, the recipients of their services of significant incidents that are likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Plain notification of significant incidents; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of potentially affected service recipients to be informed of measures against significant cyber threats
rightholder: recipients of services potentially affected by a significant cyber threat
description: Recipients potentially affected by a significant cyber threat must be told, without undue delay, of measures or remedies they can take in response and, where appropriate, of the threat itself.
exercise: Communication by the entity where applicable; authorities can order it (Arts 32(4)(e), 33(4)(e)).
quote: essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to the recipients of their services that are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Plain communication of measures and remedies against a cyber threat; no channel required. Test: yes.

right: Right of notifying entities to feedback, guidance and technical support from the CSIRT or competent authority
description: An entity that notifies a significant incident receives initial feedback within 24 hours where possible and, on request, guidance or operational advice on mitigation and additional technical support from the CSIRT.
exercise: Response within 24 hours of the early warning where possible; guidance and technical support on the entity's request; guidance on reporting to law enforcement where criminal nature is suspected.
quote: upon request of the entity, guidance or operational advice on the implementation of possible mitigation measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; also applies to voluntary notifications via Art. 30(2)
tl_reason: Feedback, guidance and technical support on mitigation are technical, but holder is a notifying entity, not a governed party. Conflict: holder.

right: Right of legitimate access seekers to obtain domain name registration data
addressee: TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services
description: Legitimate access seekers can obtain specific domain name registration data (including registrant data) on a lawful and duly substantiated request, with a reply within 72 hours.
exercise: Lawful and duly substantiated request to the registry or registrar; reply without undue delay and within 72 hours; subject to Union data protection law; disclosure policies must be public.
quote: provide access to specific domain name registration data upon lawful and duly substantiated requests by legitimate access seekers, in accordance with Union data protection law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is the registration dataset, but a substantiated plain request works and the reply is plain data; holder is a third party. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to share cybersecurity information voluntarily within information-sharing arrangements
rightholder: entities within the scope of NIS2 and, where relevant, other entities
description: Entities can lawfully exchange cybersecurity information (threats, vulnerabilities, indicators of compromise, etc.) among themselves on a voluntary basis to prevent or respond to incidents, and can join or withdraw from information-sharing arrangements.
exercise: Within cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements (Art. 29(2)-(3)); essential and important entities notify the competent authority when joining or withdrawing (Art. 29(4)).
quote: are able to exchange on a voluntary basis relevant cybersecurity information among themselves
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; enabling provision
tl_reason: Legal permission for entities to exchange information; no duty-bearer mechanism for a governed party.

right: Right to submit voluntary notifications of incidents, cyber threats and near misses
rightholder: essential and important entities; any other entities whether or not within NIS2 scope
description: Entities can voluntarily notify the CSIRT or competent authority of incidents, cyber threats and near misses; the notification is handled under the Art. 23 procedure and creates no additional obligations for the notifier.
exercise: Voluntary notification to the CSIRT or competent authority; processing per Art. 23 (mandatory notifications may be prioritised); no additional obligations (Art. 30(2)).
quote: notifications can be submitted to the CSIRTs or, where applicable, the competent authorities, on a voluntary basis
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Voluntary incident notification to the CSIRT, usually online; a plain report works. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural safeguards, including an effective remedy and fair trial, against temporary suspensions and management bans
rightholder: essential entity; natural persons with managerial responsibilities at CEO or legal representative level
description: Temporary suspension of certifications or authorisations, or temporary bans on managers, must respect procedural safeguards including the right to an effective remedy and a fair trial, the presumption of innocence and the rights of the defence.
exercise: Invoked in proceedings on Art. 32(5) measures; measures last only until the entity remedies the deficiencies.
quote: shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with the general principles of Union law and the Charter, including the right to an effective remedy and to a fair trial
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; only essential entities, not public administration entities
tl_reason: Procedural safeguards and fair trial; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard before enforcement measures
description: Before enforcement measures are adopted, the entity must be notified of the preliminary findings and given reasonable time to submit observations; measures must be reasoned in detail and respect the rights of the defence (Art. 32(7)).
exercise: Submit observations within the time set; exception where immediate action is needed to prevent or respond to incidents; applies to important entities via Art. 33(5).
quote: the competent authorities shall notify the entities concerned of their preliminary findings. They shall also allow a reasonable time for those entities to submit observations
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Right to be heard in enforcement; no technical element.

right: Right to human intervention in automated decisions
description: Solely automated decisions producing adverse legal or significant effects are prohibited unless authorised by law with safeguards, at least the right to obtain human intervention.
quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Human intervention in an automated decision; plain request and plain review. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of follow-up to a request
description: Be informed in writing about the follow-up to a request without undue delay; communications and actions free of charge (Art. 12(4)).
quote: Member States shall provide for the controller to inform the data subject in writing about the follow up to his or her request without undue delay.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Written plain information on follow-up; electronic means allowed. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on processing
description: Have available the controller's identity, DPO contact, purposes, right to complain and existence of rights; in specific cases further information such as legal basis, retention and recipients.
exercise: Further information may be delayed, restricted or omitted on national law grounds (Art. 13(3)).
quote: Member States shall provide for the controller to make available to the data subject at least the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Plain information made available on processing. Test: yes.

right: Right of access
description: Obtain confirmation of processing and access to personal data with purposes, legal basis, recipients, retention, rights and origin.
exercise: Subject to restrictions under Art. 15.
quote: Member States shall provide for the right of the data subject to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Object is the personal dataset, but plain request works and access can be plain. Conflict: digital object vs plain result.

right: Right to be informed of refusal or restriction of access
description: Be informed in writing of any refusal or restriction of access and its reasons, and of the possibility to complain or seek a judicial remedy.
exercise: Reasons may be omitted where they would undermine the restriction.
quote: Member States shall provide for the controller to inform the data subject, without undue delay, in writing of any refusal or restriction of access and of the reasons for the refusal or the restriction
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Written plain information on refusal and remedies. Test: yes.

right: Right to rectification
description: Obtain rectification of inaccurate and completion of incomplete personal data without undue delay.
quote: Member States shall provide for the right of the data subject to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data relating to him or her.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Correction of stored data; plain request works, holder only checks. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to erasure
description: Obtain erasure where processing infringes Arts 4, 8 or 10 or erasure is legally required.
quote: provide for the right of the data subject to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Erasure of stored data, technical for controller; plain request works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to restriction instead of erasure and to be informed before lifting
description: Processing is restricted instead of erased where accuracy is contested and cannot be ascertained or data are needed as evidence; the data subject is informed before lifting.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject before lifting the restriction of processing
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Restriction marking in place of erasure plus notice before lifting; nothing to operate. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed of refusal of rectification, erasure or restriction
description: Be informed in writing of any refusal and its reasons, and of the possibility to complain or seek a judicial remedy.
exercise: Information may be restricted by national law on law-enforcement grounds.
quote: Member States shall provide for the controller to inform the data subject in writing of any refusal of rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Written plain information on refusal. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise rights indirectly through the supervisory authority
description: Where information, access or rectification is restricted, exercise rights through the supervisory authority, which verifies and informs the data subject that checks took place and of the right to a judicial remedy.
exercise: Controller must inform of this possibility (Art. 17(2)); SA informs of outcome (Art. 46(1)(g)).
quote: Member States shall adopt measures providing that the rights of the data subject may also be exercised through the competent supervisory authority
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Indirect exercise through the supervisory authority; ordinary procedure, plain outcome.

right: Right to exercise rights against each joint controller
description: Where national law so provides, exercise rights against any of the joint controllers irrespective of their arrangement.
quote: Member States may provide for the data subject to exercise his or her rights under the provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive in respect of and against each of the controllers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
tl_reason: Choice of addressee among joint controllers; no technical element.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach
description: Be informed without undue delay of a breach likely to result in a high risk.
exercise: Exceptions in Art. 31(3); may be delayed/omitted on Art. 13(3) grounds (Art. 31(5)).
quote: provide for the controller to communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Plain breach notice. Test: yes.

right: Right to information from the supervisory authority on exercising rights
description: Ask the supervisory authority for information on exercising data subject rights.
exercise: On request; free of charge (Art. 46(3)).
quote: upon request, provide information to any data subject concerning the exercise of their rights under this Directive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Information from authority on request; no technical element.

right: Confidential reporting of infringements
description: Competent authorities must have effective mechanisms encouraging confidential reporting of infringements of the Directive.
exercise: Via internal confidential reporting mechanisms.
quote: Member States shall provide for competent authorities to put in place effective mechanisms to encourage confidential reporting of infringements of this Directive.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Internal confidential reporting by staff; no technical element required.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
description: Lodge a complaint with a single supervisory authority; if not competent, it transmits the complaint and informs the data subject, and provides further assistance on request (Art. 52(2)-(3)).
exercise: Free of charge (Art. 46(3)).
quote: Member States shall provide for every data subject to have the right to lodge a complaint with a single supervisory authority
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Complaint form that can also be completed electronically, other means not excluded. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the progress and outcome of a complaint
description: Be informed by the competent supervisory authority of the progress and outcome of the complaint and of the possibility of a judicial remedy.
quote: The data subject shall be informed by the competent supervisory authority of the progress and the outcome of the complaint
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint progress; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a binding decision of a supervisory authority
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Challenge in court a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning the person.
exercise: Courts of the Member State where the authority is established (Art. 53(3)).
quote: Member States shall provide for the right of a natural or legal person to an effective judicial remedy against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Judicial remedy; no technical element.

right: Right to a judicial remedy against supervisory authority inaction
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Go to court where the competent supervisory authority does not handle a complaint or does not inform the data subject within three months.
exercise: After three months.
quote: each data subject shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy where the supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Article 45(1) does not handle a complaint
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against inaction; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor
description: Bring court proceedings where rights under national provisions implementing the Directive have been infringed.
quote: Member States shall provide for the right of a data subject to an effective judicial remedy where he or she considers that his or her rights laid down in provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court action against controller; no technical element.

right: Right to mandate a not-for-profit body to act on one's behalf
description: Mandate a qualifying not-for-profit body to lodge complaints and bring judicial remedies on one's behalf.
exercise: In accordance with national procedural law.
quote: provide for the data subject to have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Mandate covers complaints and court actions; ordinary legal act, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation
rightholder: any person who has suffered damage
description: Receive compensation for material or non-material damage from unlawful processing or infringements of national implementing provisions.
quote: to have the right to receive compensation for the damage suffered from the controller or any other authority competent under Member State law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right to accessible channels for reporting payment fraud
addressee: Member States / law enforcement and competent authorities
description: Appropriate reporting channels must be available so that non-cash payment fraud offences can be reported to law enforcement and other competent authorities without undue delay.
exercise: Via national reporting channels.
quote: appropriate reporting channels are made available in order to facilitate reporting of the offences referred to in Articles 3 to 8 to law enforcement authorities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on combating fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment
tl_reason: Reporting channels to police for payment fraud; law requires no technical mechanism and an ordinary report works. Not a digital relationship. Test: yes.

right: Right of identity-misuse fraud victims to protective advice and a list of support bodies
rightholder: natural and legal persons harmed by payment fraud committed by misusing personal data
description: Victims whose personal data were misused must receive specific information and advice on protecting themselves against consequences such as reputational damage, and a list of dedicated institutions dealing with identity-related crime and victim support.
quote: offered specific information and advice on how to protect themselves against the negative consequences of the offences, such as reputational damage
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Directive on combating fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment
