tl_reason: Information and advice for identity-fraud victims from authorities; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of legal-person victims to information on complaint procedures and their case
rightholder: legal persons that are victims of payment fraud offences
description: After first contact with an authority, legal-person victims must be told how to make complaints and their role, their right to case information, how to complain if their rights are not respected, and contact details for their case.
exercise: Without undue delay after first contact with a competent authority.
quote: legal persons that are victims of the offences referred to in Articles 3 to 8 of this Directive are offered the following information without undue delay
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Natural-person victims are covered by the Victims' Rights Directive 2012/29/EU.
table_entry: Directive on combating fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment
tl_reason: Procedural information for legal-person victims from authorities; no technical element.

right: Right of hosting providers to advance information before a first removal order
description: Before issuing its first removal order to a provider, the competent authority must give it information on the applicable procedures and deadlines at least 12 hours in advance.
exercise: Not in duly justified emergencies.
quote: it shall provide that hosting service provider with information on the applicable procedures and deadlines, at least 12 hours before issuing the removal order
tl_reason: Authority's procedural information duty toward a provider; no technical mechanism or digital relationship. Test: yes.

right: Right to request scrutiny of a cross-border removal order
addressee: competent authority of the host Member State
description: Within 48 hours, the hosting provider or content provider can ask the authority of the provider's Member State of establishment to check whether a removal order from another Member State seriously or manifestly infringes the Regulation or Charter rights; if so, the order lapses and content must be reinstated (Art. 4(6)-(7)).
exercise: Reasoned request within 48 hours of receiving the order or Art. 11(2) information; decision within 72 hours, communicated to the requesting content provider.
quote: Hosting service providers and content providers shall have the right to submit, within 48 hours of receiving either a removal order or information pursuant to Article 11(2), a reasoned request
tl_reason: Reasoned request to an authority by ordinary means; no technical mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right of hosting providers to request review of an exposure or specific-measures decision
description: A provider can at any time ask the competent authority to review, amend or revoke a decision finding it exposed to terrorist content or requiring specific measures.
exercise: Reasoned decision within three months.
quote: A hosting service provider may, at any time, request the competent authority to review and, where appropriate, amend or revoke a decision as referred to in paragraph 4 or 6.
tl_reason: Provider's review request to an authority; ordinary procedure, no technical element.

right: Right of hosting providers to an effective remedy against removal orders and decisions
description: Providers can challenge removal orders and scrutiny or specific-measures decisions before the courts of the Member State whose authority issued them.
exercise: Before courts of the issuing Member State; procedures set by Member States (Art. 9(3)).
quote: shall have a right to an effective remedy. That right shall include the right to challenge such a removal order before the courts of the Member State of the competent authority
tl_reason: Judicial remedy before national courts; no technical mechanism.

right: Right of content providers to an effective remedy against removal orders
description: Users whose content was removed or blocked under a removal order can challenge the order, and any Art. 4(4) scrutiny decision, before the courts of the issuing Member State.
exercise: Before courts of the issuing Member State.
quote: Content providers whose content has been removed or access to which has been disabled following a removal order shall have the right to an effective remedy.
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against a removal order; court action needs no technical means.

right: Right to complain about removal under specific measures and seek reinstatement
description: Users whose content was removed as a result of a provider's own specific measures can complain to the provider and ask for reinstatement; unjustified removals must be reversed without undue delay.
exercise: Through the provider's complaint mechanism; reinstatement does not preclude administrative or judicial review.
quote: allowing content providers where their content has been removed or access thereto has been disabled as a result of specific measures pursuant to Article 5 to submit a complaint
tl_reason: Complaint via provider mechanism not required to be electronic; plain complaint works, reinstatement needs no technical handling by holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to the outcome of a complaint within two weeks, with reasons if rejected
description: The provider must inform the complainant of the outcome within two weeks of receipt and give reasons if the complaint is rejected.
exercise: Two weeks from receipt.
quote: It shall inform the complainant of the outcome of the complaint within two weeks of the receipt thereof.
tl_reason: Outcome and reasons communicated in plain form; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of removal of one's content
description: When a provider removes or disables access to terrorist content, it must make information on the removal available to the content provider.
exercise: Can be suspended up to 6 + 6 weeks for public-security reasons (Art. 11(3)).
quote: Where a hosting service provider removes or disables access to terrorist content, it shall make available to the content provider information on such removal or disabling.
tl_reason: Plain information on removal made available by the provider; nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain reasons and a copy of the removal order on request
description: On request, the provider must either explain the reasons for removal and the content provider's rights to challenge the order, or give a copy of the removal order.
exercise: Upon request; subject to temporary non-disclosure (Art. 11(3)).
quote: Upon request of the content provider, the hosting service provider shall either inform the content provider of the reasons for the removal or disabling and its rights to challenge the removal order
tl_reason: Request by any means; reply is reasons or a copy of the order, usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to human review of detection of possible solicitation of children
addressee: provider of number-independent interpersonal communications service
description: Automated detection of possible grooming must remain subject to the user's right to human review.
exercise: Via the provider's redress mechanism (Art. 3(1)(g)(iv)); providers must also ensure human oversight and prior human confirmation before reporting new material (Art. 3(1)(g)(ii)-(iii)).
quote: without prejudice to the right to human review
notes: Applies until 3 Apr 2028
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is automated detection (software behaviour), but human review is requested plainly and the result is a plain decision; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to complain to the provider (internal redress)
addressee: provider of number-independent interpersonal communications service
description: Users can lodge a complaint with the provider within a reasonable timeframe to present their views on detection, removal or blocking measures.
exercise: Through the provider's complaint/redress procedure; relevant data are kept to enable redress (Art. 3(1)(h)(iv)).
quote: have established appropriate procedures and redress mechanisms to ensure that users can lodge complaints with them within a reasonable timeframe for the purpose of presenting their views
notes: Applies until 3 Apr 2028
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Complaint procedure with the provider; plain complaint works, outcome plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed that communications are scanned under the derogation
addressee: provider of number-independent interpersonal communications service
description: Users must be told clearly that the provider invokes the derogation from ePrivacy confidentiality, the logic of the measures, their impact, and that data may be shared with law enforcement and child-protection organisations.
quote: inform users in a clear, prominent and comprehensible way of the fact that they have invoked, in accordance with this Regulation, the derogation
notes: Applies until 3 Apr 2028
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is the logic of scanning technology, but information is given in clear language with no mechanism to operate; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to information on redress after removal, blocking or suspension
addressee: provider of number-independent interpersonal communications service
description: When content is removed, an account blocked or a service suspended, the user must be told of the avenues for redress with the provider, the possibility to complain to a data protection authority, and the right to a judicial remedy.
quote: inform users of the following, where their content has been removed or their account has been blocked or a service offered to them has been suspended
notes: Applies until 3 Apr 2028
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Plain information on redress avenues; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy
description: Users who consider their rights infringed by processing for CSAM detection can seek an effective judicial remedy.
exercise: Under GDPR Art. 79 and ePrivacy Directive Art. 15(2).
quote: users shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy where they consider that their rights have been infringed
notes: Applies until 3 Apr 2028
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Judicial remedy; no technical mechanism.

right: Right of providers to request EU Centre analysis of data samples
rightholder: provider of hosting or interpersonal communications services
description: Providers can ask the EU Centre to analyse representative anonymised data samples to support their risk assessment; free for SMEs where reasonably necessary.
exercise: Costs borne by requesting provider except SMEs.
quote: The provider may request the EU Centre to perform an analysis of representative, anonymized data samples to identify potential online child sexual abuse, to support the risk assessment.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Provider's request for an EU Centre analysis service; result is a report; holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of providers to comment on a draft detection order request
rightholder: provider of hosting or interpersonal communications services
description: Before a detection order is requested, the provider receives the draft request and can comment on it within a reasonable period.
exercise: Within period set by the Coordinating Authority.
quote: afford the provider an opportunity to comment on the draft request, within a reasonable time period set by that Coordinating Authority
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Procedural right to comment on a draft request; no technical element.

right: Right to effective redress against detection orders
rightholder: providers that received a detection order; users affected by its execution
description: Providers and affected users can challenge a detection order before the courts of the Member State whose authority issued it.
exercise: Before courts of the issuing Member State.
quote: as well as users affected by the measures taken to execute it, shall have a right to effective redress
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Court redress against a detection order; no technical mechanism.

right: Right of providers to free detection technologies from the EU Centre
rightholder: provider subject to a detection order
description: Providers executing a detection order are entitled to acquire, install and operate EU Centre detection technologies free of charge, but are not obliged to use any specific technology.
exercise: Subject to reasonable licensing conditions (Art. 50(1)).
quote: The provider shall be entitled to acquire, install and operate, free of charge, technologies made available by the EU Centre in accordance with Article 50(1)
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is detection software the provider installs and operates, but holder is the regulated provider, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to complain to the provider about detection measures
addressee: provider subject to a detection order
description: Users can complain through an accessible, age-appropriate mechanism about the provider's detection obligations and resulting decisions such as content removal, account blocking or service suspension.
exercise: Within a reasonable timeframe; objective, effective and timely handling.
quote: establish and operate an accessible, age-appropriate and user-friendly mechanism that allows users to submit to it, within a reasonable timeframe, complaints about alleged infringements
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Complaint mechanism not required to be electronic; plain complaint works, outcome plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed about detection technologies and related rights
addressee: provider subject to a detection order
description: Users must be told that detection technologies are operated, how they work and affect confidentiality, that reports go to the EU Centre, and of their rights to judicial redress and to complain to the provider and the Coordinating Authority.
quote: The provider shall inform users in a clear, prominent and comprehensible way of the following:
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is how detection technologies work, but information is plain language and needs no mechanism; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right of users concerned to be informed of detected potential abuse
addressee: provider subject to a detection order
description: Users concerned are informed when potential online child sexual abuse is detected, once law enforcement confirms this would not interfere with investigations.
exercise: After Europol/national law-enforcement confirmation.
quote: Where a provider detects potential online child sexual abuse through the measures taken to execute the detection order, it shall inform the users concerned without undue delay
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Notification of detected abuse is plain information; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of a report to the EU Centre
addressee: provider of hosting or interpersonal communications services
description: A user reported to the EU Centre is informed of the main content of the report, how the provider learned of it, any follow-up and redress options including a complaint to the Coordinating Authority.
exercise: After EU Centre finds report manifestly unfounded or after 3 months, unless deferred at law-enforcement request.
quote: Where the provider submits a report pursuant to paragraph 1, it shall inform the user concerned, providing information on the main content of the report
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Plain information on the report and redress options. Test: yes.

right: Right to flag potential online child sexual abuse
addressee: provider of hosting or interpersonal communications services
description: Users can flag potential online child sexual abuse to the provider through an accessible, age-appropriate, user-friendly mechanism.
quote: The provider shall establish and operate an accessible, age-appropriate and user-friendly mechanism that allow s users to flag to the provider potential online child sexual abuse on the service.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Flagging mechanism not required to be electronic; a plain notice works and nothing technical returns. Test: yes.

right: Right to effective redress against removal orders
rightholder: hosting providers that received a removal order; users who provided the material
description: Hosting providers and the users who uploaded the material can challenge a removal order before the courts of the issuing Member State.
exercise: Before courts of the issuing Member State.
quote: as well as the users who provided the material, shall have the right to an effective redress
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Court redress against a removal order; no technical element.

right: Right to information on removal, reasons and copy of the removal order
description: The uploader is informed of the removal, its reasons (with a copy of the order on request) and their rights to judicial redress and to complain to the Coordinating Authority.
exercise: Without undue delay; may be deferred up to 6 + 6 weeks (Art. 15(4)).
quote: it shall without undue delay, inform the user who provided the material of the following
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Plain information and copy of the order; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of internet access providers to comment before a blocking order request
description: The provider is informed of the intended blocking order and its reasons and may comment before the request is made.
exercise: Within period set by the Coordinating Authority.
quote: It shall afford the provider an opportunity to comment on that information, within a reasonable time period set by that Coordinating Authority.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Procedural comment right of an internet access provider; no technical element.

right: Right to effective redress against blocking orders
rightholder: internet access providers; users who provided or were prevented from accessing material
description: Internet access providers and affected users can challenge a blocking order before the courts of the issuing Member State.
exercise: Before courts of the issuing Member State.
quote: shall have a right to effective redress. That right shall include the right to challenge the blocking order before the courts
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Court redress against a blocking order; no technical element.

right: Right to complain to the internet access provider about blocking
description: Users can complain to the internet access provider about alleged infringements of its blocking obligations through an accessible, age-appropriate mechanism.
exercise: Within a reasonable timeframe.
quote: The provider shall establish and operate an accessible, age-appropriate and user-friendly mechanism that allows users to submit to it, within a reasonable timeframe , complaints
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Complaint mechanism not required to be electronic; plain complaint works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed when access is blocked
description: Users blocked from a URL are informed that this is due to a blocking order, the reasons (with a copy on request), and their rights to judicial redress, complaints and reassessment requests.
quote: it shall take reasonable measures to inform the users of the following
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Plain information shown to blocked users; nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to request reassessment of wrongful blocking
rightholder: internet access provider; users who provided or were prevented from accessing material
description: The provider and affected users can ask the Coordinating Authority to assess whether users are wrongly prevented from accessing a specific item; justified requests lead to modification or revocation of the order.
exercise: Coordinating Authority assesses without undue delay and informs the requester.
quote: The provider and the users referred to in paragraph 1 shall be entitled to request the Coordinating Authority that requested the issuance of the blocking order to assess
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Request to an authority by ordinary means; result is a decision. Test: yes.

right: Right of internet access providers to request modification or revocation of a blocking order
description: The provider may request modification or revocation of a blocking order where substantial changes since issuance, e.g. preventing reasonable execution, make this necessary.
quote: The provider shall also be entitled to request modification or revocation of the blocking order
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Provider's procedural request to an authority; no technical element.

right: Victims' right to information on reports of material depicting them
description: Victims can request information on any reports to the EU Centre of known child sexual abuse material depicting them: which provider reported, when, whether it was forwarded and whether it was removed.
exercise: Request to the Coordinating Authority of residence, with proof of identity; accessible formats for persons with disabilities.
quote: Persons residing in the Union shall have the right to receive , upon their request, from the Coordinating Authority designated by the Member State where the y reside , information
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Request to a public authority by ordinary means with proof of identity; plain information returned. Test: yes.

right: Victims' right to assistance from hosting providers for removal
rightholder: persons residing in the Union depicted in known CSAM
description: Victims can ask hosting providers for reasonable assistance in having specific items of known child sexual abuse material depicting them removed or disabled.
exercise: Request indicating the relevant items (Art. 21(3)).
quote: Providers of hosting services shall provide reasonable assistance, on request, to persons residing in the Union that seek to have one or more specific items of known child sexual abuse material
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is online material (digital), but a plain request identifying the items works and nothing technical is returned; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Victims' right to EU Centre support for removal
rightholder: persons residing in the Union depicted in known CSAM
description: Victims can obtain EU Centre support, via their Coordinating Authority, to get material depicting them removed, including verification searches and notices to providers.
exercise: Request to the Coordinating Authority of residence; accessible information for persons with disabilities.
quote: Persons residing in the Union shall have the right to receive, upon their request, from the Coordinating Authority designated by the Member State where the person resides, support from the EU Centre
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Request to Coordinating Authority by ordinary means; EU Centre acts technically, holder needs no mechanism or ability. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit observations and participate in proceedings on access restriction
rightholder: provider; intended addressees; third parties with a legitimate interest
description: Before a Coordinating Authority requests temporary restriction of access to a service, interested parties may submit written observations and the provider, addressees and third parties with a legitimate interest may participate in the proceedings.
exercise: Observation period of at least two weeks.
quote: The provider, the intended addressee or addressees and any other third party demonstrating a legitimate interest shall be entitled to participate in the proceedings regarding the request.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Participation in administrative and judicial proceedings; no technical element.

right: Rights of defence in enforcement proceedings
description: Investigatory and enforcement measures must respect private life and the rights of defence, including the right to be heard and access to the file, and are subject to an effective judicial remedy.
exercise: Under national law.
quote: those measures shall only be taken in accordance with the right to respect for private life and the rights of defence, including the rights to be heard and of access to the file
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Rights of defence in enforcement proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right of users to lodge a complaint with the Coordinating Authority
description: Users can complain about a provider's infringement of the Regulation affecting them to the Coordinating Authority of their Member State, with child-friendly procedures for children (Art. 34(2)).
exercise: Complaint to Coordinating Authority of residence/establishment.
quote: shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation affecting them against providers of relevant information society services
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Complaint to an authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right of providers to access indicator databases to execute orders
rightholder: providers subject to detection or blocking orders
description: Providers executing detection or blocking orders can obtain access to the EU Centre's databases of indicators to the extent necessary.
exercise: Reasoned request referencing the order (Art. 46(6)).
quote: The EU Centre shall give providers of hosting services, providers of interpersonal communications services and providers of internet access services access to the databases of indicators
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Access to indicator databases is technical, but holder is the regulated provider executing orders, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by the EU Centre
description: Persons harmed by the EU Centre's departments or staff can claim non-contractual compensation, with the Court of Justice competent for such disputes (Art. 79(4)).
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: In the case of non-contractual liability, the EU Centre shall, in accordance with the general principles common to the laws of the Member States, make good any damage caused by its departments
notes: Proposal text; may change. Would apply 6 months after entry into force (Art. 89).
entry_current_status: Interim Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 expired on 3 Apr 2026 and was re-adopted as Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 (applies until 3 Apr 2028); permanent CSA Regulation 2022/0155(COD) pending (awaiting EP first-reading position)
tl_reason: Non-contractual compensation claim before the CJEU; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation from the producer for damage caused by a defective product
addressee: producer (incl. importer into the Community, Art. 3(2))
description: An injured person can claim compensation without proving fault for death, personal injury or damage to private-use property (above EUR 500 threshold) caused by a defective product.
exercise: Must prove damage, defect and causal link (Art. 4); 3-year limitation from awareness (Art. 10); rights extinguished 10 years after circulation (Art. 11).
quote: The producer shall be liable for damage caused by a defect in his product.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026 (repealed by Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Art. 21).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: In force (products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026)
tl_reason: Compensation claim for defective product; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to claim against the supplier where the producer cannot be identified
description: If the producer (or, for imports, the importer) cannot be identified, each supplier is treated as producer unless it informs the injured person within a reasonable time of the identity of the producer or its own supplier.
exercise: Request identity information from the supplier; supplier liable if it fails to identify.
quote: each supplier of the product shall be treated as its producer unless he informs the injured person, within a reasonable time, of the identity of the producer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026 (repealed by Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Art. 21).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: In force (products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026)
tl_reason: Claim against supplier after identity request by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Joint and several liability of multiple liable persons
description: Where several persons are liable for the same damage, the injured person can claim full compensation from any of them.
quote: they shall be liable jointly and severally
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026 (repealed by Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Art. 21).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: In force (products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026)
tl_reason: Joint and several liability rule; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Protection against contractual exclusion or limitation of producer liability
description: The producer cannot limit or exclude its liability towards the injured person by contract.
quote: The liability of the producer arising from this Directive may not, in relation to the injured person, be limited or excluded by a provision limiting his liability or exempting him from liability.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026 (repealed by Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Art. 21).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: In force (products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026)
tl_reason: Ban on contractual exclusion of liability; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by a defective product
addressee: economic operators liable under Art. 8 (manufacturer, component manufacturer, importer, authorised representative, fulfilment service provider)
description: Any natural person who suffers damage from a defective product (including software) can claim compensation for death, personal injury incl. psychological health, damage to non-professional property, and destruction or corruption of non-professional data, covering material and, where national law allows, non-material losses (Art. 6).
exercise: Claim before national courts; 3-year limitation from awareness (Art. 16); 10-year expiry, 25 years for latent personal injury (Art. 17).
quote: any natural person who suffers damage caused by a defective product (the ‘injured person’) is entitled to compensation in accordance with this Directive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Compensation claim in court, even for software or data damage; topic digital, exercise not. Test: yes.

right: Right of subrogated persons and representatives to bring compensation claims
rightholder: person subrogated to the injured person's rights; person acting on behalf of injured persons
description: Compensation claims may also be brought by insurers or others subrogated to the injured person's rights, and by persons (e.g. representative entities) acting on behalf of one or more injured persons.
exercise: Under Union or national law or contract.
quote: claims for compensation pursuant to paragraph 1 may also be brought by:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Standing of insurers and representatives to sue; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a distributor to identify the liable economic operator, failing which the distributor is liable
description: Where no EU-established liable economic operator can be identified, the injured person can ask the distributor to identify one (or its own supplier); if it fails to do so within one month, the distributor is liable.
exercise: Request to the distributor; one-month deadline.
quote: the injured person requests that distributor to identify an economic operator from among those referred to in paragraph 1 and established in the Union
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Plain request to distributor to name liable operator. Test: yes.

right: Right to hold online platforms liable as distributors when they fail to identify the liable operator
addressee: provider of online platform allowing distance contracts with traders
description: The distributor-identification mechanism also applies to online marketplaces that present products in a way leading consumers to believe the platform itself supplies them (Art. 6(3) DSA).
exercise: Request to the platform; one-month deadline as in Art. 8(3).
quote: Paragraph 3 of this Article shall also apply to any provider of an online platform that allows consumers to conclude distance contracts with traders and that is not an economic operator
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Liability claim against platform after plain request; no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Compensation from national schemes where no liable person can pay
description: Member States may use or establish national compensation schemes for victims who cannot obtain compensation because no one is liable or liable persons are insolvent or gone.
exercise: Only where the Member State uses this option.
quote: Member States may use existing national sectoral compensation schemes or establish new ones under national law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)). Member-State option.
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: National compensation scheme; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request disclosure of evidence by the defendant
description: A claimant who presents facts and evidence making the claim plausible can have the court order the defendant to disclose relevant evidence at its disposal.
exercise: Request in proceedings; limited to what is necessary and proportionate, with protection of trade secrets (Art. 9(3)-(5)).
quote: the defendant is required to disclose relevant evidence that is at the defendant’s disposal
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Court-ordered disclosure of evidence; judicial procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of the defendant to request disclosure of evidence by the claimant
description: A defendant who shows a need for evidence to counter the claim can obtain disclosure of relevant evidence held by the claimant.
exercise: Request in proceedings, in accordance with national law.
quote: at the request of a defendant that has presented facts and evidence sufficient to demonstrate the defendant’s need for evidence for the purposes of countering a claim for compensation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Defendant's procedural disclosure request; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request confidentiality measures for disclosed trade secrets
description: Where trade secrets must be disclosed, a party can ask the court to take measures preserving their confidentiality during and after proceedings.
exercise: Duly reasoned request.
quote: upon a duly reasoned request of a party or on their own initiative, to take the specific measures necessary to preserve the confidentiality of that information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Court confidentiality measures for trade secrets; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to request that disclosed evidence be presented in an accessible and understandable manner
description: A party can ask the court to require disclosed evidence to be presented in an easily accessible and understandable way, if proportionate.
exercise: Duly reasoned request to the court.
quote: to require such evidence to be presented in an easily accessible and easily understandable manner
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Request to court that evidence be understandable; procedural, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Presumption of defectiveness
description: Defectiveness is presumed if the defendant fails to disclose evidence, the product breaches mandatory safety requirements protecting against the damage, or damage results from an obvious malfunction during foreseeable use.
exercise: Rebuttable (Art. 10(5)).
quote: The defectiveness of the product shall be presumed where any of the following conditions are met:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Evidentiary presumption in court; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Presumption of causal link
description: Causation is presumed once the product is shown to be defective and the damage is of a kind typically consistent with that defect.
exercise: Rebuttable (Art. 10(5)).
quote: The causal link between the defectiveness of the product and the damage shall be presumed where it has been established that the product is defective
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Evidentiary presumption in court; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Presumption of defectiveness and/or causation in cases of excessive difficulty
description: Where technical or scientific complexity makes proof excessively difficult, the court presumes defectiveness and/or causation if the claimant shows they are likely.
exercise: Applies despite disclosure; rebuttable (Art. 10(5)).
quote: the claimant faces excessive difficulties, in particular due to technical or scientific complexity, in proving the defectiveness of the product or the causal link
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Presumption for technically complex cases; still a court rule, holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right of the defendant to rebut presumptions
description: The defendant can rebut any of the presumptions of defectiveness or causation.
quote: The defendant shall have the right to rebut any of the presumptions referred to in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Defendant's rebuttal in court; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Joint and several liability of multiple economic operators
addressee: economic operators liable for the same damage
description: Where several economic operators are liable for the same damage, the injured person can hold them liable jointly and severally.
quote: where two or more economic operators are liable for the same damage pursuant to this Directive, they can be held liable jointly and severally
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Joint and several liability rule; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of recourse between liable economic operators
rightholder: economic operator that has compensated the injured person
description: An economic operator that paid compensation can pursue remedies against other operators liable for the same damage.
exercise: In accordance with national law; waiver possible for micro/small software manufacturers (Art. 12(2)).
quote: an economic operator that has compensated the injured person shall be entitled to pursue remedies against other economic operators liable pursuant to Article 8 in accordance with national law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Recourse between operators; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Protection against exclusion or limitation of liability
description: Liability towards the injured person cannot be limited or excluded by contract or by national law.
quote: the liability of an economic operator pursuant to this Directive is not, in relation to the injured person, limited or excluded by a contractual provision or by national law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 Dec 2026 (Art. 2(1)).
entry_current_status: 85/374/EEC applies to products placed on the market before 9 Dec 2026; new PLD (EU) 2024/2853 applies from 9 Dec 2026
source_legal_status: Adopted, applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026
tl_reason: Ban on limiting liability; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Opportunity to comment on draft national standards
rightholder: all relevant parties, including those established in other Member States
description: National standardisation bodies must give access to draft national standards so that all relevant parties can submit comments.
exercise: Comments submitted to the national standardisation body.
quote: ensure access to draft national standards in such a way that all relevant parties in particular those established in other Member States have the opportunity to submit comments
tl_reason: Commenting on draft standards; ordinary participation. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholder participation in European standardisation
rightholder: stakeholders incl. SMEs, consumer organisations, environmental and social stakeholders
description: ESOs must encourage and facilitate representation and effective participation of stakeholders at all stages of developing European standards (new work items, technical discussion, comments on drafts, revision).
exercise: Mainly through Union-financed European stakeholder organisations (Annex III).
quote: European standardisation organisations shall encourage and facilitate an appropriate representation and effective participation of all relevant stakeholders, including SMEs, consumer organisations
notes: Soft obligation on standardisation bodies; limited enforceability.
tl_reason: Stakeholder participation in standardisation; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Facilitated access of SMEs to standards and standardisation
description: National standardisation bodies must facilitate SME access to standards and standard development, e.g. participation without membership, free or reduced-rate participation, free access to drafts and abstracts, reduced prices.
exercise: Measures listed are illustrative.
quote: National standardisation bodies shall encourage and facilitate the access of SMEs to standards and standards development processes
notes: Soft obligation on standardisation bodies; limited enforceability.
tl_reason: SME access to standardisation; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholder notification before key standardisation decisions
description: The Commission operates a notification system so stakeholders are informed and consulted before adopting the annual work programme, standardisation requests, decisions on formal objections, ICT specification identifications and delegated acts.
quote: The Commission shall establish a notification system for all stakeholders
tl_reason: Stakeholder notification by Commission; no mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to buy radio equipment without a charging device
description: If an economic operator sells covered equipment (e.g. phones, tablets, cameras, headphones, laptops) with a charger, it must also let consumers and other end-users buy it without one.
exercise: Choice offered at purchase.
quote: the economic operator shall also offer the consumers and other end-users the possibility of acquiring that radio equipment without any charging device
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Inserted by Dir (EU) 2022/2380, which Member States apply from 28 Dec 2024, and for laptops from 28 Apr 2026. Covers equipment in Part I of Annex Ia.
tl_reason: Option to buy equipment without a charger at purchase; ordinary purchase choice. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed whether a charger is included (pictogram)
description: A pictogram on the packaging must show whether a charging device is included. For distance sales it must appear close to the price.
exercise: Pictogram on or stuck to the packaging; shown near the price indication in distance selling.
quote: information on whether or not a charging device is included with the radio equipment referred to in Article 3(4) is displayed in a graphic form using a user-friendly and easily accessible pictogram
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Inserted by Dir (EU) 2022/2380 (laptops from 28 Apr 2026).
tl_reason: Pictogram on packaging; printed information. Test: yes.

right: Right to instructions and safety information
addressee: manufacturer (importers ensure, Art 12(4); distributors verify, Art 13(2))
description: Radio equipment must come with clear instructions and safety information in a language end-users easily understand. For transmitters this includes the frequency bands and maximum power. Art 10(10) adds information on national restrictions on putting into service.
exercise: Accompanying the product.
quote: Manufacturers shall ensure that the radio equipment is accompanied by instructions and safety information.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Instructions and safety information accompanying the product; printed information. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on charging capabilities and compatible chargers (charging label)
addressee: manufacturer (importers and distributors ensure label display, Arts 12(4), 13(2))
description: For equipment under the common-charger rules, the instructions and a label must state the charging capabilities and which chargers are compatible. The label must be on the packaging and, in distance selling, close to the price.
exercise: Label on the packaging and in the instructions; shown near the price in distance selling.
quote: the instructions shall contain information on the specifications relating to the radio equipment’s charging capabilities and the compatible charging devices
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Inserted by Dir (EU) 2022/2380 (laptops from 28 Apr 2026).
tl_reason: Charging label on packaging and instructions; printed information. Test: yes.

right: Right of the client to consent to subcontracting by a notified body
description: A notified body may subcontract conformity-assessment activities or use a subsidiary only if the client agrees.
exercise: Client gives or withholds agreement.
quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the client.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Client consent to subcontracting by a notified body; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Manufacturers can appeal notified-body decisions through an appeal procedure that Member States must provide.
exercise: Appeal procedure under national law.
quote: Member States shall ensure that an appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies is available.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Appeal against notified-body decisions; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of economic operators in corrective measures
description: When authorities require corrective action, Art 21 of Reg (EC) No 765/2008 applies. Measures must state exact grounds, the operator must be told about available remedies and time limits, and must normally be given a chance to be heard beforehand.
exercise: Under Art 21 Reg (EC) No 765/2008 and national procedural law.
quote: Article 21 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 shall apply to the measures referred to in the second subparagraph of this paragraph.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Procedural rights in corrective measures; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure is contested, the Commission must consult the economic operators concerned before deciding whether it is justified, and must send them its decision.
exercise: Consultation by the Commission; decision communicated to the operator.
quote: the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the Member States and the relevant economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure
notes: Art 42(4)-(5) provides the same for compliant equipment presenting a risk.
tl_reason: Consultation in the Union safeguard procedure; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to use self-chosen pseudonyms in electronic transactions
description: Use of pseudonyms chosen by the user in electronic transactions may not be prohibited.
exercise: Subject to Union or national rules requiring identification.
quote: the use of pseudonyms that are chosen by the user shall not be prohibited
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Covers electronic transactions only, but no mechanism is required; choosing a pseudonym is just entering a name. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to obtain a European Digital Identity Wallet
rightholder: natural and legal persons in the Union
description: Every Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet so that natural and legal persons can access public and private services cross-border while keeping control over their data.
exercise: Wallet provided by, under mandate of, or recognised by the Member State (Art. 5a(2)); due within 24 months of the implementing acts.
quote: each Member State shall provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the date of entry into force of the implementing acts
notes: Inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183; deadline tied to implementing acts (no fixed date in text).
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is a software wallet the State must provide; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right to control and selectively disclose identity data through the wallet
description: Users can request, obtain, select, combine, store, delete, share and present person identification data and attestations under their sole control, with selective disclosure, to authenticate online and offline.
exercise: Through the wallet functionalities; user-friendly, transparent and traceable by the user.
quote: securely request, obtain, select, combine, store, delete, share and present, under the sole control of the user, person identification data
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Selective disclosure and presentation run only through wallet functions across relying parties. Test: no.

right: Right to generate and use pseudonyms within the wallet
description: The wallet must let users generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally.
quote: generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally within the European Digital Identity Wallet
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Pseudonyms are generated and stored encrypted in the wallet software and presented to relying parties. Test: no.

right: Right to exchange identity data and attestations wallet-to-wallet
description: Users can authenticate another person's wallet and securely receive and share identification data and attestations between two wallets.
quote: securely authenticate another person’s European Digital Identity Wallet, and receive and share person identification data
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet-to-wallet authentication and exchange is a software function across devices. Test: no.

right: Right to a transaction log and dashboard of relying parties and data exchanged
description: Users can access a log of all wallet transactions via a common dashboard, including an up-to-date list of relying parties connected to and the data exchanged.
exercise: Via the wallet's common dashboard.
quote: access a log of all transactions carried out through the European Digital Identity Wallet via a common dashboard
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Transaction log via the wallet dashboard; holder must interpret logged data exchanges. Test: no.

right: Right to request erasure by a relying party directly from the wallet
description: Users can easily request, from the wallet dashboard, that a relying party erase their personal data under GDPR Art. 17.
exercise: Dashboard function; common protocol required by Art. 5a(5)(a)(ix).
quote: easily request the erasure by a relying party of personal data pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulation (EU) 2016/679
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Mandated dashboard function with common protocol to request erasure of digitally held data. Test: no for this channel.

right: Right to report a relying party to the data protection authority from the wallet
description: Users can easily report a relying party to the competent data protection authority when they receive an allegedly unlawful or suspicious data request.
exercise: Dashboard function; common protocol required by Art. 5a(5)(a)(x).
quote: easily report a relying party to the competent national data protection authority, where an allegedly unlawful or suspicious request for data is received
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Mandated dashboard reporting function, but a complaint to the DPA by letter still works and the outcome is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to sign or seal with qualified electronic signatures/seals through the wallet
description: The wallet must enable users to sign with qualified electronic signatures or seal with qualified electronic seals.
quote: sign by means of qualified electronic signatures or seal by means of qualified electronic seals
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Qualified electronic signing is purely a technical function whose output is used elsewhere. Test: no.

right: Right to download one's wallet data, attestations and configurations
description: Users can download, as far as technically feasible, their data, electronic attestations of attributes and configurations.
quote: download, to the extent technically feasible, the user’s data, electronic attestation of attributes and configurations
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Download of wallet data, attestations and configurations; digital output to handle. Test: no.

right: Right to exercise data portability through the wallet
description: The wallet must enable users to exercise their data portability rights.
quote: exercise the user’s rights to data portability
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet must enable portability; data must be moved to another service. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed whether a relying party is permitted to access an attestation
description: For attestations with embedded disclosure policies, the wallet must inform the user whether the requesting relying party or wallet user has permission to access the attestation.
quote: inform the user that the relying party or the user of the European Digital Identity Wallet requesting that electronic attestation of attributes has the permission to access such attestation
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet evaluates embedded disclosure policy (software behaviour), but the result is a plain yes/no permission notice. Ability criterion weak.

right: Right to sign with qualified electronic signatures free of charge
description: All natural persons can sign with qualified electronic signatures by default and free of charge through the wallet.
exercise: Member States may limit free use to non-professional purposes.
quote: offer all natural persons the ability to sign by means of qualified electronic signatures by default and free of charge
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Default, free qualified e-signature through the wallet; signing is a technical function. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of wallet security breaches
description: Users must be informed without delay of any security breach that may have compromised their wallet or its contents, in particular suspension or revocation.
exercise: Without delay.
quote: Member State shall inform users, without delay, of any security breach that could have entirely or partially compromised their European Digital Identity Wallet or its contents
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do and nothing technical is asked. Test: yes.

right: Right to verify relying parties' identity free of charge
description: Member States must provide free validation mechanisms allowing users to verify the authenticity and validity of the identity of registered relying parties.
exercise: Free of charge.
quote: allow users to verify the authenticity and validity of the identity of relying parties registered in accordance with Article 5b
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Free validation mechanism to check relying-party identity; holder checks a technical result. Test: no.

right: Right to have one's wallet revoked on request
description: The validity of a wallet can be revoked upon the explicit request of the user.
exercise: Explicit request of the user; revocation free of charge for natural persons (Art. 5a(13)).
quote: upon the explicit request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object (wallet validity) is digital, but revocation follows a plain explicit request and nothing technical returns. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to request technical support and report problems
description: Wallet providers must let users easily request technical support and report technical problems or other incidents affecting wallet use.
quote: Providers of European Digital Identity Wallets shall ensure that users can easily request technical support and report technical problems
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Support requests and problem reports work by any channel; reply is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to free issuance, use and revocation of the wallet
description: Issuance, use and revocation of the wallet are free of charge for all natural persons.
quote: The issuance, use and revocation of the European Digital Identity Wallets shall be free of charge to all natural persons.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is a software wallet, but the entitlement itself is a pricing rule needing nothing technical. Criteria conflict.

right: Right to full control over wallet use and data (no profiling or data combination without request)
description: Users have full control over their wallet and its data; the provider may not collect non-necessary usage data or combine wallet data with data from other services unless the user expressly requests it.
exercise: Combination only on the user's express request; logical separation of data.
quote: Users shall have full control of the use of and of the data in their European Digital Identity Wallet.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: User controls wallet data through its functions; combination only on express in-wallet request. Test: no.

right: Right to voluntary use and non-discrimination of non-users
addressee: public and private service providers; employers; Member States
description: Using the wallet is voluntary; persons who do not use it may not be restricted or disadvantaged in accessing services, the labour market or business, and other identification means must remain available.
quote: The use of European Digital Identity Wallets shall be voluntary. Access to public and private services, access to the labour market and freedom to conduct business shall not in any way be restricted
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Right not to use the wallet and keep other identification means; nothing technical required.

right: Right not to be tracked or profiled through wallet attestations
description: The wallet framework must prevent attestation issuers or others from obtaining data that allows tracking, linking or correlating user behaviour, unless the user explicitly authorises it; unlinkability must be enabled where identification is not needed.
exercise: Only with the user's explicit authorisation.
quote: to obtain data that allows transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Unlinkability is software behaviour, but holder need do nothing except optionally authorise tracking. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to compensation for damage related to European Digital Identity Wallets
addressee: Member State / wallet provider / party operating authentication
description: The eID liability regime of Art. 11 applies mutatis mutandis to wallets, so persons harmed by failures can claim damages.
exercise: In accordance with national liability rules (Art. 11(4)).
quote: Article 11 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the European Digital Identity Wallet.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Damages claim under national liability rules; no technical element.

right: Right of persons with disabilities to accessible wallets
description: Wallets must be accessible to persons with disabilities on an equal basis with other users, per the European Accessibility Act.
quote: European Digital Identity Wallets shall be made accessible for use, by persons with disabilities, on an equal basis with other users
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is the wallet interface's accessibility; usable only by operating the wallet. Test: no.

right: Right not to be asked for data beyond the relying party's registered use
description: Relying parties may not request from users any data other than that indicated in their registration.
exercise: Users can report breaches via Art. 5a(4)(d)(iii).
quote: Relying parties shall not request users to provide any data other than that indicated pursuant to paragraph 2, point (c).
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Concerns wallet data requests, but the duty is a prohibition on relying parties; holder need only notice over-requests. Ability conflicts.

right: Right to know the identity of the relying party
description: Relying parties that intend to rely on wallets must identify themselves to the user.
quote: Where relying parties intend to rely upon European Digital Identity Wallets, they shall identify themselves to the user.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Identification occurs within the wallet protocol, but the result is a plain identity usable without technical means. Test partly yes.

right: Right to use pseudonyms with relying parties
description: Relying parties may not refuse pseudonyms where identification of the user is not legally required.
quote: Relying parties shall not refuse the use of pseudonyms, where the identification of the user is not required by Union or national law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Relying parties must accept wallet-generated pseudonyms in authentication flows. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of wallet suspension, withdrawal or re-establishment
description: Affected users must be informed when wallets are suspended or withdrawn after a security breach, and when provision is re-established (Art. 5e(2)-(3)).
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: The Member State shall inform the users affected, the single points of contact designated pursuant to Article 46c(1), the relying parties and the Commission accordingly.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Notice of suspension or re-establishment is plain information; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to use the wallet to access online public services
description: Where electronic identification is required for an online public service, Member States must also accept the European Digital Identity Wallet.
quote: Where Member States require electronic identification and authentication to access an online service provided by a public sector body, they shall also accept European Digital Identity Wallets
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet authentication to online public services; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use the wallet with private services requiring strong authentication
addressee: private relying parties (except micro and small enterprises)
description: Private relying parties legally or contractually required to use strong user authentication (transport, energy, banking, health, telecoms etc.) must accept the wallet at the user's voluntary request.
