exercise: Upon the voluntary request of the user; within 36 months of the implementing acts.
quote: only upon the voluntary request of the user, also accept European Digital Identity Wallets that are provided in accordance with this Regulation
notes: Micro and small enterprises excluded.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet authentication with private relying parties; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use the wallet to log in to very large online platforms
addressee: providers of very large online platforms (DSA Art. 33)
description: VLOPs requiring user authentication must accept and facilitate wallet-based authentication at the user's request, limited to the minimum data necessary.
exercise: Upon the voluntary request of the user; minimum data necessary.
quote: accept and facilitate the use of European Digital Identity Wallets that are provided in accordance with this Regulation for user authentication only upon the voluntary request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet-based login to very large online platforms; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use notified eID means from another Member State for online public services
rightholder: holder of a notified electronic identification means
description: Notified eID means issued in one Member State must be recognised in another Member State to access online public services requiring substantial or high assurance.
exercise: Scheme must be on the Commission list and meet the required assurance level.
quote: the electronic identification means issued in another Member State shall be recognised in the first Member State for the purposes of cross-border authentication for that service online
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Cross-border use of notified eID means for online services; purely technical authentication. Test: no.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by failures of notified eID schemes
addressee: notifying Member State; party issuing the eID means; party operating the authentication procedure
description: Persons suffering damage in a cross-border transaction caused intentionally or negligently by failures of the notifying State, issuer or authentication operator can claim damages.
exercise: Applied in accordance with national liability rules (Art. 11(4)).
quote: The notifying Member State shall be liable for damage caused intentionally or negligently to any natural or legal person due to a failure to comply with its obligations
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Damages claim under national liability rules; no technical element.

right: Right of wallet providers and eID issuers to interoperability with gatekeeper features
rightholder: providers of European Digital Identity Wallets and issuers of notified eID means (as DMA business users)
description: Gatekeepers must give wallet providers and eID issuers free and effective interoperability with, and access to, the same operating system, hardware and software features.
exercise: Free of charge; per DMA Art. 6(7).
quote: gatekeepers shall in particular allow them effective interoperability with, and, for the purposes of interoperability, access to, the same operating system, hardware or software features
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Access to OS, hardware and software features of gatekeepers; requires building interoperable software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by trust service providers
description: Anyone who suffers material or non-material damage from an infringement by a trust service provider can seek compensation.
exercise: Claimant proves intent/negligence of non-qualified providers; for qualified providers fault is presumed; no liability beyond limitations notified in advance (Art. 13(2)); national liability rules apply.
quote: Any natural or legal person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation by a trust service provider shall have the right to seek compensation
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Compensation claim against trust service provider; no technical element.

right: Right to accessible and plain-language eID and trust services
rightholder: persons with disabilities, elderly people and persons with limited access to digital technologies
description: eID means, trust services and related end-user products must be provided in plain, intelligible language and meet accessibility requirements.
quote: shall be made available in plain and intelligible language, in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is the accessibility of eID means and trust-service products; used only by operating them. Test: no.

right: Right to be notified of security breaches by non-qualified trust service providers
description: Non-qualified trust service providers must notify identifiable affected individuals of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact.
exercise: Without undue delay, at most 24 hours after awareness.
quote: notifying the supervisory body, the identifiable affected individuals, the public if it is of public interest
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information on qualified trust service terms
rightholder: any person seeking to use a qualified trust service
description: Before contracting, the provider must inform the person, publicly and individually, of the precise terms and conditions and limitations of the service.
exercise: Before entering the contract.
quote: inform, in a clear, comprehensive and easily accessible manner, in a publicly accessible space and individually any person seeking to use a qualified trust service of the precise terms and conditions
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Pre-contractual terms information; plain language, any channel works. Test: yes.

right: Right to consent before stored data are made publicly retrievable
rightholder: person to whom the data relates
description: Data stored by a qualified trust service provider may be publicly retrievable only with the consent of the person concerned.
quote: they are publicly available for retrieval only where the consent of the person to whom the data relates has been obtained
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is public retrievability of stored data, but consent can be given by plain means. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to be notified of security breaches by qualified trust service providers
description: Qualified trust service providers must notify identifiable affected individuals of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact.
exercise: Without undue delay and within 24 hours of the incident.
quote: notify the supervisory body, the identifiable affected individuals, other relevant competent bodies where applicable
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do. Test: yes.

right: Right to have a requested certificate revocation published within 24 hours
rightholder: holder of a qualified certificate (or qualified attestation of attributes, Art. 24(4a))
description: When a qualified certificate is revoked following a request, the provider must register and publish the revocation status within 24 hours of the request; revocation is effective on publication.
exercise: Request to the provider; publication within 24 hours.
quote: publish the revocation status of the certificate in a timely manner, and in any event within 24 hours after the receipt of the request
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object (certificate revocation status) is digital, but revocation follows a plain request; holder need not handle output. Test conflicts.

right: Right of relying parties to free certificate validity and revocation information
addressee: qualified trust service provider issuing qualified certificates
description: Relying parties can obtain, free of charge and at any time, automated per-certificate information on the validity or revocation status of qualified certificates.
exercise: Automated, free of charge, also beyond the certificate's validity period.
quote: qualified trust service providers issuing qualified certificates shall provide to any relying party information on the validity or revocation status of qualified certificates issued by them
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Automated per-certificate validity and revocation status (OCSP-type service) queried by software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to use advanced/qualified electronic signatures for online public services
description: Where an online public service requires an advanced electronic signature, Member States must recognise advanced and qualified signatures in the reference formats, and may not demand more than a qualified signature cross-border.
quote: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic signature to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic signatures
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Advanced or qualified e-signatures must be accepted for online public services; signing is purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to use advanced/qualified electronic seals for online public services
description: Where an online public service requires an advanced electronic seal, Member States must recognise advanced and qualified seals in the reference formats, and may not demand more than a qualified seal cross-border.
quote: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic seal in order to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic seals
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Advanced or qualified e-seals must be accepted for online public services; sealing is purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to have qualified website authentication certificates recognised and displayed by browsers
rightholder: website operators holding a qualified certificate for website authentication
description: Browser providers must recognise qualified website authentication certificates and display the attested identity data in a user-friendly manner.
exercise: Precautionary measures only under Art. 45a.
quote: Qualified certificates for website authentication issued in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article shall be recognised by providers of web-browsers.
notes: Micro and small browser providers exempt during their first five years.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Browsers must recognise and display qualified website certificates; operator must deploy the certificate. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of certificate holders to be notified of browser precautionary measures
rightholder: entity to whom the website certificate was issued
description: If a browser takes precautionary measures against a certificate, it must notify its concerns and measures in writing to the certificate holder (and others).
exercise: Without undue delay, in writing; supervisory body investigates (Art. 45a(4)).
quote: to the Commission, the competent supervisory body, the entity to whom the certificate was issued and to the qualified trust service provider that issued that certificate
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Written notice of browser measures; plain information, letter suffices. Test: yes.

right: Right to have attributes verified against public authentic sources at the user's request
addressee: Member States (authentic sources) / qualified trust service providers
description: Member States must enable qualified attestation providers to verify, at the user's request, attributes (at least those in Annex VI) against public-sector authentic sources.
exercise: At the request of the user; within 24 months of the implementing acts.
quote: measures are taken to allow qualified trust service providers of electronic attestations of attributes to verify those attributes by electronic means at the request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Electronic verification of attributes against authentic sources yields an electronic attestation used in the wallet. Test: no.

right: Right to obtain attestations of attributes in any Member State's wallet
addressee: providers of electronic attestations of attributes
description: Attestation providers must let wallet users request, obtain, store and manage attestations regardless of which Member State provided the wallet.
quote: shall provide European Digital Identity Wallet users with the possibility to request, obtain, store and manage the electronic attestation of attributes irrespective of the Member State
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Request, store and manage electronic attestations in any Member State's wallet. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of an order to suspend or cease a wallet
description: When a supervisory body orders a wallet provider to suspend or cease provision, it must inform wallet users without undue delay.
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: The supervisory body shall inform the supervisory bodies of other Member States, the Commission, relying parties and users of the European Digital Identity Wallet without undue delay of the decision
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Notice of a suspension order is plain information; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to complete key administrative procedures fully online
rightholder: user (EU citizen, EU resident or legal person with registered office in a Member State)
description: Users must be able to access and complete the Annex II procedures (e.g. birth certificate, residence registration, car registration, business registration) fully online.
exercise: Physical presence only exceptionally on public security/health/fraud grounds and limited to strictly necessary steps (Art. 6(3)).
quote: Each Member State shall ensure that users can access and complete any of the procedures listed in Annex II fully online
tl_reason: Law requires a fully online procedure, but the underlying procedures and outputs (certificates, registrations) are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to an automatic acknowledgement of receipt and notification of completion
rightholder: user (EU citizen, EU resident or legal person with registered office in a Member State)
description: For fully online procedures, users receive an automatic acknowledgement of receipt (unless output is immediate) and an electronic notification of completion (Art. 6(2)(d)).
quote: users are provided with an automatic acknowledgement of receipt, unless the output of the procedure is delivered immediately
tl_reason: Automatic acknowledgement and completion notice are plain information; nothing technical asked. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to assistance and problem-solving services
description: Users must have easy online access through different channels to the assistance and problem-solving services listed in Annex III (e.g. SOLVIT, Your Europe Advice).
quote: The Member States and the Commission shall ensure that users, including cross-border users, have easy online access through different channels to the assistance and problem-solving services
tl_reason: Online access to assistance services through several channels; help itself is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of delays and deadline extensions in procedures
rightholder: user (EU citizen, EU resident or legal person with registered office in a Member State)
description: Where no tacit approval or similar arrangements exist, authorities must inform users of delays, deadline extensions and their consequences.
quote: competent authorities shall, where applicable, inform users of any delays and of any extension of deadlines or any consequences thereof
tl_reason: Information on delays in online procedures; plain notice, any channel works. Test: yes.

right: Right of cross-border users to non-discriminatory online access to national procedures
description: Procedures available online to domestic users must also be accessible and completable online by cross-border users without discrimination, including foreign eID, e-signatures, electronic evidence and online fee payment.
exercise: Art. 13(2): instructions in a broadly understood language, submission of differently structured information, eIDAS identification, electronic evidence and outcome, non-discriminatory online payment.
quote: it can also be accessed and completed online by cross-border users in a non-discriminatory way by means of the same or an alternative technical solution
tl_reason: Online procedures must accept foreign eID, e-signatures and electronic evidence, but the procedures' object is non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to have digitalised copies of identity documents accepted
description: Where authorities accept digitalised copies of ID cards or passports from domestic users, they must accept them from cross-border users too.
quote: those authorities shall also accept such digitalised copies in respect of cross-border users
tl_reason: Uploading a scanned ID copy is incidental; the right is non-discrimination and paper copies serve the same end. Test: yes.

right: Right to preview evidence and decide whether to proceed with the exchange
addressee: Commission and Member States (technical system); requesting authority
description: Users can preview the evidence to be used by the requesting authority and choose whether or not to proceed with the exchange.
exercise: Not required where Union or national law allows exchange without preview (Art. 14(5)).
quote: enable the possibility for the user to preview the evidence to be used by the requesting competent authority and to choose whether or not to proceed with the exchange of evidence
tl_reason: Preview space in the once-only technical system; holder checks evidence and decides. Without it no preview. Test: no.

right: Right to choose not to use the once-only system and submit evidence directly
description: Use of the technical system is voluntary and only at the user's explicit request; users may submit evidence by other means directly to the authority.
exercise: Unless Union or national law provides otherwise.
quote: The use of the technical system shall not be obligatory for users and shall only be permitted at their explicit request
tl_reason: Choice whether to use a technical system, but the right's point is a non-technical alternative (direct submission). Test: yes.

right: Right to request cross-border automated exchange of evidence (once-only)
description: At the user's explicit request, the authority handling the procedure must obtain the required evidence directly from the issuing authority in another Member State via the once-only technical system.
exercise: Explicit, freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous request; evidence limited to what was requested (Art. 14(8)).
quote: upon an explicit, freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous request of the user concerned, request evidence directly from competent authorities issuing evidence in other Member States
tl_reason: Explicit request triggers automated cross-border evidence transfer via the once-only system. Test: no.

right: Right to advance notice of extended deadlines in assistance services (and online payment)
rightholder: users of assistance and problem-solving services
description: Assistance and problem-solving services must inform users in advance of reasons for and new deadlines when deadlines are extended; fees can be paid online without discrimination (Art. 16(c)).
quote: when deadlines are extended, users are informed in advance of the reasons thereof and of the new deadline given
tl_reason: Advance notice of extended deadlines is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to give anonymous feedback on gateway services
description: Users can comment anonymously, immediately after using a gateway service, on its quality and availability through a feedback tool accessible from all gateway pages.
exercise: Feedback tool on all gateway webpages (Art. 25(2)).
quote: a user-friendly feedback tool that enables them, immediately after using any of the services referred to in Article 2(2), to comment anonymously on the quality and availability of the services
tl_reason: Law requires an online feedback tool, but the feedback and its outcome are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to report obstacles to exercising internal market rights
description: Users can anonymously signal obstacles they encounter in exercising internal market rights; Member States and the Commission must analyse, investigate and address them (Art. 26(3)).
exercise: Anonymous online tool.
quote: provide users of the gateway with a user-friendly tool to signal and give feedback anonymously on any obstacles encountered by them in exercising their internal market rights
tl_reason: Law requires an anonymous online tool, but signalling obstacles is a plain complaint. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to clear instructions and safety information in an understandable language
description: Products must come with clear instructions and safety information in a language easily understood by consumers in the Member State of sale, unless the product can be used safely without them.
exercise: Provided with the product; may additionally be digital (Art. 21).
quote: Manufacturers shall ensure that their product is accompanied by clear instructions and safety information in a language which can be easily understood by consumers
tl_reason: Product instructions in understandable language, digital optional. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit product-safety complaints and accident reports to the manufacturer
addressee: manufacturer (importer must verify or provide channels, Art. 11(9))
description: Consumers can use publicly available, accessible channels (phone, email, website) to complain and report accidents or safety issues; manufacturers must investigate complaints alleging dangerous products (Art. 9(12)).
exercise: Via the manufacturer's published communication channels; complaint data kept max. 5 years (Art. 9(13)).
quote: enabling consumers to submit complaints and to inform manufacturers of any accident or safety issue they have experienced with a product
tl_reason: Complaint via phone, email or website; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to free information on national product safety rules
description: Economic operators can request, free of charge, specific information on national implementation of the GPSR and national product safety rules.
exercise: Request to national product contact points under Art. 9 Regulation (EU) 2019/515.
quote: Member States shall provide economic operators, at their request and free of charge, with specific information with respect to the implementation of this Regulation at national level
tl_reason: Free information request to contact point; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of free access to product traceability data
rightholder: consumers, economic operators and other relevant actors
description: Where the Commission sets up a traceability system for high-risk product categories, consumers, operators and others get free access to the data according to access rights defined in the delegated act.
exercise: Only for products covered by a delegated act under Art. 18(3); scope of access per Art. 18(3)(d).
quote: Market surveillance authorities, consumers, economic operators and other relevant actors shall have access free of charge to the data referred to in paragraph 3
notes: Conditional on Commission delegated act.
tl_reason: Data carrier/traceability system implies technical access, but data only 'including by electronic means', conditional on delegated act; relationship not digital. Mechanism conflicts.

right: Right to product safety information in online and distance-sales offers
addressee: economic operators selling at a distance
description: Online and distance offers must clearly show manufacturer (and EU responsible person) name and contact details, product identification incl. picture, and warnings or safety information.
exercise: Displayed in the offer.
quote: the offer of those products shall clearly and visibly indicate at least the following information:
tl_reason: Plain safety information shown in online offer; readable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to a single point of contact at online marketplaces for product safety issues
description: Online marketplaces must designate a single point of contact allowing consumers to communicate directly and rapidly on product safety issues.
quote: providers of online marketplaces shall designate a single point of contact to enable consumers to communicate directly and rapidly with them in relation to product safety issues
tl_reason: Contact point at marketplace; plain communication channel. Test: yes.

right: Right to have product-safety notices processed by online marketplaces within three working days
rightholder: any person submitting a notice under Art. 16 DSA
description: Notices about product safety issues submitted via the DSA notice-and-action mechanism must be processed without undue delay and within three working days.
exercise: Notice under Art. 16 Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
quote: Providers of online marketplaces shall, without undue delay and in any event within three working days from the receipt of the notice, process the notices related to product safety issues
tl_reason: Notice must go through electronic DSA Art. 16 mechanism, but notice and outcome are non-technical. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to product safety information on online marketplace listings
description: Marketplaces must design their interfaces so that each listing shows manufacturer and responsible person details, product identification and picture, and warnings or safety information.
quote: ensures that the information is displayed or otherwise made easily accessible by consumers on the product listing
tl_reason: Plain product information in listing interface; content not digital. Test: yes.

right: Right of traders to a prior warning before suspension by an online marketplace
description: Marketplaces may suspend traders that frequently offer non-compliant products only for a reasonable period and after a prior warning.
quote: shall suspend, for a reasonable period of time and after having issued a prior warning, the provision of their services to traders that frequently offer products which are non-compliant
tl_reason: Prior warning before trader suspension; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be informed of removal of their dangerous-product offers
description: Marketplaces must inform the relevant economic operator when they decide to remove or disable access to content offering a dangerous product.
quote: inform the relevant economic operator of the decision to remove or disable access to the content referring to an offer of a dangerous product
tl_reason: Information to operator on removal; no technical element for holder. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of economic operators in market surveillance (Art. 18 MSR applied to GPSR products)
description: Market surveillance of consumer products under the GPSR is subject to the MSR provisions, including Art. 18 procedural rights: reasoned measures, notice of remedies and a right to be heard.
exercise: See Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: Article 10, Article 11(1) to (7), Articles 12 to 15, Article 16(1) to (5), Articles 18 and 19 and Articles 21 to 24 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to products covered by this Regulation.
notes: Cross-reference to Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the public to access information on dangerous products and measures taken
description: The public has access to information on product identification, the nature of the risk and measures taken against products presenting risks, including via the Safety Gate Portal (Art. 34(1)).
exercise: Subject to restrictions for monitoring and investigation; accessible formats for persons with disabilities.
quote: In particular, the public shall have access to information on product identification, the nature of the risk and the measures taken.
notes: Chapter VIII 'Right to information and to a remedy'.
tl_reason: Public information, partly via Safety Gate Portal; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to competent authorities on product safety and unsatisfactory recall remedies
description: Consumers and others can complain to authorities about product safety, surveillance activities, and unsatisfactory recall remedies, and receive information on the follow-up.
exercise: Complaint to the competent national authority; follow-up information per national law.
quote: Member States shall give consumers and other interested parties the opportunity to submit complaints to the competent authorities on product safety
tl_reason: Complaint to authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to report risky products to the Commission via the Safety Gate Portal
description: Consumers can inform the Commission of products that may present a risk through a dedicated section of the Safety Gate Portal; the Commission follows up and informs them of its action.
exercise: Via the Safety Gate Portal; modalities set by implementing act (Art. 34(4)).
quote: Consumers and other interested parties shall have the possibility to inform the Commission of products that might present a risk to the health and safety of consumers
tl_reason: Law routes reports through Safety Gate Portal, but report and follow-up are non-technical. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to direct notification of product safety recalls and safety warnings
addressee: economic operators and providers of online marketplaces
description: Identifiable affected consumers must be notified directly and without undue delay of a recall or safety warning, using customer data held; written recall notices must follow Art. 36 (hazard, action to take, remedies, free phone line).
exercise: Direct notification; otherwise public recall notice through other channels (Art. 35(4)); marketplaces under Art. 22(12)(a)(i).
quote: shall ensure that all affected consumers that can be identified are notified directly and without undue delay
tl_reason: Direct recall notification by any channel; holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Option to provide separate contact details for safety-related purposes only
addressee: economic operators and providers of online marketplaces with product registration or loyalty programmes
description: Customers in product registration or loyalty schemes must be able to give separate contact details used only to contact them about recalls or safety warnings.
exercise: Data limited to the minimum and used only for recalls/safety warnings.
quote: they shall offer the possibility to their customers to provide separate contact details only for safety-related purposes
tl_reason: Option to give separate contact details in registration scheme; plain field, form often online. Test: yes.

right: Right to an effective, cost-free and timely remedy in a product safety recall
addressee: economic operator responsible for the recall
description: In any recall, the responsible economic operator must offer the consumer an effective, cost-free and timely remedy without significant inconvenience; the consumer bears no shipping or return costs and non-portable products are collected (Art. 37(5)).
exercise: Claim against the operator responsible for the recall; without prejudice to Directives (EU) 2019/770 and 2019/771.
quote: the economic operator responsible for the product safety recall shall offer the consumer an effective, cost-free and timely remedy
tl_reason: Recall remedy claim; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose between at least two recall remedies (repair, replacement, refund)
addressee: economic operator responsible for the recall
description: The consumer must be offered a choice between at least two of: repair, replacement with a safe equivalent, or refund of at least the price paid; consumer repair only if easy and safe with free parts or updates (Art. 37(3)).
exercise: Only one remedy may be offered where others are impossible or disproportionate.
quote: the economic operator shall offer the consumer the choice between at least two of the following remedies:
tl_reason: Choice of recall remedy; plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund where recall repair or replacement is not completed in time
addressee: economic operator responsible for the recall
description: The consumer is always entitled to a refund if repair or replacement is not completed within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience; disposal does not affect refund or replacement rights (Art. 37(4)).
quote: The consumer shall always be entitled to a refund of the product when the economic operator responsible for the product safety recall has not completed the repair or replacement
tl_reason: Refund claim; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Representative actions against GPSR infringements
rightholder: qualified entities on behalf of consumers
addressee: economic operators and providers of online marketplaces / courts
description: Infringements of the GPSR that harm consumers' collective interests can be pursued through representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive.
exercise: Via qualified entities under Directive (EU) 2020/1828 (Annex I point 8 as replaced by Art. 49).
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements by economic operators and providers of online marketplaces of provisions of this Regulation
tl_reason: Representative action by qualified entities; judicial. Test: yes.

right: Right to instructions for use and safety information
addressee: manufacturer (importers and distributors must ensure it, Arts 13(4), 15(2)(c))
description: Machinery must come with instructions for use and safety information in a language the user easily understands. Digital instructions must be printable and downloadable and stay online for the product's lifetime and at least 10 years. For products that non-professional users may use, essential safety information must be on paper.
exercise: Provided with the product; digital instructions accessible online for at least 10 years.
quote: present them in a format that makes it possible for the user to print and download the instructions for use and save them on an electronic device so that he or she can access them at all times
tl_reason: Instructions may be digital and downloadable, but content is plain and paper safety information is required. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free paper copy of the instructions for use
description: Where instructions are provided digitally, the user can ask at the time of purchase to get the instructions for use on paper, free of charge.
exercise: Request at the time of purchase; manufacturer supplies within one month, free of charge.
quote: at the request of the user at the time of the purchase, the manufacturer shall provide the instructions for use in paper format free of charge within one month
tl_reason: Free paper copy of instructions on request; non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free paper copy of assembly instructions for partly completed machinery
rightholder: person who incorporates the partly completed machinery
description: The person incorporating partly completed machinery is entitled to assembly instructions (digital ones must be downloadable and stay online for 10 years) and can ask at purchase for a free paper copy.
exercise: Request at the time of purchase; delivered within one month, free of charge.
quote: at the request of the person who incorporates the partly completed machinery at the time of purchase, the manufacturer shall provide the assembly instructions in paper format free of charge
notes: B2B context
tl_reason: Assembly instructions on paper on request; B2B, non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Right of the client to consent to subcontracting by a notified body
description: A notified body may subcontract conformity-assessment activities or use a subsidiary only if the client agrees.
exercise: Client gives or withholds agreement.
quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the client.
notes: Arts 26-42 apply from 20 Jan 2024 (Art 54)
tl_reason: Client consent to subcontracting by a notified body; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Manufacturers can challenge a notified body's decisions (e.g. refusal or withdrawal of a certificate) through an appeals procedure that the body must make transparent and accessible.
exercise: Via the notified body's appeals procedure.
quote: A notified body shall ensure that a transparent and accessible appeals procedure against its decisions is available.
notes: Arts 26-42 apply from 20 Jan 2024 (Art 54)
tl_reason: Appeal against notified-body decisions; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national restrictive measure is challenged, the Commission must consult the economic operators concerned before deciding whether the measure is justified, and must send them its decision.
exercise: Consultation by the Commission; decision communicated to the operator.
quote: the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the Member States and the relevant economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure
notes: Art 45(4) provides the same consultation for compliant products presenting a risk. Under Art 52(1), Chapter VI has applied since 19 Jul 2023 to products placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC.
tl_reason: Consultation in the Union safeguard procedure; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to plainly drafted terms and to the interpretation most favourable to the consumer
description: Written terms offered to the consumer must be in plain, intelligible language, and where the meaning of a term is in doubt the interpretation most favourable to the consumer prevails.
exercise: Invoked in individual disputes with the seller or supplier; the favourable-interpretation rule does not apply in collective proceedings under Art. 7(2).
quote: Where there is doubt about the meaning of a term, the interpretation most favourable to the consumer shall prevail.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Plain-language terms and interpretation rule; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be bound by unfair contract terms
description: Non-individually negotiated terms that, contrary to good faith, cause a significant imbalance to the consumer's detriment are not binding on the consumer; the rest of the contract continues if it can survive without them.
exercise: Raised against the seller or supplier, typically before national courts; the seller bears the burden of proving that a standard term was individually negotiated (Art. 3(2)); indicative list of unfair terms in the Annex.
quote: unfair terms used in a contract concluded with a consumer by a seller or supplier shall, as provided for under their national law, not be binding on the consumer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Core subject matter and price adequacy excluded from the test if plainly worded (Art. 4(2)).
tl_reason: Unfair terms not binding; contract law. Test: yes.

right: Right to bring proceedings against the continued use of unfair standard terms
rightholder: persons or organisations having a legitimate interest under national law in protecting consumers
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies (against sellers or suppliers)
description: Persons or organisations with a legitimate interest can ask a court or administrative body to decide whether terms drawn up for general use are unfair, so that their continued use can be stopped.
exercise: Action under national law; may be directed separately or jointly against several sellers or suppliers of the same sector or their associations (Art. 7(3)).
quote: persons or organizations, having a legitimate interest under national law in protecting consumers, may take action according to the national law concerned before the courts
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Injunction proceedings by organisations; judicial. Test: yes.

right: Right to identification and contact information about the service provider
description: Recipients have easy, direct and permanent access to the provider's name, geographic address, email and contact details, trade register entry, supervisory authority, professional details and VAT number.
quote: the service provider shall render easily, directly and permanently accessible to the recipients of the service and competent authorities, at least the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Identification details displayed on the service; plain information, nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to clear price indications
description: Where prices are referred to, they must be indicated clearly and unambiguously, stating whether tax and delivery costs are included.
quote: where information society services refer to prices, these are to be indicated clearly and unambiguously and, in particular, must indicate whether they are inclusive of tax and delivery costs
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Clear price indication is plain information; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to identifiable commercial communications and promotional offers
description: Commercial communications must be clearly identifiable as such, as must the person on whose behalf they are made; promotional offers and games must be identifiable with clear, accessible conditions.
quote: the commercial communication shall be clearly identifiable as such;
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Labelling of commercial communications is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to recognise unsolicited commercial email on receipt
description: Where a Member State permits unsolicited commercial email, such messages must be clearly and unambiguously identifiable as such as soon as they are received.
quote: shall be identifiable clearly and unambiguously as such as soon as it is received by the recipient
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Only where the Member State permits unsolicited commercial email.
tl_reason: Identifiability of commercial email is plain labelling; nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to opt out of unsolicited commercial email via opt-out registers
description: Natural persons who do not wish to receive unsolicited commercial email can register in opt-out registers, which senders must consult regularly and respect.
exercise: Registration in national opt-out register.
quote: consult regularly and respect the opt-out registers in which natural persons not wishing to receive such commercial communications can register themselves
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Registration in an opt-out register works by ordinary means; result (no spam) needs no technical handling. Test: yes.

right: Right to conclude legally valid contracts by electronic means
description: Contracts concluded electronically may not be deprived of legal effectiveness or validity because they were made electronically, and legal requirements must not obstruct electronic contracting.
quote: Member States shall ensure that their legal system allows contracts to be concluded by electronic means.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option to exclude real estate, court/public-authority, suretyship and family/succession contracts (Art. 9(2)).
tl_reason: Legal validity of electronic contracts; law requires no mechanism and paper contracting still works. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-order information on the electronic contracting process
description: Before placing an order, recipients receive clear information on the technical steps to conclude the contract, whether it will be filed and accessible, how to correct input errors, the available languages, and relevant codes of conduct (Art. 10(2)).
exercise: Prior to the order; may be derogated from by agreement between non-consumers; not for contracts concluded exclusively by email.
quote: the following information is given by the service provider clearly, comprehensibly and unambiguously and prior to the order being placed by the recipient of the service
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Pre-order information on contracting steps is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to store and reproduce contract terms
description: Contract terms and general conditions must be provided in a form that lets the recipient store and reproduce them.
exercise: Applies to all contracts, incl. B2B and email contracts.
quote: Contract terms and general conditions provided to the recipient must be made available in a way that allows him to store and reproduce them.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Terms must be storable and reproducible; a paper or plain copy satisfies this, no specific mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to acknowledgement of receipt of an order
description: When an order is placed through technological means, the provider must acknowledge receipt without undue delay and electronically.
exercise: Non-consumers may agree otherwise; not for email-only contracts (Art. 11(3)).
quote: the service provider has to acknowledge the receipt of the recipient's order without undue delay and by electronic means
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Electronic acknowledgement is a plain confirmation; holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right to means to identify and correct input errors before ordering
description: Recipients must be given appropriate, effective and accessible technical means to identify and correct input errors before placing an order.
exercise: Non-consumers may agree otherwise; not for email-only contracts.
quote: the service provider makes available to the recipient of the service appropriate, effective and accessible technical means allowing him to identify and correct input errors
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Provider must supply technical means in the order interface to correct input errors; without that function the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right to use out-of-court dispute settlement schemes
description: In disputes with an information society service provider, recipients can use out-of-court settlement schemes available under national law, including electronic means, without legal obstacles.
quote: their legislation does not hamper the use of out-of-court schemes, available under national law, for dispute settlement, including appropriate electronic means
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Out-of-court schemes may use electronic means, but an ordinary procedure works and the result is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to rapid court action including interim measures
rightholder: any person whose interests are impaired
description: Court actions concerning information society services must allow rapid measures, including interim measures, to end an alleged infringement and prevent further harm.
exercise: Under national procedural law.
quote: court actions available under national law concerning information society services' activities allow for the rapid adoption of measures, including interim measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court action including interim measures; no technical element.

right: Collective injunctions by qualified entities for e-commerce infringements
description: Adds the Directive to the Annex of the Injunctions Directive, so qualified entities can seek injunctions protecting consumers' collective interests against infringements of e-commerce rules.
exercise: Under national law transposing the injunctions/representative actions regime.
quote: The Annex to Directive 98/27/EC shall be supplemented as follows:
notes: Directive 98/27/EC has since been replaced (Directive 2009/22/EC, then Directive (EU) 2020/1828).
tl_reason: Collective injunctions by qualified entities; no technical element.

right: Right to obtain information on contractual rights and redress from national contact points
description: Recipients and providers can obtain from electronically accessible national contact points general information on contractual rights and obligations and complaint and redress mechanisms, plus details of bodies offering further help.
exercise: Electronic access at least.
quote: Member States shall establish contact points which shall be accessible at least by electronic means and from which recipients and service providers may:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Contact points must be electronically accessible, but request and general information are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right to take legal action or complain to an administrative authority against unfair commercial practices
rightholder: persons or organisations regarded under national law as having a legitimate interest, including competitors
addressee: Member State courts or competent administrative authority
description: Persons or organisations with a legitimate interest, including competitors, can take legal action against unfair commercial practices and/or bring them before an administrative authority competent to decide on complaints or to start proceedings.
exercise: Each Member State decides which facility applies; available regardless of where affected consumers are; cessation or prohibition orders possible without proof of loss, intention or negligence (Art. 11(2)); decisions of administrative authorities subject to judicial review (Art. 11(3)).
quote: persons or organisations regarded under national law as having a legitimate interest in combating unfair commercial practices, including competitors, may
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Legal action against unfair practices; judicial or administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by unfair commercial practices
rightholder: consumer harmed by an unfair commercial practice
description: Consumers harmed by unfair commercial practices have access to proportionate and effective remedies, including compensation for the damage they suffered.
exercise: Conditions and effects set by national law, which may take into account the gravity and nature of the practice and the damage; without prejudice to other Union or national remedies (Art. 11a(2)).
quote: Consumers harmed by unfair commercial practices, shall have access to proportionate and effective remedies, including compensation for damage suffered by the consumer
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a price reduction or termination of the contract for unfair commercial practices
rightholder: consumer harmed by an unfair commercial practice
description: Where relevant, consumers harmed by an unfair commercial practice can obtain a price reduction or terminate the contract.
exercise: Conditions and effects set by national law.
quote: where relevant, a price reduction or the termination of the contract
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Price reduction or termination; contract remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information (contracts other than distance or off-premises)
description: Before being bound by an on-premises contract, the consumer must receive clear information on the main characteristics, trader identity, total price, delivery and complaint handling, the legal guarantee, durability guarantees, software updates, duration and termination, functionality, interoperability and reparability.
exercise: Provided by the trader before conclusion unless apparent from the context; Member States may exempt day-to-day transactions performed immediately (Art. 5(3)).
quote: Before the consumer is bound by a contract other than a distance or an off-premises contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer with the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: On-premises pre-contractual information; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information (distance and off-premises contracts)
description: Before a distance or off-premises contract, the consumer must receive detailed information including trader contact details, total price, any price personalisation by automated decision-making, withdrawal conditions and the model withdrawal form, legal guarantee, after-sales services, duration, out-of-court redress and reparability.
exercise: Information forms an integral part of the contract (Art. 6(5)); on paper or durable medium for off-premises contracts (Art. 7(1)); key items shown directly before an online order (Art. 8(2)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 6(9)).
quote: Before the consumer is bound by a distance or off-premises contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer with the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information often shown online; plain content, paper works. Test: yes.

right: Right not to bear undisclosed charges or return costs
description: If the trader did not inform the consumer of additional charges or other costs, or of the cost of returning goods, the consumer does not have to bear them.
exercise: Invoked against the trader when charged.
quote: the consumer shall not bear those charges or costs
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Not bearing undisclosed charges; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to specific information when buying on an online marketplace
description: Before concluding a contract on an online marketplace, the consumer must be told the main ranking parameters, whether the third-party seller is a trader, that EU consumer rights do not apply if it is not, and how contractual obligations are shared between the seller and the marketplace.
exercise: Provided by the marketplace provider in a way appropriate to the means of distance communication.
quote: the provider of the online marketplace shall, without prejudice to Directive 2005/29/EC, provide the consumer with the following information in a clear and comprehensible manner
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Information on marketplace ranking parameters concerns software behaviour, but is plain-language and needs no technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to a copy or confirmation of an off-premises contract
description: For off-premises contracts the consumer receives a copy of the signed contract or a confirmation, including any consent and acknowledgement relating to loss of the withdrawal right.
exercise: On paper or, if the consumer agrees, another durable medium.
quote: The trader shall provide the consumer with a copy of the signed contract or the confirmation of the contract on paper or, if the consumer agrees, on another durable medium
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Copy of contract on paper or durable medium. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be bound by an online order without a clearly labelled payment button
description: For online orders that involve payment, key information must be shown directly before ordering and the order button must state 'order with obligation to pay' or equivalent; if not, the consumer is not bound by the contract or order.
exercise: Invoked against the trader; also applies to passenger transport and package travel (Art. 3(3)).
quote: If the trader has not complied with this subparagraph, the consumer shall not be bound by the contract or order.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Applies to online order buttons, but non-bindingness is invoked by plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told the caller's identity and commercial purpose in telephone sales
description: When a trader phones a consumer to conclude a distance contract, the trader must disclose at the start its identity (and that of any principal) and the commercial purpose of the call.
exercise: At the beginning of the call; Member States may require written confirmation before the consumer is bound (Art. 8(6)).
quote: disclose his identity and, where applicable, the identity of the person on whose behalf he makes that call, and the commercial purpose of the call
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Caller identity disclosure in phone sales; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to confirmation of a distance contract on a durable medium
description: After a distance contract, the consumer receives a confirmation on a durable medium containing the pre-contractual information and any consent or acknowledgement on loss of the withdrawal right.
exercise: Within a reasonable time, at the latest on delivery of goods or before performance of the service begins.
quote: The trader shall provide the consumer with the confirmation of the contract concluded, on a durable medium within a reasonable time after the conclusion of the distance contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Confirmation of distance contract on durable medium, usually email; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of withdrawal from distance and off-premises contracts
description: The consumer may withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract within 14 days without giving reasons and without costs other than direct return costs and those in Arts 13(2) and 14.
exercise: Period runs from conclusion (services, utilities, online digital content) or from physical possession of goods (Art. 9(2)); extended by up to 12 months if the consumer was not informed (Art. 10); Member States may extend to 30 days for unsolicited home visits and excursions (Art. 9(1a)); exercised by the model form or any unequivocal statement sent before expiry (Art. 11); exceptions in Art. 16.
quote: the consumer shall have a period of 14 days to withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract, without giving any reason
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal by model form or any statement, often online; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to withdraw using an online withdrawal function
description: For distance contracts concluded through an online interface, the consumer can withdraw through a prominently displayed, continuously available 'withdraw from contract here' function followed by a 'confirm withdrawal' function, and receives an acknowledgement of receipt on a durable medium.
exercise: Online withdrawal statement with name, contract details and the electronic means for the confirmation; submission before the period expires is timely (Art. 11a(5)); also applies to distance financial services contracts (Art. 3(1b)).
quote: For distance contracts concluded by the means of an online interface, the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also withdraw from the contract by using a withdrawal function.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Trader must provide 'withdraw from contract here' function; this right is the button itself. Test: no.

right: Right to reimbursement of all payments after withdrawal
description: After withdrawal the trader must refund all payments, including standard delivery costs, within 14 days of being informed, using the same means of payment and without fees for the consumer.
exercise: Trader may withhold the refund until goods are received back or proof of dispatch is supplied (Art. 13(3)); extra cost of a non-standard delivery chosen by the consumer is not refunded (Art. 13(2)).
quote: The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including, if applicable, the costs of delivery without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Refund after withdrawal; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to retrieve user-generated content after withdrawal from a digital content or service contract
description: After withdrawal, the consumer can obtain the non-personal content they provided or created while using the digital content or service, free of charge and in a commonly used, machine-readable format; the trader must otherwise stop using it.
exercise: Request to the trader (Art. 13(6)); within a reasonable time; exceptions for content with no utility outside the service, relating only to the consumer's activity, or aggregated (Art. 13(5)); personal data governed by the GDPR (Art. 13(4)).
quote: The consumer shall be entitled to retrieve that digital content free of charge, without hindrance from the trader, within a reasonable time and in a commonly used and machine-readable format.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Content returned in commonly used machine-readable format for reuse elsewhere; result unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to bear no cost for performance during the withdrawal period in specified cases
description: The consumer pays nothing for services, utilities or online digital content supplied during the withdrawal period if the trader failed to give the required information or did not obtain the consumer's express request, consent, acknowledgement or confirmation.
exercise: Invoked against the trader after withdrawal; no other liability for exercising withdrawal (Art. 14(5)); no liability for diminished value of goods if not informed of the withdrawal right (Art. 14(2)).
quote: The consumer shall bear no cost for:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for performance during withdrawal period; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Automatic cost-free termination of ancillary contracts on withdrawal
description: When the consumer withdraws from a distance or off-premises contract, any ancillary contracts end automatically without cost to the consumer.
exercise: Follows automatically from withdrawal; detailed rules set by Member States (Art. 15(2)).
quote: any ancillary contracts shall be automatically terminated, without any costs for the consumer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Automatic termination of ancillary contracts. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information for distance financial services contracts
description: In good time before a distance financial services contract, the consumer receives information on the trader, the service, total price, risks, personalised pricing, withdrawal right, early termination, applicable law, languages, out-of-court redress and guarantee funds.
exercise: On a durable medium and easy to read (Art. 16a(6)); layered information must be viewable and printable as one document (Art. 16a(7)); reduced set for voice telephony with the consumer's agreement, remainder immediately after conclusion (Art. 16a(4)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 16a(8)).
quote: In good time before the consumer is bound by a distance contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer, in a clear and comprehensible manner
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Distance financial-services information on durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told of trader identity, commercial purpose and call recording in financial services phone calls
description: In trader-initiated phone calls about financial services, the trader's identity and commercial purpose must be made clear at the start, and the consumer must be told if the call is or may be recorded.
exercise: At the beginning of the call.
quote: When a call is being recorded, or might be recorded, the trader shall also notify the consumer that this is the case.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Phone-call disclosures; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to a withdrawal reminder when information was given less than one day before conclusion
description: If pre-contractual information reached the consumer less than a day before a distance financial services contract was concluded, the trader must send a reminder of the right to withdraw and how to do it.
exercise: Reminder on a durable medium between one and seven days after conclusion.
quote: Member States shall require that the trader sends a reminder to the consumer of the possibility to withdraw from the distance contract and of the procedure to follow for withdrawing
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal reminder on durable medium in distance context; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumers with disabilities to pre-contractual information in an accessible format
description: Consumers with disabilities, including visual impairment, can obtain the financial services pre-contractual information in an appropriate and accessible format.
exercise: On request to the trader.
quote: The information referred to in paragraph 1 shall be provided upon request in an appropriate and accessible format to consumers with disabilities, including those with a visual impairment.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Accessible-format information on request; format need not be digital. Test: yes.

right: Right of withdrawal from distance financial services contracts
description: The consumer may withdraw from a distance financial services contract within 14 calendar days (30 for personal pension operations) without penalty and without giving reasons.
exercise: Period runs from conclusion or from receipt of terms and information if later; if information was not received, it ends 12 months and 14 days after conclusion (no end date if not informed of the withdrawal right); timely if sent before expiry (Art. 16b(3)); online withdrawal function available (Art. 11a); exceptions for market-fluctuation services, short travel/baggage insurance and fully performed contracts (Art. 16b(2)); sector-specific Union acts prevail (Art. 16b(6)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that the consumer has a period of 14 calendar days to withdraw from a contract without penalty and without giving any reason.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal by statement, online function optional; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be released from ancillary contracts on withdrawal from a financial services contract
description: When the consumer withdraws from a distance financial services contract, they are not bound by related ancillary service contracts, and terminating them costs nothing.
exercise: Follows from withdrawal under Art. 16b.
quote: the consumer shall not be bound by the ancillary contract if the consumer exercises his or her right of withdrawal in accordance with this Article
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Release from ancillary contracts; automatic. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund within 30 days after withdrawal from a financial services contract
description: After withdrawal the trader must return all sums received within 30 calendar days, keeping only a proportionate, non-penal amount for services actually provided.
exercise: The consumer can be charged only if duly informed of the amount and if performance began at the consumer's request (Art. 16c(1), (3)); Member States may exclude any payment for insurance contracts (Art. 16c(2)).
quote: return to the consumer any sums the trader has received from him or her in accordance with the distance contract, except for the amount referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Refund after withdrawal; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to adequate explanations before a financial services contract
description: Before conclusion, the consumer receives free explanations of the pre-contractual information, the contract's essential characteristics and its specific effects (including consequences of payment default) so they can judge whether it suits their needs and finances.
exercise: Free of charge, before conclusion; manner and extent may be specified by Member States (Art. 16d(2)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 16d(4)).
quote: traders are required to provide adequate explanations to the consumer concerning the proposed financial services contracts
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Explanations before distance financial contract; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to request human intervention when online tools are used
description: Where the trader uses online tools for distance financial services, the consumer can request and obtain human intervention at the pre-contractual stage and, in justified cases, after conclusion.
exercise: Request to the trader; in the same language as the pre-contractual information.
quote: the consumer shall have a right to request and to obtain human intervention at the pre-contractual stage, and in justified cases after the distance contract has been concluded
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is online/automated tools, but request is plain and result is human contact. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to delivery of goods within the agreed time or 30 days
description: Unless otherwise agreed, the trader must deliver goods by transferring physical possession or control to the consumer without undue delay and within 30 days of conclusion.
exercise: Enforced through the termination right in Art. 18(2) and other national remedies (Art. 18(4)).
quote: the trader shall deliver the goods by transferring the physical possession or control of the goods to the consumer without undue delay, but not later than 30 days from the conclusion of the contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Delivery of goods; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the contract for late delivery
description: If goods are not delivered on time, the consumer may set an additional period and terminate if delivery still fails; termination is immediate where the trader refused delivery or the date was essential. The trader must then refund all sums paid.
exercise: Call on the trader to deliver within an appropriate additional period, then terminate; refund without undue delay (Art. 18(3)); other national remedies remain (Art. 18(4)).
quote: If the trader fails to deliver the goods within that additional period of time, the consumer shall be entitled to terminate the contract.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Termination for late delivery; contract remedy. Test: yes.

right: Protection against payment-method fees above cost
description: Traders may not charge consumers fees for using a given means of payment that exceed the trader's own cost.
exercise: Invoked against the trader; also applies to financial services, passenger transport and package travel.
quote: Member States shall prohibit traders from charging consumers, in respect of the use of a given means of payment, fees that exceed the cost borne by the trader for the use of such means.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Ban on excessive payment fees; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Risk passes to the consumer only on physical possession
description: When the trader dispatches goods, risk of loss or damage stays with the trader until the consumer (or a third party they name, other than the carrier) takes physical possession, unless the consumer chose a carrier the trader did not offer.
exercise: Invoked against the trader if goods are lost or damaged in transit.
quote: the risk of loss of or damage to the goods shall pass to the consumer when he or a third party indicated by the consumer and other than the carrier has acquired the physical possession of the goods
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Passing of risk; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to contact the trader by phone at no more than the basic rate
description: When calling a trader's telephone line about a concluded contract, the consumer is not obliged to pay more than the basic rate.
exercise: Applies to post-contract hotlines; telecom providers may still charge for the call.
quote: the consumer, when contacting the trader is not bound to pay more than the basic rate
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Phone hotline at basic rate; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to refuse extra payments without express consent (no pre-ticked boxes)
description: Any extra payment beyond the main price requires the consumer's express consent; consent inferred from default options the consumer must reject entitles the consumer to a refund.
exercise: Claim reimbursement from the trader.
quote: has inferred it by using default options which the consumer is required to reject in order to avoid the additional payment, the consumer shall be entitled to reimbursement of this payment
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-ticked boxes mostly online, but refund claimed by plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumer and professional organisations to take enforcement action
rightholder: consumer organisations and professional organisations having a legitimate interest (as determined by national law)
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Consumer organisations and professional organisations with a legitimate interest can go to court or to administrative bodies to ensure the national rules transposing the Directive are applied.
exercise: Standing determined by national law.
quote: may take action under national law before the courts or before the competent administrative bodies to ensure that the national provisions transposing this Directive are applied
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Public bodies also listed but not recorded.
tl_reason: Enforcement action by organisations; judicial. Test: yes.

right: Exemption from payment for unsolicited goods or services (inertia selling)
description: The consumer owes nothing for unsolicited supply of goods, utilities or digital content or unsolicited services, and silence does not count as consent.
exercise: Invoked against the trader.
quote: The consumer shall be exempted from the obligation to provide any consideration in cases of unsolicited supply
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for unsolicited supply; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to have standard-compliant e-invoices accepted and processed by public buyers
rightholder: suppliers and contractors invoicing under public procurement contracts
description: Suppliers can send electronic invoices that comply with the European e-invoicing standard and a listed syntax, and contracting authorities and entities must receive and process them.
exercise: Applies to invoices under contracts covered by Directives 2009/81/EC, 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU (Art. 1); does not itself oblige suppliers to e-invoice.
quote: Member States shall ensure that contracting authorities and contracting entities receive and process electronic invoices which comply with the European standard on electronic invoicing
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Holder must produce e-invoices in the European standard and syntax; buyer must accept them. Without the format no right. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to access online interfaces without geo-blocking
rightholder: customer (consumer who is an EU national or resident, or undertaking established in the EU, buying for end use)
description: Traders may not block or limit a customer's access to their website or app because of the customer's nationality, place of residence or place of establishment.
