description: Member States may require the individual member's approval of clauses increasing their economic obligations, where the member cannot exit under Art. 86i.
quote: Member States may require, in such specific circumstances, that such clause or the amendment to the instrument of constitution be approved by the member concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Individual approval of burdensome clauses; corporate consent, no technical element.

right: Exit right of dissenting members for adequate cash compensation (conversion)
rightholder: members who voted against the cross-border conversion
description: Members who voted against can dispose of their shares for adequate cash compensation.
exercise: Declare decision within max. one month after the general meeting (electronic address required); payment within two months after the conversion takes effect; departure State law and courts (Art. 86i(2)-(5)).
quote: at least the members of a company who voted against the approval of the draft terms of the cross-border conversion have the right to dispose of their shares for adequate cash compensation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Exit for cash compensation; financial right, technology at most incidental.

right: Right to claim additional cash compensation (conversion)
rightholder: members who exercised the exit right
description: Exiting members who consider the compensation inadequate can claim additional cash compensation before the competent authority.
exercise: Within national time limit; decision may extend to all exiting members.
quote: but who consider that the cash compensation offered by the company has not been adequately set, are entitled to claim additional cash compensation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Claim for additional compensation before an authority; no technical element.

right: Right of creditors to apply for adequate safeguards (conversion)
rightholder: creditors with prior claims not yet due
description: Creditors dissatisfied with offered safeguards can apply to an authority for adequate safeguards if the conversion puts their claims at stake.
exercise: Within three months of disclosure of the draft terms.
quote: creditors who are dissatisfied with the safeguards offered in the draft terms of the cross-border conversion, as provided for in point (f) of Article 86d, may apply
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Creditor application for safeguards; no technical element.

right: Right of creditors to sue the converted company in the departure Member State
addressee: courts of the departure Member State
description: Creditors can bring proceedings against the converted company in the departure Member State for two years after the conversion.
exercise: Within two years of the conversion taking effect.
quote: creditors whose claims antedate the disclosure of the draft terms of the cross-border conversion are able to institute proceedings against the company also in the departure Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Proceedings in the departure State; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right of employees to information, consultation and a reasoned response (conversion)
description: Employees' information and consultation rights must be respected before the draft terms or report are decided, with a reasoned response before the general meeting.
exercise: Under Directives 2002/14/EC and 2009/38/EC.
quote: in such a way that a reasoned response is given to the employees before the general meeting referred to in Article 86h
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Employee information and consultation; no technical element.

right: Right of employees to preserved board-level participation (conversion)
description: Where the destination law offers less participation, employee participation is negotiated under SE rules, prior rules continue meanwhile, protection lasts four years, and employees are told the outcome (Art. 86l(8)).
quote: the participation of employees in the converted company and their involvement in the definition of such rights shall be regulated by the Member States
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Board-level participation; labour right, no technical element.

right: Right of the company to reasons for refusal of a pre-conversion certificate
addressee: competent authority of the departure Member State
description: If the certificate is refused, the authority must give reasons and may allow time to remedy; scrutiny within three months, with reasons notified for any delay (Art. 86m(11)).
exercise: Application can be made fully online (Art. 86m(4)).
quote: the competent authority shall not issue the pre‐conversion certificate and shall inform the company of the reasons for its decision
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Reasons for refusal of certificate; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right of employees to continuation of employment rights after a conversion
description: Rights and obligations from employment contracts and relationships pass to the converted company.
quote: arising from contracts of employment or from employment relationships and existing at the date on which the cross-border conversion takes effect shall be those of the converted company
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Employment rights pass to converted company; no technical element.

right: Right to claim damages from the independent expert (conversion)
rightholder: persons harmed by the expert report (e.g. members)
description: Member States must provide civil liability rules for the independent expert who reports on the conversion.
exercise: Under national liability rules.
quote: Member States shall lay down rules governing at least the civil liability of the independent expert responsible for drawing up the report referred to in Article 86f.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Civil liability of expert; damages claim, no technical element.

right: Right of affected share classes to a separate vote on a merger
description: Merger decisions require a separate vote by each class of shareholders whose rights are affected.
quote: Where there is more than one class of shares, the decision concerning a merger shall be subject to a separate vote by at least each class of shareholders whose rights are affected by the transaction.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Separate class vote on merger; no technical element.

right: Right of minority shareholders to require a general meeting of the acquiring company
rightholder: shareholders of the acquiring company holding the minimum percentage (max. 5%)
description: Where national law dispenses with the acquiring company's general meeting, shareholders holding up to 5% can require one to be called to decide on the merger.
quote: is entitled to require that a general meeting of the acquiring company be called to decide whether to approve the merger
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Minority request for a general meeting; no technical element.

right: Right of shareholders to inspect merger documents
description: Shareholders can inspect the draft terms, three years' accounts, interim statement and management and expert reports at the registered office.
exercise: At least one month before the general meeting; website alternative (Art. 97(4)).
quote: All shareholders shall be entitled to inspect at least the following documents at the registered office at least one month before the date fixed for the general meeting
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Inspection of documents at registered office; no technical element.

right: Right of shareholders to free copies of merger documents
description: Shareholders can obtain full or partial copies of the merger documents on request, free of charge (by e-mail if they consented).

quote: are entered in the register and are disclosed, in accordance with Article 16(3), within 10 working days from the date of completion of all formalities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Deadline for register entry and disclosure; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right of a company to correct register information before strike-off
rightholder: company subject to a registration-verification procedure
description: Where doubts exist about continued registration, the company must be given the possibility to correct the relevant information within a reasonable period.
exercise: Within a reasonable period set under national procedures.
quote: The rules governing those procedures shall include the possibility for a company to correct the relevant information within a reasonable period
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Opportunity to correct information before strike-off; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to register extracts compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallet
rightholder: any applicant for copies or extracts
description: Electronic copies and extracts supplied by the register must be usable in the European Digital Identity Wallet.
quote: electronic copies and extracts of the documents and information provided by the register are compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallet
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Electronic extracts must be wallet-compatible; result only usable by loading it into the wallet. Test: no.

right: Right to obtain copies of partnerships' register documents on application
description: The right to obtain (certified) copies from the register on application extends to the documents partnerships must disclose under Art. 14a.
exercise: Price not above administrative cost.
quote: This Article shall apply mutatis mutandis to copies of all or any part of the documents and information referred to in Article 14a.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Copies on application, paper or electronic; plain documents. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain an EU Company Certificate
description: Anyone can obtain from the register, on paper or electronically (also via BRIS), an EU Company Certificate accepted in all Member States as sufficient evidence of incorporation and key company data (Art. 16b(1)).
exercise: Application to the register; price not above administrative cost (Art. 16b(5)); exempt from legalisation (Art. 16d(2)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that the EU Company Certificate can be obtained from the register upon an application submitted to the register by electronic or by paper means.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Certificate obtainable by paper or electronic application; plain company data. Test: yes.

right: Right of a company to its own EU Company Certificate free of charge
rightholder: each company or partnership listed in Annexes II and IIB
description: Each company can obtain its electronic EU Company Certificate free of charge, at least once per calendar year.
exercise: Free unless serious prejudice to register financing, but always once per year.
quote: In any case, each company shall be able to obtain its EU Company Certificate free of charge at least once per calendar year.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Free electronic certificate is a pricing rule; content is plain company data and a paper version exists. Test: yes.

right: Right to use a digital EU power of attorney accepted across Member States
rightholder: companies and partnerships listed in Annexes II and IIB
addressee: Member States / authorities in other Member States
description: Companies can authorise a representative for cross-border company-law procedures with a digital EU power of attorney, which must be accepted as evidence of the representative's authority.
exercise: Drawn up under national requirements with identity/capacity verification; authenticated by trust services and wallet-compatible.
quote: companies listed in Annexes II and IIB can use a template for the digital EU power of attorney in accordance with this Article to authorise a person to represent the company
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Digital power of attorney authenticated by trust services and wallet-compatible, but representation could be granted on paper. Test conflicts.

right: Right to exemption from legalisation and apostille for register documents
rightholder: persons presenting register documents in another Member State
description: Certified copies and extracts from registers, EU Company Certificates, digital EU powers of attorney, pre-operation certificates and notarial/administrative acts in company procedures are exempt from legalisation and apostille.
quote: Where copies and extracts of documents and information provided and certified as true copies by a register, including certified translations, are to be presented in another Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Exemption from legalisation and apostille; formal requirement, no technical element.

right: Right to be notified when documents or certificates are not accepted
rightholder: persons who submitted register documents or an EU Company Certificate
addressee: requesting authority in another Member State
description: Documents may be rejected only if the issuing register does not confirm their authenticity, and the submitter must then be notified promptly.
exercise: Without undue delay and within 10 working days of the contact point's reply.
quote: the requesting authority shall notify those who submitted such documents and information or the EU Company Certificate of that decision without undue delay and no later than 10 working days
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Notice of non-acceptance of documents; administrative information, no technical element.

right: Right not to be required to provide unnecessary certified translations
rightholder: persons presenting register documents in another Member State
description: Certified translations of instruments of constitution and other register documents may be required only when justified by their purpose and strictly necessary.
quote: a certified translation is to be required only when justified by the purpose for which the document is to be used
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: No unnecessary certified translations; formal requirement, no technical element.

right: Right to free information on a company's average number of employees
description: The average number of employees, where required in financial statements, is added to the free-of-charge company information available through BRIS.
exercise: Member States may restrict free access to other Member States' authorities (Art. 19(4)).
quote: the average number of employees of the company during the financial year, where national law requires such information to be made available in the company’s financial statements
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Free access tied to the interconnected registers system, but the information is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to free-of-charge basic information on partnerships
description: Basic data on partnerships (name, form, seat, registration number/EUID, status, representatives, branches) are available free of charge via BRIS.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the following documents and information regarding companies listed in Annex IIB are available free of charge through the system of interconnection of registers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Free access tied to the interconnected registers system, but the information is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to free-of-charge information on groups of companies
description: Information on ultimate (or intermediate) parent companies and their subsidiaries is available free of charge through BRIS for groups preparing consolidated accounts.
quote: the following information is available free of charge through the system of interconnection of registers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Free access tied to the interconnected registers system, but the information is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Once-only right of companies registering a branch not to resubmit register documents
rightholder: company registering a branch in another Member State
addressee: register of the branch Member State
description: A company registering a branch cannot be asked for documents already in its own register; the branch register retrieves them via BRIS or the EU Company Certificate.
quote: that company is not subject to requests to provide documents and information relevant for the registration procedure that are available in the register
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Register retrieves documents via BRIS; holder merely is not asked to resubmit. Test: yes.

right: Right to free-of-charge information on branches of third-country companies
description: Basic data on branches of non-EU companies (names, legal form, governing law, register, branch address, representatives, identifier) are available free of charge via BRIS.
quote: Member States shall ensure that at least the following documents and information are available free of charge through the system of interconnection of registers:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; amends Directive (EU) 2017/1132.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25 (digital tools in company law)
tl_reason: Free access tied to the interconnected registers system, but the information is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right of economic operators to free information on national product rules
description: Economic operators can request, free of charge, information on national transposition and implementation of Union harmonisation legislation applicable to products.
exercise: Request under Art. 9 Regulation (EU) 2019/515 procedures.
quote: Member States shall put in place procedures for providing economic operators, at their request and free of charge, with information
tl_reason: Free information request to contact point. Test: yes.

right: Right to have accredited test reports and certificates taken into account
description: When economic operators present test reports or certificates from accredited conformity assessment bodies, authorities must take due account of them.
quote: market surveillance authorities shall take due account of those reports or certificates
tl_reason: Authorities consider test reports; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to have complaints on product risks or non-compliance followed up
description: Market surveillance authorities must have procedures to follow up complaints or reports on product risks or non-compliance.
exercise: Complaint or report to the national market surveillance authority.
quote: procedures for following up on complaints or reports on issues relating to risks or non-compliance
tl_reason: Complaint to market surveillance authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Protection of professional and commercial secrecy and personal data
rightholder: economic operators and other persons whose information is held
description: Market surveillance authorities must respect confidentiality, professional and commercial secrecy and protect personal data.
quote: Market surveillance authorities shall respect the principles of confidentiality and of professional and commercial secrecy and shall protect personal data in accordance with Union and national law.
tl_reason: Confidentiality duty of authorities; holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right to a reasoned market surveillance measure
description: Any market surveillance measure, decision or order must state the exact grounds on which it is based.
quote: Any measure, decision or order taken or made by market surveillance authorities pursuant to Union harmonisation legislation or this Regulation shall state the exact grounds on which it is based.
notes: Article titled 'Procedural rights of economic operators'.
tl_reason: Reasoned administrative measure. Test: yes.

right: Right to notification of measures and information on available remedies
description: Measures must be communicated without delay to the economic operator, together with the remedies available under national law and their time limits.
quote: shall at the same time be informed of the remedies available to it under the law of the Member State concerned and of the time limits to which those remedies are subject
notes: Article titled 'Procedural rights of economic operators'.
tl_reason: Notification of measures and remedies. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before a market surveillance measure
description: Before a measure is taken, the economic operator must be given at least 10 working days to be heard; in urgent cases it is heard as soon as possible afterwards and the measure is promptly reviewed.
exercise: Minimum 10 working days.
quote: the economic operator concerned shall be given the opportunity to be heard within an appropriate period of not less than 10 working days
notes: Article titled 'Procedural rights of economic operators'.
tl_reason: Right to be heard in administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to release of goods for free circulation if suspension is not maintained
rightholder: person declaring the product for release for free circulation
description: A product whose customs release was suspended must be released if, within four working days, market surveillance authorities have not requested that the suspension be maintained, or they approve release.
exercise: Other customs formalities must be fulfilled; release is not proof of conformity.
quote: that product shall be released for free circulation where all the other requirements and formalities relating to such a release have been fulfilled
tl_reason: Customs release rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to clear and easily available terms and conditions
description: Terms and conditions must be in plain language, available at all stages including pre-contract, and set out suspension and termination grounds, extra distribution channels and effects on IP rights.
quote: are easily available to business users at all stages of their commercial relationship with the provider of online intermediation services, including in the pre-contractual stage
notes: Non-compliant terms are void (Art. 3(3)).
tl_reason: Plain-language terms and conditions of an online service; information only. Test: yes.

right: Right to advance notice of changes to terms and conditions
description: Business users are notified on a durable medium of proposed changes, which cannot be implemented before a reasonable notice period of at least 15 days, or longer where adaptations are needed.
exercise: Notice on durable medium; minimum 15 days; exceptions in Art. 3(4).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall notify, on a durable medium, to the business users concerned any proposed changes of their terms and conditions.
tl_reason: Notice of changes on a durable medium is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the contract upon notified changes
description: A business user can terminate its contract before the notice period for proposed changes expires.
exercise: Termination takes effect within 15 days from receipt of the notice, unless a shorter contractual period applies.
quote: The business user concerned shall have the right to terminate the contract with the provider of online intermediation services before the expiry of the notice period.
tl_reason: Contract termination right; no technical element.

right: Right to waive the notice period
description: A business user can waive the notice period for changes to terms and conditions.
exercise: Written statement or clear affirmative action (submitting new goods or services counts, except where significant technical adjustments are required).
quote: The business user concerned may, either by means of a written statement or a clear affirmative action, waive the notice period
tl_reason: Waiver by written statement or conduct; contract right, no technical element.

right: Right to invoke nullity of non-compliant terms and changes
description: Terms that breach the transparency requirements and changes implemented without proper notice are null and void, which the business user can rely on.
quote: as well as changes to terms and conditions implemented by a provider of online intermediation services contrary to the provisions of paragraph 2 shall be null and void
notes: Also covers terms not complying with Art. 3(1).
tl_reason: Nullity of non-compliant terms; contract law, no technical element.

right: Right to have the business user's identity clearly visible
description: The platform must make the identity of the business user offering goods or services clearly visible.
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall ensure that the identity of the business user providing the goods or services on the online intermediation services is clearly visible.
tl_reason: Display of business identity on the platform; plain information, nothing to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to a statement of reasons for restriction or suspension
description: When the platform restricts or suspends a business user's goods or services, it must give a statement of reasons citing the specific facts, including third-party notifications, and the applicable ground.
exercise: On a durable medium, before or when the measure takes effect; exceptions in Art. 4(5) second subparagraph.
quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, prior to or at the time of the restriction or suspension taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium
tl_reason: Statement of reasons on a durable medium is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to 30 days' notice and reasons before termination
description: Before terminating all its services to a business user, the platform must give a statement of reasons at least 30 days in advance.
exercise: Durable medium; where the notice period does not apply (Art. 4(4)), statement of reasons without undue delay.
quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, at least 30 days prior to the termination taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium
tl_reason: Advance notice and reasons are plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to clarify the facts in the complaint process after restriction, suspension or termination
description: A business user affected by restriction, suspension or termination can clarify the facts and circumstances through the internal complaint-handling process.
exercise: Via the Art. 11 internal complaint-handling system.
quote: the provider of online intermediation services shall give the business user the opportunity to clarify the facts and circumstances in the framework of the internal complaint-handling process
tl_reason: Clarifying facts within the complaint process; non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Right to reinstatement, including data access, after a revoked decision
description: If the platform revokes a restriction, suspension or termination, it must reinstate the business user without undue delay, including access to data generated before the measure.
quote: it shall reinstate the business user without undue delay, including providing the business user with any access to personal or other data, or both
tl_reason: Reinstatement is a contractual remedy needing no mechanism, but it restores access to digital account data; digital object conflicts with test.

right: Right to ranking transparency
addressee: providers of online intermediation services and of online search engines
description: Platforms must state in their terms the main ranking parameters and their relative importance, search engines must publish a description, and both must disclose paid ranking possibilities.
exercise: In the terms and conditions (platforms) or a public description on the search engine; algorithms need not be disclosed (Art. 5(6)).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall set out in their terms and conditions the main parameters determining ranking and the reasons for the relative importance of those main parameters
tl_reason: Object is the ranking algorithm, but parameters are described in plain-language terms; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to inspect a third-party notice that led to delisting or re-ranking
description: If a search engine alters the ranking or delists a website following a third-party notification, the corporate website user can inspect the contents of that notification.
quote: the provider shall offer the possibility for the corporate website user to inspect the contents of the notification.
tl_reason: Inspection of a notification's contents; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on ancillary goods and services
description: Terms must describe ancillary goods and services offered to consumers and whether and how business users may offer their own.
exercise: In the terms and conditions.
quote: a description of whether and under which conditions the business user is also allowed to offer its own ancillary goods and services through the online intermediation services
tl_reason: Information in terms and conditions; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on differentiated treatment
addressee: providers of online intermediation services and of online search engines
description: Platforms and search engines must describe any more favourable treatment of their own or controlled offers, e.g. on data access, ranking, fees and access to services, and the reasons for it.
exercise: In the terms and conditions (platforms) or a description (search engines).
quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall include in their terms and conditions a description of any differentiated treatment which they give, or might give
tl_reason: Description of differentiated treatment; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Protection against retroactive changes to terms and conditions
description: Platforms may not impose retroactive changes to terms unless legally required or beneficial to business users.
quote: not impose retroactive changes to terms and conditions, except when they are required to respect a legal or regulatory obligation or when the retroactive changes are beneficial for the business users
tl_reason: Ban on retroactive contract changes; no technical element.

right: Right to information on termination conditions and post-contract data access
description: Terms must state how business users can terminate the relationship and what access to their information remains after the contract ends.
exercise: In the terms and conditions.
quote: ensure that their terms and conditions include information on the conditions under which business users can terminate the contractual relationship
tl_reason: Information in terms on termination and post-contract data access; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on access to data
description: Terms must describe what data the platform and the business user can access, under what conditions, and whether data are shared with third parties, including any possibility to opt out of that sharing.
exercise: In the terms and conditions.
quote: a description of the technical and contractual access, or absence thereof, of business users to any personal data or other data, or both
notes: Information duty only; does not itself grant data access.
tl_reason: Description of data access in terms; information only, grants no access. Test: yes.

right: Right to the grounds for restrictions on offering different conditions elsewhere
description: Where a platform restricts business users from offering better conditions through other channels, it must state the economic, commercial or legal grounds in its terms and make them public.
exercise: In the terms and conditions and publicly available.
quote: they shall include the grounds for that restriction in their terms and conditions and make those grounds easily available to the public
tl_reason: Grounds for restrictions stated in terms; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to an internal complaint-handling system
description: Business users can lodge complaints about non-compliance, technical issues or platform measures affecting them, and receive an individualised outcome in plain language.
exercise: Easily accessible and free of charge; handled swiftly within a reasonable time frame.
quote: It shall allow business users to lodge complaints directly with the provider concerned regarding any of the following issues:
notes: Not applicable to small enterprises (Art. 11(5)).
tl_reason: Internal complaint system not required to be electronic; outcome in plain language. Test: yes.

right: Right to mediation
description: Business users can use at least two impartial, affordable mediators named in the terms to try to settle disputes out of court, with the platform engaging in good faith and bearing a reasonable share of costs.
exercise: Voluntary mediation; does not affect the right to go to court at any time (Art. 12(5)).
quote: two or more mediators with which they are willing to engage to attempt to reach an agreement with business users on the settlement, out of court, of any disputes
notes: Not applicable to small enterprises (Art. 12(7)).
tl_reason: Mediation; no technical element.

right: Right to information on the functioning and effectiveness of mediation
description: On request, before or during mediation, the business user receives information on how mediation works and how effective it has been for the platform's activities.
exercise: Request to the provider.
quote: If requested by a business user, before entering into or during mediation, the provider of online intermediation services shall make available, to the business user, information on the functioning
tl_reason: Information on mediation on request; no technical element.

right: Right of representative organisations to bring injunction actions
rightholder: organisations and associations with a legitimate interest in representing business users or corporate website users
addressee: competent national courts (against platforms and search engines)
description: Qualifying representative organisations can sue in national courts to stop or prohibit non-compliance by platforms or search engines.
exercise: Organisation must be properly established, non-profit, act in the collective interest and be independent of platform financing (Art. 14(3)); may be designated by Member States (Art. 14(5)).
quote: shall have the right to take action before competent national courts in the Union, in accordance with the rules of the law of the Member State where the action is brought
notes: Public bodies also hold this right (Art. 14(4)) but are public authorities.
tl_reason: Injunction actions by representative organisations; no technical element.

right: Right of business users to bring individual court actions
description: Business users and corporate website users can sue in national courts on the basis of individual rights to stop non-compliance with the Regulation.
exercise: Under the procedural law of the Member State where the action is brought.
quote: the rights of business users and corporate website users to start any action before competent national courts
notes: Framed as a without-prejudice clause confirming individual actions.
tl_reason: Individual court actions; no technical element.

right: Right to rebut the gatekeeper presumption
description: An undertaking meeting the thresholds can submit substantiated arguments that it nevertheless does not satisfy the qualitative gatekeeper criteria.
exercise: With the notification under Art. 3(3); may lead to a market investigation under Art. 17(3).
quote: The undertaking providing core platform services may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets all the thresholds
tl_reason: Procedural rebuttal before the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right to request reconsideration of a designation decision
description: A designation decision can be reconsidered, amended or repealed on request where facts changed substantially or it relied on incomplete, incorrect or misleading information.
exercise: Request to the Commission.
quote: The Commission may, upon request or on its own initiative, reconsider, amend or repeal at any moment a designation decision adopted pursuant to Article 3
notes: The text does not specify who may make the request.
tl_reason: Reconsideration request to the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right to refuse or withdraw consent to combination and cross-use of personal data
description: Gatekeepers may process end users' data for ads based on third-party services, combine or cross-use data across services, or sign users in to combine data only after a specific choice and GDPR consent.
exercise: Specific choice presented; consent may be refused or withdrawn; after refusal or withdrawal, the request may not be repeated for the same purpose more than once a year.
quote: unless the end user has been presented with the specific choice and has given consent within the meaning of Article 4, point (11), and Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
notes: Gatekeeper obligations apply 6 months after the service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must present a specific choice in the interface; refusal or withdrawal is a single choice. Test: no. Consistency pass: no interface function required; refusing or a letter still works.

right: Right to offer different prices or conditions through other channels
description: Business users can offer the same products to end users via other intermediaries or their own sites at different prices or conditions (no parity clauses).
quote: The gatekeeper shall not prevent business users from offering the same products or services to end users through third-party online intermediation services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Commercial freedom (no parity clauses); no technical element.

right: Right to promote offers to and contract with end users outside the platform
description: Business users can, free of charge, communicate and promote offers to end users acquired on the platform or elsewhere and conclude contracts with them, whether or not via the gatekeeper's services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow business users, free of charge, to communicate and promote offers, including under different conditions, to end users acquired via its core platform service
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Commercial freedom to promote offers and contract; no technical element.

right: Right to access content acquired outside the platform via business-user apps
description: End users can access and use content, subscriptions and features through a business user's app on the gatekeeper's platform, even if acquired outside the platform.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow end users to access and use, through its core platform services, content, subscriptions, features or other items, by using the software application of a business user
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must permit using externally acquired content in business-user apps; usable only by operating apps across services. Test: no.

right: Right to raise non-compliance with public authorities and courts
description: Gatekeepers may not prevent or restrict business users or end users from raising non-compliance issues with any public authority, including national courts.
exercise: Lawful contractual complaint-handling mechanisms remain possible.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not directly or indirectly prevent or restrict business users or end users from raising any issue of non-compliance with the relevant Union or national law by the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Freedom to raise issues with authorities and courts; no technical element.

right: Right not to be required to use the gatekeeper's identification, browser engine or payment services
description: End users and business users cannot be forced to use the gatekeeper's identification service, web browser engine, payment service or in-app payment system when using business users' services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require end users to use, or business users to use, to offer, or to interoperate with, an identification service, a web browser engine or a payment service
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is software (ID, browser engine, payment), but protection is passive and alternatives depend on business users; ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right not to be required to subscribe to further core platform services
description: Access to one core platform service may not be made conditional on subscribing to or registering with another of the gatekeeper's core platform services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require business users or end users to subscribe to, or register with, any further core platform services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Ban on tying registration to further services; holder operates nothing, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of advertisers to daily price and fee information
rightholder: advertisers and third parties authorised by them
description: Advertisers can obtain, for each ad, the price and fees paid, the publisher's remuneration (subject to publisher consent, otherwise the daily average) and the metrics used.
exercise: Upon request; daily; free of charge.
quote: upon the advertiser’s request, with information on a daily basis free of charge, concerning each advertisement placed by the advertiser
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is per-ad transaction data, but the law only requires information on request without a technical format; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right of publishers to daily remuneration and fee information
rightholder: publishers and third parties authorised by them
description: Publishers can obtain, for each ad displayed, the remuneration received and fees paid, the advertiser's price (subject to consent, otherwise the daily average) and the metrics used.
exercise: Upon request; daily; free of charge.
quote: upon the publisher’s request, with free of charge information on a daily basis, concerning each advertisement displayed on the publisher’s inventory
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is per-ad remuneration data, but the law only requires information on request without a technical format; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Protection against the gatekeeper's use of business users' non-public data in competition
description: Gatekeepers may not use non-public data generated or provided by business users (and their customers) on the platform to compete against them.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not use, in competition with business users, any data that is not publicly available that is generated or provided by those business users
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Restriction on the gatekeeper's internal data use; holder operates nothing, no mechanism.

right: Right to un-install software applications
description: End users can easily un-install apps on the gatekeeper's operating system, except apps essential for the device or OS that cannot be offered standalone by third parties.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily un-install any software applications on the operating system of the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must technically enable uninstalling; exercised only through the device interface. Test: no.

right: Right to change default settings
description: End users can easily change default settings on the gatekeeper's operating system, virtual assistant and web browser that steer them to the gatekeeper's own products.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily change default settings on the operating system, virtual assistant and web browser of the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Default settings must be technically changeable; the right is a setting. Test: no.

right: Right to a choice screen for search engine, virtual assistant and browser
description: At first use, end users are prompted to choose their default online search engine, virtual assistant or web browser from a list of main available providers.
exercise: Prompt at first use of the listed search engine, virtual assistant or browser.
quote: prompting end users, at the moment of the end users’ first use of an online search engine, virtual assistant or web browser of the gatekeeper listed in the designation decision
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Choice screen in the interface; a single choice that cannot exist without it. Test: no.

right: Right to install and use third-party apps and app stores (sideloading) and set them as default
rightholder: end users; providers of software applications and app stores
description: Third-party apps and app stores can be installed, used and accessed outside the gatekeeper's store, and end users can easily set them as default when prompted.
exercise: Gatekeeper may take strictly necessary, proportionate and duly justified integrity and security measures.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable the installation and effective use of third-party software applications or software application stores
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must technically enable third-party apps and stores; holder installs and operates them. Test: no.

right: Right to non-discriminatory ranking (no self-preferencing)
rightholder: third parties offering services or products (business users)
description: Gatekeepers may not rank, index or crawl their own products more favourably than similar third-party products and must apply transparent, fair and non-discriminatory ranking conditions.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not treat more favourably, in ranking and related indexing and crawling, services and products offered by the gatekeeper itself than similar services or products of a third party.
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is ranking and indexing software, but protection is passive for business users; no mechanism to operate; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to switch between apps and services
description: Gatekeepers may not technically or otherwise restrict end users from switching between and subscribing to different apps and services, including internet access services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not restrict technically or otherwise the ability of end users to switch between, and subscribe to, different software applications and services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Switching apps and services is done only technically; gatekeeper must not technically restrict it. Test: no.

right: Right to interoperability with operating system and virtual assistant features
rightholder: providers of services and hardware; business users; alternative providers of ancillary services
description: Third-party service and hardware providers get free, effective interoperability with the same OS, hardware and software features available to the gatekeeper's own services and hardware.
exercise: Free of charge; gatekeeper may take strictly necessary and duly justified integrity measures.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow providers of services and providers of hardware, free of charge, effective interoperability with, and access for the purposes of interoperability to
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Interoperability with OS and hardware features requires technical integration, but holders are third-party providers, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right of advertisers and publishers to performance measuring tools and verification data
rightholder: advertisers, publishers and third parties authorised by them
description: Advertisers and publishers get access to the gatekeeper's performance measuring tools and the aggregated and non-aggregated data needed to verify ad inventory independently.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge.
quote: upon their request and free of charge, with access to the performance measuring tools of the gatekeeper and the data necessary for advertisers and publishers to carry out their own
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Access to measuring tools and verification data; result is data to check, unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to data portability
rightholder: end users and third parties authorised by them
description: End users can port data they provided or generated on the core platform service, with free tools and continuous, real-time access.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge; continuous and real-time access.
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide end users and third parties authorised by an end user, at their request and free of charge, with effective portability of data provided by the end user
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Continuous real-time portability through tools; data must be taken to another service. Test: no.

right: Right of business users to access data generated on the platform
rightholder: business users and third parties authorised by them
description: Business users get free, high-quality, continuous and real-time access to aggregated and non-aggregated data generated through their use of the platform and their customers' engagement.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge; personal data only where directly connected to the end users' use of the business user's offer and the end user opts in by consent.
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide business users and third parties authorised by a business user, at their request, free of charge, with effective, high-quality, continuous and real-time access to
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Continuous real-time data access implies API-based access by business users; unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right of rival search engines to access search data on FRAND terms
rightholder: third-party undertakings providing online search engines
description: Competing search engines can obtain ranking, query, click and view data from the gatekeeper's search engine on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.
exercise: Upon request; personal data anonymised.
quote: any third-party undertaking providing online search engines, at its request, with access on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms to ranking, query, click and view data
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Access to ranking, query, click and view data is technical, but holders are rival search engines, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to FRAND access conditions to app stores, search engines and social networks
description: Business users get fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory general conditions of access to the gatekeeper's app stores, search engines and social networks.
exercise: Published general conditions of access, assessed by the Commission.
quote: The gatekeeper shall apply fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory general conditions of access for business users to its software application stores
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: FRAND access conditions are commercial terms; no technical element.

right: Right to an alternative dispute settlement mechanism
description: The gatekeeper's published access conditions must include an alternative dispute settlement mechanism available to business users.
quote: For that purpose, the gatekeeper shall publish general conditions of access, including an alternative dispute settlement mechanism.
notes: Applies to app stores, search engines and social networks listed in the designation decision.
tl_reason: Alternative dispute settlement; no technical element.

right: Right to terminate a core platform service without undue difficulty
description: General termination conditions may not be disproportionate, and termination must be possible without undue difficulty.
quote: The gatekeeper shall ensure that the conditions of termination can be exercised without undue difficulty.
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Termination without undue difficulty; contract termination online, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to request interoperability of messaging services
rightholder: providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services offering or intending to offer services in the Union
description: Rival messaging providers can request interoperability with the gatekeeper's messaging service's basic functionalities, phased in over time, with the same security level including end-to-end encryption.
exercise: Request after the reference offer is published (Art. 7(4)); free of charge; reasonable requests met within 3 months; functionalities phased per Art. 7(2).
quote: any provider of number-independent interpersonal communications services offering or intending to offer such services in the Union may request interoperability
notes: Only messaging services listed in the designation decision.
tl_reason: Messaging interoperability requires technical integration, but holder is a competing provider, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to request an extension of interoperability deadlines
description: A gatekeeper can ask for an exceptional extension of interoperability deadlines where needed for effective interoperability and security.
exercise: Reasoned request to the Commission.
quote: The Commission may, exceptionally, upon a reasoned request by the gatekeeper, extend the time limits for compliance under paragraph 2 or 5
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's request for deadline extension; no technical element for a governed party.

right: Right of end users to choose whether to use interoperable messaging features
rightholder: end users of the gatekeeper's and the requesting provider's messaging services
description: End users remain free to decide whether to use the interoperable basic functionalities.
quote: shall remain free to decide whether to make use of the interoperable basic functionalities that may be provided by the gatekeeper pursuant to paragraph 1
notes: Only personal data strictly necessary for interoperability may be exchanged (Art. 7(8)).
tl_reason: End users choose in the interface whether to use interoperable features; the choice exists only as a software option. Test: no.

right: Right to request a compliance specification dialogue
description: A gatekeeper can ask the Commission to assess whether its intended or implemented measures for Articles 6 and 7 are effective.
exercise: Reasoned submission plus non-confidential version; Commission has discretion to engage.
quote: A gatekeeper may request the Commission to engage in a process to determine whether the measures that that gatekeeper intends to implement or has implemented
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's request for a specification dialogue; procedural.

right: Right to request suspension of an obligation on economic-viability grounds
description: A gatekeeper can request exceptional suspension of a specific obligation where compliance would endanger the economic viability of its EU operation, including provisional suspension in urgent cases.
exercise: Reasoned request; decision within 3 months of a complete request; reviewed annually.
quote: Where the gatekeeper demonstrates in a reasoned request that compliance with a specific obligation laid down in Article 5, 6 or 7
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's suspension request; procedural.

right: Right to request an exemption on public health or public security grounds
description: A gatekeeper can request an exemption from a specific obligation on public health or public security grounds, including provisional suspension in urgent cases.
exercise: Reasoned request; decision within 3 months of a complete request.
quote: The Commission may, acting on a reasoned request by a gatekeeper or on its own initiative, adopt an implementing act setting out its decision, to exempt that gatekeeper
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's exemption request; procedural.

right: Right of business users to obtain end-user consent directly on equal terms
description: Where consent is needed for compliance, the gatekeeper must let business users obtain it directly (or provide anonymised data) and may not make it more burdensome than for its own services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not make the obtaining of that consent by the business user more burdensome than for its own services.
tl_reason: Business freedom to obtain consent on equal terms; market-access rule, holder a business.

right: Right not to be penalised or manipulated for exercising DMA rights and choices
description: Gatekeepers may not degrade service conditions or quality for users exercising their DMA rights or choices, or make exercising them unduly difficult, including through non-neutral choices or manipulative interface design.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not degrade the conditions or quality of any of the core platform services provided to business users or end users who avail themselves of the rights or choices laid down
tl_reason: Object is service quality and choice-interface design, but protection is passive; holder operates nothing; ability criterion fails.

right: Right of interested third parties to comment on preliminary findings, remedies and commitments
description: Interested third parties can comment on the Commission's published non-confidential summaries of envisaged remedies and commitments (also of specification measures under Art. 8(6)).
exercise: Comments within the reasonable timeframe set by the Commission.
quote: Interested third parties may submit their comments within a reasonable timeframe which shall be set by the Commission.
notes: Equivalent comment opportunity in specification proceedings (Art. 8(6)).
tl_reason: Comments in Commission proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to inform authorities about gatekeeper practices
rightholder: any third party, including business users, competitors, end users and their representatives
addressee: national competent authority or the Commission
description: Anyone can inform the national competent authority or the Commission about gatekeeper practices within the Regulation's scope.
exercise: Information to the national authority or directly to the Commission; authorities have full discretion and no duty to follow up (Art. 27(2)).
quote: may inform the national competent authority of the Member State, enforcing the rules referred to in Article 1(6), or the Commission directly, about any practice or behaviour by gatekeepers
notes: No enforceable follow-up.
tl_reason: Informing authorities by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard
rightholder: gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned
description: Before key decisions (specification, suspension, exemption, market investigations, interim measures, commitments, non-compliance, fines), the party concerned can comment on preliminary findings and envisaged measures.
exercise: Written observations within the time limit set in the preliminary findings, at least 14 days; decisions may rely only on objections the party could comment on.
quote: the Commission shall give the gatekeeper or undertaking or association of undertakings concerned the opportunity of being heard on:
tl_reason: Right to be heard before the Commission; procedural.

right: Rights of defence and right of access to the Commission's file
rightholder: gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned
description: The party concerned has full rights of defence and may access the Commission's file under terms of disclosure, excluding business secrets of others, confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Access under terms of disclosure; disputes settled by Commission decision.
quote: The gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned shall be entitled to have access to the Commission's file under terms of disclosure
tl_reason: Rights of defence and file access; procedural.

right: Right to bring representative actions for consumers
addressee: national courts or administrative authorities (against gatekeepers)
description: Qualified entities can bring representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive against gatekeeper infringements that harm consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements by gatekeepers of provisions of this Regulation that harm or may harm the collective interests
notes: Cross-reference extending Directive 2020/1828 (see also Art. 52).
tl_reason: Representative actions by qualified entities; no technical element.

right: Right to report breaches with whistleblower protection
description: Persons who report breaches of the DMA enjoy the reporting channels and protection against retaliation of the Whistleblower Directive.
exercise: Under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of all breaches of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such breaches.
notes: Cross-reference extending Directive 2019/1937 (see also Art. 51).
tl_reason: Whistleblower reporting channels and protection; no technical element.

right: Right to have Commission decisions reviewed by the Court of Justice
rightholder: undertakings subject to Commission decisions (gatekeepers and others)
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Undertakings can challenge Commission decisions before the Court of Justice, which has unlimited jurisdiction over fines and periodic penalty payments and may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU (Arts 261 and 263 TFEU).
quote: the Court of Justice has unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions by which the Commission has imposed fines or periodic penalty payments
notes: Arts 21(3) and 23(6) expressly require information decisions and inspection decisions to indicate 'the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice'.
tl_reason: Court review of Commission decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to offer commitments
description: An undertaking under investigation can offer commitments (including repayment of the subsidy with interest, Art. 7(6)) that, if accepted, are made binding instead of imposed redressive measures.
exercise: Commitments must fully and effectively remedy the distortion; in concentrations offering commitments extends the review period by 15 working days (Art. 24(1)(b)).
quote: The Commission may accept commitments offered by the undertaking under investigation where such commitments fully and effectively remedy the distortion in the internal market.
tl_reason: Offering commitments in investigation; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the opening or closure of an investigation
description: The undertaking under investigation must be informed of a decision to open an in-depth investigation, and of the closure of a preliminary review (Art. 10(4)).
exercise: In public procurement cases the economic operator is informed without delay (Art. 30(3)).
quote: inform the undertaking under investigation;
tl_reason: Being informed of investigation steps; plain notice. Test: yes.

right: Right to refuse to be interviewed
description: The Commission may interview natural or legal persons only if they consent to be interviewed.
quote: The Commission may interview a natural or legal person who consents to be interviewed for the purpose of collecting information relating to the subject matter of an investigation.
tl_reason: Consent to interview in competition-type investigation. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to have an inspection decision reviewed by the Court of Justice
rightholder: undertakings and associations of undertakings subject to inspection
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: An undertaking subject to an inspection decision can challenge it before the Court of Justice under Art. 263 TFEU; the decision must state this right.
exercise: Annulment action under Art. 263 TFEU.
quote: stating the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice pursuant to Article 263 TFEU.
tl_reason: Annulment action before CJEU. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a final two-week time limit before fines for missing information
description: Before fining an undertaking for incomplete or late information, the Commission must set a final two-week deadline to supply the missing information.
quote: the Commission shall set a final time limit of two weeks to receive the missing information from the undertaking or from the association of undertakings.
tl_reason: Procedural deadline before fines. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to notify a concentration early on the basis of good-faith intention
rightholder: undertakings concerned in a proposed concentration
description: Parties may notify a proposed concentration before signing, when they demonstrate a good-faith intention to conclude an agreement or have announced a public bid.
exercise: Notification to the Commission.
quote: The undertakings concerned may also notify the proposed concentration when they demonstrate to the Commission a good faith intention to conclude an agreement
tl_reason: Early merger notification; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a derogation from the standstill obligation
rightholder: undertakings concerned by a notifiable concentration
description: Undertakings can ask the Commission for a derogation from the prohibition on implementing a notified concentration before clearance.
exercise: Reasoned request at any time, before notification or after the transaction; may be subject to conditions.
quote: The Commission may, upon request, grant a derogation from the obligations laid down in paragraphs 1 or 2.
tl_reason: Reasoned request for derogation; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to request an extension of the in-depth investigation period
rightholder: undertakings concerned by a notified concentration
description: The parties can obtain an extension of the 90-working-day in-depth review period by request, which the Commission must grant.
exercise: One request only, within 15 working days of the opening of the in-depth investigation; total extensions max 20 working days.
quote: The time limits provided for in paragraph 1, point (b) of this Article shall be extended if the undertakings concerned make a request to that effect
tl_reason: Request to extend review period. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to implement a concentration if the Commission misses the decision deadline
rightholder: undertakings concerned by a notified concentration
description: If the Commission does not adopt a decision within the in-depth review time limit, the parties may implement the concentration.
quote: If the Commission does not adopt a decision within that time limit, the undertakings concerned shall be allowed to implement the concentration.
tl_reason: Implementation after missed deadline; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to complete an incomplete procurement notification
rightholder: economic operators participating in public procurement procedures
description: Before a tender is declared irregular for an incomplete notification, the economic operator is told of the findings and given 10 working days to complete it.
exercise: 10 working days from the Commission's request.
quote: request that the economic operator completes its content within 10 working days
tl_reason: Completing procurement notification within deadline. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to report suspected foreign subsidies or false declarations in procurement
description: Any natural or legal person may report to the Commission information on distortive foreign subsidies and suspicions of false declarations in public procurement procedures.
exercise: Report to the Commission; no obligation on the Commission to act.
quote: Other legal or natural persons may report to the Commission any information relating to foreign subsidies distorting the internal market
tl_reason: Reporting information to the Commission by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Protection against unequal treatment in procurement because of an FSR investigation
rightholder: economic operators involved in a public procurement procedure
description: Economic operators under FSR investigation must not be treated by contracting authorities contrary to the principles of proportionality, non-discrimination, equal treatment and transparency.
exercise: Enforceable through national procurement review procedures.
quote: shall not result in the contracting authority or the contracting entity treating the economic operators concerned in a way that is contrary to those principles.
tl_reason: Equal treatment in procurement. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit information on distortive foreign subsidies
rightholder: natural or legal persons or associations
description: Any person or association may give the Commission information about foreign subsidies that may distort the internal market; the Commission may use it to open a review or request a notification.
exercise: Submission to the Commission; acts as an informal complaint (see also Art. 9(1)).
quote: A natural or legal person or association may communicate to the Commission any information it may have about foreign subsidies that may distort the internal market.
tl_reason: Submitting information to the Commission; informal complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right of interested persons to submit views on an in-depth investigation
description: When an in-depth investigation is opened, a summary notice is published inviting any natural or legal person to express their views in writing.
exercise: Written views within the period set in the notice published in the Official Journal (Art. 10(3)(d)).
quote: allowing any natural or legal person, Member States or the third country that granted the foreign subsidy, to express their views
tl_reason: Written views in an investigation. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to notification of decisions and to flag confidential information
rightholder: undertakings or associations of undertakings to which a decision is addressed
description: Decisions must be notified to the addressee without delay, and the addressee can indicate which information in the decision it considers confidential before publication.
quote: shall give that undertaking or association of undertakings the opportunity to indicate to the Commission which information in the decision it considers to be confidential
tl_reason: Notification of decision and confidentiality flagging; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive a copy of a decision prohibiting a contract award
rightholder: economic operator to which the award of a contract is prohibited
description: Where a decision prohibiting award or declaring a tender irregular is addressed to the contracting authority, the affected economic operator receives a copy.
quote: The Commission shall provide the economic operator to which the award of the contract is prohibited with a copy of that decision.
tl_reason: Receiving copy of a decision; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard (submit observations) before adverse decisions
description: Before decisions on redressive measures, commitments, interim measures, fines, revocation, concentrations or procurement, the undertaking can submit observations; decisions may rest only on grounds it could comment on.
exercise: For interim measures, the hearing may follow the decision as soon as possible (Art. 42(2)).
quote: give the undertaking under investigation the opportunity to submit observations on the grounds on which the Commission intends to adopt its decision
tl_reason: Right to be heard; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to the Commission's file
description: To exercise its right to be heard, the undertaking under investigation is entitled to access the Commission's file, excluding confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Subject to protection of business secrets; disclosure terms may be agreed or imposed by the Commission.
quote: the undertaking under investigation shall be entitled to have access to the file of the Commission
tl_reason: Access to Commission file in proceedings; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to judicial review of fines with unlimited jurisdiction
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Undertakings can challenge fines and periodic penalty payments before the Court of Justice, which may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU (Art. 261 TFEU).
quote: the Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions by which the Commission has imposed fines or periodic penalty payments
tl_reason: Judicial review of fines. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Exclusive right to authorise communication to the public by satellite
rightholder: authors (incl. principal director of films, Art. 1(5))
description: Authorise satellite broadcasts of copyright works.
exercise: Authorisation only by agreement (Art. 3(1)); act located in the uplink Member State (Art. 1(2)(b)); exercisable against uplink operator or commissioning broadcaster for third-country uplinks (Art. 1(2)(d)).
quote: Member States shall provide an exclusive right for the author to authorize the communication to the public by satellite of copyright works
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Exclusive authors' right over satellite broadcasting, authorised by agreement; IP right, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Unrepresented rightholder's right to opt out of extended collective agreements
rightholder: rightholders not represented by the collecting society
description: Exclude at any time the extension of a collective satellite-broadcasting agreement to one's works and exercise rights individually or collectively.
exercise: Not for cinematographic works (Art. 3(3)).
quote: the unrepresented rightholder shall, at any time, have the possibility of excluding the extension of the collective agreement to his works
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option (extended collective agreements).
tl_reason: Opt-out from extended collective agreement by notice to collecting society; no technical mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Related rights for satellite communication
description: Enjoy for satellite broadcasting the rental/lending-directive related rights (fixation, broadcasting/communication incl. equitable remuneration for phonograms, distribution).
exercise: Via Directive 92/100/EEC (now 2006/115/EC).
quote: the rights of performers, phonogram producers and broadcasting organizations shall be protected in accordance with the provisions of Articles 6, 7, 8 and 10 of Directive 92/100/EEC.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Related rights for satellite broadcasting; exclusive IP and remuneration rights, no technical element. Test: yes.
