right: Co-production exclusivity holder's consent right for satellite broadcasts
rightholder: co-producer or assignee holding (language) exclusivity under a pre-1995 co-production agreement
description: Satellite broadcasting authorised by another co-producer requires the exclusivity holder's prior consent where it would prejudice that exclusivity.
quote: shall require the prior consent of the holder of that exclusivity, whether co-producer or assignee.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Transitional provision.
tl_reason: Co-producer's prior consent to satellite broadcasts; contractual/IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Cable retransmission right (mandatory collective exercise)
rightholder: copyright owners and holders of related rights
description: Grant or refuse authorisation for cable retransmission of programmes from other Member States, exercised through a collecting society.
exercise: Only via collecting society; broadcasters exercise own rights individually (Art. 10).
quote: the right of copyright owners and holders or related rights to grant or refuse authorization to a cable operator for a cable retransmission may be exercised only through a collecting society
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Cable retransmission right exercised only via collecting society; IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Non-member rightholder's right to claim cable retransmission proceeds
rightholder: rightholders who have not mandated a collecting society
description: Have the same rights as members under the agreement with the cable operator, choose which collecting society is deemed mandated, and claim those rights within at least 3 years.
quote: he shall be able to claim those rights within a period, to be fixed by the Member State concerned, which shall not be shorter than three years from the date of the cable retransmission
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Claim to retransmission proceeds from deemed-mandated society; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to call upon mediators in cable retransmission negotiations
rightholder: parties to cable retransmission negotiations (collecting societies, broadcasters, cable operators)
description: Request mediation where no agreement on cable retransmission authorisation is concluded.
exercise: Mediators may propose terms, deemed accepted absent objection within 3 months (Art. 11(3)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that either party may call upon the assistance of one or more mediators.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Mediation in cable retransmission negotiations; dispute procedure between organisations, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to good-faith negotiations on cable retransmission
addressee: other negotiating party (via civil or administrative law)
description: Have counterparties enter and conduct negotiations in good faith and not hinder them without valid justification.
exercise: Enforced by civil or administrative law.
quote: the parties enter and conduct negotiations regarding authorization for cable retransmission in good faith and do not prevent or hinder negotiation without valid justification.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Good-faith negotiation duty between organisations; market right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Reproduction right
rightholder: authors; performers; phonogram producers; film producers; broadcasting organisations
description: Authorise or prohibit direct or indirect, temporary or permanent reproduction of works and other protected subject matter.
exercise: Subject to the exceptions in Art. 5; remedies under Art. 8.
quote: Member States shall provide for the exclusive right to authorise or prohibit direct or indirect, temporary or permanent reproduction by any means and in any form, in whole or in part:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Exclusive reproduction right; IP right enforced via remedies, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right of communication to the public (authors)
description: Authorise or prohibit any communication to the public of works, including on-demand making available online.
exercise: Not exhausted by any act of communication (Art. 3(3)).
quote: Member States shall provide authors with the exclusive right to authorise or prohibit any communication to the public of their works
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Exclusive communication/making-available right; online topic but plain IP right, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Making-available right (related rightholders)
rightholder: performers; phonogram producers; film producers; broadcasting organisations
description: Authorise or prohibit the on-demand making available to the public of fixations, phonograms, films and broadcasts.
exercise: Not exhausted (Art. 3(3)).
quote: Member States shall provide for the exclusive right to authorise or prohibit the making available to the public, by wire or wireless means
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Exclusive making-available right of related rightholders; IP right, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Distribution right
description: Authorise or prohibit any form of distribution to the public of the original or copies of works.
exercise: Exhausted by first sale/transfer in the EU by or with consent of the rightholder (Art. 4(2)).
quote: Member States shall provide for authors, in respect of the original of their works or of copies thereof, the exclusive right to authorise or prohibit any form of distribution
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Exclusive distribution right; IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to fair compensation for private copying (and reprography)
addressee: Member State (levy/compensation scheme); persons making or enabling copies
description: Receive fair compensation where a Member State allows private copying (5(2)(b)), reprography (5(2)(a)) or copying by social institutions (5(2)(e)).
exercise: Usually via levy schemes administered by collecting societies; takes account of technological measures.
quote: on condition that the rightholders receive fair compensation which takes account of the application or nonapplication of technological measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Arises only if the Member State adopts the exception (Member-State option).
tl_reason: Fair compensation via levy schemes; remuneration right, no technical element for holder. Test: yes.

right: Legal protection against circumvention of technological measures
addressee: persons circumventing or trafficking in circumvention tools (via national law)
description: Take action against knowing circumvention of effective technological protection measures and against trafficking in circumvention devices or services (Art. 6(2)).
exercise: Damages, injunction and seizure of devices (Art. 8(2)).
quote: Member States shall provide adequate legal protection against the circumvention of any effective technological measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Protection exists only for effective technological measures the holder applies (technical, constitutive), but holder is the rightholder, not the governed party; enforced in court.

right: Exception beneficiaries' right to the means to benefit from exceptions despite technological measures
rightholder: beneficiaries of exceptions in Art. 5(2)(a),(c),(d),(e) and 5(3)(a),(b),(e) with legal access (e.g. libraries, schools, persons with disabilities)
description: Obtain from rightholders the means needed to benefit from certain exceptions where technological measures would otherwise prevent it.
exercise: Only absent voluntary measures; Member-State option for private copying (2nd subpara); not for on-demand services on agreed contractual terms (4th subpara).
quote: Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that rightholders make available to the beneficiary of an exception or limitation provided for in national law
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rightholders must provide means to bypass TPMs (technical), but exercise runs through Member State measures, means may be non-technical, beneficiaries mostly institutions.

right: Legal protection of rights-management information
addressee: persons removing/altering RMI or distributing works with altered RMI
description: Take action against knowing removal or alteration of electronic rights-management information and distribution of works whose RMI was removed, where this facilitates infringement.
exercise: Remedies under Art. 8.
quote: Member States shall provide for adequate legal protection against any person knowingly performing without authority any of the following acts:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Protection presupposes electronic rights-management information the holder attaches (technical), but holder is the rightholder, not governed party; enforced via court remedies.

right: Right to sue for damages, injunction and seizure
rightholder: rightholders whose interests are affected by infringing activity
description: Bring an action for damages and/or apply for an injunction and seizure of infringing material and circumvention devices.
exercise: Before courts of the Member State where the infringing activity takes place.
quote: rightholders whose interests are affected by an infringing activity carried out on its territory can bring an action for damages and/or apply for an injunction
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Action for damages, injunction and seizure; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for an injunction against intermediaries
addressee: national courts; intermediaries whose services are used to infringe
description: Apply for injunctions against intermediaries (e.g. ISPs, hosts) whose services are used by third parties to infringe copyright or related rights.
quote: Member States shall ensure that rightholders are in a position to apply for an injunction against intermediaries whose services are used by a third party to infringe a copyright or related right.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court injunction against intermediaries; digital topic only, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Freedom of reception and retransmission of audiovisual media services
rightholder: viewers and media service providers from other Member States
description: Member States must ensure freedom of reception and must not restrict retransmission of audiovisual media services from other Member States in the coordinated fields.
exercise: Derogations only under the conditions of Art. 3(2)-(5).
quote: Member States shall ensure freedom of reception and shall not restrict retransmissions on their territory of audiovisual media services from other Member States
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Freedom of reception owed by Member States; no mechanism or technical ability.

right: Right of defence before derogation measures restricting reception
description: Before a receiving Member State derogates from freedom of reception, the media service provider must be notified in writing and given the opportunity to express its views on the alleged infringements.
exercise: Written notification of alleged infringements and intended measures; opportunity to be heard (urgent cases under Art. 3(5)).
quote: The Member State concerned shall respect the rights of defence of the media service provider concerned and, in particular, give that provider the opportunity to express its views
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rights of defence of media providers; procedural.

right: Right of defence in anti-circumvention proceedings
description: Before a Member State takes measures against a provider for circumventing stricter national rules, the provider must be heard on the alleged circumvention and the intended measures.
exercise: Opportunity to express views before measures are taken; Commission compatibility decision required.
quote: it has respected the rights of defence of the media service provider concerned and, in particular, has given that media service provider the opportunity to express its views
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rights of defence in anti-circumvention proceedings; procedural.

right: Right to information identifying the media service provider
description: Recipients have easy, direct and permanent access to the provider's name, geographical address, contact details including email or website, and the Member State and regulators with jurisdiction.
quote: a media service provider under its jurisdiction shall make easily, directly and permanently accessible to the recipients of a service at least the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option to require ownership information (Art. 5(2)). General, non-individualised information.
tl_reason: Provider identification details made accessible; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to progressively more accessible audiovisual media services
description: Audiovisual media services must be made continuously and progressively more accessible to persons with disabilities through proportionate measures.
quote: services provided by media service providers under their jurisdiction are made continuously and progressively more accessible to persons with disabilities through proportionate measures
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Accessibility relies on technical features (subtitles, audio description), but the duty is programmatic without a specific mechanism; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to complain to an accessibility point of contact
rightholder: any person (in particular persons with disabilities)
addressee: national online point of contact designated by the Member State
description: Each Member State provides a single, accessible online point of contact where persons can obtain information and lodge complaints on accessibility issues of audiovisual media services.
exercise: Online point of contact, accessible including to persons with disabilities.
quote: publicly available online point of contact for providing information and receiving complaints regarding any accessibility issues referred to in this Article
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Point of contact must be online, but complaint and information are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right to accessible emergency information
description: Emergency information, including public announcements in natural disasters, disseminated through audiovisual media services must be accessible to persons with disabilities.
quote: is provided in a manner which is accessible to persons with disabilities.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Accessible emergency information relies on technical accessibility features, but the result is plain information; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to consent to commercial overlays or modification of services
addressee: third parties (e.g. platforms, device and interface providers), via Member State measures
description: Audiovisual media services may not be overlaid for commercial purposes or modified without the explicit consent of the media service provider.
exercise: Explicit consent of the provider required; Member States set details and exceptions.
quote: audiovisual media services provided by media service providers are not, without the explicit consent of those providers, overlaid for commercial purposes or modified
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Provider's consent to overlays is a commercial permission; holder operates no mechanism.

right: Right of rights holders to respect of agreed release windows for cinematographic works
description: Media service providers may not transmit cinematographic works outside the periods agreed with the rights holders.
quote: do not transmit cinematographic works outside periods agreed with the rights holders
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Respect of agreed release windows; IP and contract matter, no technical element.

right: Right of access to events of high interest for short news reports
addressee: broadcasters holding exclusive rights / Member States
description: Any EU broadcaster can access events of high public interest broadcast exclusively by another broadcaster on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms, freely choosing short extracts for general news programmes.
exercise: Seek access from the exclusive broadcaster (or a same-country rights holder, Art. 15(2)); source identification; use only in general news programmes; any compensation capped at additional costs directly incurred (Art. 15(6)).
quote: any broadcaster established in the Union has access on a fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory basis to events of high interest to the public which are transmitted on an exclusive basis
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member States may set an equivalent system (Art. 15(4)).
tl_reason: Broadcasters' access to events for short reports; no technical element for a governed party.

right: Right of reply
rightholder: any natural or legal person, regardless of nationality, whose legitimate interests were damaged by incorrect facts in a TV programme
description: A person whose reputation or other legitimate interests were damaged by an assertion of incorrect facts in a television programme can obtain a reply or equivalent remedy.
exercise: Substantiated request; reply transmitted within a reasonable time and in a manner appropriate to the broadcast; no unreasonable conditions; may be refused on the grounds in Art. 28(4); procedure set by national law and usable by residents of other Member States.
quote: have been damaged by an assertion of incorrect facts in a television programme must have a right of reply or equivalent remedies
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Category chosen as closest fit (correction of incorrect facts).
tl_reason: Right of reply by substantiated request; no technical element.

right: Right to judicial review of right-of-reply disputes
description: Disputes over the exercise of the right of reply or equivalent remedies can be brought before a court for judicial review.
quote: Provision shall be made for procedures whereby disputes as to the exercise of the right of reply or the equivalent remedies can be subject to judicial review.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Judicial review of reply disputes; no technical element.

right: Right to report or flag harmful content on video-sharing platforms
description: Users can report or flag content harmful to minors, hate speech, terrorist, child sexual abuse or racist content to the platform through transparent and user-friendly mechanisms.
exercise: Flagging mechanism provided by the platform.
quote: establishing and operating transparent and user-friendly mechanisms for users of a video-sharing platform to report or flag to the video-sharing platform provider concerned the content
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; measures applied as appropriate and proportionate (Art. 28b(3)).
tl_reason: Flagging mechanism not required to be electronic; a plain report works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told what effect was given to a flag
description: Users receive an explanation of what effect the platform gave to their report or flag.
quote: establishing and operating systems through which video-sharing platform providers explain to users of video-sharing platforms what effect has been given to the reporting and flagging
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Explanation of the effect of a flag is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to rate content on video-sharing platforms
description: Users can rate potentially harmful content through easy-to-use rating systems.
quote: establishing and operating easy-to-use systems allowing users of video-sharing platforms to rate the content referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rating exists only as a platform function; without the rating system the right cannot be exercised. Test: no.

right: Right to parental control tools
description: End-users get parental control systems under their own control for content that may impair minors' development.
quote: providing for parental control systems that are under the control of the end-user with respect to content which may impair the physical, mental or moral development of minors
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Data of minors collected for this purpose may not be used commercially.
tl_reason: Parental control systems are settings the end-user configures; without them the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right to an internal complaint procedure on video-sharing platforms
description: Users can complain to the platform about the implementation of flagging, explanation, age verification, rating and parental control measures, and have complaints handled and resolved.
exercise: Transparent, easy-to-use and effective procedure operated by the platform.
quote: establishing and operating transparent, easy-to-use and effective procedures for the handling and resolution of users' complaints to the video-sharing platform provider
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Complaint procedure with the platform; plain complaint works, outcome plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to out-of-court redress against video-sharing platforms
description: Users can settle disputes with video-sharing platforms about the protective measures impartially out of court, without losing national legal protection.
quote: Member States shall ensure that out-of-court redress mechanisms are available for the settlement of disputes between users and video-sharing platform providers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Out-of-court redress; no technical element.

right: Right to assert rights before a court against video-sharing platforms
description: Users can enforce their rights relating to the platform's protective measures before a court.
quote: Member States shall ensure that users can assert their rights before a court in relation to video-sharing platform providers pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 3.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court action; no technical element.

right: Right of a regulator's head to a justified, pre-notified dismissal decision
rightholder: head or collegiate members of a national regulatory authority or body
description: Heads or board members of media regulators may be dismissed only if they no longer meet pre-set conditions, by a duly justified decision notified in advance and made public.
quote: A dismissal decision shall be duly justified, subject to prior notification and made available to the public.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Primarily an independence safeguard.
tl_reason: Dismissal safeguards for regulator heads; no technical element.

right: Right to appeal decisions of the national media regulator
rightholder: parties affected by decisions of the national regulatory authority (e.g. providers)
description: Persons affected by a decision of the national regulatory authority can appeal it to an independent appeal body, which may be a court.
exercise: Decision stands pending appeal unless interim measures are granted under national law.
quote: Member States shall ensure that effective appeal mechanisms exist at national level. The appeal body, which may be a court, shall be independent of the parties involved in the appeal.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Appeal against regulator decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to cross-border portability of paid online content services
addressee: provider of a paid online content service
description: Access and use a paid online content subscription while temporarily in another Member State in the same manner as at home (same content, devices, users, functionalities).
exercise: After residence verification (Art. 5); no additional charges (Art. 3(2)); provider may not reduce quality (Art. 3(3)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: shall enable a subscriber who is temporarily present in a Member State to access and use the online content service in the same manner as in the Member State of residence
tl_reason: Provider must enable cross-border access to the online content service; the right is the service's technical availability abroad. Without it, no exercise. Test: no.

right: Right to information on quality of delivery abroad
addressee: provider of a paid online content service
description: Be informed in advance about the quality of delivery of the service when used in another Member State.
exercise: Before providing the ported service, by adequate and proportionate means.
quote: provide the subscriber with information concerning the quality of delivery of the online content service provided in accordance with paragraph 1
tl_reason: Plain information on delivery quality given by adequate means before ported service; no technical handling. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' right to waive residence verification and to withdraw that waiver
rightholder: holders of copyright, related or other rights in the content
addressee: provider of the online content service
description: Authorise portability without residence verification and withdraw that authorisation on reasonable notice; contracts may not restrict withdrawal (Art. 5(5)).
exercise: Reasonable notice to the provider.
quote: shall be entitled to withdraw the authorisation given pursuant to the first subparagraph subject to giving reasonable notice to the provider.
tl_reason: Rightholders' authorisation and withdrawal by notice to provider; contractual/IP choice, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of opt-in portability for free services
addressee: provider of a free online content service
description: Be informed before the provider of a free service starts offering cross-border portability.
exercise: Only where the free service opts in (Art. 6(1)).
quote: The provider shall inform its subscribers, the relevant holders of copyright and related rights
tl_reason: Plain information that a free online service offers portability; delivered online, usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to authorise retransmission (mandatory collective exercise)
rightholder: holders of the exclusive right of communication to the public (other than broadcasters)
addressee: operators of retransmission services (IPTV, satellite, mobile etc.)
description: Grant or refuse authorisation for retransmissions of programmes from other Member States, exercised through a collective management organisation.
exercise: Only via CMO; broadcasters exercise own rights individually (Art. 5(1)).
quote: Acts of retransmission of programmes have to be authorised by the holders of the exclusive right of communication to the public.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Retransmission authorisation via collective management; IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Non-member rightholder's right to claim retransmission proceeds
rightholder: rightholders who have not transferred management to a CMO
description: Have the same rights and obligations as members under the CMO's retransmission agreement and claim them within at least 3 years.
quote: Member States shall ensure that a rightholder has the same rights and obligations resulting from an agreement between an operator of a retransmission service and a collective management organisation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Claim to retransmission proceeds from CMO; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to good-faith negotiations on retransmission
rightholder: broadcasting organisations and operators of retransmission services
description: Have negotiations on retransmission authorisation conducted in good faith.
quote: those negotiations are to be conducted in good faith.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Good-faith negotiation duty between broadcasters and operators; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to call upon mediators in retransmission negotiations
rightholder: CMOs, retransmission operators and broadcasting organisations
description: Request mediation where no retransmission agreement is concluded.
exercise: Per Art. 11 of Directive 93/83/EEC.
quote: Member States shall ensure that it is possible to call upon the assistance of one or more mediators
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Mediation in retransmission negotiations; dispute procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' authorisation right for direct injection
description: Require both the broadcaster and the signal distributor in a direct-injection chain to obtain their authorisation for the single act of communication to the public.
exercise: Member States may extend mandatory collective management (Art. 8(2)).
quote: shall be deemed to be participating in a single act of communication to the public in respect of which they shall obtain authorisation from rightholders.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Authorisation right for direct injection; IP right, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to carry out text and data mining for scientific research
rightholder: research organisations and cultural heritage institutions
description: Make reproductions and extractions of lawfully accessible works for text and data mining for scientific research, without authorisation.
exercise: Copies stored securely and retainable for research incl. verification (Art. 3(2)); rightholders may apply proportionate security measures (Art. 3(3)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: for reproductions and extractions made by research organisations and cultural heritage institutions in order to carry out, for the purposes of scientific research, text and data mining
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: TDM inherently requires software the holder runs, but no duty-bearer mechanism (mere copyright exception) and holder is a research organisation, not governed party.

right: Rightholders' right to reserve text and data mining (opt-out)
addressee: persons carrying out text and data mining
description: Exclude their works from the general TDM exception (Art. 4(1)) by an express reservation, e.g. machine-readable means for online content, so TDM then requires authorisation.
exercise: Reservation in an appropriate manner (machine-readable for online content).
quote: has not been expressly reserved by their rightholders in an appropriate manner, such as machine-readable means in the case of content made publicly available online
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Reservation for online content must be machine-readable and respected by TDM users; without it the opt-out has no effect. Test: no.

right: Right to use works digitally for illustration for teaching
rightholder: educational establishments, their teaching staff and pupils/students
description: Use works digitally, including cross-border, for illustration for teaching to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose.
exercise: Under the establishment's responsibility, on premises or via a secure electronic environment; source and author indicated; Member States may give priority to available licences (Art. 5(2)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: in order to allow the digital use of works and other subject matter for the sole purpose of illustration for teaching, to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose to be achieved
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Exception covers digital use via a secure electronic environment (technical), but holder runs it, no duty-bearer mechanism; holder is educational, not governed party.

right: Right to fair compensation for teaching uses
description: Receive fair compensation for digital teaching uses under Art. 5(1) where the Member State so provides.
quote: Member States may provide for fair compensation for rightholders for the use of their works or other subject matter pursuant to paragraph 1.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Fair compensation for teaching uses; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of cultural heritage institutions to make preservation copies
description: Make copies of works permanently in their collections, in any format or medium, to the extent necessary for preservation.
exercise: Contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: in order to allow cultural heritage institutions to make copies of any works or other subject matter that are permanently in their collections, in any format or medium, for purposes of preservation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Preservation copies in any format or medium; copyright exception, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Exception beneficiaries' right to the means to benefit from Arts 3-6 despite technological measures
rightholder: beneficiaries of the exceptions in Arts 3-6
description: Obtain the means needed to benefit from the TDM, teaching and preservation exceptions where technological measures would prevent it (Art. 6(4) InfoSoc applied).
exercise: Absent voluntary measures by rightholders.
quote: The first, third and fifth subparagraphs of Article 6(4) of Directive 2001/29/EC shall apply to Articles 3 to 6 of this Directive.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Means to bypass TPMs for TDM, teaching, preservation (technical), but via Member State measures, means unspecified, beneficiaries mostly institutions.

right: Rightholders' right to opt out of out-of-commerce works licensing and exception
addressee: collective management organisations; cultural heritage institutions
description: Exclude works at any time, easily and effectively, from extended collective licences or the exception for out-of-commerce works, generally or in specific cases, even after use has begun.
exercise: Information on the option on the EUIPO portal at least 6 months before use (Art. 10).
quote: Member States shall provide that all rightholders may, at any time, easily and effectively, exclude their works or other subject matter from the licensing mechanism set out in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Opt-out from out-of-commerce licensing by notice; EUIPO portal only informs; no technical mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right to opt out of extended collective licensing
rightholder: rightholders who have not mandated the CMO
description: Exclude works at any time, easily and effectively, from an extended collective licensing mechanism.
quote: rightholders who have not authorised the organisation granting the licence may at any time easily and effectively exclude their works or other subject matter from the licensing mechanism
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies where the Member State introduces extended collective licensing (Member-State option).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Opt-out from extended collective licensing by notice to CMO; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to use a negotiation mechanism for video-on-demand licensing
rightholder: parties seeking to conclude VoD licensing agreements (rightholders, VoD service providers)
addressee: impartial body or mediators designated by the Member State
description: Obtain assistance from an impartial body or mediators, including proposals, when facing difficulties licensing audiovisual works for VoD.
quote: may rely on the assistance of an impartial body or of mediators.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Assistance of impartial body or mediators for VoD licensing; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Press publishers' right for online uses
rightholder: publishers of press publications established in a Member State
description: Authorise or prohibit reproduction and making available of their press publications online by information society service providers.
exercise: Not for private/non-commercial use by individuals, hyperlinking, or individual words/very short extracts; expires 2 years after publication (Art. 15(4)).
quote: Member States shall provide publishers of press publications established in a Member State with the rights provided for in Article 2 and Article 3(2) of Directive 2001/29/EC
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Only press publications first published on or after 6 June 2019.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Press publishers' exclusive right for online uses; IP right on digital topic, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Authors' right to a share of press publishers' revenues
rightholder: authors of works incorporated in press publications
description: Receive an appropriate share of the revenues press publishers obtain from information society service providers.
quote: Member States shall provide that authors of works incorporated in a press publication receive an appropriate share of the revenues that press publishers receive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Share of publishers' revenues; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Publishers' claim to a share of compensation for uses under exceptions
rightholder: publishers to whom an author transferred or licensed a right
description: Be entitled to a share of compensation (e.g. private copying levies) for uses under exceptions to the transferred or licensed right.
quote: such a transfer or licence constitutes a sufficient legal basis for the publisher to be entitled to a share of the compensation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Publishers' share of compensation; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' authorisation right vis-à-vis online content-sharing service providers
rightholder: rightholders (authors and related rightholders under Art. 3 InfoSoc)
description: Require OCSSPs to obtain their authorisation (e.g. licence) to give the public access to works uploaded by users; licences also cover non-commercial users (Art. 17(2)).
exercise: Absent authorisation the OCSSP is liable unless it meets the best-efforts conditions of Art. 17(4).
quote: An online content-sharing service provider shall therefore obtain an authorisation from the rightholders referred to in Article 3(1) and (2) of Directive 2001/29/EC
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Authorisation (licence) right against content-sharing platforms; IP right, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' notice-and-takedown and staydown
description: Send a sufficiently substantiated notice to have works disabled or removed and future uploads prevented, and provide information so specific works are kept unavailable.
exercise: Requests must be duly justified (Art. 17(9)); lighter regime for new small OCSSPs (Art. 17(6)).
quote: acted expeditiously, upon receiving a sufficiently substantiated notice from the rightholders, to disable access to, or to remove from their websites, the notified works or other subject matter
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Substantiated notice to platform works by any means; filtering is platform technology, holder handles no technical output. Test: yes.

right: Users' right to rely on quotation and parody exceptions when uploading
description: Upload and share user-generated content relying on quotation, criticism, review, caricature, parody or pastiche; cooperation must not block non-infringing content.
exercise: Backed by complaint, out-of-court and judicial redress (Art. 17(9)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that users in each Member State are able to rely on any of the following existing exceptions or limitations when uploading and making available content generated by users
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory user right.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Right to upload via the platform's interface without non-infringing content being blocked by filters (software behaviour). Without the upload mechanism, no exercise. Test: no.

right: Rightholders' right to information from OCSSPs
description: Receive, on request, adequate information on how the OCSSP's practices under Art. 17(4) work and, where licensed, on the use of their content.
exercise: On request.
quote: Member States shall provide that online content-sharing service providers provide rightholders, at their request, with adequate information on the functioning of their practices
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Object is functioning of platform content-recognition practices (software behaviour), but plain request and plain answer suffice; holder is rightholder.

right: Users' right to a complaint and redress mechanism
description: Complain to the OCSSP about the disabling or removal of their uploaded content and have complaints processed without undue delay.
exercise: Rightholders must justify removal requests.
quote: online content-sharing service providers put in place an effective and expeditious complaint and redress mechanism that is available to users of their services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Platform must provide complaint mechanism over removed uploads (digital object), but channel not specified as electronic and a plain complaint works. Conflict: test partly yes.

right: Users' right to human review of removal decisions
description: Have decisions to disable access to or remove uploaded content reviewed by a human.
exercise: Within the complaint mechanism.
quote: decisions to disable access to or remove uploaded content shall be subject to human review
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Object is an often automated removal decision (software behaviour), but human review is requested plainly and the outcome is a plain decision. Conflict: digital object versus test yes.

right: Users' access to out-of-court redress
description: Settle disputes over removed content impartially through out-of-court mechanisms, without losing legal protection.
quote: Member States shall also ensure that out-of-court redress mechanisms are available for the settlement of disputes.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Out-of-court redress body for disputes; ordinary dispute procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Users' right of access to court to assert an exception
description: Go to a court or other judicial authority to assert the use of an exception or limitation.
quote: Member States shall ensure that users have access to a court or another relevant judicial authority to assert the use of an exception or limitation to copyright and related rights.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Access to court to assert an exception; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Users' right to be informed of exceptions in terms and conditions
description: Be informed in the OCSSP's terms and conditions that they may use works under exceptions and limitations.
quote: Online content-sharing service providers shall inform their users in their terms and conditions that they can use works and other subject matter under exceptions or limitations
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Information on exceptions in online terms and conditions; plain-language information, no technical handling. Test: yes.

right: Right to appropriate and proportionate remuneration
addressee: party to whom rights are licensed or transferred
description: Receive appropriate and proportionate remuneration when licensing or transferring exclusive exploitation rights.
exercise: Mechanisms set by Member States (Art. 18(2)); not for computer-program authors (Art. 23(2)).
quote: they are entitled to receive appropriate and proportionate remuneration.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Appropriate remuneration from licensees; remuneration/contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to regular information on exploitation and revenues
addressee: licensees/transferees or their successors in title
description: Receive at least annually up-to-date, relevant and comprehensive information on the exploitation of their works, revenues generated and remuneration due.
exercise: Proportionality limits (Art. 19(3)-(4)); collective agreements may apply (Art. 19(5)); not for CMOs (Art. 19(6)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 23(1)).
quote: authors and performers receive on a regular basis, at least once a year, and taking into account the specificities of each sector, up to date, relevant and comprehensive information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to licence/transfer agreements from 7 June 2022 (Art. 27).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Annual information on exploitation and revenues; plain reporting, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to additional information from sub-licensees
rightholder: authors and performers or their representatives
addressee: sub-licensees; first contractual counterpart (identity of sub-licensees)
description: On request, obtain additional information from sub-licensees where the first counterpart lacks it, and learn the sub-licensees' identity.
exercise: Request directly or via the contractual counterpart, as Member States provide.
quote: authors and performers or their representatives shall, at their request, receive from sub-licensees additional information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies from 7 June 2022 (Art. 27).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Additional information from sub-licensees on request; plain information, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Contract adjustment mechanism (bestseller clause)
rightholder: authors and performers or their representatives
addressee: contractual counterpart or its successors in title
description: Claim additional, appropriate and fair remuneration where the agreed remuneration is disproportionately low compared to subsequent revenues.
exercise: Absent comparable collective-bargaining mechanism; not against CMOs (Art. 20(2)); ADR available (Art. 21); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 23(1)).
quote: authors and performers or their representatives are entitled to claim additional, appropriate and fair remuneration from the party with whom they entered into a contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Contract adjustment claim for additional remuneration; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to alternative dispute resolution on transparency and contract adjustment
rightholder: authors and performers (and their representative organisations at their request)
description: Submit disputes on transparency (Art. 19) or contract adjustment (Art. 20) to a voluntary ADR procedure, which representative organisations may start at an author's request.
quote: disputes concerning the transparency obligation under Article 19 and the contract adjustment mechanism under Article 20 may be submitted to a voluntary, alternative dispute resolution procedure.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Voluntary ADR on transparency and contract adjustment; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of revocation for lack of exploitation
rightholder: authors and performers who licensed/transferred rights exclusively
description: Revoke in whole or part an exclusive licence or transfer, or end its exclusivity, where the work is not exploited.
exercise: After a reasonable time; notify the counterpart and set a deadline for exploitation (Art. 22(3)); excluded if lack of exploitation is remediable by the author (Art. 22(4)); derogation only via collective agreements (Art. 22(5)).
quote: the author or performer may revoke in whole or in part the licence or the transfer of rights where there is a lack of exploitation of that work or other protected subject matter.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Revocation of licence for non-exploitation by notice; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to opt for taxation of intra-Community acquisitions below the threshold
rightholder: taxable persons (exempt/flat-rate) and non-taxable legal persons
description: Persons whose intra-Community acquisitions are outside VAT because they are below the threshold may opt to have them taxed under the general scheme.
exercise: Option under national rules; covers at least two calendar years.
quote: Member States shall grant taxable persons and non-taxable legal persons eligible under point (b) of paragraph 1 the right to opt for the general scheme provided for in Article 2(1)(b)(i).
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Tax option under national rules; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to opt for destination-based taxation of cross-border B2C supplies below EUR 10 000
rightholder: taxable person making cross-border B2C distance sales or telecom/broadcasting/electronic services
description: Small suppliers below the EUR 10 000 EU-wide threshold may opt to apply the place-of-supply rules of the customer's Member State instead of taxing at origin.
exercise: Option binding for at least two calendar years.
quote: shall grant taxable persons carrying out supplies eligible under paragraph 1 the right to opt for the place of supply to be determined in accordance with point (a) of Article 33 and Article 58
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; replaced by Dir (EU) 2025/516 from 1 January 2027
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Place-of-supply tax option; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to reduce the taxable amount after cancellation, refusal, non-payment or price reduction
description: Where a transaction is cancelled or refused, remains unpaid, or the price is reduced after supply, the taxable amount (and VAT due) is reduced accordingly.
exercise: Under conditions set by Member States; Member States may derogate for non-payment (Art. 90(2)).
quote: In the case of cancellation, refusal or total or partial non-payment, or where the price is reduced after the supply takes place, the taxable amount shall be reduced accordingly
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; bad-debt relief may be excluded by Member State
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Reduction of taxable amount; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Option to tax otherwise exempt financial and real-estate transactions
description: Where a Member State allows it, taxable persons may opt to charge VAT on exempt financial services, supplies of old buildings and non-building land, and letting of immovable property (thereby gaining deduction rights).
exercise: Detailed rules and scope restrictions set by Member State.
quote: Member States may allow taxable persons a right of option for taxation in respect of the following transactions
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option (similar option under Art. 391 for derogating Member States)
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to tax exempt transactions; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: VAT exemption (tax-free shopping) for goods exported in travellers' personal luggage
rightholder: traveller not established in the Community
description: Non-EU resident travellers buying goods they carry out of the EU in personal luggage can have the supply exempted (typically via VAT refund), if goods leave within three months and the purchase exceeds EUR 175 (or a lower national limit).
exercise: Proof of export via invoice endorsed by the customs office of exit; identity document showing non-EU residence.
quote: Where the supply of goods referred to in point (b) of Article 146(1) relates to goods to be carried in the personal luggage of travellers, the exemption shall apply only if
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Tax-free export proven by customs-endorsed invoice; paper procedure, no technical mechanism.

right: Right to deduct input VAT
description: A taxable person may deduct from the VAT it owes the VAT paid or due on goods and services, intra-Community acquisitions and imports used for its taxed transactions.
exercise: Through the VAT return; must hold a valid invoice or import document (Art. 178); right arises when the tax becomes chargeable (Art. 167).
quote: the taxable person shall be entitled, in the Member State in which he carries out these transactions, to deduct the following from the VAT which he is liable to pay
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Substantive input VAT deduction claimed in the return; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to deduct input VAT for exempt-with-credit and foreign transactions
description: Input VAT is also deductible where goods and services are used for transactions abroad that would be deductible domestically, for exports and intra-Community supplies, and for certain exempt financial services to non-EU customers.
exercise: Via the VAT return.
quote: In addition to the deduction referred to in Article 168, the taxable person shall be entitled to deduct the VAT referred to therein
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Substantive input VAT deduction; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to a VAT refund for taxable persons established outside the EU
rightholder: taxable person not established in the Community
description: Non-EU businesses can obtain a refund of EU VAT incurred, under the Thirteenth Directive 86/560/EEC.
exercise: Application under Directive 86/560/EEC (reciprocity conditions may apply).
quote: VAT shall be refunded to taxable persons who are not established within the territory of the Community in accordance with the detailed implementing rules laid down in Directive 86/560/EEC.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Refund under Directive 86/560/EEC by ordinary application; no technical mechanism.

right: Right of occasional sellers of new means of transport to deduct VAT
rightholder: any person regarded as taxable person for occasional supply of a new means of transport
description: A person (often a private individual) who occasionally sells a new vehicle, vessel or aircraft to another Member State may deduct the VAT paid on its purchase, up to the VAT that would be due if the supply were not exempt.
exercise: Right arises and is exercised only at the time of the supply.
quote: be entitled to deduct the VAT included in the purchase price or paid in respect of the importation or the intra-Community acquisition of this means of transport
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Deduction for occasional seller of a new means of transport; tax right, no technical element.

right: Refund or carry-forward of excess input VAT
description: Where deductions exceed VAT due in a period, the excess is refunded or carried forward to the next period.
exercise: Conditions set by Member States; may be refused if insignificant.
quote: the Member States may, in accordance with conditions which they shall determine, either make a refund or carry the excess forward to the following period
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Refund or carry-forward of excess VAT; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Adjustment of deductions that were lower than entitled
description: The initial deduction is adjusted where it was higher or lower than the taxable person's entitlement, allowing correction of under-deductions.
exercise: Detailed rules set by Member States (Art. 186).
quote: The initial deduction shall be adjusted where it is higher or lower than that to which the taxable person was entitled.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Adjustment of deductions; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Right to be identified by an individual VAT number
rightholder: taxable persons and non-taxable legal persons listed
description: Member States must allocate an individual VAT identification number to taxable persons making deductible supplies, intra-Community acquisitions or cross-border reverse-charge services, and to persons opting under Art. 3(3).
exercise: Registration with the national tax authority.
quote: Member States shall take the measures necessary to ensure that the following persons are identified by means of an individual number
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Allocation of a VAT identification number; administrative registration, no technical mechanism.

right: Right of business customers to receive an invoice
rightholder: customer that is a taxable person or non-taxable legal person
description: Suppliers must ensure an invoice is issued for supplies and advance payments to other taxable persons and non-taxable legal persons, enabling the customer's deduction.
quote: Every taxable person shall ensure that, in respect of the following, an invoice is issued, either by himself or by his customer or, in his name and on his behalf, by a third party
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Right to receive an invoice, paper or electronic; no technical mechanism required.

right: Option to issue simplified invoices
description: Taxable persons may issue simplified invoices for amounts up to EUR 100, for amending documents, and where they benefit from the small-enterprise exemption.
exercise: Not for intra-Community supplies or certain reverse-charge cases (Art. 220a(2)).
quote: Member States shall allow taxable persons to issue a simplified invoice in any of the following cases
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to issue simplified invoices; invoicing formality, no technical element.

right: Option to issue summary invoices
description: Taxable persons may issue one summary invoice for several supplies whose VAT becomes chargeable in the same calendar month.
quote: Member States shall allow taxable persons to issue summary invoices which detail several separate supplies of goods or services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; replaced by Dir (EU) 2025/516 from 1 July 2030
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to issue summary invoices; invoicing formality, no technical element.

right: Option of self-billing by the customer
description: Customers may draw up invoices on behalf of the supplier where both parties agree in advance and the supplier can accept each invoice.
exercise: Prior agreement and acceptance procedure.
quote: Invoices may be drawn up by the customer in respect of the supply to him, by a taxable person, of goods or services, where there is a prior agreement between the two parties
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Self-billing by prior agreement; contractual invoicing arrangement, no technical element.

right: Recipient's right to accept or refuse electronic invoices
description: Electronic invoices may be used only if the recipient accepts them; a Member State that mandates domestic e-invoicing may remove this consent requirement for recipients established in its territory.
quote: The use of an electronic invoice shall be subject to acceptance by the recipient.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; second paragraph (derogation) inserted by Dir (EU) 2025/516; article replaced from 1 July 2030
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Right to refuse electronic invoices; refusal is a plain declaration and paper invoices need no technical means. Technology is the topic, not a condition. Test: yes.

right: Freedom to choose where invoices are stored
description: Taxable persons may decide where to store invoices, provided they are made available to the authorities without undue delay on request.
exercise: Member States may require notification of storage abroad or domestic storage of non-electronic invoices (Art. 245(2)).
quote: the taxable person may decide the place of storage of all invoices provided that he makes the invoices or information stored in accordance with Article 244 available to the competent authorities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Choice of place of invoice storage; no technical mechanism for the holder.

right: Right to submit VAT returns electronically
description: Member States must allow VAT returns to be filed electronically (and may make it mandatory).
exercise: Under national conditions.
quote: Member States shall allow, and may require, the VAT return referred to in paragraph 1 to be submitted by electronic means
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Member States must provide electronic VAT filing the holder operates, but the return and its result are non-technical. Required e-channel vs non-digital object.

right: Right to the small-enterprise exemption in other Member States (cross-border SME scheme)
rightholder: small enterprise established in another Member State
addressee: Member State granting the exemption / Member State of establishment
description: A small business with Union turnover up to EUR 100 000 may use the VAT exemption of another Member State that operates the scheme, if its supplies there stay below that State's threshold.
exercise: Prior notification to the Member State of establishment and 'EX' identification number (Art. 284(3)); exemption applies within 35 working days; quarterly reporting (Art. 284b).
quote: shall also grant that exemption to the supplies of goods and services in their own territory made by taxable persons established in another Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Notification for cross-border SME exemption; Member States may require electronic submission, otherwise paper works; result non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Option for small enterprises to opt out of the exemption
rightholder: taxable person entitled to the small-enterprise exemption
description: Small enterprises eligible for exemption may instead opt for normal VAT arrangements (with deduction) or simplified procedures.
exercise: Detailed rules set by Member States.
quote: Taxable persons who are entitled to exemption from VAT may opt either for the normal VAT arrangements or for the simplified procedures provided for in Article 281.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to leave the small-enterprise exemption; tax option, no technical element.

right: Right of exempt small enterprises to file a simplified annual VAT return
description: Where not released from returns altogether, exempt small enterprises may file a simplified annual return, or opt for the normal tax period.
quote: Member States shall allow such exempt small enterprises to submit a simplified VAT return to cover the period of a calendar year.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to file a simplified annual return; filing formality, no mechanism required by this provision.

right: Option for flat-rate farmers to apply normal VAT arrangements
description: A farmer covered by the flat-rate scheme may opt for the normal VAT arrangements or simplified procedures.
exercise: Under rules and conditions set by each Member State.
quote: Every flat-rate farmer may opt, subject to the rules and conditions to be laid down by each Member State, for application of the normal VAT arrangements
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; only where Member State applies the flat-rate scheme
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Farmer's option for normal VAT arrangements; tax option, no technical element.

right: Right of customers to deduct flat-rate compensation paid
rightholder: taxable customer of a flat-rate farmer
description: A taxable customer who pays flat-rate compensation to a farmer may deduct that amount from its VAT liability.
exercise: Under the normal deduction conditions and national procedures.
quote: Where the taxable customer pays flat-rate compensation pursuant to Article 301(1), he shall be entitled
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Deduction of flat-rate compensation; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Right to a refund of flat-rate compensation for cross-border customers
rightholder: customer of a flat-rate farmer in another Member State or outside the EU
description: Member States refund flat-rate compensation paid by customers in intra-Community or export situations.
exercise: Refund method set by Member States (may use Directives 79/1072/EEC, 86/560/EEC).
quote: Member States shall refund to the customer the amount of the flat-rate compensation he has paid in respect of any of the following transactions
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Refund of flat-rate compensation; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Right of taxable dealers to opt for the margin scheme for works of art, collectors' items and antiques
description: Dealers may opt to apply the margin scheme to art, collectors' items and antiques they imported or acquired from creators or non-dealer taxable persons.
exercise: Option covers at least two calendar years.
quote: Member States shall grant taxable dealers the right to opt for application of the margin scheme to the following transactions
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option for the margin scheme; tax option, no technical element.

right: Option to apply normal VAT arrangements to margin-scheme supplies
description: Dealers may apply normal VAT to any supply otherwise under the margin scheme, gaining the related deduction rights (Art. 320).
exercise: Per supply.
quote: The taxable dealer may apply the normal VAT arrangements to any supply covered by the margin scheme.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option for normal VAT per supply; tax option, no technical element.

right: Right of investment gold producers to opt for taxation
rightholder: taxable persons producing or transforming investment gold
description: Producers/transformers of investment gold may opt to tax supplies of investment gold to other taxable persons that would otherwise be exempt.
exercise: Detailed rules set by Member States (Art. 351).
quote: Member States shall allow taxable persons who produce investment gold or transform gold into investment gold the right to opt for the taxation of supplies of investment gold to another taxable person
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to tax investment gold; tax option, no technical element.

right: Option for industrial gold suppliers to tax supplies of gold bars or wafers
rightholder: taxable persons normally supplying gold for industrial purposes
description: Where allowed by the Member State, industrial gold suppliers may opt to tax supplies of investment gold bars/wafers to other taxable persons.
quote: Member States may allow taxable persons who, in the course of their economic activity, normally supply gold for industrial purposes, the right to opt for the taxation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; Member-State option
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Option to tax gold bars or wafers; tax option, no technical element.

right: Option for agents to tax intermediation of investment gold
rightholder: agent acting in the name and on behalf of another
description: Where the supplier has opted to tax investment gold, the agent intermediating the supply may opt to tax its services too.
quote: Where the supplier has exercised the right under Articles 348 and 349 to opt for taxation, Member States shall allow the agent to opt for taxation of the services referred to in Article 347.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Agent's option to tax intermediation; tax option, no technical element.

right: Right of investment gold traders to deduct input VAT despite exempt supplies
rightholder: taxable person making exempt supplies of investment gold
description: Traders whose onward supply of investment gold is exempt may still deduct VAT on gold bought from opting suppliers, gold transformed into investment gold, and services changing form, weight or purity.
quote: Where his subsequent supply of investment gold is exempt pursuant to this Chapter, the taxable person shall be entitled to deduct the following
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Input VAT deduction for investment gold traders; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Right of investment gold producers to deduct input VAT
rightholder: taxable persons producing or transforming investment gold
description: Producers and transformers of investment gold may deduct VAT on inputs linked to production or transformation as if their exempt supply were taxed.
quote: Taxable persons who produce investment gold or transform gold into investment gold shall be entitled to deduct the VAT due or paid by them
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Input VAT deduction for gold producers; substantive tax right, no technical element.

right: Right to use the non-Union One-Stop-Shop scheme
rightholder: taxable person not established in the Community supplying services to non-taxable persons
description: Non-EU businesses supplying services to EU consumers may register in one Member State and declare and pay VAT for all Member States there; input VAT is refunded under Directive 86/560/EEC (Art. 368).
exercise: Electronic registration and quarterly returns in the Member State of identification.
quote: Member States shall permit any taxable person not established within the Community supplying services to a non-taxable person who is established in a Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; replaced by Dir (EU) 2025/516 from 1 January 2027
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Non-Union OSS registration and quarterly returns must be electronic (Arts 360, 364), but the declarations and result are non-technical. Required e-channel vs non-digital object.

right: Right to use the Union One-Stop-Shop scheme
rightholder: taxable persons making intra-Community distance sales, facilitating platforms, or non-established service suppliers to consumers
description: Eligible businesses may declare and pay VAT due in other Member States on B2C distance sales and services through a single registration; input VAT abroad is refunded under Directive 2008/9/EC.
exercise: Electronic notification to the Member State of identification (Art. 369c).
quote: Member States shall permit the following taxable persons to use this special scheme
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; replaced by Dir (EU) 2025/516 from 1 July 2028
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Union OSS notifications and returns must be electronic (Arts 369c, 369g), but the declarations are non-technical. Required e-channel vs non-digital object.

right: Right to use the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) scheme
rightholder: taxable persons making distance sales of imported goods (EUR 150 or less), directly or via an intermediary
description: Sellers of low-value imported goods to EU consumers may declare and pay VAT through a single registration (possibly via an EU intermediary), with VAT chargeable at the time of payment.
exercise: Registration in Member State of identification; one intermediary at a time.
quote: Member States shall permit the following taxable persons carrying out distance sales of goods imported from third territories or third countries to use this special scheme
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: IOSS notifications and monthly returns must be electronic (Arts 369o, 369s), but the declarations are non-technical. Required e-channel vs non-digital object.

right: Right to use special arrangements for declaring and paying import VAT on low-value consignments
rightholder: person presenting goods to customs (e.g. postal operator, courier)
description: Where IOSS is not used, the person presenting low-value goods to customs may collect VAT from the recipient and pay it monthly through special arrangements.
exercise: Monthly electronic declaration (Art. 369zb).
quote: the Member State of importation shall permit the person presenting the goods to customs on behalf of the person for whom the goods are destined
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law; consignments of intrinsic value up to EUR 150
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (VAT in the Digital Age)
tl_reason: Member States must allow an electronic monthly declaration (Art. 369zb); declaration and payment non-technical. Required e-channel vs non-digital object.

right: Right to a VAT refund for taxable persons established in another Member State
rightholder: taxable person not established in the Member State of refund but established in another Member State
