source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Judicial review of supervisory decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to justified and communicated supervisory measures
description: Measures involving penalties or restrictions on passporting must be properly justified and communicated to the institution.
quote: shall be properly justified and communicated to the payment institution concerned
notes: Proposal text; may change. Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Supervisory measures must be justified and communicated; administrative procedure.

right: Right of clients to be informed of major ICT-related incidents
description: Where a major ICT-related incident affects clients' financial interests, they must be informed without undue delay of the incident and mitigation measures; for significant cyber threats, potentially affected clients must be told of protective measures they may take.
exercise: Without undue delay once the financial entity becomes aware.
quote: Where a major ICT-related incident occurs and has an impact on the financial interests of clients, financial entities shall, without undue delay as soon as they become aware of it
tl_reason: Clients told of major ICT incidents and protective measures; plain notice, no mechanism prescribed, usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to an attestation of completed threat-led penetration testing
description: After a TLPT, the authority must give the financial entity an attestation that the test met the requirements, enabling mutual recognition across authorities.
exercise: After submitting findings, remediation plans and documentation (Art. 26(6)).
quote: Authorities shall provide financial entities with an attestation confirming that the test was performed in accordance with the requirements
notes: Only entities required to perform TLPT
tl_reason: Attestation from the authority after testing; administrative document, no holder mechanism.

right: Right of financial entities to terminate ICT service contracts
description: ICT service contracts must be terminable by the financial entity for significant breaches, risk-relevant changes, evidenced ICT risk weaknesses or where supervision is impaired; termination rights and notice periods must be in the contract (Art. 30(2)(h)).
exercise: Contractual termination under the circumstances listed.
quote: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated in any of the following circumstances
notes: Mandatory contract term
tl_reason: Contractual termination right; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to access, recovery and return of data from ICT providers
description: Contracts must ensure access to, recovery and return of personal and non-personal data in an easily accessible format on the provider's insolvency, resolution, discontinuation or contract termination.
quote: provisions on ensuring access, recovery and return in an easily accessible format of personal and non-personal data processed by the financial entity
notes: Mandatory contract term
tl_reason: Access, recovery and return of data in an accessible format for migration; only fulfillable by technical export, holder must handle the data. Test: no.

right: Rights of access, inspection and audit over critical ICT providers
description: Contracts for ICT services supporting critical or important functions must give the financial entity unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit, and to take copies of relevant documentation.
exercise: Directly or via an appointed third party; microenterprises may delegate to an independent third party.
quote: unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit by the financial entity, or an appointed third party, and by the competent authority
notes: Mandatory contract term; critical or important functions
tl_reason: Audit and inspection of ICT services may need technical access to systems, but document copies and on-site inspection also work. Mechanism unspecified.

right: Right to a transition period for exit from critical ICT services
description: Contracts must provide a mandatory transition period during which the provider keeps providing services so the financial entity can migrate to another provider or in-house.
quote: allowing the financial entity to migrate to another ICT third-party service provider or change to in-house solutions consistent with the complexity of the service provided
notes: Mandatory contract term; critical or important functions
tl_reason: Transition period serves technical migration of ICT services, but the provision only guarantees continued service, no mechanism. Ability vs mechanism conflict.

right: Right to submit a reasoned statement before designation as critical ICT provider
description: An ICT provider notified of an assessment leading to designation as critical may submit a reasoned statement, which the Lead Overseer must consider.
exercise: Within 6 weeks of notification.
quote: Within 6 weeks from the date of the notification, the ICT third-party service provider may submit to the Lead Overseer a reasoned statement
tl_reason: Reasoned statement in a designation procedure; procedural, no technical element.

right: Option to request designation as a critical ICT third-party service provider
description: ICT providers not on the critical list may apply to be designated critical; the ESAs must decide and notify within six months.
exercise: Reasoned application to EBA, ESMA or EIOPA.
quote: The ICT third-party service providers that are not included in the list referred to in paragraph 9 may request to be designated as critical
tl_reason: Application to be designated critical; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to be consulted before Lead Overseer recommendations
description: Before issuing recommendations, the Lead Overseer must let the provider submit information on the expected impact on customers outside DORA's scope and propose mitigating solutions.
exercise: Within 30 calendar days.
quote: the Lead Overseer shall give the opportunity to the ICT third-party service provider to provide, within 30 calendar days, relevant information evidencing the expected impact on customers
tl_reason: Consultation before recommendations; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to complain to national courts about irregular enforcement of penalty payments
description: Complaints about irregular conduct of enforcement of periodic penalty payments fall within the jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where enforcement takes place.
exercise: Under national civil procedure.
quote: Courts of the Member State concerned shall have jurisdiction over complaints related to irregular conduct of enforcement.
tl_reason: Court jurisdiction over enforcement complaints; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right to be heard and to access the file before periodic penalty payments
description: Before imposing a periodic penalty payment, the Lead Overseer must hear the provider, base decisions only on findings it could comment on, respect rights of defence and grant access to the file.
quote: the Lead Overseer shall give the representatives of the critical ICT third-party service provider subject to the proceedings the opportunity to be heard on the findings
tl_reason: Right to be heard and access the file; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right not to answer a simple request for information
description: When the Lead Overseer sends a simple (non-binding) information request, it must state that the provider is not obliged to answer, though voluntary answers must not be incorrect or misleading.
quote: inform the representative of the critical ICT third-party service provider from whom the information is requested that he or she is not obliged to provide the information
tl_reason: Right not to answer a simple information request; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to appeal Lead Overseer decisions to the ESA Board of Appeal and the Court of Justice
addressee: ESA Board of Appeal / Court of Justice
description: Binding information requests, investigation and inspection decisions (Arts 38(4), 39(6)) must indicate the right to appeal to the ESA Board of Appeal and to Court of Justice review.
exercise: Under Arts 60-61 of Regulations (EU) Nos 1093/2010, 1094/2010, 1095/2010.
quote: indicate the right to appeal the decision to ESA’s Board of Appeal and to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice of the European Union
tl_reason: Appeal to Board of Appeal and Court of Justice; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right to give a reasoned explanation for not following Lead Overseer recommendations
description: Within 60 calendar days of recommendations, a critical provider may either commit to follow them or explain its reasons for not doing so.
exercise: Within 60 calendar days; insufficient explanations may be publicly disclosed.
quote: shall either notify the Lead Overseer of their intention to follow the recommendations or provide a reasoned explanation for not following such recommendations
tl_reason: Reasoned explanation for not following recommendations; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right of appeal against administrative penalties and remedial measures
description: Decisions imposing administrative penalties or remedial measures must be properly reasoned and subject to a right of appeal.
exercise: Under national law.
quote: Member States shall ensure that any decision imposing administrative penalties or remedial measures set out in paragraph 2, point (c), is properly reasoned and is subject to a right of appeal.
tl_reason: Appeal against administrative penalties; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right of offerors to offer crypto-assets throughout the Union without further information requirements
rightholder: offeror / person seeking admission to trading
description: Once the white paper is published, the offeror may offer the crypto-assets (other than ARTs/EMTs) throughout the Union and have them admitted to trading, and cannot be subjected to further information requirements.
exercise: After publication of the white paper under Art. 9 (and any modified paper under Art. 12).
quote: offerors may offer crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens throughout the Union
notes: Article titled 'Rights of offerors'; market-access right
tl_reason: Union-wide market access after white paper publication; no technical element.

right: Right of withdrawal from crypto-asset purchase
addressee: offeror / crypto-asset service provider placing on its behalf
description: A retail holder who buys crypto-assets (other than ARTs/EMTs) directly from the offeror or a placing CASP may withdraw within 14 calendar days without fees, costs or reasons and must be reimbursed within 14 days using the same means of payment.
exercise: Notify the offeror/placing CASP within 14 days of the purchase agreement; not available once the asset is admitted to trading before purchase or after the end of a time-limited subscription period.
quote: Retail holders shall have a period of 14 calendar days within which to withdraw from their agreement to purchase crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens
notes: Information on the right must be given in the white paper (Art. 13(3))
tl_reason: Withdrawal notice to the offeror, usually given online; a letter works and the refund is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to return of funds when an offer is cancelled
description: If an offer to the public of crypto-assets (other than ARTs/EMTs) is cancelled, funds collected from holders or prospective holders must be returned to them.
exercise: Return no later than 25 calendar days after the date of cancellation.
quote: offerors of such crypto-asset shall ensure that any funds collected from holders or prospective holders are duly returned to them no later than 25 calendar days after the date of cancellation
tl_reason: Return of funds when an offer is cancelled; monetary, no technical mechanism.

right: Right to compensation for incomplete, unclear or misleading crypto-asset white paper
addressee: offeror / person seeking admission to trading / trading platform operator and members of its management body
description: A holder can claim damages for loss caused by white paper information that is not complete, fair or clear or is misleading; contractual exclusions of this liability are void.
exercise: Civil claim under national law; holder must show the infringement and that reliance on the information affected the decision to buy, sell or exchange; summary-only liability is limited (Art. 15(5)).
quote: shall be liable to a holder of the crypto-asset for any loss incurred due to that infringement
notes: Without prejudice to other civil liability under national law
tl_reason: Civil damages claim for a misleading white paper; no technical mechanism.

right: EU-wide validity of authorisation to offer asset-referenced tokens
description: An authorisation granted by the home competent authority allows the issuer to offer the ART to the public, or seek its admission to trading, throughout the Union.
quote: shall allow an issuer of an asset-referenced token to offer to the public, throughout the Union, the asset-referenced token for which it has been authorised
notes: Market-access (passport) right
tl_reason: EU-wide validity of authorisation; market-access passport, no technical element.

right: Right to a reasoned decision on an ART authorisation application within set deadlines
description: The applicant issuer must be told whether its application is complete (Art. 20(1)) and receive a fully reasoned decision granting or refusing authorisation, notified within five working days of the decision.
exercise: Decision within 25 working days of receipt of the EBA/ESMA/ECB opinions; completeness check within 25 working days (Art. 20(1)).
quote: take a fully reasoned decision granting or refusing authorisation to the applicant issuer and, within five working days of taking that decision, notify it to the applicant issuer
tl_reason: Reasoned authorisation decision within deadlines; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to compensation for misleading white paper of an asset-referenced token
addressee: issuer of the asset-referenced token and members of its management body
description: A holder of an ART can claim damages for loss caused by incomplete, unfair, unclear or misleading information in the issuer's white paper; contractual exclusions are void.
exercise: Civil claim; holder bears the burden of showing the infringement and reliance (Art. 26(3)).
quote: that issuer and the members of its administrative, management or supervisory body shall be liable to a holder of such asset-referenced token for any loss incurred due to that infringement
tl_reason: Civil damages claim for a misleading white paper; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to file complaints with an ART issuer free of charge
rightholder: holder of asset-referenced tokens; other interested parties incl. consumer associations
addressee: issuer of asset-referenced tokens / third-party distributors
description: Holders can complain free of charge to the issuer (or third-party distributor) using a complaint template; complaints must be investigated fairly and the outcome communicated.
exercise: Free of charge; issuer must provide a template and communicate the outcome within a reasonable period.
quote: Holders of asset-referenced tokens shall be able to file complaints free of charge with the issuers of their asset-referenced tokens
tl_reason: Free complaint to the issuer using a template; a letter works and the outcome is plain. Test: yes.

right: Permanent right of redemption of asset-referenced tokens
addressee: issuer of asset-referenced tokens (and the reserve of assets)
description: Holders may at any time require the issuer to redeem their ARTs, by payment of the market value of the referenced assets in funds or by delivery of those assets, free of charge; where bought with fiat funds, redemption in the same currency must be offered.
exercise: Request to the issuer under its redemption policy; no fee (Art. 39(3)); claim extends to the reserve assets if the issuer cannot meet its obligations.
quote: Holders of asset-referenced tokens shall have a right of redemption at all times against the issuers of the asset-referenced tokens
notes: Recovery-plan measures may temporarily limit or suspend redemptions (Art. 46)
tl_reason: Plain request yields funds or assets, but the tokens must be surrendered by DLT transfer from the holder's wallet. Mechanism vs result conflict.

right: Procedural guarantees for proposed acquirers of qualifying holdings in ART issuers
description: A proposed acquirer must receive written acknowledgment within two working days, be told the assessment deadline, receive reasons if the acquisition is opposed, and benefits from deemed approval if no opposition is notified in time.
exercise: Notification to the competent authority; assessment within 60 working days (suspension max. 20/30 working days).
quote: When acknowledging receipt of the notification, the competent authority shall inform the proposed acquirer of the date of expiry of the assessment period.
tl_reason: Procedural guarantees in acquisition assessment; administrative, no technical element.

right: Right to comment on EBA draft decision classifying an ART as significant
description: Before EBA classifies (or declassifies, Art. 43(8)) an ART as significant, the issuer receives the draft decision and may submit written observations which EBA must duly consider.
exercise: Written observations within 20 working days of notification of the draft decision.
quote: shall have 20 working days from the date of notification of EBA’s draft decision to provide observations and comments in writing
tl_reason: Written observations on an EBA draft decision; procedural, no technical element.

right: Option to request voluntary classification of an ART as significant
description: An applicant issuer may ask in its application or notification for its ART to be classified as significant; EBA must decide within 60 working days.
exercise: Request in the authorisation application (Art. 18) or credit-institution notification (Art. 17), with a programme of operations showing at least three Art. 43(1) criteria.
quote: Applicant issuers of asset-referenced tokens may indicate in their application for authorisation pursuant to Article 18, or in their notification pursuant to Article 17, that they wish
tl_reason: Request for voluntary significance classification; administrative, no technical element.

right: Non-discriminatory access to custody of significant ARTs
rightholder: crypto-asset service providers authorised for custody (and holders)
description: Issuers of significant ARTs must allow their tokens to be held in custody by different authorised CASPs, including unaffiliated ones, on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.
quote: shall ensure that such tokens can be held in custody by different crypto-asset service providers
notes: Only significant ARTs
tl_reason: Tokens must be custodiable by unaffiliated CASPs (technical interoperability), but it is FRAND market access for businesses. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to redeem e-money tokens at par value at any time
description: Holders have a claim against the issuer and may require redemption at any time at par value, paid in funds other than electronic money, without a fee.
exercise: Request to the issuer; conditions stated in the white paper; no fee (Art. 49(6)).
quote: Upon request by a holder of an e-money token, the issuer of that e-money token shall redeem it, at any time and at par value
tl_reason: Plain request yields funds at par, but the tokens must be surrendered by DLT transfer from the holder's wallet. Mechanism vs result conflict.

right: Right to compensation for misleading white paper of an e-money token
addressee: issuer of the e-money token and members of its management body
description: A holder of an EMT can claim damages for loss caused by incomplete, unfair, unclear or misleading information in the issuer's white paper; contractual exclusions are void.
exercise: Civil claim; holder bears the burden of proof on infringement and reliance (Art. 52(3)).
quote: that issuer and the members of its administrative, management or supervisory body shall be liable to a holder of such e-money token for any loss incurred due to that infringement
tl_reason: Civil damages claim for a misleading white paper; no technical mechanism.

right: Right to comment on EBA draft decision classifying an EMT as significant
description: Before EBA classifies (or declassifies, Art. 56(8)) an EMT as significant, the issuer receives the draft decision and may submit written observations.
exercise: Written observations within 20 working days of notification.
quote: Issuers of such e-money tokens, their competent authorities, the ECB and, where applicable, the central bank of the Member State concerned shall have 20 working days
tl_reason: Written observations on an EBA draft decision; procedural, no technical element.

right: Option to request voluntary classification of an EMT as significant
rightholder: issuer of e-money tokens (credit institution / e-money institution)
description: An EMT issuer may ask for its token to be classified as significant; EBA must decide within 60 working days.
exercise: Request with a detailed programme of operations.
quote: may indicate that it wishes for its e-money token to be classified as a significant e-money token
tl_reason: Request for voluntary significance classification; administrative, no technical element.

right: Right of authorised CASPs to provide services throughout the Union
description: Authorised CASPs may provide services across the Union via establishment or free provision of services, without physical presence in host Member States.
exercise: Cross-border notification to home authority; may start on receipt of communication or at the latest 15 calendar days after submitting the information (Art. 65(4)).
quote: Crypto-asset service providers shall be allowed to provide crypto-asset services throughout the Union
notes: Passport right
tl_reason: Union-wide passport for CASPs; market access, no technical element.

right: Right of certain financial entities to provide crypto-asset services by notification
rightholder: credit institution, CSD, investment firm, e-money institution, UCITS manager/AIFM, market operator
description: Already-authorised financial entities may provide equivalent crypto-asset services without a separate CASP authorisation, by notifying the competent authority in advance.
exercise: Notification at least 40 working days before first providing the services, with the information in Art. 60(7).
quote: A credit institution may provide crypto-asset services if it notifies the information referred to in paragraph 7 to the competent authority of its home Member State at least 40 working days before
tl_reason: Provision of crypto services by prior notification; administrative, no technical element.

right: Procedural rights of applicants for CASP authorisation
description: Applicants receive written acknowledgment within five working days, notice when the application is complete, and a fully reasoned decision within 40 working days of a complete application, notified within five working days.
exercise: Application under Art. 62; assessment suspension max. 20 working days.
quote: Competent authorities shall notify the applicant of their decision within five working days of the date of that decision.
tl_reason: Procedural guarantees in authorisation; administrative, no technical element.

right: Transfer of client crypto-assets and funds when a CASP loses authorisation
rightholder: client of a crypto-asset service provider
description: CASPs must have procedures ensuring timely and orderly transfer of clients' crypto-assets and funds to another CASP if their authorisation is withdrawn.
quote: adequate procedures ensuring the timely and orderly transfer of their clients’ crypto-assets and funds to another crypto-asset service provider when an authorisation is withdrawn
tl_reason: Crypto-assets can only move by DLT transfer to another CASP, but the provider executes it and the holder may stay passive. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to risk warnings and white-paper links from CASPs
rightholder: client of a crypto-asset service provider
description: Clients must be warned of the risks of crypto-asset transactions and, for trading, exchange, advice and portfolio management, be given hyperlinks to the relevant white papers.
quote: Crypto-asset service providers shall warn clients of the risks associated with transactions in crypto-assets.
tl_reason: Risk warnings and hyperlinks to white papers; plain information delivered online, usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain records of services and transactions
rightholder: client of a crypto-asset service provider
description: Records of the CASP's services, orders and transactions must be provided to clients on request.
exercise: Request to the CASP; records kept five years (up to seven if the authority requests).
quote: The records kept pursuant to the first subparagraph shall be provided to clients upon request
tl_reason: Request by letter works; records of orders and transactions may come back as data or as a plain statement. Result only sometimes a digital artefact.

right: Information on payment services provided alongside crypto-asset services
rightholder: client of a crypto-asset service provider
description: Where a CASP (or a third party) provides related payment services, clients must be told the nature, terms and conditions (including applicable law and client rights) and who provides them.
quote: Where payment services are provided, crypto-asset service providers shall inform their clients of all of the following
tl_reason: Plain information on related payment services in an online service relationship; no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right to file complaints with a CASP free of charge
rightholder: client of a crypto-asset service provider
description: Clients can file complaints free of charge, must be informed of this possibility and given a template, and must receive the outcome of a timely and fair investigation.
exercise: Free of charge; outcome communicated within a reasonable period.
quote: Clients shall be able to file complaints free of charge with crypto-asset service providers.
tl_reason: Free complaint to the CASP using a template; a letter works and the outcome is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of CASPs to terminate outsourcing agreements
description: Outsourcing agreements must give the CASP a right to terminate them.
exercise: Under the written outsourcing agreement.
quote: Outsourcing agreements shall give crypto-asset service providers the right to terminate those agreements.
notes: Mandatory contract term
tl_reason: Contractual termination of outsourcing; no technical element.

right: Right to a written custody agreement with minimum content
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: Custody clients must receive an agreement specifying the parties, service, custody policy, communication/authentication means, security systems, fees and applicable law.
quote: Crypto-asset service providers providing custody and administration of crypto-assets on behalf of clients shall conclude an agreement with their clients
tl_reason: Custody agreement describing communication, authentication and security; plain contract document, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right to a summary of the custody policy on request
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: Clients may request an electronic summary of the custodian's custody policy.
exercise: Request to the custodian; electronic format.
quote: A summary of the custody policy shall be made available to clients at their request in an electronic format.
tl_reason: Summary of custody policy in electronic format; plain-language content usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Entitlement to newly created crypto-assets and rights (forks, airdrops)
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: Where DLT changes or other events create or modify rights, the client is entitled to any newly created crypto-assets or rights in proportion to its positions, unless a prior agreement expressly provides otherwise.
quote: the client shall be entitled to any crypto-assets or any rights newly created on the basis and to the extent of the client’s positions at the time of the occurrence of that change or event
tl_reason: Entitlement to fork or airdrop tokens: object is digital, but it is a passive allocation with no holder mechanism. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to statements of position
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: Custody clients receive an electronic statement of their crypto-asset positions (balances, value, transfers) at least quarterly and on request, plus prompt information on operations requiring their response.
exercise: Quarterly and on request; electronic format.
quote: shall provide their clients, at least once every three months and at the request of the client concerned, with a statement of position of the crypto-assets recorded in the name of those clients
tl_reason: Electronic statement of positions; plain balances and values, usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to return of crypto-assets held in custody
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: Custodians must have procedures to return clients' crypto-assets or the means of access to them as soon as possible.
quote: shall ensure that necessary procedures are in place to return crypto-assets held on behalf of their clients, or the means of access, as soon as possible to those clients
tl_reason: Return of crypto-assets or access keys only possible by DLT transfer to the holder's wallet, which the holder must operate. Test: no.

right: Right to compensation for loss of crypto-assets held in custody
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing custody and administration
description: The custodian is liable to clients for loss of crypto-assets or means of access caused by an incident attributable to it, capped at the market value at the time of loss.
exercise: Claim against the custodian; no liability for incidents independent of its service/operations.
quote: shall be liable to their clients for the loss of any crypto-assets or of the means of access to the crypto-assets as a result of an incident that is attributable to them
tl_reason: Liability for lost crypto-assets capped at market value; compensation claim, no technical mechanism.

right: Fair and open access to crypto-asset trading platforms
addressee: operator of a trading platform for crypto-assets
description: Trading platform operating rules must set objective, non-discriminatory and proportionate participation criteria promoting fair and open access for clients.
quote: set objective, non-discriminatory rules and proportionate criteria for participation in the trading activities, which promote fair and open access to the trading platform for clients willing to trade
tl_reason: Non-discriminatory participation criteria for a trading platform; market access, no technical mechanism for the holder.

right: Consent to matched principal trading
addressee: operator of a trading platform for crypto-assets
description: A trading platform operator may engage in matched principal trading only where the client has consented.
exercise: Client consent required in advance.
quote: shall only be allowed to engage in matched principal trading where the client has consented to that process
tl_reason: Prior client consent to matched principal trading; plain consent, usually given online, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right to execution of exchange orders at the displayed price
description: Exchange orders must be executed at the prices displayed when the order becomes final, and clients must be told when an order is deemed final.
quote: shall execute client orders at the prices displayed at the time when the order for exchange is final
tl_reason: Execution at displayed price is a pricing guarantee owed by the provider; no holder mechanism.

right: Right to best execution of orders
description: CASPs executing orders must take all necessary steps to obtain the best possible result for clients (price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution etc.), except where following specific client instructions.
quote: shall take all necessary steps to obtain, while executing orders, the best possible result for their clients
tl_reason: Best execution duty owed by the provider; no holder mechanism.

right: Information on, and prior consent to, the order execution policy
description: Clients must receive clear information on the order execution policy and significant changes, and their prior consent to the policy must be obtained.
quote: Crypto-asset service providers shall obtain prior consent from each client regarding the order execution policy.
tl_reason: Information on and consent to the execution policy; plain notice and consent, typically online. Test: yes.

right: Right to demonstration that orders were executed per policy
description: On request, the CASP must demonstrate to the client that its orders were executed in accordance with the execution policy.
exercise: Request to the CASP.
quote: shall be able to demonstrate to their clients, at their request, that they have executed their orders in accordance with their order execution policy
tl_reason: Demonstration of policy-compliant execution on request; a letter works and the answer is plain. Test: yes.

right: Consent to execution outside a trading platform
description: Orders may be executed outside a trading platform only after informing the client and obtaining prior express consent (general or per transaction).
exercise: Prior express consent, general or per transaction.
quote: shall obtain the prior express consent of their clients before proceeding to execute their orders outside a trading platform
tl_reason: Prior express consent to off-platform execution; plain consent, usually given online, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Pre-contractual information for offerors using placing services
rightholder: offeror / person seeking admission to trading
description: Before agreeing a placement, the placing CASP must inform the offeror of the type of placement, fees, likely timing, process and price, and targeted purchasers, and obtain the issuer's agreement to that information.
quote: Crypto-asset service providers placing crypto-assets shall communicate the following information to the offeror, to the person seeking admission to trading
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information between placing CASP and offeror; commercial disclosure, no technical element.

right: Right to a suitability assessment before advice or portfolio management
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing advice or portfolio management
description: Advisers and portfolio managers must assess whether services or crypto-assets suit the client's knowledge, experience, objectives, risk tolerance and ability to bear losses, and must not recommend unsuitable ones (Art. 81(11)).
exercise: Reviewed at least every two years (Art. 81(12)).
quote: shall assess whether the crypto-asset services or crypto-assets are suitable for their clients or prospective clients
tl_reason: Suitability assessment duty owed by adviser; no holder mechanism.

right: Pre-advice disclosures on independence, costs, inducements and risks
description: Before advice, clients must be told whether it is independent and how broad the analysis is, all costs and charges (Art. 81(4)), any inducements (Art. 81(6)), and receive risk warnings (Art. 81(9)).
exercise: In good time before advice is provided.
quote: shall, in good time before providing advice on crypto-assets, inform prospective clients whether the advice is
tl_reason: Pre-advice disclosures on independence, costs and risks; plain information in an online service relationship. Test: yes.

right: Right to a suitability report
description: After the suitability assessment or its review, the client receives an electronic report specifying the advice and how it meets the client's preferences and characteristics.
exercise: Electronic format.
quote: shall provide clients with a report on suitability specifying the advice given and how that advice meets the preferences, objectives and other characteristics of clients
tl_reason: Suitability report in electronic format; plain-language content usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to periodic portfolio management statements
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing portfolio management
description: Portfolio management clients receive electronic statements every three months reviewing activities, performance and suitability (unless they have online access they actually use).
exercise: Quarterly; electronic format.
quote: shall provide periodic statements to their clients, in an electronic format, of the portfolio management activities carried out on their behalf
tl_reason: Periodic portfolio statements in electronic format; plain content usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Right to a written transfer-services agreement
addressee: crypto-asset service provider providing transfer services
description: Transfer-service clients must receive an agreement setting out identities, transfer modalities, security systems, fees and applicable law.
quote: Crypto-asset service providers providing transfer services for crypto-assets on behalf of clients shall conclude an agreement with their clients
tl_reason: Transfer-services agreement with modalities, security and fees; plain contract document, no mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Procedural guarantees for proposed acquirers of qualifying holdings in CASPs
description: A proposed acquirer receives acknowledgment within two working days, knows the 60-working-day assessment deadline, gets reasons for any opposition and benefits from deemed approval if not opposed in time.
exercise: Written notification to the CASP's competent authority.
quote: shall notify the proposed acquirer thereof within two working days and in any event before the date referred to in paragraph 4
tl_reason: Procedural guarantees in acquisition assessment; administrative, no technical element.

right: Right to complain to the competent authority
rightholder: clients and other interested parties, including consumer associations
description: Clients and interested parties can submit complaints to national competent authorities about alleged MiCA infringements by offerors, issuers or CASPs.
exercise: In writing (incl. electronically) in an official language accepted by the authority; procedures published on its website.
quote: Competent authorities shall set up procedures that allow clients and other interested parties, including consumer associations, to submit complaints to them
tl_reason: Complaint to the authority in writing, including electronically; a letter works and the outcome is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of appeal before a court against competent authority decisions
rightholder: person subject to a decision of a competent authority
description: Decisions of competent authorities under MiCA must be properly reasoned and can be appealed before a court.
exercise: National judicial procedure.
quote: Member States shall ensure that decisions taken by competent authorities under this Regulation are properly reasoned and subject to the right of appeal before a court.
tl_reason: Court appeal against authority decisions; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right of appeal against failure to decide on an authorisation application
description: If a complete authorisation application receives no decision within six months, the applicant may appeal to a court.
exercise: Six months after submission of a complete application.
quote: The right of appeal before a court shall also apply where, in respect of an application for authorisation which provides all of the required information, no decision is taken within six months
tl_reason: Court appeal against failure to decide; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Standing of consumer and professional organisations to bring proceedings
rightholder: consumer organisations; professional organisations; public bodies
addressee: Member State / courts or administrative bodies
description: Designated bodies, including consumer organisations protecting crypto-asset holders, may take action before courts or administrative bodies to ensure MiCA is applied.
exercise: As determined by national law.
quote: consumer organisations having a legitimate interest in protecting holders of crypto-assets
notes: Member States choose which of the listed bodies have standing
tl_reason: Standing of organisations to bring proceedings; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Whistleblower protection for reporting MiCA infringements
description: Persons reporting infringements of MiCA benefit from the reporting channels and protections of the Whistleblower Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
exercise: Per Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
notes: Cross-reference to Directive (EU) 2019/1937
tl_reason: Whistleblower channels and protection; reporting by ordinary means, no technical mechanism.

right: Right to appeal EBA decisions to the EBA Board of Appeal and the Court of Justice
rightholder: addressee of an EBA decision (issuers of significant ARTs/EMTs and related persons)
addressee: EBA Board of Appeal / Court of Justice
description: EBA decisions requiring information must indicate, and are subject to, the right of appeal to the EBA Board of Appeal and review by the Court of Justice.
exercise: Under Arts 60-61 of Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010.
quote: indicate the right to appeal the decision before EBA’s Board of Appeal and to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice
tl_reason: Appeal to Board of Appeal and Court of Justice; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right to be heard by the EBA investigation officer
rightholder: persons subject to an EBA investigation
description: Before submitting findings to EBA, the investigation officer must give the persons investigated an opportunity to be heard, and may base findings only on facts they could comment on; rights of defence apply (Art. 134(6)).
quote: the investigation officer shall give the persons subject to the investigation the opportunity to be heard on the matters being investigated
tl_reason: Right to be heard in an investigation; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right of access to the investigation file
rightholder: persons subject to an EBA investigation
description: Persons investigated are notified when the file is submitted and may access it, subject to others' business secrets and excluding confidential third-party information and internal preparatory documents.
quote: The persons subject to the investigation shall be entitled to have access to the file, subject to the legitimate interest of other persons in the protection of their business secrets.
tl_reason: Access to the investigation file; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to be heard before EBA supervisory measures, fines or penalty payments
rightholder: persons subject to an EBA investigation
description: EBA must hear the persons concerned on its findings before deciding on supervisory measures, fines or periodic penalty payments (or as soon as possible after an urgent interim decision).
quote: Before taking any decision pursuant to Article 130, 131 or 132, EBA shall give the persons subject to an investigation the opportunity to be heard on its findings.
tl_reason: Right to be heard before measures; procedural, no technical element.

right: Rights of defence and access to EBA's file
rightholder: persons subject to an EBA investigation
description: Rights of defence must be fully respected and persons investigated may access EBA's file, subject to business secrets and excluding confidential information and internal preparatory documents.
quote: Those persons shall be entitled to have access to EBA’s file
tl_reason: Rights of defence and file access; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to Court of Justice review of EBA fines and penalties
rightholder: addressee of an EBA fine or penalty
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Fines, periodic penalty payments and other EBA penalties can be challenged before the Court of Justice, which has unlimited jurisdiction to annul, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the Court of Justice.
quote: The Court of Justice shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions whereby EBA has imposed a fine, a periodic penalty payment or any administrative penalty or other administrative measure
tl_reason: Court of Justice review of fines; judicial remedy, no technical element.

right: Right of legal entities to join a European chips infrastructure consortium
description: Once an ECIC is established, other public or private legal entities may join it as members at any time on fair and reasonable terms set in its statutes.
exercise: Per the ECIC statutes; Member States may complain about unjustified refusal to the Chips JU Public Authorities Board (Art. 7(9)).
quote: other public or private legal entities may join it as members at any time on fair and reasonable terms specified in the statutes of the ECIC
tl_reason: Joining a consortium on statutory terms. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for the establishment of an ECIC
rightholder: founding members (Member States or public or private legal entities from at least three Member States), via a coordinator
description: Founding members can apply, through their coordinator, for the Commission to establish a European chips infrastructure consortium; the Commission decides by implementing act and notifies them.
exercise: Written application to the Commission with statutes and required content; decision by implementing act (Art. 7(5)).
quote: The coordinator of a potential ECIC shall, on behalf of all of the founding members, submit an application to the Commission in writing.
notes: Private legal entities may be founding members alongside Member States.
tl_reason: Written application to establish a consortium. Test: yes.

right: Preferential access of integrated production facilities to pilot lines
addressee: pilot lines under the Chips for Europe Initiative / Chips JU
description: Integrated production facilities have preferential access to the Initiative's pilot lines for continued innovation, without excluding effective fair-terms access for other undertakings, in particular start-ups and SMEs.
quote: integrated production facilities shall have preferential access to the pilot lines established in accordance with Article 5, point (b)
notes: Second sentence protects effective access on fair terms for other interested undertakings (start-ups, SMEs).
tl_reason: Preferential access to physical pilot lines; market access. Test: yes.

right: Preferential access of open EU foundries to pilot lines
addressee: pilot lines under the Chips for Europe Initiative / Chips JU
description: Open EU foundries have preferential access to the Initiative's pilot lines for continued innovation, without excluding effective fair-terms access for other undertakings, in particular start-ups and SMEs.
quote: open EU foundries shall have preferential access to the pilot lines established in accordance with Article 5, point (b)
notes: Second sentence protects effective access on fair terms for other interested undertakings (start-ups, SMEs).
tl_reason: Preferential access to physical pilot lines; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for integrated production facility or open EU foundry status
rightholder: any undertaking or consortium of undertakings
description: Any undertaking or consortium can apply to the Commission for a project to be granted IPF or OEF status, which brings public-interest and fast-track permitting benefits.
exercise: Application to the Commission; decision and notification within six months of a complete application, with opportunity to complete an incomplete file (Art. 15(3)).
quote: Any undertaking or any consortium of undertakings may submit an application to the Commission to grant a project the status of integrated production facility or open EU foundry.
tl_reason: Application for facility status; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of status duration or modification of implementation plans
rightholder: operator of an integrated production facility or open EU foundry
description: The operator can ask the Commission to review the duration of the status or modify its implementation plans where justified by unforeseen external circumstances.
exercise: Request to the Commission; must be duly justified.
quote: The operator of the facility may request the Commission to review the duration of the status or to modify its implementation plans
tl_reason: Request to review status; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment and propose measures before loss of status
rightholder: operator of an integrated production facility or open EU foundry
description: Where the Commission finds the facility no longer meets the requirements, the operator must be given the opportunity to comment and propose appropriate measures.
quote: it shall give the operator of the integrated production facility or open EU foundry the opportunity to comment and to propose appropriate measures
tl_reason: Right to comment before loss of status; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of appeal against withdrawal of status
rightholder: operator of an integrated production facility or open EU foundry
addressee: Commission / Court of Justice of the EU
description: A decision withdrawing IPF or OEF status must be properly reasoned and the operator has a right of appeal against it.
quote: Any decision withdrawing the status of an integrated production facility or open EU foundry shall be properly reasoned and subject to a right of appeal by the operator.
tl_reason: Appeal against withdrawal of status. Test: yes.

right: Fast-tracked permit-granting for integrated production facilities and open EU foundries
rightholder: integrated production facilities and open EU foundries (applicants)
description: Administrative applications for planning, construction and operation of IPFs and OEFs must be processed efficiently and given the most rapid treatment legally possible, with highest national significance status where it exists (Art. 18(2)).
exercise: Applies to national permit applications; optional single coordinator per project (Art. 18(4)).
quote: all national authorities concerned shall ensure that the most rapid treatment legally possible is given to these applications
tl_reason: Fast-track permitting; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to justify non-supply of information in a crisis information request
rightholder: undertakings operating along the semiconductor supply chain
description: An undertaking that does not supply information requested during the crisis stage escapes fines where it has sufficient reasons for not supplying it.
exercise: Only when the crisis stage is activated; request must state legal basis, time limit and penalties (Art. 25(4)).
quote: except where the undertaking has sufficient reasons for not supplying the requested information
notes: Crisis-stage measure.
tl_reason: Justifying non-supply of information; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to a fair and reasonable price for priority-rated orders
rightholder: integrated production facilities, open EU foundries and other undertakings subject to a priority-rated order
description: Priority-rated orders imposed during a semiconductor crisis must be placed at a fair and reasonable price, having regard to the undertaking's legitimate aims and costs.
quote: The priority-rated order shall be placed at fair and reasonable price.
notes: Crisis-stage measure.
tl_reason: Fair price for priority orders; remuneration. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before a priority-rated order
rightholder: envisaged recipient of a priority-rated order
description: Before issuing a priority-rated order the Commission must hear the envisaged recipient on feasibility and details, and may not issue it if the undertaking cannot perform it or it would impose an unreasonable economic burden.
exercise: Hearing before the decision.
quote: the Commission shall give the envisaged recipient of a priority-rated order the opportunity to be heard on the feasibility and details of the order
notes: Crisis-stage measure.
tl_reason: Right to be heard before priority order. Test: yes.

right: Exemption from contractual liability when complying with a priority-rated order
rightholder: undertaking required to accept and prioritise a priority-rated order
description: An undertaking complying with a priority-rated order is not liable for breaches of contract necessary to comply with the mandated prioritisation.
exercise: Only to the extent the breach was necessary for compliance.
quote: it shall not be liable for any breach of contractual obligations that is required to comply with the priority-rated orders
notes: Crisis-stage measure.
tl_reason: Exemption from contractual liability. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to judicial review of fines and periodic penalty payments
rightholder: undertakings fined under the Chips Act
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Undertakings can challenge Commission decisions fixing fines or periodic penalty payments before the Court of Justice, which has unlimited jurisdiction to cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: The Court of Justice shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions whereby the Commission has fixed a fine or a periodic penalty payment.
tl_reason: Judicial review of fines. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before the imposition of penalties
description: Before a penalty decision, the undertaking can comment on the Commission's preliminary findings and intended measures; the decision may rest only on objections it could comment on.
exercise: Written observations within a time limit of at least 14 days (Art. 36(2)); justifications considered (Art. 33(2)).
quote: the Commission shall give the undertaking concerned the opportunity of being heard on:
tl_reason: Right to be heard before penalties. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to the Commission's file
description: In penalty proceedings the undertaking is entitled to access the Commission's file under negotiated disclosure, excluding confidential information, internal documents and Commission-Member State correspondence.
exercise: Subject to protection of business secrets.
quote: The undertaking concerned shall be entitled to have access to the Commission’s file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
tl_reason: Access to Commission file; procedural. Test: yes.

article: Annex II Reg (EU) 2018/1724 (row added by Art. 42(2))
right: Right to complete critical raw materials permit procedures fully online
rightholder: project promoters / users of the Single Digital Gateway
description: By adding critical raw materials permit procedures to Annex II of the Single Digital Gateway Regulation, users can carry out these procedures fully online.
exercise: Through the Single Digital Gateway / national online portals.
quote: Procedure related to all relevant permits to build and operate critical raw materials projects, including building, chemical and grid connection permits and environmental assessments
notes: Derived via Art. 6 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 (online access to procedures).
tl_reason: Law requires permit procedures be completable fully online via the Single Digital Gateway, but application and permit are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to apply for recognition as a Strategic Project
description: A project promoter can apply to the Commission to have a critical raw material project recognised as a Strategic Project, gaining priority status and accelerated permitting.
exercise: Single template; open call with at least four cut-off dates per year; completeness notice within 30 days; reasoned decision within 90 days, extendable once by up to 90 days with written reasons (Art. 7(3)-(10)).
quote: Applications for recognition of a critical raw material project as a Strategic Project shall be submitted by the project promoter to the Commission.
notes: The Member State concerned can block recognition by objection (Art. 7(8)).
tl_reason: Application for Strategic Project status; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasons and to reply before withdrawal of Strategic Project status
description: Before withdrawing recognition, the Commission must give the promoter its reasons and an opportunity to reply, and take the reply into account.
quote: the Commission shall provide the project promoter with reasons for its decision, the project promoter shall be given the opportunity to reply
tl_reason: Reasons and reply before withdrawal; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to retain Strategic Project status after an update of the strategic raw materials list
description: A Strategic Project that no longer meets the criteria solely because Annex I (strategic raw materials list) was updated keeps its status for three years.
exercise: Three years from the date of the Annex I update.
quote: solely due to an update of Annex I shall be allowed to maintain their status as Strategic Projects for three years
tl_reason: Retention of status after list update. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a single point of contact and assistance in permit-granting
rightholder: project promoters of critical raw material projects
description: Project promoters deal with a single point of contact that coordinates the permit-granting process and assists them with administrative matters; they can contact the responsible administrative unit (Art. 9(5)).
exercise: Contact the single point of contact designated by the Member State.
quote: The single point of contact concerned shall be the sole point of contact for the project promoter and shall assist the project promoter in understanding any administrative matter
notes: Single points of contact to be established by 24 Feb 2025 (Art. 9(1)); applies to all critical raw material projects, not only Strategic Projects.
tl_reason: Single point of contact assistance; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit permit-granting documents electronically
rightholder: project promoters of critical raw material projects
addressee: national single point of contact / permitting authorities
description: Project promoters may submit all documents relevant to the permit-granting process in electronic form.
quote: Project promoters shall be allowed to submit all documents relevant to the permit-granting process in electronic form.
tl_reason: Law requires electronic submission be allowed, but paper still works and permit result is non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to easy access to dispute-settlement information and procedures
rightholder: applicants in permit-granting for critical raw material projects
description: Applicants must have easy access to information on, and procedures for, settling disputes about the permit-granting process, including alternative dispute resolution where applicable.
quote: Member States shall ensure that applicants have easy access to information on and procedures for the settlement of disputes concerning the permit-granting process
tl_reason: Access to dispute-settlement information; plain. Test: yes.

right: Priority status of Strategic Projects in permit-granting
rightholder: promoters of Strategic Projects in the Union
description: Strategic Projects get the highest national significance status where it exists, the most rapid permit-granting possible (Art. 10(3)) and urgent treatment of related disputes and litigation where national law provides (Art. 10(5)).
quote: Strategic Projects in the Union shall be granted the status of the highest national significance possible, where such a status exists in national law
tl_reason: Priority status in permitting. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a time-limited permit-granting process for Strategic Projects
rightholder: promoters of Strategic Projects in the Union
addressee: Member State / single point of contact
description: Permit-granting for Strategic Projects may not exceed 27 months (extraction) or 15 months (processing/recycling), or 24/12 months for projects already in permitting; completeness must be acknowledged within 45 days and a schedule drawn up.
exercise: Extensions only exceptionally (max 6 or 3 months) with written reasons to the promoter (Art. 11(4)); completeness acknowledgement within 45 days (Art. 11(6)); EIA reasoned conclusion within 90 days (Art. 12(3)).
quote: For Strategic Projects in the Union, the permit-granting process shall not exceed:
tl_reason: Time-limited permitting; administrative deadline. Test: yes.

right: Right to a scoping opinion on the environmental impact assessment report
description: A Strategic Project promoter requests an opinion on the scope and detail of the EIA report, which the single point of contact must issue within 45 days.
exercise: Request within 30 days after notification of recognition and before submitting the application; opinion within 45 days.
quote: The single point of contact concerned shall ensure that the opinion referred to in the first subparagraph is issued as soon as possible and within a period of time not exceeding 45 days
notes: Not applicable to projects already in permitting before recognition (Art. 12(6)).
tl_reason: Scoping opinion on EIA on request; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to request advice on completing project financing
description: At the promoter's request, the Board's financing subgroup discusses and advises on how to complete the project's financing (private sources, EIB, national instruments, EU programmes).
exercise: Request to the standing subgroup established under Art. 36(8)(a).
quote: shall, at the request of a project promoter of a Strategic Project, discuss and provide advice on how the financing of its project can be completed
tl_reason: Advice on project financing on request. Test: yes.

right: Right to participate in the offtake-matching system
rightholder: promoters of Strategic Projects; potential offtakers
description: Strategic Project promoters can submit offers, and potential offtakers bids (Art. 17(2)), in a Commission system that brings them into contact to conclude offtake agreements.
exercise: Via the Commission system; operated in accordance with competition rules.
quote: The system referred to in paragraph 1 shall allow project promoters of Strategic Projects to make offers indicating:
tl_reason: Commission offtake-matching system; offers and bids are plain commercial information, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of key market operators to refuse data disclosure revealing trade secrets
rightholder: key market operators along the critical raw materials value chain
description: Key market operators may refuse to submit monitoring data that would disclose trade or business secrets and need only submit data already available to them, giving reasons.
exercise: Reasons must be provided to the requesting Member State.
quote: Key market operators may refuse to submit data requested pursuant to point (a) of the first subparagraph if the sharing of such data would lead to the disclosure of trade or business secrets.
tl_reason: Refusal to disclose trade secrets with reasons. Test: yes.

right: Open participation in joint purchasing (demand aggregation)
rightholder: interested undertakings established in the Union
description: Participation in the Commission's demand-aggregation and joint purchasing system for strategic raw materials is open and transparent to all interested Union undertakings meeting minimum amounts.
exercise: Minimum demand amounts set by the Commission (Art. 25(3)(b)); entities under EU sanctions excluded (Art. 25(6)).
quote: Participation in the system referred to in paragraph 3, point (b) shall be open and transparent to all interested undertakings established in the Union.
tl_reason: Participation in joint purchasing; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to jointly negotiate purchases of strategic raw materials
rightholder: Union undertakings participating in the joint purchasing system
description: Participating undertakings may jointly negotiate purchase prices and terms, or use joint purchasing, to obtain better conditions or prevent shortages.
exercise: On a transparent basis and in compliance with EU competition law.
quote: Union undertakings participating in the system referred to in paragraph 1 may, on a transparent basis, jointly negotiate the purchase
tl_reason: Joint negotiation of purchases; contract freedom. Test: yes.

right: Access of repairers and recyclers to permanent magnet information
addressee: persons placing products with permanent magnets on the market
description: Information linked to the product's data carrier (magnet weight, location, composition, safe removal) must be accessible to repairers and recyclers.
exercise: Via data carrier/unique product identifier; kept for typical lifetime plus 10 years.
quote: The information referred to in paragraph 4 shall be accessible to repairers, recyclers, market surveillance authorities and customs authorities.
notes: Applies two years after the implementing act on labelling format enters into force (Art. 28(3)); later for MRI devices and vehicles (Art. 28(10)).
tl_reason: Information reached via product data carrier (technical), but held by professional repairers/recyclers, not a governed party; content is plain. Holder vs mechanism conflict.

right: Right of customers to recycled-content information before purchase
addressee: natural and legal persons placing products with permanent magnets on the market
description: Customers must have access to information on the share of recycled neodymium and other materials in permanent magnets before being bound by a sales contract, and must not be misled by labels.
exercise: Before conclusion of the sales contract, including distance selling.
quote: shall ensure that their customers have access to the information referred to in paragraph 1 before being bound by a sales contract
notes: Applies from the date the Art. 29(1) obligation applies (24 May 2027 or two years after the delegated act, whichever is later).
tl_reason: Pre-contract information on recycled content; plain labelling. Test: yes.

right: Right of scheme owners to apply for recognition of certification schemes
rightholder: scheme owners (industry associations, groupings of interested organisations)
description: Owners of sustainability certification schemes for critical raw materials may apply to the Commission for recognition of their schemes.
exercise: Application with evidence of meeting Annex IV criteria; single template.
quote: may apply to have their schemes recognised by the Commission
notes: Governments are also eligible scheme owners but are excluded as rightholders here.
tl_reason: Application for scheme recognition; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit feedback on recognised certification schemes
description: Stakeholders can submit feedback on the implementation of recognised schemes via the Commission's free-access register website; feedback is passed to scheme owners.
exercise: Via the register website.
quote: That website shall also allow for the collation of feedback from all relevant stakeholders concerning the implementation of recognised schemes.
tl_reason: Feedback collected through a mandated register website, but feedback and its handling are plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right of customers to the environmental footprint declaration before purchase
addressee: natural and legal persons placing critical raw materials on the market
description: Customers buying critical raw materials covered by footprint rules must have access to the environmental footprint declaration before being bound by a sales contract and must not be misled by labels.
exercise: Before conclusion of the sales contract, including distance selling.
quote: shall ensure that their customers have access to the environmental footprint declaration before being bound by a sales contract
notes: Applies only once delegated calculation and verification rules are adopted for the material (Art. 31(1), (6)).
tl_reason: Footprint declaration before purchase; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Entitlement to a Sovereignty Seal for qualifying projects
rightholder: applicants whose projects contribute to STEP objectives
description: A project that contributes to a STEP objective and passes the minimum quality requirements of a call under Digital Europe, Horizon Europe, EDF or the Innovation Fund is awarded a Sovereignty Seal, usable to obtain support from other EU programmes and funds.
exercise: Through evaluation in a call for proposals; seal valid for project implementation, lapses if not started within five years or relocated outside the Union (Art. 4(9)).
quote: The Commission shall award a Sovereignty Seal to any project contributing to any of the STEP objectives, provided that the project has been assessed and complies with minimum quality requirements
notes: Funding-programme instrument; seal is a quality label, not a funding entitlement.
tl_reason: Sovereignty Seal through funding call evaluation; funding right. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of particular network security risks
description: Be informed of a particular risk of a network security breach and, where the risk is outside the provider's measures, of possible remedies and likely costs.
quote: the provider of a publicly available electronic communications service must inform the subscribers concerning such risk
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Plain information on network security risks and remedies; no channel required. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach
description: Be notified without undue delay of a personal data breach likely to adversely affect one's personal data or privacy, with contact points and recommended mitigation measures.
exercise: Not required if data were rendered unintelligible to the authority's satisfaction; authority may require notification.
quote: the provider shall also notify the subscriber or individual of the breach without undue delay
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Plain breach notice with recommended measures. Test: yes.

right: Right to confidentiality of communications
addressee: Member State / any person other than users
description: Communications and related traffic data are confidential; interception or surveillance by others requires the users' consent unless legally authorised.
exercise: Restrictions only under Art. 15(1).
quote: they shall prohibit listening, tapping, storage or other kinds of interception or surveillance of communications and the related traffic data by persons other than users
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Object is communications and traffic data, but a protective prohibition: nothing to operate, enforced by ordinary remedies. Conflict: digital object vs no mechanism.

right: Right to consent to storing or accessing information on terminal equipment (cookies)
addressee: any party storing or accessing information on terminal equipment
description: Storage of or access to information on one's device is allowed only with consent after clear and comprehensive information, except where strictly necessary for transmission or a requested service.
exercise: Consent with prior clear and comprehensive information.
quote: the subscriber or user concerned has given his or her consent, having been provided with clear and comprehensive information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Consent to storage or access on one's own device, given in the interface or settings; a letter cannot stop device access. Test: no. Consistency pass: no interface function required; refusing or a letter still works.

right: Right to consent to and withdraw consent for traffic data processing for marketing or value added services
description: Traffic data may be used for marketing or value added services only with prior consent, which can be withdrawn at any time.
exercise: Any time.
quote: Users or subscribers shall be given the possibility to withdraw their consent for the processing of traffic data at any time.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Object is traffic data; withdrawal possibility is usually a setting, but a plain request withdraws. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on traffic data processing
description: Be informed of the types of traffic data processed and the duration of processing for billing and, before consent, for marketing or value added services.
quote: The service provider must inform the subscriber or user of the types of traffic data which are processed and of the duration of such processing
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Plain information on types and duration of traffic data processing. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive non-itemised bills
description: Choose to receive bills without itemisation of calls.
quote: Subscribers shall have the right to receive non-itemised bills.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Choice of bill format, often in account settings; a request works, result is a plain bill. Test: yes.

right: Right to withhold one's calling line identification
description: Prevent presentation of one's number to the called party, per call (users) or per line (subscribers), simply and free of charge.
exercise: Simple means, free of charge; also for calls to third countries (Art. 8(5)).
quote: the service provider must offer the calling user the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge, of preventing the presentation of the calling line identification on a per-call basis
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Provider must offer a simple per-call or per-line function to hide caller ID; the right is that network function. Test: no.

right: Right to suppress incoming calling line identification
description: Prevent presentation of the calling line identification of incoming calls.
exercise: Simple means, free for reasonable use.
quote: the service provider must offer the called subscriber the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge for reasonable use of this function
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Function to suppress incoming caller ID must be offered; exists only as a network or device feature. Test: no.

right: Right to reject anonymous incoming calls
description: Reject incoming calls where the caller has withheld their calling line identification.
exercise: Simple means.
quote: the service provider must offer the called subscriber the possibility, using a simple means, of rejecting incoming calls where the presentation of the calling line identification has been prevented
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Function to reject anonymous calls must be offered; exists only as a network feature. Test: no.

right: Right to withhold connected line identification
description: Prevent presentation of the connected line identification to the calling user.
exercise: Simple means, free of charge.
quote: the service provider must offer the called subscriber the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge, of preventing the presentation of the connected line identification to the calling user
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Function to withhold connected line ID must be offered; exists only as a network feature. Test: no.

right: Right to consent to, be informed about and withdraw consent for location data processing
addressee: electronic communications service provider / value added service provider
description: Location data (other than traffic data) may only be processed anonymised or with consent after information on type, purpose, duration and third-party transmission; consent can be withdrawn at any time.
exercise: Any time.
quote: Users or subscribers shall be given the possibility to withdraw their consent for the processing of location data other than traffic data at any time.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: Withdrawn by the Commission (2025); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC remains applicable
tl_reason: Object is location data; consent and withdrawal usually in-app, but a plain withdrawal works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to temporarily refuse location data processing
description: Even after consenting, temporarily refuse location data processing for each connection or transmission, simply and free of charge.
exercise: Simple means, free of charge.
