quote: Natural persons shall have the right to request not to be informed of such findings.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Plain request not to be informed. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data holders to receive the share of fees covering their costs
description: Receive the part of the data permit fees that compensates their costs of compiling and preparing data for secondary use.
exercise: Holder provides a cost estimate to the health data access body.
quote: The part of the fees linked to the health data holder’s costs shall be paid to the health data holder.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Share of fees covering costs; remuneration. Test: yes.

right: Right to dispute settlement on secondary-use fees
rightholder: health data holders and health data users
addressee: certified dispute settlement body (Art. 10 Data Act)
description: If they disagree with the fee set by the health data access body, refer the matter to a Data Act dispute settlement body.
quote: Where health data holders or health data users disagree with the fee set by the health data access body, they shall have access to dispute settlement bodies
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Dispute settlement on fees. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of estimated fees and to withdraw an application
description: Be informed of estimated fees before a permit or response is issued and withdraw the application or request, paying only costs already incurred.
quote: The health data applicant shall be informed about the option to withdraw the health data access application or health data request.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Fee information and withdrawal of application; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before enforcement measures by health data access bodies
rightholder: health data users and health data holders
description: Be notified of findings of non-compliance and state views before measures such as permit revocation, exclusion or periodic penalties; receive the measures and reasons (Art. 63(5)).
exercise: Within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks.
quote: The health data access body concerned shall give the health data user or health data holder concerned the opportunity to state their views within a reasonable period that shall not exceed four weeks.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Right to be heard before enforcement; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural safeguards and judicial remedies against fines by health data access bodies
rightholder: health data holders and health data users
addressee: Member State (courts) / health data access body
description: Administrative fines imposed by health data access bodies are subject to due process and effective judicial remedies.
quote: shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Procedural safeguards and judicial remedies against fines. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for access to electronic health data for secondary use
description: Submit a health data access application for permitted purposes (Art. 53(1)), e.g. research, innovation, education or improving care.
exercise: Single application for multi-country access (Art. 67(3)); purposes (a)-(c) reserved to public bodies (Art. 53(2)).
quote: A natural or legal person may submit a health data access application for the purposes referred to in Article 53(1) to a health data access body.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Application to a health data access body; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to a decision on a health data access application within three months
description: Obtain a decision issuing or refusing a data permit within three months of a complete application, be notified of incompleteness and allowed to complete it, and be told reasons for any extension.
exercise: Extension by up to three months with notice and reasons.
quote: the health data access body shall issue or refuse a data permit within three months of receiving a complete health data access application
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Decision deadline on applications; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to a justification for refusal of a data permit
description: Receive a justification when a data permit is refused.
quote: Where the health data access body refuses to issue a data permit, it shall provide a justification for that refusal to the health data applicant.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Justification of refusal; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data users to access and process data under a data permit
description: Access and process the permitted electronic health data in a secure processing environment in accordance with the data permit.
exercise: Data made available within two months of receipt from holders (Art. 68(7)).
quote: Health data users shall have the right to access and process the electronic health data in a secure processing environment in accordance with the data permit issued to them
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Access and processing only inside a secure processing environment; requires own analysis software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to request extension or amendment of a data permit
description: Request a one-time extension of the data permit (max. further 10 years) and, where needed, an amendment (Art. 68(13)); request storage of the dataset formula.
exercise: Justified request at least one month before expiry; possible higher fees.
quote: That duration may be extended once, for a period which does not exceed 10 years, at the request of the health data user
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Extension or amendment of a permit by request; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit a health data request for anonymised statistical results
description: Request a response in anonymised statistical format only (no access to underlying data).
exercise: Assessment within 3 months and response within a further 3 months where possible (Art. 69(4)).
quote: The health data applicant may submit a health data request for the purposes referred to in Article 53 with the aim of obtaining a response only in an anonymised statistical format.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Plain request answered only with anonymised statistics; result may be a data file or a plain table. Result criterion conflicts.

right: Right to opt out of secondary use of one's electronic health data
addressee: Member State / health data access bodies / health data holders
description: Opt out at any time, without reasons and reversibly, from processing of one's personal electronic health data for secondary use.
exercise: Accessible opt-out mechanism (Art. 71(2)); effective for permits approved after opt-out (Art. 71(3)); MS may provide public-interest exceptions (Art. 71(4)); complaints go to GDPR supervisory authority (Arts 65, 81(4)).
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to opt out at any time, and without providing any reason, from the processing of personal electronic health data relating to them for secondary use
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Object is processing of electronic health data, but the national opt-out mechanism may be non-electronic and a plain statement suffices. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right of health data holders to apply for trusted health data holder status (Member-State option)
addressee: Member State / health data access body
description: Where a Member State establishes the procedure, apply to be designated a trusted health data holder handling applications under a simplified procedure.
exercise: Must provide a compliant secure processing environment, expertise and guarantees.
quote: Member States may establish a procedure whereby health data holders can apply to be designated as trusted health data holders
notes: Member-State option. Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Application for trusted data holder status; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a health data access body
rightholder: natural and legal persons whose rights or interests are negatively affected
description: Complain about matters under Chapter IV (secondary use) to a health data access body.
exercise: Individually or collectively; informed of progress and decision (Art. 81(2)); accessible tools (Art. 81(3)); opt-out complaints transmitted to GDPR supervisory authority (Art. 81(4)); representation possible (Art. 101).
quote: collectively, with a health data access body, provided that their rights or interests are negatively affected
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Complaint to health data access body. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data holders to be informed of third-country access requests
addressee: digital health authorities, health data access bodies, health data users
description: Be informed of a third-country administrative authority's request to access their non-personal health data before it is complied with.
exercise: Except for law-enforcement requests, for as long as necessary.
quote: shall inform the health data holder about the existence of a request of a third-country administrative authority to access its data before complying with that request
tl_reason: Notification of a third-country access request; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by infringements of the EHDS Regulation
rightholder: any natural or legal person that suffered material or non-material damage
description: Claim compensation for material or non-material damage resulting from an infringement of the Regulation.
exercise: In accordance with Union and national law.
quote: Any natural or legal person that has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation
tl_reason: Compensation for damage. Test: yes.

right: Right to be represented by a not-for-profit body
addressee: Member State (digital health authorities, health data access bodies)
description: Mandate a not-for-profit data-protection organisation to lodge a complaint or exercise complaint rights under Arts 21 and 81 on one's behalf.
quote: he or she shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association, constituted in accordance with national law, having statutory public interest objectives
tl_reason: Mandating a not-for-profit body to complain; delegation without technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to online registration with automatic, immediate issue of a registration number
description: Register a unit online, free of charge where possible, and receive a registration number automatically and immediately on submitting the declaration.
exercise: Declaration-based (Art. 4(3)(a)); one registration procedure per unit (Art. 4(3)(d)); documents may be submitted digitally (Art. 4(6)); further information requests do not delay the number (Art. 5(3)).
quote: allow for the automatic and immediate issue of a registration number, that shall not include personal data, for a specific unit upon the submission by the host of the information
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Law requires online registration with automatic number issue, but the declaration and registration number are non-technical. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts.

right: Right to appeal in registration procedures
description: Use effective appeal mechanisms against decisions in registration procedures.
exercise: Per national law.
quote: registration procedures are subject to effective appeal mechanisms within the Member State
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Appeal against registration decisions. Test: yes.

right: Right to update registration information and remove a unit from the registry
description: Update registration information and documentation, and remove a unit from the registry (Art. 4(3)(g)); data are kept at most 18 months after removal (Art. 5(5)).
exercise: Through the technical means provided by the Member State.
quote: technical means are in place to enable a host to update information and documentation
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Law requires technical means to update or remove registry entries, but the updates and result are non-technical. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts.

right: Right to request reuse of registration information for subsequent registrations
description: Ask that information already provided be reused for later registrations (once-only).
quote: Member States shall ensure that hosts are able to request that the information or documentation provided pursuant to Article 5(1) and (2) be reused for the purposes of subsequent registrations.
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Once-only reuse of submitted information by plain request; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before suspension or withdrawal of a registration number
description: Receive written notice with reasons of an intended suspension or withdrawal, be heard and rectify, and receive the decision and order in writing.
exercise: Within a reasonable period specified by the authority.
quote: The host shall be given the opportunity to be heard and, where appropriate, to rectify the information or documentation in question within a reasonable period
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Right to be heard before suspension; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to reinstatement of a suspended registration number
description: Have a suspended registration number reinstated once the information has been rectified and verified.
quote: the competent authorities shall reinstate the registration number
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Reinstatement of registration number; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of redress mechanisms
description: Be informed of available redress against rectification requests, suspension, withdrawal and reinstatement decisions.
quote: The competent authority shall inform the hosts about the mechanisms for redress available in relation to the steps taken pursuant to paragraphs 2 to 6 and 8.
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Information on redress; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of hosts to be informed of the results of platform random checks
description: Be informed without undue delay of random-check results concerning incorrect declarations, misuse or invalid registration numbers.
quote: Online short-term rental platforms shall inform, without undue delay, the competent authorities and the hosts of the results of the random checks
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Platform informs host of random-check results; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of hosts to be informed of applicable registration procedures
description: Be adequately informed by the platform whether a registration procedure applies in a given area.
quote: Online short-term rental platforms shall inform hosts adequately of the applicability in a given area of registration procedures
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Platform informs host about registration procedures; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to the Digital Services Coordinator about platform compliance (via DSA Chapter IV)
rightholder: recipients of the platform service (hosts, guests)
description: Because DSA Chapter IV applies to enforcement of Arts 7(1) and 8, recipients can use the DSA complaint mechanism (DSA Art. 53) about a platform's compliance-by-design duties.
exercise: Complaint to the DSC of the Member State where the recipient is located or established (DSA Art. 53).
quote: For the purposes of the enforcement of Article 7(1) and Article 8 of this Regulation, Chapter IV of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 shall apply
notes: Derived by cross-reference to DSA Chapter IV; whether DSA Art. 54 compensation also extends to these duties is unclear and not recorded.
table_entry: Regulation on data collection for short-term rental
tl_reason: Complaint to Digital Services Coordinator. Test: yes.

right: Right of a complainant to communicate only with the authority where the complaint was lodged
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: In cross-border cases the complainant may deal exclusively with the supervisory authority where they lodged their complaint.
quote: A complainant shall have the possibility to communicate exclusively with the supervisory authority with which the complainant has lodged his or her complaint
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural right to deal with one authority; no technical element.

right: Right to a decision on a complaint subject to judicial review
description: Handling of every complaint must end with a decision that can be challenged under GDPR Art. 78.
quote: The handling of a complaint shall always lead to a decision that is subject to an effective judicial remedy
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural right to a reviewable decision; no technical element.

right: Right to have a cross-border complaint admitted on harmonised minimum information
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: A cross-border complaint is admissible if it contains only the listed information (identity, controller, description of infringement); no further information may be required, and prior contact with the controller is not needed except for rights requiring a request (Art. 4(3)).
exercise: National administrative modalities continue to apply.
quote: No information additional to that referred to in the first subparagraph shall be required in order for a complaint concerning cross-border processing to be admissible.
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Admissibility on minimum information; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of inadmissibility and its reasons within two weeks
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: If a complaint lacks required information, the authority must declare it inadmissible within two weeks and give reasons.
exercise: Within two weeks of receipt.
quote: within two weeks of receiving that complaint, declare that complaint inadmissible and inform the complainant of the reasons thereof
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural information on inadmissibility; no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of transmission of the complaint to the lead authority
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: Be informed when an admissible complaint is transmitted to the presumed lead supervisory authority (within six weeks).
exercise: Within six weeks of receipt.
quote: no later than six weeks from the receipt of that complaint and inform the complainant of that transmission
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint transmission; no technical element.

right: Right to object to early resolution of a complaint
description: Where an authority considers a rights-related complaint devoid of purpose because the infringement ended, the complainant is informed of this and its consequences and may object within four weeks.
exercise: Objection within four weeks of being informed; otherwise the complaint is deemed resolved (Art. 5(3)-(4)).
quote: of the possibility for the complainant to submit an objection to the early resolution within four weeks of receiving such information
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural objection to early resolution; no technical element.

right: Right of parties under investigation to be heard in the simple cooperation procedure
description: Before a draft decision under the simple cooperation procedure, parties under investigation must be given the right to be heard.
exercise: Under national procedural law of the lead authority.
quote: the parties under investigation are provided with the right to be heard
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard of a party under investigation; procedural.

right: Right of the complainant to make views known in the simple cooperation procedure
addressee: lead supervisory authority / authority with which complaint lodged
description: Before a draft decision under the simple cooperation procedure, the complainant must be given an opportunity to make his or her views known.
exercise: Under applicable national procedural law.
quote: the complainant is provided with an opportunity to make his or her views known
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Complainant's views in the procedure; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to a judicial remedy against inaction based on procedural time limits
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Failure to submit a draft or revised draft decision or adopt a final decision within the Regulation's time limits is taken into account in determining whether a complaint was not handled for GDPR Art. 78(2) actions.
exercise: Linked to time limits in this Regulation and GDPR Art. 65(6).
quote: In determining whether a supervisory authority has not handled a complaint pursuant to Article 78(2) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, consideration shall be given to whether that supervisory authority
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against inaction; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard before a complaint is rejected or dismissed
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged / lead supervisory authority
description: Be informed of the reasons for a preliminary view to reject or dismiss a complaint and make views known in writing before a draft decision.
exercise: Time limit set by lead authority: 3 to 6 weeks; told consequences of not responding.
quote: provide the complainant with the opportunity to make his or her views known in writing and inform the complainant of the consequences of not making his or her views known
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard before rejection; procedural.

right: Right to be heard on new elements in a revised draft decision rejecting a complaint
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: If a revised draft decision rejecting or dismissing a complaint raises new elements, the complainant must be able to comment before it is submitted.
exercise: Per the Art. 16 procedure.
quote: provide the complainant with the opportunity to make his or her views known on such new elements
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard on new elements; procedural.

right: Right to be informed of available judicial remedy on rejection of a complaint
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: When a complaint is fully or partially rejected or dismissed, the complainant must be informed of the judicial remedy under GDPR Art. 78.
quote: shall inform the complainant of the judicial remedy available to him or her in accordance with Article 78 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Procedural information on judicial remedy; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard on preliminary findings
description: Receive preliminary findings setting out all facts, evidence, legal assessment, envisaged corrective measures and fine factors, and reply in writing or at an oral hearing; the draft decision may rely only on matters the party could comment on (Art. 19(7)).
exercise: Time limit 3 to 6 weeks from notification; access to file at notification (Art. 19(6)).
quote: within which those parties may provide their views in writing, or hold a hearing within the same time-limit in order to hear the views of the parties under investigation orally
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard on preliminary findings; procedural.

right: Right of the complainant to receive preliminary findings and comment
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: Receive the (non-confidential) preliminary findings in a complaint-based case and make views known in writing.
exercise: Time limit 3 to 6 weeks; subject to Arts 24-25 on access and confidentiality.
quote: the supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall provide the complainant with those preliminary findings
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Receipt of preliminary findings and comment; procedural.

right: Right of the complainant to receive the final decision
addressee: lead supervisory authority / authority with which complaint lodged
description: Receive a non-confidential version of the final decision (operative part and grounds) or a summary, and on request always the non-confidential version.
exercise: On request for the full non-confidential version.
quote: the complainant shall, upon request, be provided with a version of the decision referred to in the first subparagraph that includes its operative part in full
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Receipt of the final decision; procedural.

right: Right to be heard on a revised draft decision finding an infringement
description: If a revised draft decision finding an infringement raises new elements, the parties under investigation must be able to make their views known.
exercise: Time limit 3 to 6 weeks.
quote: provide the parties under investigation with the opportunity to make their views known on such new elements
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard on revised draft decision; procedural.

right: Right of access to the administrative file
rightholder: party under investigation; complainant where the decision may adversely affect them
addressee: lead supervisory authority (party) / authority with which complaint lodged (complainant)
description: On request, obtain access to the administrative file (inculpatory and exculpatory evidence) to exercise the right to be heard, excluding inter-authority correspondence and confidential information.
exercise: On request; access to relevant and reasoned objections where necessary to defend rights (Art. 24(4)).
quote: Upon request of a party under investigation, or a complainant where the decision is liable to affect his or her interests adversely, the lead supervisory authority shall grant access
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Access to administrative file; procedural right in administrative proceedings.

right: Right to claim confidential treatment of submitted information
rightholder: party under investigation, complainant or third person
description: Identify submitted information as confidential (trade secrets or other confidential information) with reasons, so that it is not disclosed to other parties.
exercise: Provide full and proposed non-confidential versions; substantiate within the time limit set (max. 6 weeks, Art. 25(5)).
quote: A party under investigation, a complainant, or a third person submitting information that it considers to be confidential shall clearly identify that information, giving reasons
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Claim of confidential treatment; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to be heard by the EDPB before a binding dispute resolution decision
rightholder: party under investigation; complainant where the decision could reject or dismiss the complaint
description: Before the Board adopts an Art. 65(1)(a) GDPR binding decision, make views known in writing on new factual or legal elements and the objections it intends to follow.
exercise: Time limit up to two weeks (Art. 28(2)).
quote: the Board shall provide the party under investigation, or, where the Board’s decision could result in a full or partial rejection or dismissal of a complaint, the complainant
notes: Applies to cross-border GDPR cases; Chapters III-IV apply to complaints lodged/investigations opened after 2 April 2027 (Art. 36).
tl_reason: Right to be heard by the EDPB; procedural.

right: Right of third parties to adapt reused interoperability solutions
rightholder: third party reusing an interoperability solution
addressee: sharing Union entity or public sector body
description: A third party reusing a shared interoperability solution may adapt it to its own needs, unless third-party IP prevents it; if the solution was published, the adapted version must be published too.
quote: A Union entity or public sector body, or a third party reusing an interoperability solution, may adapt it to its own needs
notes: The obligation to share on request runs only between Union entities and public sector bodies (Art. 4(1)).
tl_reason: Adapting reused interoperability software requires building, but it is a permission with no mechanism owed to third parties. Holder and mechanism criteria conflict.

right: Right to give feedback on the Interoperable Europe portal
rightholder: citizens, businesses (in particular SMEs) and civil society organisations
description: Access the portal free of charge and provide feedback on its published content.
quote: allowing citizens, businesses, in particular SMEs, and civil society organisations to provide feedback on the published content
tl_reason: Feedback only via the Interoperable Europe portal, but feedback and its result are plain text. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts.

right: Right to register as a member of the Interoperable Europe Community
rightholder: public and private stakeholders, civil society organisations and academic contributors resident or registered in a Member State
description: Register on the portal as a member of the Interoperable Europe Community, which advises the Board; membership is unlimited in time and can be revoked only for proportionate and justified reasons (Art. 16(3)).
exercise: Registration on the Interoperable Europe portal.
quote: academic contributors residing or having their registered office in a Member State may register on the Interoperable Europe portal as members of the Interoperable Europe Community
tl_reason: Registration as community member only on the portal; membership itself is non-technical. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts.

right: Right to removal of personal data from the SEP register/database
rightholder: persons whose personal data are in the SEP register or database
description: Request removal of personal data after the SEP expires or is removed.
exercise: After 18 months from expiry/removal.
quote: Upon request, personal data may be removed from the register or the database after 18 months from the expiry of the SEP or removal of the SEP from the register.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Removal of personal data from the electronic SEP register/database: object digital, but a plain request works and no mechanism is required. Conflict: test yes.

right: SEP holder's right to be notified of changes
rightholder: SEP holder and its EU legal representative
description: Be notified of any change in the register or database concerning its SEP.
quote: shall be notified of any change in the register or the database when that change concern a particular SEP.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Notification of register changes to SEP holder; plain information, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to registration certificates and certified copies
description: Obtain registration certificates or certified copies of register/database data on request.
exercise: Possibly subject to a fee.
quote: Upon request, the competence centre shall issue registration certificates or certified copies of the data and documents in the register or the database.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Certificates and certified copies on request; no electronic channel mandated, plain documents. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholder's right to redaction of confidential information
rightholder: stakeholders (SEP holders, implementers, their agents and associations)
description: Have confidential information redacted before publication or transmission.
exercise: Reasoned request.
quote: Upon a reasoned request by a stakeholder, any confidential information shall be redacted in a non-confidential format before the competence centre publishes or transmits such information.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Redaction of confidential information on reasoned request; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Implementer's right to notify a standard
description: Notify a standard (and its specifications and implementations) to the competence centre if SEP holders fail to do so, triggering the register entry.
exercise: Also for existing standards within the transitional window (Art. 66(2)).
quote: any implementer may notify, to the competence centre the information referred to in paragraph (1)
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Implementer's notification of a standard; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholders' right to comment on standard notifications
description: Submit comments on published standard notifications.
exercise: Within 30 days of publication.
quote: Stakeholders may submit their comments to the competence centre within 30 days from the publication of the list.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Comments on standard notifications; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holders' right to a conciliator for an aggregate royalty
rightholder: SEP holders representing at least 20% of a standard's SEPs
description: Request appointment of a conciliator to mediate a joint aggregate royalty submission.
exercise: Within 90 days of publication of the standard or 120 days of first EU sale of a new implementation (Art. 17(2)).
quote: representing at least 20 % of all SEPs of a standard may request the competence centre to appoint a conciliator from the roster of conciliators
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Request for conciliator on aggregate royalty; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a non-binding expert opinion on aggregate royalty
description: Request a non-binding expert opinion on a global aggregate royalty for a standard; other stakeholders may request to participate (Art. 18(5)).
exercise: Within 150 days of publication or first EU sale of new implementations; panel appointed if participation thresholds are met (Art. 18(6)).
quote: A SEP holder or an implementer may request the competence centre for a non-binding expert opinion on a global aggregate royalty.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Request for expert opinion on aggregate royalty; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to register a SEP
description: Register a SEP for a standard listed in the register.
exercise: Within 6 months of the register notice or of grant; fee payable (Art. 20(3), (6)); unregistered SEPs cannot be enforced nor royalties claimed (Art. 24).
quote: Upon request of a SEP holder the competence centre shall register any patent in force in one or more Member States
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: SEP registration on request and fee; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holder's right to correct its registration
description: Request correction of its SEP registration or database information.
exercise: Free of charge (Art. 23(9)).
quote: A SEP holder may request a correction of its SEP registration or of the information contained in the database by filing an appropriate request to the competence centre
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Correction of own SEP registration on request; administrative procedure, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Third party's right to request correction of a SEP registration
description: Request correction of a SEP registration or database information, with reasons and independent evidence.
exercise: SEP holder invited to correct; suspension if not corrected (Art. 23(3)-(5)); free of charge.
quote: Any third party may request the competence centre to correct a SEP registration or information contained in the database.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Third-party request to correct a SEP registration with evidence; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal suspension of a SEP registration
rightholder: SEP holder whose registration was suspended
description: Challenge a suspension of the SEP from the register before the EUIPO Boards of Appeal (same under Art. 22(5)).
exercise: Within 2 months of suspension.
quote: may apply before the Boards of Appeal of the EUIPO for a decision on the matter.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Appeal against suspension to Boards of Appeal; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holder's right to remove a SEP from the register
description: Request removal of its SEP for expiry, invalidation, a final non-essentiality judgment or a negative essentiality check.
exercise: Not while an essentiality check is pending (Art. 25(2)).
quote: A SEP holder may request the removal of its registered SEP from the register and the database, on the following grounds:
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Request to remove SEP from register on legal grounds; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holder's right to propose SEPs for essentiality checks
description: Voluntarily propose up to 100 SEPs per standard per year for essentiality checks.
exercise: Fees borne by the requesting holder (Art. 63(3)(c)).
quote: Each SEP holder may voluntarily propose annually up to 100 registered SEPs from different patent families to be checked for essentiality
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Proposing SEPs for essentiality checks; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Implementer's right to propose SEPs for essentiality checks
description: Voluntarily propose up to 100 registered SEPs per standard per year to be checked for essentiality.
exercise: Fees borne by the requesting implementer (Art. 63(3)(c)).
quote: Any implementer may voluntarily propose annually up to 100 registered SEPs from different patent families to be checked for essentiality
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Implementer proposing SEPs for essentiality checks; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholder's right to request review of an essentiality check
addressee: EUIPO competence centre; Boards of Appeal
description: Request review of an essentiality check or peer evaluation for breach of formal or procedural requirements or the code of conduct, and appeal the outcome to the Boards of Appeal (Art. 29(11)).
exercise: Within 1 month of publication of the reasoned opinion; appeal within 2 months.
quote: at the request of any stakeholder submitted within one month from the publication of the reasoned opinion or final reasoned opinion
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Review of essentiality check and appeal; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Stakeholders' right to submit observations on essentiality
description: Submit written observations on the essentiality of SEPs selected for checks; the SEP holder may reply (Art. 30(2)).
exercise: Within 90 days of publication of the sampled SEPs.
quote: any stakeholder may submit to the competence centre written observations concerning the essentiality of the selected SEPs.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Written observations on essentiality; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holder's right to be heard in the essentiality check
description: Be told why a SEP may not be essential and submit observations or an amended claim chart; receive the reasoned opinion (Art. 31(6)).
exercise: Within the period set.
quote: the competence centre shall inform the SEP holder of any such reasons and specify a period within which the SEP holder may submit its observations, or submit an amended claim chart.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Right to be heard in essentiality check; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SEP holder's right to request peer evaluation
description: Request re-examination of a preliminary negative essentiality finding by a peer evaluator.
exercise: Before the observation period expires; fee (Art. 63(3)(c)).
quote: the SEP holder may request peer evaluation before the expiry of the period to submit its observations
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Request for peer evaluation; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to initiate a FRAND determination
description: Start a structured FRAND conciliation before the EUIPO; required before suing on a SEP or seeking a court FRAND determination; may continue unilaterally if the other side does not engage (Art. 38(3)-(4)).
exercise: Written request (Art. 36); max 9 months (Art. 37); limitation periods suspended (Art. 37(2)).
quote: The FRAND determination in respect of a standard and implementation for which an entry in the register has been created, shall be initiated by any of the following persons:
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Initiating FRAND conciliation by written request; dispute procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a provisional financial injunction pending FRAND determination
rightholder: either party to the FRAND determination
description: Ask a national court for a provisional injunction of a financial nature against the alleged infringer while the FRAND determination runs.
exercise: Excludes seizure of property and goods.
quote: is without prejudice to the possibility for either party to request, pending the FRAND determination, the competent court of a Member State to issue a provisional injunction of a financial nature
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Provisional financial injunction from national court; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SME right to limit territorial scope of FRAND determination
rightholder: SMEs party to a FRAND determination
description: Request that the FRAND determination be limited territorially instead of covering a global licence.
quote: SMEs that are parties to the FRAND determination may request to limit the territorial scope of the FRAND determination.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: SME request to limit territorial scope of FRAND determination; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to object to the FRAND determination on legal grounds
description: Object that the conciliator cannot make a FRAND determination (e.g. prior binding determination or agreement).
exercise: No later than the first written submission.
quote: A party may submit an objection stating that the conciliator is unable to make a FRAND determination on legal grounds
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Objection on legal grounds in FRAND determination; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Complying party's options where the other party fails to engage
rightholder: complying party to a FRAND determination
description: Ask the conciliator to make a FRAND proposal on the available information or to terminate the procedure.
quote: the complying party may ask the conciliator to take one of the following actions:
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Options of complying party in FRAND procedure; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate FRAND determination for parallel third-country proceedings
description: Have the FRAND determination terminated where the other party has started parallel proceedings in a third country.
quote: shall terminate the FRAND determination upon the request of any other party.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Termination for parallel third-country proceedings; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request an oral hearing
description: Obtain an oral hearing in the FRAND determination.
exercise: Within 20 days after reasoned proposals.
quote: If the conciliator considers it necessary or if a party so requests, an oral hearing shall be held
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Request for oral hearing; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to confidentiality of submitted information
description: Have specific information withheld from the other party, providing a non-confidential version (Art. 54(3)).
quote: A party may request the conciliator that specific information in a submitted document is kept confidential.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Confidentiality of submitted information; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment on the conciliator's reasoned proposal
description: Submit observations and suggest amendments to the conciliator's reasoned FRAND proposal.
quote: Either party may submit observations to the proposal and suggest amendments to the proposal by the conciliator
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Comments on conciliator's proposal; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to reject the conciliator's FRAND proposal
description: Decline the reasoned FRAND proposal by written declaration, terminating the procedure and opening court proceedings.
exercise: Notice of termination enables court action (Art. 56(4)).
quote: a written declaration is made by a party not to accept the reasoned proposal of a determination of FRAND terms and conditions by the conciliator
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Rejecting FRAND proposal by written declaration; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to use the conciliator's report in court
description: Receive the conciliator's report (Art. 57(1)) and file it in court proceedings against the other party notwithstanding any procedural bar.
quote: Either party to the FRAND determination may file the report in any proceedings before a competent court of a Member State against the other party to the FRAND determination
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Filing conciliator's report in court; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: SMEs' right to free training and support on SEPs
description: Obtain free training and support on SEP-related matters.
quote: The competence centre shall offer training and support on SEP related matters for micro, small and medium-size enterprises free of charge.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Free SEP training and support for SMEs; support entitlement, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to use the EUIPO Alternative Dispute Resolution Centre
description: Use the EUIPO ADR Centre to settle disputes relating to intellectual property rights.
quote: Any natural or legal person may use the services of the Centre for settling disputes relating to intellectual property rights
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted.
tl_reason: Use of EUIPO ADR Centre for IP disputes; dispute procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to the registered design
rightholder: designer or successor in title (employer for designs made by employees, Art. 11(3))
description: The entitlement to the registered national design right vests in the designer or successor in title; jointly developed designs vest jointly.
exercise: Apply for registration with the national IP office (Art. 25).
quote: The right to the registered design shall vest in the designer or the designer’s successor in title.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Recast Directive: transposition by 9 Dec 2027 (Art. 36); until then the equivalent rule of Directive 98/71/EC applies where one existed.
tl_reason: Entitlement to a national registered design; IP right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of any person to seek invalidity on absolute grounds
rightholder: any natural or legal person; groups representing manufacturers, producers, service suppliers, traders or consumers
description: Seek a declaration of invalidity of a registered national design that is not a 'design' or does not meet Arts 3-8 (novelty, individual character etc.).
exercise: Before national courts, or an administrative invalidity procedure where the Member State provides one (Art. 31(3)); possible after lapse/surrender (Art. 14(8)).
quote: The grounds for invalidity provided for in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b), may be invoked by the following:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Recast Directive: transposition by 9 Dec 2027 (Art. 36); until then the equivalent rule of Directive 98/71/EC applies where one existed.
tl_reason: Invalidity action on absolute grounds before court or office; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of the entitled person to seek invalidity of a design held by a non-entitled holder
rightholder: person entitled to the design right under national law
description: Have a registered design declared invalid where a court/authority decided the holder is not entitled to it.
quote: may be invoked solely by the person who is entitled to the design right under the law of the Member State concerned.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Recast Directive: transposition by 9 Dec 2027 (Art. 36); until then the equivalent rule of Directive 98/71/EC applies where one existed.
tl_reason: Invalidity action by entitled person; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of holders of earlier rights to seek invalidity of a conflicting design
rightholder: applicant for or holder of the earlier right; persons entitled to exercise it; authorised licensee
description: Have a registered design declared invalid for conflict with a prior design, use of an earlier distinctive sign, or unauthorised use of a copyright work.
exercise: Barred where the holder expressly consented to registration (Art. 14(7)); administrative procedure under Art. 31(3)(c) where provided.
quote: The grounds for invalidity provided for in paragraph 1, points (e), (f) and (g), may be invoked solely by the following:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Recast Directive: transposition by 9 Dec 2027 (Art. 36); until then the equivalent rule of Directive 98/71/EC applies where one existed.
tl_reason: Invalidity action based on earlier rights; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Exclusive right conferred by a registered design
rightholder: holder of a registered (national) design right
description: Use the design exclusively and prevent unauthorised use, incl. making, marketing, importing/exporting, stocking and creating or sharing files that enable the product to be made (Art. 16(2)).
exercise: Infringement action under national law; subject to limitations (Art. 18), repair clause (Art. 19), exhaustion (Art. 20); renewable up to 25 years (Art. 10).
quote: The registration of a design shall confer on its holder the exclusive right to use it and to prevent any third party not having the consent of the holder from using it.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Recast Directive: transposition by 9 Dec 2027 (Art. 36); until then the equivalent rule of Directive 98/71/EC applies where one existed.
tl_reason: Exclusive design right (covers 3D-printing files as a topic) enforced by infringement action; no mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to stop infringing goods in transit from third countries
rightholder: holder of a registered design right
addressee: third parties bringing goods into the Member State; customs authorities
description: Prevent third parties from bringing into the Member State, in the course of trade, non-released goods bearing an identical or essentially indistinguishable design.
exercise: Via customs proceedings under Reg (EU) 608/2013; lapses if it is shown the holder cannot prohibit marketing in the country of final destination.
quote: The holder of a registered design right shall be entitled to prevent all third parties from bringing products, in the course of trade, from third countries into the Member State
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. New in the recast.
tl_reason: Stopping infringing goods in transit via customs; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Repair clause: freedom to use component-part designs to repair complex products
rightholder: any person (makers, sellers and users of spare parts, repairers)
description: Use a registered design of a component part of a complex product solely to repair it and restore its original appearance without infringing the design right.
exercise: Manufacturers/sellers must duly inform consumers of origin (Art. 19(2)); no duty to guarantee end use (Art. 19(3)); Member States with existing protection may keep it for designs applied for before 8 Dec 2024 until 9 Dec 2032 (Art. 19(4)).
quote: Protection shall not be conferred on a registered design which constitutes a component part of a complex product upon whose appearance the design of the component part is dependent
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. New EU-wide repair clause; transitional period to 9 Dec 2032 in some Member States.
tl_reason: Repair clause is an IP limitation for physical spare parts; no digital mechanism involved. Test: yes.

right: Consumer right to information on the origin of spare parts used for repair
addressee: manufacturer or seller of the component part
description: Be informed, by a clear and visible indication on the product or in another appropriate form, of the commercial origin and manufacturer of a repair part to choose between competing parts.
exercise: Condition for relying on the repair clause; no separate sanction stated.
quote: who failed to duly inform consumers, through a clear and visible indication on the product or in another appropriate form, about the commercial origin, and the identity of the manufacturer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Origin information on the product or in another appropriate form; no technical mechanism or ability required. Test: yes.

right: Right of prior use
rightholder: third party who in good faith commenced use or serious preparations in the Member State before the filing/priority date
addressee: holder of the registered design right
description: Continue to exploit an independently created design falling within a later registered design for the purposes for which use had begun or been prepared.
exercise: Must establish good-faith prior use/preparations and no copying.
quote: A right of prior use shall exist for any third party who can establish that, before the date of filing of the application
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. New in the recast.
tl_reason: Prior-use defence against later registered design; legal entitlement, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request deferment of publication
description: Request that publication of the registered design be deferred for up to 30 months from filing/priority.
exercise: Request when filing; holder may ask for earlier publication (Art. 30(4)) or prevent publication by surrender (Art. 30(5)).
quote: The applicant for a registered design may request, when filing the application, that the publication of the registered design be deferred for a period of up to 30 months
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Request for deferred publication when filing; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to renew the registration
rightholder: holder of the registered design right or person authorised by law or contract
description: Renew the registration for further 5-year periods up to 25 years on request and payment of fees.
exercise: Within 6 months before expiry, or 6 months after with an additional fee (Art. 32(3)).
quote: Registration of a design shall be renewed at the request of the holder of the registered design right or any person authorised to request the renewal by law or by contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Renewal on request and fee payment; administrative procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of upcoming expiry
rightholder: holder of the registered design right
description: Be informed of the expiry of the registration at least 6 months beforehand.
exercise: Office not liable for failure, which does not affect expiry.
quote: The office shall inform the holder of the registered design right of the expiry of the registration at least six months before the date of such expiry.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Office notice of upcoming expiry; plain information, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment on an envisaged Union compulsory licence
rightholder: right holder, potential licensees and other persons with an interest
description: Submit comments on voluntary licensing prospects, the need for the licence and its content including remuneration, after the Commission's public notice.
exercise: Within the time set in the notice; right holder's opportunity to comment is a condition for grant (Art. 4(d)).
quote: an invitation to the right holder, to potential licensees and to other persons with an interest to submit comments to the Commission and the competent advisory body
tl_reason: Comments on envisaged compulsory licence after public notice; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to individual information and to comment before grant
description: Be informed individually that a licence is being considered, receive the envisaged content and a summary of the advisory opinion, and comment.
exercise: Within the time limit set by the Commission.
quote: the Commission shall inform the right holder and potential licensees concerned individually, as soon as reasonably practicable, of the fact that it is considering granting a Union compulsory licence
tl_reason: Individual information and comment before grant; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right holder's right to adequate remuneration
description: Receive adequate remuneration from the compulsory licensee, reflecting the economic value of the licensed activities.
exercise: Amount and timeframe set by the Commission in the licence (Arts 8(e), 9(2)).
quote: The licensee shall pay an adequate remuneration to the right holder.
tl_reason: Adequate remuneration from compulsory licensee; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Licensee's right to a refund if the patent is not granted
description: Recover remuneration paid where the licensed published application does not lead to a patent (or utility model).
quote: the right holder shall refund to the licensee the remuneration paid under this Article.
tl_reason: Refund of remuneration if patent not granted; monetary claim, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right holder's right to be informed of export suspensions
description: Be informed when customs suspend export of products possibly made under a Union compulsory licence, and of non-compliance findings (Art. 12(5)).
quote: The Commission shall inform the right holder and, where appropriate, the licensee.
tl_reason: Information on export suspensions; plain information, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of a Union compulsory licence
description: Request the Commission to review and modify the licence.
exercise: Reasoned request.
quote: The Commission shall review the Union compulsory licence upon a reasoned request by the right holder or the licensee
tl_reason: Reasoned request for review of compulsory licence; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of newly covered right holders to be informed and comment
rightholder: right holders to be added to the licence
description: Be informed and comment (on voluntary licensing and remuneration) before the licence is extended to their rights.
quote: it shall inform the right holders concerned and invite them to submit comments on the possibility of reaching, within a reasonable timeframe, a voluntary licensing agreement with the licensee
tl_reason: Information and comment before extension of licence; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to notification of termination or expiry
description: Be notified when a licence is terminated or expires, with advance notice where appropriate.
quote: the Commission shall notify the right holder and the licensee accordingly.
tl_reason: Notification of termination or expiry; plain information, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for a Union-wide compulsory licence for pharmaceutical exports
description: Apply to the Commission for a single Union compulsory licence to make and export pharmaceutical products to countries with public-health problems where activities span several Member States.
exercise: Application meeting Art. 6(3)(a)-(f) of Reg 816/2006, specifying the Member States concerned.
quote: Any person may submit an application for a Union compulsory licence referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article.
notes: Amending provision.
tl_reason: Application for Union compulsory licence for pharmaceutical exports; administrative market-access procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Licensee's right to be heard before fines
description: Be heard and submit observations before the Commission imposes fines or periodic penalty payments.
exercise: At least 14 days to submit observations (Art. 19(2)); decision only on points the parties could comment on (Art. 19(3)).
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to Article 15 or 16, the Commission shall give the licensee the opportunity to be heard on the alleged infringement.
tl_reason: Right to be heard before fines; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to the Commission's file
description: Access the Commission's file under negotiated disclosure terms, excluding confidential and internal documents.
quote: They shall be entitled to have access to the Commission’s file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
tl_reason: Access to Commission file under negotiated disclosure; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Third parties' right to be heard in fine proceedings
rightholder: natural or legal persons with sufficient interest
description: Be heard in fine proceedings on application by showing a sufficient interest.
quote: Applications to be heard on the part of such persons shall be granted, where those persons show a sufficient interest.
tl_reason: Third parties heard in fine proceedings on showing interest; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to Court review of fines
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Challenge fines or periodic penalty payments before the Court, which may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Art. 261/263 TFEU action.
quote: the Court has unlimited jurisdiction to review Commission decisions imposing fines or periodic penalty payments.
tl_reason: Court review of fines; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Consent before a security clearance procedure is started
rightholder: individual applying for authorisation to access EU classified information
addressee: Security Authority of the Union institution or body
description: The institution must obtain the individual's written consent before sending the security clearance questionnaire to the national security authority.
exercise: Written consent to the institution's Security Authority.
quote: must seek the written consent of the individual for the security clearance procedure before sending a completed security clearance questionnaire
notes: Proposal text; may change. Found in Annex II (outside the articles).
tl_reason: Written consent before security clearance; administrative, no technical element.

right: Right to report vulnerabilities in Union entities' systems to CERT-EU as coordinated vulnerability disclosure coordinator
rightholder: natural or legal persons reporting a vulnerability
description: CERT-EU acts for Union entities as the CVD coordinator equivalent to national CSIRT coordinators under NIS2 Art. 12(1), so persons can report vulnerabilities affecting Union entities to CERT-EU and obtain its intermediation.
exercise: Report to CERT-EU; NIS2 Art. 12(1) features (trusted intermediary, anonymity) apply by reference.
quote: act on the part of Union entities as the equivalent of the coordinator designated for the purposes of coordinated vulnerability disclosure pursuant to Article 12(1) of Directive (EU) 2022/2555
notes: Derived by cross-reference to NIS2 Art. 12(1)
tl_reason: Vulnerability report to CERT-EU by message; digital topic, technology incidental to channel. Test: yes.

right: Right of public access to CERT-EU documents
rightholder: any natural or legal person (per Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001)
description: Requests for public access to documents held by CERT-EU are handled under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001, with consultation of the Union entities or Member States whose documents are concerned.
exercise: Application under Regulation 1049/2001.
quote: shall apply with regard to requests for public access to documents held by CERT-EU
notes: Right granted by reference to Regulation 1049/2001
tl_reason: Access to documents under Reg. 1049/2001; ordinary application.

right: Right of users to be informed of measures against significant incidents and cyber threats
rightholder: users of the affected network and information systems of Union entities
description: Users potentially affected by a significant incident or significant cyber threat must be told, without undue delay, of measures or remedies they can take and, where appropriate, of the threat itself.
exercise: Communication by the Union entity where applicable, without undue delay.
quote: Union entities shall communicate, without undue delay, to the users of the network and information systems affected
tl_reason: Plain communication of measures against incidents or threats; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Automatic security updates with opt-out and option to postpone
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Where applicable, products must install security updates automatically by default, but users get a clear, easy opt-out, notification of available updates and the option to postpone them temporarily.
exercise: Through the product's settings.
quote: with a clear and easy-to-use opt-out mechanism, through the notification of available updates to users, and the option to temporarily postpone them
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I (Art. 13(1)); main obligations apply from 11 Dec 2027 (Art. 71).
tl_reason: Opt-out and postponement of automatic updates through product settings; the right is a setting in the software. Test: no.

right: Opt-out from security logging of internal activity
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Security-related recording and monitoring of internal activity (access to or modification of data, services or functions) must come with an opt-out for the user.
exercise: Through the product's settings.
quote: including the access to or modification of data, services or functions, with an opt-out mechanism for the user
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Opt-out from security logging via product settings; the right exists only as a software option. Test: no.

right: Secure, permanent deletion of all data and settings
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Users must be able to securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently, and transfer data securely where it can be moved to other products.
exercise: Through the product's functions.
quote: provide the possibility for users to securely and easily remove on a permanent basis all data and settings
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Product must offer a function to remove all data and settings permanently; exercised only through it. Test: no.

right: Free security updates without delay
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Available security updates must be disseminated without delay and free of charge, with advisory messages on what users should do (business users of tailor-made products may agree otherwise).
quote: they are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed between a manufacturer and a business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, free of charge
notes: Vulnerability-handling requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Free security updates are software delivered to and installed on the device; cannot be fulfilled or used without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right of component maintainers to be informed of vulnerabilities and receive fixes
rightholder: person or entity manufacturing or maintaining an integrated component (incl. open-source maintainers)
description: When a manufacturer finds a vulnerability in an integrated component, including an open-source one, it must report it to whoever makes or maintains that component. It must also share any code or documentation it developed to fix it.
exercise: Report and, where available, code shared by the manufacturer, in machine-readable format where appropriate.
quote: report the vulnerability to the person or entity manufacturing or maintaining the component, and address and remediate the vulnerability
tl_reason: Vulnerability reports and fix code, possibly machine-readable, for component maintainers; using them means integrating code. Specialist holder. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to vulnerability handling and security updates during the support period
description: Throughout the support period, the manufacturer must handle the product's vulnerabilities effectively, including by providing security updates. The support period must match the expected use time and be at least five years, unless the product is expected to be used for less.
exercise: Security updates issued by the manufacturer during the support period.
quote: Without prejudice to the second subparagraph, the support period shall be at least five years.
notes: Several details are in Annex I, which is not in the enacting-terms extract: Part II(8) says security updates are free of charge (unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made B2B products); Part I(2)(c) says automatic security updates are on by default with an opt-out; Part I(2)(m) gives secure removal of data and settings.
tl_reason: Vulnerability handling through security updates during the support period; fulfilled only as software installed on the product. Test: no.

right: Right to continued availability of issued security updates
description: Each security update released during the support period must stay available for at least 10 years after issue, or for the rest of the support period if that is longer.
exercise: Download from the manufacturer.
quote: which has been made available to users during the support period, remains available after it has been issued for a minimum of 10 years or for the remainder of the support period
tl_reason: Issued updates must stay downloadable for 10 years; holder must find, download and install them. Test: no.

right: Right to free access to the latest version of a software product
description: If a manufacturer gives security support only for the latest substantially modified version, users of earlier versions must get that version free of charge and without extra costs to adapt their hardware or software environment.
exercise: Access provided by the manufacturer.
quote: provided that the users of the versions that were previously placed on the market have access to the version last placed on the market free of charge
notes: Condition on the manufacturer's choice to support only the latest version
tl_reason: Free access to the latest software version; holder must obtain and install it. Test: no.

right: Right to a single point of contact for communicating with the manufacturer and reporting vulnerabilities
description: Users can contact the manufacturer directly and quickly through a single point of contact, for example to report vulnerabilities, using their preferred means of communication, not only automated tools.
exercise: Via the single point of contact listed in the user information (Annex II).
quote: The single point of contact shall allow users to choose their preferred means of communication and shall not limit such means to automated tools.
tl_reason: Single point of contact using the user's preferred means, not only automated tools; plain communication. Test: yes.

right: Right to user information and instructions
description: Products must come with clear information and instructions for secure installation, operation and use (Annex II), in a language users understand. These must stay available, and accessible online if published there, for at least 10 years or for the support period if longer.
exercise: On paper or electronically, with the product.
quote: Manufacturers shall keep the information and instructions to the user set out in Annex II at the disposal of users and market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years
tl_reason: Instructions on paper or electronically; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to know the end date of the support period at purchase
description: At the time of purchase, the end date of the support period (at least month and year) must be clear and easy to find, and where applicable shown on the product, its packaging or by digital means.
exercise: Shown at the time of purchase.
quote: the end date of the support period referred to in paragraph 8, including at least the month and the year, is clearly and understandably specified at the time of purchase
tl_reason: Support end date shown at purchase on product, packaging or digitally; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified when the product reaches end of support
description: Where technically feasible, users must receive a notification that their product has reached the end of its support period.
exercise: Notification shown to the user.
quote: manufacturers shall display a notification to users informing them that their product with digital elements has reached the end of its support period
notes: Only where technically feasible
tl_reason: Notification must be displayed by the product software; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to be informed of the manufacturer's cessation of operations
addressee: manufacturer; importer (Art 19(8)) and distributor (Art 20(6)) where they become aware of it
description: Before a manufacturer stops operating and can no longer comply, it must tell users of its products by any means available and as far as possible. Importers and distributors must do the same if they learn of the cessation.
exercise: Notice by any means available, as far as possible.
quote: the users of the relevant products with digital elements placed on the market, of the impending cessation of operations
tl_reason: Notice of cessation by any available means; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
description: Once aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident, the manufacturer must inform affected users, and where needed tell them what mitigation and corrective measures they can take. If the manufacturer does not do so in time, the CSIRT may inform users.
exercise: Information from the manufacturer, where appropriate in a structured, machine-readable format.
