quote: the manufacturer shall inform the impacted users of the product with digital elements, and where appropriate all users, of that vulnerability or incident
notes: Under Art 69(3), also covers products placed on the market before 11 Dec 2027. Art 24(3) extends it to open-source software stewards.
tl_reason: Plain notice possible, but mitigation measures require technical action and information may be machine-readable. Conflict: result only sometimes technical.

right: Right to voluntarily report vulnerabilities, cyber threats, incidents and near misses
addressee: CSIRT designated as coordinator or ENISA
description: Anyone can voluntarily report vulnerabilities and cyber threats in products with digital elements (Art 15(1)), and incidents or near misses (Art 15(2)), to a CSIRT or ENISA. The CSIRT then informs the manufacturer.
exercise: Via the single reporting platform (Art 16) to a CSIRT designated as coordinator or ENISA.
quote: Manufacturers as well as other natural or legal persons may notify any vulnerability contained in a product with digital elements as well as cyber threats
notes: Art 15(2) covers incidents and near misses in the same way.
tl_reason: Report via the platform or otherwise; channel incidental, but identifying vulnerabilities presupposes technical skill. Conflict: ability technical, mechanism incidental.

right: Right of reporters to confidentiality and protection from added obligations or liability
addressee: CSIRTs designated as coordinators and ENISA
description: Information from a person who reports is kept confidential. A voluntary report creates no new obligations for the reporter, and the mere act of reporting brings no increased liability (Art 17(4)).
exercise: Applies automatically to anyone who notifies under Art 14 or 15.
quote: voluntary reporting shall not result in the imposition of any additional obligations upon a notifying natural or legal person
notes: Without prejudice to criminal investigations. See also Art 17(4).
tl_reason: Confidentiality and no added liability for reporters; legal protection. Test: yes.

right: Right of manufacturers to request delayed dissemination of a sensitive notification
description: Given how sensitive the notified information is, a manufacturer can ask the CSIRT to delay passing its notification on to other CSIRTs, on justified cybersecurity grounds and only for as long as strictly necessary.
exercise: Request made with the notification; the CSIRT decides and must justify any withholding to ENISA.
quote: upon request by the manufacturer and in light of the level of sensitivity of the notified information as indicated by the manufacturer under Article 14(2), point (a)
notes: Linked to the Art 14 notifications, which apply from 11 Sep 2026. Related: CSIRT must consult the manufacturer before informing the public (Art 17(2)); ENISA adds vulnerabilities to the EU database in agreement with the manufacturer (Art 17(5)).
tl_reason: Manufacturer requests delayed dissemination; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of the manufacturer to consent to subcontracting by a notified body
description: A notified body may subcontract conformity-assessment activities or use a subsidiary only if the manufacturer agrees.
exercise: Manufacturer gives or withholds agreement.
quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the manufacturer.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 11 Jun 2026 (Art 71(2))
tl_reason: Manufacturer consent to subcontracting by a notified body; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Manufacturers can appeal notified-body decisions, such as refusing, restricting or withdrawing a certificate, through an appeal procedure that Member States must provide.
exercise: Appeal procedure under national law.
quote: Member States shall ensure that an appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies is available.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 11 Jun 2026 (Art 71(2))
tl_reason: Appeal against notified-body decisions; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to market surveillance authorities
description: Consumers can submit complaints about possible non-compliance. Authorities must tell them where to complain (Art 11 Reg (EU) 2019/1020) and how to reach mechanisms for reporting vulnerabilities, incidents and cyber threats.
exercise: Complaint to the national market surveillance authority.
quote: Market surveillance authorities shall inform consumers of where to submit complaints that could indicate non-compliance with this Regulation
tl_reason: Complaint to the market surveillance authority; ordinary complaint. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of economic operators in corrective measures
description: When authorities require corrective action, Art 18 of Reg (EU) 2019/1020 applies. Measures must state reasons, the operator must be told about available remedies, and the operator has the right to be heard.
exercise: Under Art 18 Reg (EU) 2019/1020 and national procedural law.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to the corrective actions.
notes: Art 54(8) also preserves these procedural rights
tl_reason: Procedural rights in corrective measures; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure is contested, the Commission must consult the economic operators concerned before deciding whether it is justified.
exercise: Consultation by the Commission.
quote: the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the relevant Member State and the economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure
notes: The Commission must also consult economic operators before Union-level measures (Arts 56(4), 57(4), 57(8)), and implementing acts are communicated to them (Arts 56(6), 57(10)).
tl_reason: Consultation in the Union safeguard procedure; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive
addressee: courts / administrative authorities of Member States
description: Qualified entities can bring representative actions under Directive (EU) 2020/1828 against infringements by economic operators that harm, or may harm, consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Representative action brought by a qualified entity.
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements by economic operators of provisions of this Regulation
notes: Art 67 adds the CRA to Annex I of Directive (EU) 2020/1828
tl_reason: Representative action by qualified entities; judicial remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right of suspects and accused persons to request a European Production or Preservation Order
rightholder: suspect or accused person (or their lawyer)
description: A suspect or accused person, or their lawyer, can request the issuing of a European Production or Preservation Order to obtain exculpatory electronic evidence.
exercise: Within the framework of defence rights under national criminal procedure.
quote: The issuing of a European Production Order or of a European Preservation Order may also be requested by a suspect or an accused person, or by a lawyer on that person’s behalf
tl_reason: Defence request for a production order through counsel; criminal procedure, holder handles nothing technical.

right: Right of controllers to be informed when their processor produces data
rightholder: controller on whose behalf data are processed
description: A processor that produces data under an order must inform the controller, unless the issuing authority requests confidentiality for as long as necessary.
exercise: Delay must be justified in the case file and the EPOC.
quote: the processor that stores or otherwise processes the data on behalf of the controller shall inform the controller about the production of the data
tl_reason: Controller informed by processor of production; plain B2B information, no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to receive orders in an accepted language
rightholder: addressee service provider (designated establishment or legal representative)
description: Certificates (EPOC/EPOC-PR) must be translated into an official language accepted by the addressee or of the Member State where it is located.
quote: the EPOC or the EPOC-PR shall be translated into an official language of the Union accepted by the addressee
tl_reason: Translation of orders for service providers; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to flag immunities, privileges or press-freedom concerns
description: If execution could interfere with immunities, privileges or press-freedom rules of the enforcing State, the provider informs the authorities, which must then decide whether to withdraw, adapt or maintain the order (also for preservation orders, Art. 11(4)).
exercise: Using the Annex III form.
quote: Where the addressee considers, based solely on the information contained in the EPOC, that the execution of the EPOC could interfere with immunities or privileges
tl_reason: Flagging immunities via a form; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to seek clarification of incomplete or erroneous orders
description: Where an EPOC is incomplete or contains manifest errors, the provider may seek clarification and its production obligations are suspended until clarification is given (for preservation orders, exempt if no reply within 5 days, Art. 11(5)).
exercise: Annex III form; authority must reply within 5 days.
quote: The obligations set out in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall not apply until such clarification or correction is provided by the issuing authority or the enforcing authority.
tl_reason: Seeking clarification of orders; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to invoke de facto impossibility
description: A provider unable to comply for reasons not attributable to it can explain the impossibility and be released from executing the order.
exercise: Annex III form; other non-compliance reasons under Art. 10(8).
quote: Where the addressee cannot comply with its obligation to produce the requested data because of a de facto impossibility due to circumstances not attributable to the addressee
tl_reason: Invoking impossibility; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of the production of one's data
rightholder: person whose data are being requested
description: The issuing authority must inform the person whose data were obtained under a European Production Order, including information on available remedies (Art. 13(3)).
exercise: Without undue delay; may be delayed, restricted or omitted under the conditions of Art. 13(3) Directive (EU) 2016/680.
quote: The issuing authority shall, without undue delay, inform the person whose data are being requested about the production of data on the basis of a European Production Order.
tl_reason: Authority informs person of data production; plain notice, no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to reimbursement of costs
description: Service providers may claim reimbursement of their costs from the issuing State where its national law provides this for similar domestic orders.
exercise: Under the issuing State's national rules (published by the Commission).
quote: The service provider may claim reimbursement of its costs from the issuing State, if that possibility is provided for in the national law of the issuing State for domestic orders in similar situations
tl_reason: Cost reimbursement; financial claim, no technical element.

right: Exemption of service providers from liability for good-faith compliance
description: Service providers cannot be held liable towards users or third parties for prejudice resulting exclusively from good-faith compliance with an EPOC or EPOC-PR.
exercise: Without prejudice to data protection obligations.
quote: service providers shall not be held liable in Member States for prejudice caused to their users or third parties that exclusively results from compliance in good faith with an EPOC or an EPOC-PR
tl_reason: Liability exemption; no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to object to enforcement of an order
description: In enforcement proceedings the provider must be informed of, and may object on, the limited grounds in Art. 16(4)-(5); the enforcing authority decides taking its information into account (Art. 16(6)).
exercise: Within the compliance/objection deadline notified by the enforcing authority.
quote: the possibility of objecting to the execution of the order concerned by invoking one or more of the grounds listed in paragraph 4, points (a) to (f), or in paragraph 5, points (a) to (e)
tl_reason: Objection in enforcement proceedings; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right to a judicial remedy against pecuniary penalties
description: Service providers can challenge in court a decision imposing a pecuniary penalty for non-compliance.
quote: An effective judicial remedy shall be available against a decision to impose a pecuniary penalty.
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against penalties; no technical element.

right: Right of service providers to raise a reasoned objection based on conflicting third-country law
addressee: issuing authority; competent court of the issuing State
description: A provider can object that compliance would conflict with third-country law; if the authority upholds the order, a court reviews it and execution is suspended pending review.
exercise: Reasoned objection within 10 days of receiving the EPOC (Annex III form); court may lift or uphold the order.
quote: Where an addressee considers that compliance with a European Production Order would conflict with an obligation under the applicable law of a third country, it shall inform the issuing authority
tl_reason: Reasoned objection on third-country law; procedural right, no technical element.

right: Right to an effective remedy against a European Production Order
rightholder: any person whose data were requested
description: Any person whose data were requested can challenge the order, including its legality, necessity and proportionality.
exercise: Before a court in the issuing State under national law (Art. 18(2)); same time limits as domestic cases (Art. 18(4)); without prejudice to GDPR/LED remedies.
quote: any person whose data were requested via a European Production Order shall have the right to effective remedies against that order
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against a production order; no technical element.

right: Right of suspects and accused persons to remedies during the criminal proceedings
addressee: criminal court in the issuing State
description: Where the data subject is a suspect or accused, they can seek effective remedies during the criminal proceedings in which the data are used.
quote: Where that person is a suspect or an accused person, such person shall have the right to effective remedies during the criminal proceedings in which the data were being used.
tl_reason: Remedies in criminal proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to defence and fair proceedings in assessing electronic evidence
addressee: issuing State and any Member State receiving the evidence
description: Courts assessing evidence obtained via a European Production Order must respect the rights of defence and the fairness of proceedings.
quote: shall ensure that the rights of defence and fairness of the proceedings are respected when assessing evidence obtained through the European Production Order
tl_reason: Defence and fair-trial guarantees; no technical element.

right: Protection against AI-generated intimate or sexual imagery made without explicit consent
addressee: providers and deployers of AI systems
description: AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit images, video or audio of an identifiable person are prohibited unless that person has given explicit, informed consent.
exercise: Prohibition applies to placing on the market/use where such generation is the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable without safeguards (Art. 5(1a)); breaches can be reported via Art. 85 complaint.
quote: without that person’s freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1); framed as a prohibition, the depicted person's consent is the only lawful basis.
tl_reason: Object is AI-generated imagery, but holder is not a user and acts only through plain consent or complaint. Object vs holder/ability conflict.

right: Right not to be subject to an adverse decision based solely on real-time remote biometric identification output
rightholder: person identified by real-time remote biometric identification
description: No decision producing an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output of a real-time remote biometric identification system used for law enforcement.
exercise: Safeguard within the authorisation regime for law-enforcement use; enforceable through national remedies.
quote: No decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output of the ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system.
tl_reason: Concerns decisions based on biometric-ID output, but safeguard is procedural; holder operates nothing. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of deployers to receive instructions for use of high-risk AI systems
description: Deployers must receive concise, complete, correct and clear instructions for use (provider identity, characteristics, limitations, human oversight, logs) enabling them to interpret outputs and use the system appropriately.
exercise: Instructions accompany the system in digital or other format; minimum content in Art. 13(3).
quote: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate digital format or otherwise that include concise, complete, correct and clear information
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Instructions explain an AI system and its logs, but may be any format and readable without technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of deployers and distributors to be informed of non-conformity and corrective actions
description: Where a high-risk AI system is not in conformity, the provider must take corrective action (fix, withdraw, disable, recall) and inform distributors and, where applicable, deployers, authorised representatives and importers.
exercise: Immediate information by the provider once it considers the system non-conforming.
quote: They shall inform the distributors of the high-risk AI system concerned and, where applicable, the deployers, the authorised representative and importers accordingly.
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Notice of non-conformity and corrective action; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of a new provider to information, technical access and assistance from the initial provider
rightholder: new provider (distributor, importer, deployer or third party that becomes provider)
addressee: initial provider of the AI system
description: A person who becomes provider of a high-risk AI system (e.g. by rebranding, substantial modification or change of purpose) can obtain from the initial provider technical documentation, information on known limitations and failure modes, and targeted technical access for testing.
exercise: Does not apply where the initial provider clearly specified that its system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system; IP and trade secrets protected (Art. 25(5)).
quote: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers and shall make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance
notes: Paragraph as amended (M1). Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Initial provider must give technical documentation and targeted technical access for testing; usable only technically. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of high-risk AI providers to contractually specified information and assistance from component suppliers
rightholder: provider of a high-risk AI system
addressee: third party supplying AI systems, models, tools, services or components
description: Providers of high-risk AI systems and their suppliers must agree in writing on the information, capabilities, technical access and assistance needed for the provider to comply with the Regulation.
exercise: Written agreement; does not apply to free and open-source components other than GPAI models; AI Office may recommend voluntary model terms.
quote: shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance based on the generally acknowledged state of the art
notes: B2B right. Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Contractual right to agreed information and technical access; exercised by negotiation, result partly technical. Mechanism vs exercise conflict.

right: Right of workers and their representatives to be informed before high-risk AI is used at the workplace
description: Before putting into service or using a high-risk AI system at the workplace, employers must inform workers' representatives and affected workers that they will be subject to it.
exercise: Prior information, in line with Union and national rules and practice on information of workers.
quote: deployers who are employers shall inform workers’ representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Information concerns workplace AI system, but delivered through ordinary worker information. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right not to be subject to an adverse decision based solely on post-remote biometric identification output
rightholder: person subject to post-remote biometric identification
description: Law enforcement authorities may not take a decision producing adverse legal effects on a person based solely on the output of a post-remote biometric identification system; each use requires judicial or administrative authorisation.
exercise: Authorisation ex ante or within 48 hours; data deleted if authorisation refused.
quote: no decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken by the law enforcement authorities based solely on the output of such post-remote biometric identification systems
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Concerns decisions based on biometric-ID output, but safeguard is procedural; holder operates nothing. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed of being subject to a high-risk AI system in decision-making
addressee: deployer of Annex III high-risk AI system
description: Natural persons must be told when a deployer uses an Annex III high-risk AI system to make, or assist in making, decisions about them.
exercise: For law-enforcement use, Art. 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies instead.
quote: that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
notes: Annex III systems only; applies from 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 113(c)(i), as amended).
tl_reason: Notice that high-risk AI is used; object digital but notice is plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to request extension of a notified body certificate
description: Providers may ask the notified body to extend the validity of a conformity certificate for further periods based on a re-assessment.
exercise: Request to the notified body; extension up to 5 years (Annex I) or 4 years (Annex III) per period.
quote: At the request of the provider, the validity of a certificate may be extended for further periods
tl_reason: Certificate extension request to notified body. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Providers can appeal notified-body decisions, including on certificates issued, suspended, withdrawn or restricted; the notified body must give reasons for such decisions.
exercise: Appeal procedure to be made available against notified body decisions.
quote: An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
tl_reason: Appeal against notified body decision. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed when interacting with an AI system
rightholder: natural persons interacting with an AI system
description: People must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system (e.g. a chatbot) unless this is obvious from the context.
exercise: Clear and distinguishable information at the latest at first interaction, meeting accessibility requirements (Art. 50(5)); law-enforcement exception.
quote: the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
tl_reason: Disclosure that one interacts with AI; object is software but notice is plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed of exposure to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation
rightholder: natural persons exposed to the system
addressee: deployer of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system
description: Persons exposed to an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system must be informed of its operation.
exercise: Information at the latest at first exposure (Art. 50(5)); exception for systems permitted by law for criminal investigations.
quote: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system
tl_reason: Notice of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation; object digital, notice plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed that content is a deep fake or AI-generated public-interest text
rightholder: natural persons exposed to the content
description: Deployers must disclose that image, audio or video deep fakes, and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, have been artificially generated or manipulated.
exercise: Disclosure at first exposure (Art. 50(5)); lighter disclosure for evidently artistic/satirical works; text exception where human editorial control applies.
quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
tl_reason: Deep-fake disclosure on digital content; label is plain but holder must interpret content. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to contest classification as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
description: A GPAI provider meeting the systemic-risk compute threshold may submit substantiated arguments that its model nonetheless does not present systemic risks.
exercise: Arguments submitted with the notification (within two weeks of meeting the threshold); Commission decides (Art. 52(3)).
quote: may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets that requirement, the general-purpose AI model does not present
tl_reason: Provider's submission against designation; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to request reassessment of a systemic-risk designation
rightholder: provider of general-purpose AI model designated with systemic risk
description: A provider whose model was designated as having systemic risk can request the Commission to reassess the designation on the basis of new reasons.
exercise: Reasoned request with objective, detailed and new reasons; at the earliest six months after the designation or a decision maintaining it.
quote: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk pursuant to paragraph 4, the Commission shall take the request into account
tl_reason: Reassessment request; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of downstream providers to information and documentation on general-purpose AI models
rightholder: providers of AI systems integrating a general-purpose AI model (downstream providers)
description: Downstream providers can obtain up-to-date information and documentation (at least Annex XII elements) to understand the model's capabilities and limitations and comply with their own obligations.
exercise: Subject to protection of IP and trade secrets; not applicable to free and open-source models without systemic risk (Art. 53(2)).
quote: draw up, keep up-to-date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems
tl_reason: Model documentation explains a digital system, but is a document usable without technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Respect of copyright holders' text-and-data-mining opt-out by general-purpose AI providers
description: GPAI providers must have a copyright policy and identify and comply with rightholders' machine-readable reservations of rights against text and data mining under Art. 4(3) CDSM Directive.
exercise: Rightholders express the reservation under Art. 4(3) Directive (EU) 2019/790; enforcement via AI Office and copyright law.
quote: identify and comply with, including through state-of-the-art technologies, a reservation of rights expressed pursuant to Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790
tl_reason: Holder must express a machine-readable TDM reservation that GPAI providers must respect. Test: no.

right: Right to written proof of sandbox activities and an exit report
rightholder: provider or prospective provider participating in an AI regulatory sandbox
description: Sandbox participants can request written proof of activities successfully carried out in the sandbox and receive an exit report, usable to demonstrate compliance in conformity assessment.
exercise: Upon request to the competent authority; exit report published only with agreement of provider and authority (Art. 57(8)).
quote: Upon request of the provider or prospective provider of the AI system, the competent authority shall provide a written proof of the activities successfully carried out in the sandbox.
tl_reason: Written proof of sandbox activities. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for an AI regulatory sandbox and receive a decision within three months
rightholder: provider or prospective provider of an AI system
description: Sandboxes must be open to any applying provider meeting transparent and fair eligibility and selection criteria, with a decision within three months; access is free of charge for SMEs and start-ups (Art. 58(2)(d)).
exercise: Application to the national competent authority; may apply in partnership with deployers (Art. 58(2)(b)).
quote: that AI regulatory sandboxes are open to any applying provider or prospective provider of an AI system who fulfils eligibility and selection criteria, which shall be transparent and fair
notes: Principles to be implemented via Commission implementing acts.
tl_reason: Sandbox application; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Tacit approval of a real-world testing plan after 30 days
rightholder: provider or prospective provider of high-risk AI system
description: If the market surveillance authority does not answer within 30 days, the real-world testing and testing plan are deemed approved (unless national law excludes tacit approval).
exercise: Submit real-world testing plan to the MSA of the Member State where testing takes place.
quote: where the market surveillance authority has not provided an answer within 30 days, the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan shall be understood to have been approved
tl_reason: Tacit approval of testing plan; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to have AI predictions, recommendations or decisions reversed or disregarded during real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions
addressee: provider / prospective provider and deployer conducting the test
description: Outputs of a high-risk AI system tested in real-world conditions must be capable of being effectively reversed and disregarded; subjects must be told how to request this (Art. 61(1)(d)).
exercise: Request according to the arrangements communicated before consent (Art. 61(1)(d)).
quote: the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded.
tl_reason: AI outputs must be technically reversible, but holder requests by plain means. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to withdraw from real-world testing at any time
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions or legally designated representative
description: Test subjects may withdraw at any time by revoking consent, without detriment and without giving reasons.
exercise: Revocation of informed consent; does not affect activities already carried out.
quote: may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time by revoking their informed consent
tl_reason: Revoking informed consent to testing; plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to request deletion of personal data after withdrawing from real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions or legally designated representative
description: On withdrawal, test subjects may request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data.
exercise: Request to the provider or prospective provider.
quote: may request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data
tl_reason: Object is personal dataset, but deletion is requested plainly and needs no technical use. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to prior information and to refuse informed consent to real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions
description: Participation in real-world testing requires freely given informed consent after clear information on the nature, conditions, duration, rights (including refusal and withdrawal), reversal arrangements and contact details.
exercise: Consent obtained before participation; law-enforcement exception in Art. 60(4)(i).
quote: freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing and after their having been duly informed
notes: Art. 61(1)(c) expressly refers to 'their right to refuse to participate in, and the right to withdraw from' testing.
tl_reason: Prior information and refusal of consent; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to a copy of the documented informed consent
rightholder: subject of testing or legal representative
description: Test subjects receive a dated and documented copy of their informed consent.
quote: The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
tl_reason: Copy of documented consent; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Priority access of SMEs and start-ups to AI regulatory sandboxes
rightholder: SMEs, including start-ups, with registered office or branch in the Union
description: SMEs and start-ups meeting the eligibility and selection criteria get priority access to AI regulatory sandboxes.
exercise: Application to national sandbox; eligibility and selection criteria apply.
quote: provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes
tl_reason: Priority sandbox access; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of SMEs and deployers to advice and answers to queries on the AI Act
description: Member States must use or establish dedicated channels to advise SMEs, deployers and innovators and respond to their queries on implementing the Regulation, including sandbox participation.
exercise: Via national dedicated communication channels.
quote: to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation, including as regards participation in AI regulatory sandboxes
tl_reason: Advice from national channels. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified of the opening of an AI Office investigation
rightholder: operator (provider or deployer) of AI system under AI Office competence
description: When the AI Office opens an investigation into suspected non-compliance, it must notify the operator concerned.
quote: Upon starting such an investigation, the AI Office shall notify the operator of the AI system concerned.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1); covers AI systems within Art. 75(1).
tl_reason: Notification of investigation. Test: yes.

right: Right to offer binding commitments to the AI Office
description: An operator under investigation can offer commitments to ensure compliance, which the AI Office may make binding and close the case; rejection requires a reasoned decision.
exercise: Offered during proceedings under Art. 75a(2) or in the structured dialogue (Art. 75c(3)).
quote: the operator concerned offers commitments to ensure compliance with the relevant provisions of this Regulation, the AI Office may, by decision, make those commitments binding on the operator concerned
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Offering commitments in proceedings. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive preliminary findings before an AI Office non-compliance decision
description: Before a non-compliance decision, the AI Office must communicate its preliminary findings and the measures it is considering, allowing the operator to respond.
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to paragraph 1, the AI Office shall communicate its preliminary findings to the operator concerned.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Preliminary findings before decision. Test: yes.

right: Right to judicial review by the CJEU of AI Office decisions and fines
rightholder: operator subject to AI Office decision
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Operators can challenge AI Office decisions before the CJEU, which has unlimited jurisdiction over fines and periodic penalty payments and may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU; AI Office must indicate this right in decisions requesting information or ordering inspections (Art. 75a(3)-(4)).
quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the AI Office fixing a fine or periodic penalty payment pursuant to this Article.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Judicial review before CJEU. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights under Art. 18 of the Market Surveillance Regulation in AI Office proceedings
description: Operators supervised by the AI Office enjoy the market-surveillance procedural rights: reasoned decisions, notification with information on remedies, and a right to be heard.
exercise: See Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to operators subject to the AI Office’s competence pursuant to Article 75(1) of this Regulation
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Rights of defence and access to the AI Office file
description: Operators' rights of defence must be respected and they are entitled to access the AI Office file under negotiated disclosure, excluding confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Access in view of a possible Art. 75c(1) decision; AI Office decides disclosure terms if parties disagree.
quote: those operators shall be entitled to have access to the AI Office file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Rights of defence and file access. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasons and information on how to challenge a decision suspending or modifying real-world testing
description: Decisions suspending, terminating or requiring modification of real-world testing, and objections to a testing plan, must state reasons and explain how the provider can challenge them.
quote: the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection.
tl_reason: Reasons and challenge information. Test: yes.

right: Protection of confidential information, trade secrets and source code disclosed to authorities
rightholder: natural or legal person whose information is obtained
addressee: Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and others applying the Regulation
description: Persons whose information is obtained in applying the Regulation can rely on its confidentiality, in particular protection of IP rights, confidential business information, trade secrets and source code.
quote: the intellectual property rights and confidential business information or trade secrets of a natural or legal person, including source code
tl_reason: Confidentiality of information held by authorities. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of operators in national procedures on AI systems presenting a risk
description: Where an authority requires corrective action, withdrawal or recall of a risky AI system, the operator benefits from the procedural rights of Art. 18 Market Surveillance Regulation (reasons, remedies information, right to be heard).
exercise: Also preserved in the Union safeguard phase (Art. 79(8)).
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to the measures referred to in the second subparagraph of this paragraph.
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Right of operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure against an AI system is contested, the Commission must consult the operator(s) before deciding whether the measure is justified.
exercise: Commission decision within six months (60 days for Art. 5 cases).
quote: the Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State and the operator or operators
tl_reason: Consultation in safeguard procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of operators to be consulted and informed on measures against compliant but risky AI systems
description: Where a compliant high-risk AI system is found to present a risk, the Commission consults the operators on the national measures and communicates its decision to them (Art. 82(5)).
quote: The Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the Member States concerned and the relevant operators, and shall evaluate the national measures taken.
tl_reason: Consultation on national measures. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority
description: Anyone with grounds to consider that the AI Act has been infringed can complain to the relevant market surveillance authority.
exercise: Handled under the MSA's dedicated procedures in line with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020; without prejudice to other remedies.
quote: any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority
tl_reason: Complaint to market surveillance authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
addressee: deployer of Annex III high-risk AI system (except point 2)
description: A person subject to a decision based on the output of an Annex III high-risk AI system that has legal or similarly significant adverse effects on their health, safety or fundamental rights can obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the AI system's role and the main elements of the decision.
exercise: Request to the deployer; applies only where not otherwise provided under Union law (Art. 86(3)) and subject to Union/national exceptions (Art. 86(2)).
quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken
notes: Text says 'any affected person'; in practice depends on Annex III high-risk classification applying from 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 113(c)(i)).
tl_reason: Object is AI-assisted decision, but explanation is requested plainly and delivered in clear language. Object vs test conflict.

right: Protection of persons reporting infringements of the AI Act (whistleblowers)
description: Persons reporting breaches of the AI Act benefit from the Whistleblower Directive: reporting channels and protection against retaliation.
exercise: Via internal/external reporting channels under Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
notes: Cross-reference to Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
tl_reason: Whistleblower protection; ordinary reporting channels. Test: yes.

right: Right of downstream providers to lodge a complaint about general-purpose AI model providers
description: Downstream providers can complain to the AI Office alleging that a GPAI model provider infringed the Regulation.
exercise: Duly reasoned complaint indicating the provider's contact point, facts, provisions concerned and reasons.
quote: Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation.
tl_reason: Complaint to AI Office. Test: yes.

right: Right of GPAI providers with systemic risk to offer binding commitments
rightholder: provider of general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
description: During a structured dialogue, the provider may offer commitments to implement mitigation measures, which the Commission may make binding instead of imposing measures.
quote: the provider of the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk offers commitments to implement mitigation measures to address a systemic risk at Union level
tl_reason: Offering commitments. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of general-purpose AI model providers
description: GPAI providers enjoy the procedural rights of Art. 18 Market Surveillance Regulation (reasoned decisions, information on remedies, right to be heard) in Commission enforcement.
exercise: See Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model
notes: Article titled 'Procedural rights of economic operators of the general-purpose AI model'.
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural safeguards and effective judicial remedies against fines
rightholder: operator subject to national administrative fines
addressee: Member State / market surveillance authority / courts
description: The imposition of penalties and fines under the AI Act is subject to due process and effective judicial remedies.
exercise: Under national law.
quote: The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
tl_reason: Judicial remedies against fines. Test: yes.

right: Right of complainants to be associated with EDPS fining proceedings
description: Where the EDPS conducts proceedings against an EU institution under the AI Act, any complainants are closely associated with the proceedings.
quote: Complainants, if any, shall be associated closely with the proceedings.
notes: Proceedings concern Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
tl_reason: Association with EDPS proceedings; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of GPAI providers to be heard before a fine
description: Before fining a GPAI provider, the Commission must communicate its preliminary findings and give the provider an opportunity to be heard.
quote: the Commission shall communicate its preliminary findings to the provider of the general-purpose AI model and give it an opportunity to be heard
notes: Art. 101 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (Art. 113(b)).
tl_reason: Right to be heard before fine. Test: yes.

right: Right to CJEU review of Commission fines on GPAI providers
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: GPAI providers can challenge Commission fining decisions before the CJEU, which may cancel, reduce or increase the fine.
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine under this Article.
tl_reason: Judicial review before CJEU. Test: yes.

right: Right to product sustainability information (performance, repair and use)
description: Products covered by ecodesign delegated acts must come with information such as a repairability or durability score, carbon footprint, and how to install, use, maintain and repair the product. The information must be in a language customers easily understand.
exercise: Via the digital product passport, the product, its packaging, a label, a manual or a free website (Art 7(7)).
quote: information for customers and other actors on how to install, use, maintain and repair the product, in order to minimise its impact on the environment and to ensure optimum durability
notes: Only where set by a product-specific delegated act under Art 4. The labels are covered in Art 16.
tl_reason: Sustainability information via passport, label, manual or website; channel optional, content plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to consent before personal data are stored in the digital product passport
description: A customer's personal data may not be stored in a digital product passport without that customer's explicit consent.
exercise: Explicit consent, in line with Art 6 GDPR.
quote: personal data relating to customers shall not be stored in the digital product passport without their explicit consent
tl_reason: Object is a digital product passport dataset, but explicit consent can be given or refused by any means. Conflict: digital object, plain exercise.

right: Right of dealers and online marketplaces to obtain the DPP data carrier on request
rightholder: dealers and providers of online marketplaces
addressee: economic operator placing the product on the market
description: Dealers and online marketplaces can request a digital copy of the data carrier or unique product identifier, or a webpage link, so they can show the passport to remote customers.
exercise: Request; provided free of charge, promptly and within five working days.
quote: provide the digital copy referred to in point (a) or a webpage link free of charge promptly and in any event within five working days of receiving a request to do so.
notes: Only for products with a DPP required by delegated act
tl_reason: Digital copy of the data carrier or link to show the passport online; usable only technically. Business holder. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to free and easy access to the digital product passport
rightholder: customers, professional repairers, independent operators, refurbishers, remanufacturers, recyclers, civil society organisations, trade unions and other relevant actors
addressee: economic operator responsible for the DPP / DPP service providers
description: Customers and other value-chain actors can access the digital product passport free of charge and easily, within the access rights set for each product group.
exercise: Through the data carrier on the product or packaging, or the Commission web portal (Art 14). Customers must be able to access it before they are bound by a contract (Art 9(2)(e)).
quote: shall have free of charge and easy access to the digital product passport based on their respective access rights
notes: The scope of access is set by product-specific delegated acts. Art 11(e) keeps the DPP available even after the operator's insolvency.
tl_reason: Passport is a digital record reached via data carrier or web portal; access impossible without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to digital instructions accessible for the product's lifetime
description: Products must come with digital instructions that can be downloaded and saved and that stay online for the expected lifetime, and at least 10 years. Safety information relevant to health and safety must be on paper.
exercise: Via the DPP data carrier, or as indicated on the product or packaging.
quote: present the digital instructions in a format that makes it possible to download and save them on an electronic device so that the user can access them at all times
notes: Only for products covered by a delegated act
tl_reason: Digital, downloadable instructions, but a paper copy is available and content is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free paper copy of the digital instructions
description: A customer can ask for the digital instructions on paper, free of charge, at purchase or up to six months afterwards.
exercise: Request at purchase or within six months; provided free of charge within one month of the request.
quote: Where the customer so requests at the time of the purchase, or up to six months after that purchase, the manufacturer shall provide the digital instructions in a paper format, free of charge
notes: Only for products covered by a delegated act
tl_reason: Paper copy of instructions on request; non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit complaints about potential non-conformity to the manufacturer
description: Manufacturers must provide public communication channels, accessible to persons with disabilities, where customers can submit complaints or concerns about possible non-conformity. These are kept in a register.
exercise: By telephone, electronic address or a dedicated website section; complaints are kept in a register for up to five years.
quote: in order to allow customers to submit complaints or concerns regarding the potential non-conformity of products
notes: Only for products covered by a delegated act
tl_reason: Complaints by telephone, e-mail or website; plain channel. Test: yes.

right: Right of the authorised representative to terminate the mandate
description: The mandate must allow the authorised representative to terminate it if the manufacturer acts contrary to its obligations under the Regulation.
exercise: Termination of the written mandate.
quote: terminate the mandate if the manufacturer acts contrary to its obligations under this Regulation
tl_reason: Authorised representative terminates the mandate; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to access the DPP, product information and labels at the point of sale
description: Dealers must make sure that customers and potential customers can easily reach the product information, the digital product passport and the labels, including when buying at a distance.
exercise: At the dealer, including in distance selling (Art 31(1)-(3)).
quote: Dealers shall ensure that the digital product passport is easily accessible for customers and potential customers, including in the event of distance selling
notes: Only for products covered by a delegated act
tl_reason: Dealer must make passport, product information and labels accessible; passport part technical, labels plain. Conflict: mixed object.

right: Right of dealers to obtain product labels on request
addressee: economic operator placing the product on the market
description: Dealers can request printed labels or digital copies of the ecodesign label, free of charge.
exercise: Request; provided free of charge, promptly and within 5 working days.
quote: provide printed labels or digital copies of the label to the dealer free of charge, promptly and in any event within 5 working days of the dealer’s request
notes: Only where a delegated act requires a label
tl_reason: Printed labels or digital copies on request; printed labels suffice. Test: yes.

right: Right to manufacturer and product identification in distance-selling offers
addressee: economic operators selling at a distance
description: Online and other distance offers must clearly show the manufacturer's name and contact details, the EU-based responsible operator where the manufacturer is outside the EU, and information identifying the product, including a picture.
exercise: Displayed in the product offer.
quote: economic operators shall ensure that the product offer clearly and visibly provides at least the following information
notes: Only for products covered by a delegated act
tl_reason: Manufacturer and product identification shown in online offers; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to see the product's in-use data
description: Where a delegated act requires it, the product must record in-use data, such as energy consumption or performance, and make it visible to the end user.
exercise: On the product itself.
quote: record the in-use data and make such data visible to the end user
notes: Only where a delegated act sets a requirement under Art 4(6)(c)
tl_reason: Product must record in-use data and display it; data generated by the product exist only technically. Test: no.

right: Right to consent before remote collection of in-use data
description: Non-personal in-use data may be collected remotely over the internet for reporting to the Commission only after the end user has given explicit consent.
exercise: Explicit consent from the end user.
quote: following explicit consent being given by the end user to make those data available
notes: Only where a delegated act requires in-use data reporting
tl_reason: Consent before remote collection of in-use data over the internet; digital data flow, but consent by any means works. Conflict: digital object, plain exercise.

right: Right of manufacturers to obtain product information from supply chain actors
description: Where a delegated act so specifies, manufacturers can request relevant information on supplied products or services from their supply chain actors, free of charge. If no such information exists, suppliers must allow the manufacturer to assess the products and give access to documents or facilities.
exercise: Request to the supplier; free of charge.
quote: provide, upon request and free of charge, manufacturers, notified bodies and competent national authorities with available relevant information
notes: Only where a delegated act so specifies. B2B.
tl_reason: Supply-chain information on request; B2B information. Test: yes.

right: Right to refuse software/firmware updates that worsen product performance
description: Software or firmware updates may not degrade performance beyond the permitted margins unless the customer explicitly consents beforehand. Rejecting the update must not change anything.
exercise: Consent or refusal before the update is installed.
quote: except where the customer explicitly consents prior to the update to such worsening of performance. No change shall occur as a result of rejecting the update.
notes: Even with consent, an update may never make the product non-compliant. Also applies to products under Directive 2009/125/EC implementing measures (Art 79(2)).
tl_reason: Refusing performance-degrading software updates on one's device; exercised at the update prompt, object is software behaviour. Test: no.

right: Right of the client to consent to subcontracting by a notified body
description: A notified body may subcontract conformity-assessment activities or use a subsidiary only if the client agrees.
exercise: Client gives or withholds agreement.
quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the client.
tl_reason: Client consent to subcontracting by a notified body; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure against a product is contested, the Commission must consult the economic operators concerned before ruling on it, and must send them its decision.
exercise: Consultation by the Commission; decision communicated to the operator.
quote: the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the Member States and the relevant economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure
tl_reason: Consultation in the Union safeguard procedure; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by non-compliant products
addressee: manufacturer; or, if it is outside the EU, the importer or authorised representative; failing those, the fulfilment service provider
description: Consumers who suffer damage because a product does not comply with ecodesign requirements can claim compensation from the liable economic operator, following the cascade of manufacturer, then importer or authorised representative, then fulfilment service provider.
exercise: Claim against the liable operator under national civil procedure. Other consumer remedies remain available.
quote: the following economic operators shall be liable for damage suffered by the consumer
notes: Article headed 'Consumer redress'. Without prejudice to other Union or national remedies.
tl_reason: Compensation for damage from non-compliant products; monetary claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive
addressee: courts / administrative authorities of Member States
description: The ESPR is listed in Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828, so qualified entities can bring representative actions for injunctions or redress against infringements that harm consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Representative action brought by a qualified entity under national law transposing Dir (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: Point (27) of Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 is replaced by the following
notes: Amendment of Directive (EU) 2020/1828
tl_reason: Representative action by qualified entities; judicial remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right to request court-ordered disclosure of evidence on high-risk AI systems
addressee: national court; provider, person with provider obligations, or user of high-risk AI system
description: A (potential) claimant who was refused evidence about a high-risk AI system suspected of causing damage can ask the court to order its disclosure.
exercise: Prior request to the provider/user refused; claimant must present facts and evidence supporting plausibility of the claim; disclosure limited to what is necessary and proportionate.
quote: either upon the request of a potential claimant who has previously asked a provider
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Evidence is AI-system documentation and logs needing interpretation, but obtained through court procedure. Object vs exercise conflict.

right: Right to request preservation of evidence
description: A claimant can ask the court to order specific measures to preserve evidence about a high-risk AI system.
exercise: Application to the national court; proportionality applies.
quote: Member States shall ensure that national courts, upon the request of a claimant, are empowered to order specific measures to preserve the evidence mentioned in paragraph 1.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court-ordered preservation of evidence; holder handles nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right to request confidentiality measures for trade secrets in disclosed evidence
description: Parties can ask the court to take specific measures to preserve the confidentiality of trade secrets disclosed as evidence.
exercise: Duly reasoned request to the court.
quote: upon a duly reasoned request of a party or on their own initiative, to take specific measures necessary to preserve confidentiality
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Court confidentiality measures. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural remedies against disclosure or preservation orders
rightholder: person ordered to disclose or preserve evidence
description: Providers, users or others ordered to disclose or preserve evidence must have appropriate procedural remedies against such orders.
exercise: Under national procedural law.
quote: has appropriate procedural remedies in response to such orders
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Procedural remedies against orders. Test: yes.

right: Presumption of non-compliance with duty of care where defendant fails to disclose
description: If a defendant does not comply with a court order to disclose or preserve evidence, the court presumes the defendant's non-compliance with the relevant duty of care.
exercise: Rebuttable by the defendant.
quote: a national court shall presume the defendant’s non-compliance with a relevant duty of care
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Evidentiary presumption in court. Test: yes.

right: Right of the defendant to rebut the presumption of non-compliance
description: The defendant can rebut the presumption of non-compliance arising from failure to disclose evidence.
quote: The defendant shall have the right to rebut that presumption.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rebuttal in court. Test: yes.

right: Rebuttable presumption of causal link between fault and AI output
description: In fault-based damages claims, courts presume the causal link between the defendant's fault and the AI system's output (or failure to produce output) when fault is shown, influence on the output is reasonably likely and the output caused the damage.
exercise: Conditions in Art. 4(1)-(6) (stricter for high-risk providers/users, limited for non-high-risk and personal use).
quote: the causal link between the fault of the defendant and the output produced by the AI system or the failure of the AI system to produce an output
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Presumption of causality about AI output; a court rule, holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right of the defendant to rebut the presumption of causality
description: The defendant can rebut the presumed causal link.
quote: The defendant shall have the right to rebut the presumption laid down in paragraph 1.
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Rebuttal in court. Test: yes.

right: Representative actions for AI liability claims (amending Annex I Dir (EU) 2020/1828)
rightholder: qualified entities on behalf of consumers
description: Adds the AI Liability Directive to the Representative Actions Directive, allowing qualified entities to bring collective actions for its infringements.
exercise: Via Directive (EU) 2020/1828 procedures.
quote: on adapting non contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)
notes: Proposal text; withdrawn by the Commission in 2025, never adopted. Directive: would be exercised via national transposition law.
tl_reason: Representative actions by qualified entities. Test: yes.

right: Right to repair on the binding terms of a European Repair Information Form
description: Where a repairer issues the European Repair Information Form (free of charge, before the repair contract), its conditions such as price, repair time and replacement goods cannot be changed for 30 days, and the repairer must carry out the repair on those terms if the consumer accepts.
exercise: Request the form from the repairer (also via the European online platform); form on a durable medium; necessary diagnostic costs may be charged if the consumer is informed (Art. 4(3)).
quote: the conditions set out in the European Repair Information Form, the repairer shall be obliged to perform the repair service under those conditions
notes: Providing the form is optional for repairers ('may provide'); binding once supplied. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Repair form may be requested via online platform; terms plain, durable medium. Test: yes.

right: Right to have goods repaired by the manufacturer beyond the legal guarantee
addressee: manufacturer (or EU authorised representative, importer or distributor)
description: For goods covered by EU repairability requirements (Annex II product groups), the consumer can ask the manufacturer to repair them, free of charge or for a reasonable price and within a reasonable time, unless repair is impossible.
exercise: Request to the manufacturer; if established outside the EU, its authorised representative, then importer, then distributor (Art. 5(3)); manufacturer may lend a replacement or offer a refurbished good if repair is impossible (Art. 5(2)); may not refuse because of prior repair by others (Art. 5(7)).
quote: upon the consumer’s request, the manufacturer shall repair goods for which, and to the extent that, repairability requirements are provided for by Union legal acts listed in Annex II
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Plain request to manufacturer to repair goods; result physical. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose any repairer
description: Consumers may have their goods repaired by any repairer they choose, without prejudice to the manufacturer's repair obligation.
exercise: Supported by the ban on contractual clauses, hardware or software techniques impeding repair and on blocking compatible, second-hand or 3D-printed spare parts used by independent repairers (Art. 5(6)).
quote: Without prejudice to the obligation to repair under this Article, consumers may seek repair from any repairer of their choice.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Manufacturer must not use software locks against independent repair, but holder needs no technical ability; physical goods repairable without it. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to use the European online platform for repair free of charge
description: Consumers can use the national sections or national platforms of the European online platform for repair free of charge to find repairers and refurbishers, request the European Repair Information Form and report inaccuracies.
exercise: Via the platform (search functions, ERIF request, contact forms, Art. 7(6)).
quote: The use of national sections and national online platforms in the European online platform shall be free of charge for consumers.
notes: Common interface and national platforms due by 31 July 2027 (Art. 7(2)-(3)). Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Right is use of a public online platform, but searching repairers and requesting forms is non-technical. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right of repairers and refurbishers to register voluntarily on the European online platform
rightholder: repairers and, where applicable, sellers of refurbished goods, purchasers of defective goods for refurbishment and community-led repair initiatives
description: Repairers (and, where the Member State extends the scope, refurbishers and community repair initiatives) may register on the platform, update their information and show adherence to quality standards.
exercise: Registration via the national contact point or national platform; Member States may set access conditions such as prior approval or professional qualifications (Art. 9(2)).
quote: The registration shall be voluntary for repairers and, where applicable, sellers of goods that have been subject to refurbishment
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Registration on repair platform or via contact point; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to a 12-month extension of the legal guarantee when repair is chosen
description: Where the goods are repaired as the remedy for non-conformity, the seller's liability period is extended once by 12 months.
exercise: Automatic upon repair; Member States without fixed periods may instead ensure at least three years (inserted Art. 10(5a)).
quote: Where, in accordance with Article 13(2), repair takes place as the remedy to bring the goods into conformity, the liability period shall be extended once by 12 months.
notes: Applies to sales contracts concluded from 31 July 2026 (Art. 21). Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Guarantee extension after repair; automatic. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumer, environmental and professional organisations to take enforcement action
rightholder: organisations having a legitimate interest in protecting consumers or the environment; professional organisations (as determined by national law)
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Consumer, environmental and professional organisations with a legitimate interest can go to court or administrative bodies to ensure the transposing national rules are applied.
exercise: Standing determined by national law; representative actions also possible under Dir (EU) 2020/1828 (Art. 17).
quote: to take action under national law before the courts or competent administrative bodies of the Member State to ensure that the national provisions transposing this Directive are applied
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Public bodies also listed but not recorded.
tl_reason: Enforcement action by organisations. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the choice between repair and replacement and of the guarantee extension
description: Before providing a remedy, the seller must inform the consumer of the right to choose between repair and replacement and of the 12-month liability extension after repair.
exercise: Before the remedy is provided.
quote: Before the seller provides the remedy to bring the goods into conformity, the seller shall inform the consumer about the consumer’s right to choose between repair and replacement
notes: Applies to sales contracts concluded from 31 July 2026 (Art. 21). Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Information on remedy choice; plain. Test: yes.

right: Freedom to provide compliant political advertising services
description: Political advertising services that comply with the Regulation may not be prohibited or restricted, including geographically, on transparency grounds.
quote: The provision of political advertising services shall not be prohibited or restricted, including geographically, on grounds related to transparency
notes: Internal market clause.
tl_reason: Internal market freedom for service providers; no technical element.

right: Right of sponsors to non-discriminatory access to political advertising services
rightholder: sponsors; European political parties and political groups in the European Parliament
description: Providers may not restrict their services on discriminatory grounds based solely on the sponsor's place of residence or establishment, nor restrict European political parties or EP groups solely by place of establishment.
quote: shall not make the provision of their services subject to discriminatory restrictions solely based on the place of residence or establishment of the sponsor
notes: Applies from entry into force (Art. 30(2)). In the 3 months before an election or referendum, services are limited to EU sponsors (Art. 5(2)).
tl_reason: Non-discriminatory access for sponsors; market access, no technical element.

right: Right to identify political advertisements and their sponsor
description: Each political advertisement carries a prominent label stating it is political advertising, identifying the sponsor and any linked election or process, indicating targeting, and pointing to the transparency notice.
exercise: Labels adapted to the medium and kept in place when the advertisement is further disseminated.
quote: Those labels shall be prominent, shall enable individuals to easily identify a political advertisement as such
notes: Per-advertisement information, not individualised.
tl_reason: Labels on political ads are plain information adapted to the medium. Test: yes.

right: Right to access the transparency notice of a political advertisement
description: Persons can retrieve a transparency notice for each political advertisement with sponsor identity and contacts, funding amounts and origin, the linked election, targeting information, the notice mechanism and reach.
exercise: Included in the advertisement or easily retrievable at all times during publication; plain language, accessible, machine-readable when electronic.
quote: Transparency notices shall be included in each political advertisement or be easily retrievable at all times during the period of publication of the political advertisement.
notes: Per-advertisement information, not individualised.
tl_reason: Notice retrievable from online ads and machine-readable when electronic, but medium-neutral and plain; result only sometimes a digital artefact.

right: Right of sponsors to be informed of non-publication or discontinuation decisions
rightholder: sponsors and providers of political advertising services
description: Where a publisher refuses or stops publishing an advertisement because its transparency information cannot be completed or corrected, it must inform the sponsor or provider concerned.
exercise: Information without undue delay.
quote: The political advertising publisher shall without undue delay inform the sponsors or the providers of political advertising services concerned about any decisions under the fifth subparagraph
tl_reason: Information to sponsors on publisher decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to notify possibly non-compliant political advertisements
description: Anyone can notify a publisher that a political advertisement it published does not comply with the Regulation.
exercise: Free, user-friendly mechanism accessible from the transparency notice, electronic where possible; notification with reasons, identification of the ad, name and email.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall have in place the necessary mechanisms to enable natural or legal persons to notify them if a particular political advertisement that they have published
tl_reason: Notification mechanism electronic only where possible; a plain notice works. Test: yes.

right: Right to confirmation and information on the follow-up to a notification
rightholder: natural or legal persons who submitted a notification
