description: The notifier receives a confirmation of receipt, information on the follow-up given and on redress possibilities; the notification is examined diligently and, in the last month before an election, processed within 48 hours.
exercise: Confirmation without undue delay; VLOPs/VLOSEs must inform of follow-up, other publishers at least upon request (Art. 15(6)(b)); collective responses allowed (Art. 15(10)).
quote: Political advertising publishers shall without undue delay send a confirmation of receipt of the notification received pursuant to paragraph 1 to the natural or legal person who submitted it.
notes: Lighter duties for micro and SME publishers.
tl_reason: Confirmation and follow-up information are plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of sponsors to be informed of measures taken after notifications
rightholder: sponsors and providers of political advertising services
description: Sponsors and providers are told without undue delay of measures that affect the availability or presentation of their political advertisement following a notification.
quote: Political advertising publishers shall without undue delay inform the sponsors or providers of political advertising services concerned of any measures they take following notifications
tl_reason: Information to sponsors on measures taken; no technical element.

right: Right to a reasoned authority information request with redress information
rightholder: providers of political advertising services and sponsors
description: An authority's request for information must state its reasons (save for criminal investigations) and indicate the redress available to the provider and sponsor.
quote: information on the redress available to the relevant provider of political advertising services and to the sponsor of the political advertising service.
tl_reason: Reasoned authority information request; procedural.

right: Right of interested entities to obtain information on political advertising
rightholder: interested entities: vetted researchers, members of authorised civil society organisations, political actors, electoral observers, journalists
description: Independent researchers, civil society members, political actors, electoral observers and journalists can request the records and transparency information that providers must hold under Arts 9, 11 and 12.
exercise: Request; free of charge (reasonable fee only for significant costs); reply within one month at the latest; refusals of manifestly unclear or excessive requests must be reasoned with redress information.
quote: At the request of interested entities, providers of political advertising services shall transmit promptly and free of charge, and where technically possible in a machine-readable format
notes: Requesters must be independent from commercial interests.
tl_reason: Records sent machine-readable where technically possible, but a plain request works and holders are not the governed party; result only sometimes digital.

right: Right to give or withhold separate explicit consent to political ad targeting
description: Personal data may be used for targeting or ad-delivery of online political ads only with the data subject's explicit consent given separately for political advertising, and only on data collected from the data subject.
exercise: Explicit, separate consent under GDPR/EUDPR; withdrawable.
quote: the data subject has provided explicit consent within the meaning of Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 to the processing of personal data separately for the purpose of political advertising
notes: Profiling with special-category data is banned (Art. 18(1)(c)), as is targeting persons known to be at least one year under voting age (Art. 18(2)). Supervised by data protection authorities (Art. 22(1)).
tl_reason: Separate explicit consent for online political ad targeting is given or refused through the controller's interface choice. Test: no. Consistency pass: no interface function required; refusing or a letter still works.

right: Right not to be asked again for consent after an automated refusal
description: A data subject who has signalled by automated means that they do not consent to political-advertising processing may not be asked again unless circumstances change substantially.
exercise: Automated refusal signal.
quote: the data subject is not requested to consent if he or she has already indicated by automated means that he or she does not consent to data processing for political advertising purposes
tl_reason: Refusal signalled by automated means must be respected; presupposes software or settings that send the signal. Test: no.

right: Right to an equivalent alternative without political advertising
description: A data subject who refuses consent must be offered an equivalent way to use the online service without receiving political advertising.
quote: the data subject who does not give his or her consent is to be offered an equivalent alternative for using the online service without receiving political advertising.
tl_reason: An equivalent option to use the online service without political ads must exist in the service. Test: no.

right: Right to an explanation of political ad targeting
rightholder: individual concerned (recipient of a targeted political ad)
description: With a targeted political ad, the individual receives information on the logic and main parameters of targeting, including groups targeted, categories of data, targeting goals, use of AI systems, period and reach.
exercise: Provided with the political advertisement; accessible, plain language, machine-readable where feasible (Art. 19(4)).
quote: additional information necessary to allow the individual concerned to understand the logic involved and the main parameters of the techniques used
tl_reason: Targeting logic delivered with each online ad; holder retrieves and interprets parameters, not obtainable per ad by letter. Test: no.

right: Right to an easy means to exercise data protection rights from the political ad
description: Each targeted political ad must reference effective means to exercise GDPR/EUDPR rights, in particular to amend data or withdraw consent, including a link to an interface for doing so.
exercise: Link to an interface for exercising rights, provided with the ad or in the transparency notice.
quote: a reference to effective means to support individuals exercise their rights under Regulations (EU) 2016/679 or (EU) 2018/1725
tl_reason: Ad must link to an interface for amending data or withdrawing consent; the right is that interface function. Test: no.

right: Right of interested entities to obtain targeting information
description: Researchers, civil society members, political actors, electoral observers and journalists can request the Art. 19 targeting and ad-delivery information from controllers.
exercise: Request; free of charge.
quote: Controllers shall take appropriate measures to transmit to interested entities referred to in Article 17(2), at their request and free of charge, the information referred to in Article 19.
tl_reason: Targeting information may be machine-readable, but a plain request works and holders are not the governed party; result only sometimes digital.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a competent authority
description: Anyone can notify a competent authority of possible infringements, which must duly address it and, on request, inform the notifier of the follow-up.
exercise: Notification to the competent authority; addressed without undue delay in the last month before elections; transferred to the competent authority in another Member State where relevant.
quote: competent authorities shall duly address every notification of possible infringements of this Regulation and, upon request, inform the person or entity who made the notification of the follow up
notes: Data protection authorities are competent for Arts 18-19 (Art. 22(1)).
tl_reason: Notification to a competent authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Legal presumption of an employment relationship
addressee: digital labour platform; Member State courts/authorities
description: The contractual relationship with the platform is presumed to be an employment relationship where facts indicating direction and control are found; the platform bears the burden of proving otherwise.
exercise: Applies in all relevant administrative or judicial proceedings on employment status (not tax, criminal or social security unless national law extends it).
quote: The contractual relationship between a digital labour platform and a person performing platform work through that platform shall be legally presumed to be an employment relationship
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). For contracts ongoing on 2 Dec 2026 the presumption applies only from that date (Art. 5(6)).
tl_reason: Legal presumption of employment in proceedings. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to initiate proceedings to determine correct employment status
rightholder: persons performing platform work and their representatives
description: Persons performing platform work (and, per national law, their representatives) can start administrative or judicial proceedings to have their correct employment status determined, benefiting from the legal presumption.
exercise: Before national courts or competent authorities; the presumption must not increase the burden on the person (Art. 5(2)).
quote: Persons performing platform work and, in accordance with national law and practice, their representatives shall have the right to initiate the proceedings
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Initiating proceedings on employment status. Test: yes.

right: Protection against prohibited processing of personal data by automated systems
description: Platforms may not use automated systems to process data on emotional/psychological state, private conversations, data collected while not working, data to predict exercise of fundamental rights, data inferring sensitive characteristics, or biometric identification data.
exercise: Enforceable via data protection authority (Art. 24(1)) and redress (Art. 18); applies from the start of recruitment (Art. 7(2)).
quote: Digital labour platforms shall not, by means of automated monitoring systems or automated decision-making systems:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Covers all persons performing platform work, including the self-employed.
tl_reason: Prohibition on platform processing; holder operates nothing, enforced by complaint. Digital topic only. Test: yes.

right: Right to be consulted on the data protection impact assessment
rightholder: persons performing platform work and their representatives
description: When carrying out a DPIA of automated monitoring/decision-making systems, the platform must seek the views of persons performing platform work and their representatives.
exercise: During the GDPR Art. 35 DPIA process.
quote: shall seek the views of persons performing platform work and their representatives
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Consultation on DPIA; plain participation. Test: yes.

right: Right of workers' representatives to receive the DPIA
description: Workers' representatives are entitled to receive the data protection impact assessment of the platform's automated systems.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide the assessment as referred to in paragraph 1 to workers’ representatives.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Extended to representatives of non-worker persons by Art. 15.
tl_reason: Representatives receive DPIA document; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on automated monitoring and decision-making systems
description: Persons performing platform work must be informed, in writing and in plain language, of the use of automated monitoring and decision-making systems, the data and main parameters used, and grounds for account restriction, suspension, termination or refusal of payment.
exercise: Concise written form at the latest on the first working day and before changes affecting working conditions (Art. 9(2)-(3)).
quote: Member States shall require digital labour platforms to inform persons performing platform work, platform workers’ representatives and, upon request, national competent authorities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Object is software behaviour (automated systems, parameters), but information is written plain language, usable without technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to request information on automated systems at any time, including in comprehensive form
description: Persons performing platform work can request at any time the concise information on systems affecting them, and request comprehensive and detailed information on all relevant systems.
exercise: Request to the platform; written document, may be electronic.
quote: Upon the request of the persons performing platform work, digital labour platforms shall also provide them, in a comprehensive and detailed form, with the information referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Information on automated systems on request; object digital but plain request and written result. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of workers' representatives to comprehensive information on automated systems
description: Workers' representatives receive comprehensive and detailed information on all automated monitoring and decision-making systems, before their use, before changes, and at any time on request.
exercise: On request at any time, and proactively before use or changes.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide workers’ representatives, in a comprehensive and detailed form, with the information referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Extended to representatives of non-worker persons by Art. 15.
tl_reason: Representatives get detailed information on automated systems; object digital but result plain document. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of job candidates to information on automated systems used in recruitment
rightholder: persons undergoing a recruitment or selection procedure
description: Candidates must receive concise written information about the automated monitoring or decision-making systems used in the recruitment or selection procedure before it starts.
exercise: Before the start of the recruitment or selection procedure.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide the information referred to in paragraph 1 to persons undergoing a recruitment or selection procedure.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Candidates informed about automated recruitment systems; object digital, but concise written information. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to data portability, including ratings and reviews
description: Persons performing platform work can port personal data generated through their work (including ratings and reviews), using free tools provided by the platform, and can request direct transmission to a third party.
exercise: Free of charge; on request the platform transmits the data directly to a third party.
quote: Persons performing platform work shall have the right to the portability of personal data generated through their performance of work
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Complements GDPR Art. 20.
tl_reason: Port work data incl. ratings using platform-provided tools, direct transmission to third party; data must be moved elsewhere. Test: no.

right: Protection of human oversight staff against dismissal and adverse treatment
rightholder: persons charged by the platform with oversight and evaluation of automated systems
description: Staff charged with overseeing automated systems are protected from dismissal, disciplinary measures and other adverse treatment when exercising their oversight functions (including overriding automated decisions).
quote: Those persons shall enjoy protection from dismissal or its equivalent, disciplinary measures and other adverse treatment where they exercise their functions.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Employment protection of oversight staff. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on the evaluation of automated decisions
rightholder: persons performing platform work; platform workers’ representatives
description: Information on the platform's periodic (at least two-yearly) evaluation of the impact of automated decisions is transmitted to workers' representatives and made available to persons performing platform work on request.
exercise: On request for persons performing platform work; automatically for workers' representatives (who are also involved in the evaluation, Art. 10(1)).
quote: Digital labour platforms shall also make that information available to persons performing platform work and the national competent authorities upon their request.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Evaluation of automated decisions' impact on request; object concerns systems but result is a plain report. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to have account restriction, suspension or termination decided by a human
description: Decisions to restrict, suspend or terminate the contractual relationship or account of a person performing platform work, or of equivalent detriment, must be taken by a human being.
quote: or any other decision of equivalent detriment shall be taken by a human being.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Human must decide account restriction; duty fulfilled non-technically, holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right to an explanation of automated decisions and access to a contact person
description: Persons performing platform work can obtain, without undue delay, an oral or written explanation of any decision taken or supported by an automated decision-making system, and can discuss the facts and reasons with a designated contact person.
exercise: Request to the platform; clear and plain language; designated contact person with competence and authority.
quote: persons performing platform work have the right to obtain an oral or written explanation from the digital labour platform for any decision taken or supported by an automated decision-making system
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Not applicable to persons who are business users under Reg. 2019/1150 (Art. 11(5)).
tl_reason: Explanation of automated decision, oral or written in plain language; object digital, plain request works. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to a written statement of reasons for significant automated decisions
description: The platform must give a written statement of reasons for automated decisions to restrict, suspend or terminate the account, refuse payment, decide on contractual status or affect essential aspects of the relationship.
exercise: Without undue delay and at the latest on the date the decision takes effect.
quote: Digital labour platforms shall provide the person performing platform work with a written statement of the reasons for any decision taken or supported by an automated decision-making system
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Second subparagraph of Art. 11(1).
tl_reason: Written statement of reasons for automated decisions; object digital but result plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to request review of automated decisions
rightholder: persons performing platform work and representatives acting on their behalf
description: Persons performing platform work (or their representatives) can ask the platform to review an automated decision and receive a precise, substantiated written reply.
exercise: Request to the platform; written reply without undue delay and within two weeks of receipt.
quote: shall have the right to request the digital labour platform to review the decisions referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Request review of automated decision, written reply; object digital but plain request and reply. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to rectification of an infringing decision or adequate compensation
description: Where an automated decision infringes the person's rights, the platform must rectify it within two weeks or, if rectification is impossible, offer adequate compensation for the damage sustained.
exercise: Rectification without delay and within two weeks of adoption of the decision.
quote: Where such rectification is not possible, the digital labour platform shall offer adequate compensation for the damage sustained.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Rectification of decision or compensation; remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right to information, consultation and participation on health and safety risks of automated systems
description: Platform workers and their representatives must be informed, consulted and allowed to participate in evaluating occupational safety and health risks of automated systems and in preventive measures.
exercise: In accordance with Arts 10 and 11 of Directive 89/391/EEC.
quote: digital labour platforms shall ensure effective information and consultation and the participation of platform workers and/or their representatives
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Platform workers (employees) only.
tl_reason: Information and consultation on health and safety; labour procedure. Test: yes.

right: Access to effective reporting channels for violence and harassment
description: Platforms must provide effective reporting channels that platform workers can use to report violence and harassment.
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms take preventive measures, including providing for effective reporting channels.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Reporting channels for harassment, likely in-app but no technical form required; plain report. Test: yes.

right: Right of workers' representatives to information and consultation on automated systems
description: Workers' representatives must be informed and consulted on decisions likely to lead to the introduction of, or substantial changes in, automated monitoring or decision-making systems.
exercise: Under the arrangements of Directive 2002/14/EC.
quote: of workers’ representatives by digital labour platforms also covers decisions likely to lead to the introduction of or to substantial changes in the use of automated monitoring systems
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Consultation of representatives on management decisions; labour procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of workers' representatives to be assisted by an expert
description: Platform workers' representatives may be assisted by an expert of their choice in information and consultation procedures; the platform bears proportionate expert costs where it has more than 250 workers in the Member State.
exercise: Frequency of requests may be set by Member States.
quote: The platform workers’ representatives may be assisted by an expert of their choice
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Expert assistance in consultation. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of platform workers to direct information where there are no representatives
description: Where there are no workers' representatives, the platform must inform platform workers directly, in writing, of decisions likely to introduce or substantially change automated systems.
exercise: Written document, may be electronic; clear and plain language.
quote: Where there are no representatives of platform workers, Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms directly inform the platform workers concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Written plain-language information, optionally electronic, on decisions to introduce systems. Test: yes.

right: Representatives of non-worker persons may exercise representatives' data-protection rights
rightholder: representatives of persons performing platform work other than workers’ representatives
description: Representatives of self-employed persons performing platform work can exercise the information and review-request rights of workers' representatives (Arts 8(2), 9(1), 9(4), 10(4), 11(2)) as regards personal data protection.
exercise: Only when acting on behalf of persons who are not platform workers, regarding protection of their personal data.
quote: Representatives of persons performing platform work other than workers’ representatives shall be able to exercise the rights provided to workers’ representatives under Article 8(2)
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Representatives exercise information/review rights on automated systems; object digital, results plain documents. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of representatives to information on platform work
rightholder: representatives of persons performing platform work
description: Representatives receive information on the number of persons working via the platform and their status, the general terms and conditions, average activity duration, hours and income, and intermediaries used.
exercise: Updated at least every six months (annually for SMEs where Member State so provides); average income data only on request (Art. 17(3)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that digital labour platforms make the following information available to competent authorities and to representatives of persons performing platform work:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Statistical and contractual information to representatives; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to ask for additional clarifications on platform work information
rightholder: representatives of persons performing platform work
description: Representatives can ask the platform for additional clarifications and details on the information provided, including on the employment contract, and must receive a substantiated reply.
exercise: Request to the platform; substantiated reply without undue delay.
quote: representatives of persons performing platform work shall have the right to ask digital labour platforms for additional clarifications and details
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Request clarifications, substantiated reply; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to redress, including adequate compensation
rightholder: persons performing platform work, including those whose relationship has ended
addressee: Member State (courts / dispute resolution bodies); digital labour platform
description: Persons performing platform work have access to timely, effective and impartial dispute resolution and a right to redress, including adequate compensation, for infringements of their rights under the Directive.
exercise: Before national dispute resolution bodies or courts; also after the relationship has ended.
quote: have access to timely, effective and impartial dispute resolution and a right to redress, including adequate compensation for the damage sustained
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Without prejudice to GDPR Arts 79 and 82.
tl_reason: Redress and compensation. No technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of representatives and organisations to act on behalf or in support of persons performing platform work
rightholder: representatives of persons performing platform work; legal entities with a legitimate interest
description: Representatives and legal entities with a legitimate interest can bring judicial or administrative proceedings to enforce Directive rights, on behalf or in support of one or more persons performing platform work.
exercise: In accordance with national law and practice.
quote: are able to engage in any judicial or administrative procedure to enforce any of the rights or obligations arising from this Directive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Without prejudice to GDPR Art. 80.
tl_reason: Representatives bring proceedings; judicial remedy, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to private communication channels with peers and representatives
description: Platforms must give persons performing platform work the possibility to contact and communicate privately and securely with each other and with their representatives, without the platform accessing or monitoring those communications.
exercise: Via the platform's digital infrastructure or similarly effective means.
quote: with the possibility to contact and communicate privately and securely with each other, and to contact or be contacted by representatives of persons performing platform work
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Private channel in platform's digital infrastructure, but law allows 'similarly effective means'. Mechanism permitted, not required.

right: Access to evidence held by the platform in proceedings
rightholder: claimants in proceedings concerning the Directive
addressee: national courts/competent authorities; digital labour platform
description: In proceedings concerning the Directive, courts or competent authorities can order the platform to disclose relevant evidence in its control, including confidential information subject to protective measures.
exercise: Disclosure ordered by the court or competent authority in pending proceedings.
quote: national courts or competent authorities are able to order the digital labour platform to disclose any relevant evidence which lies in its control
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Framed as a court power; benefits persons bringing claims.
tl_reason: Court-ordered disclosure of evidence. Test: yes.

right: Protection against adverse treatment for complaints or proceedings
rightholder: persons performing platform work and their representatives
description: Persons performing platform work and their representatives are protected from adverse treatment or consequences resulting from a complaint to the platform or proceedings to enforce Directive rights.
quote: to protect persons performing platform work, including those who are their representatives, from any adverse treatment by the digital labour platform
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Protection against adverse treatment. Test: yes.

right: Protection from dismissal for exercising Directive rights
description: Dismissal, contract termination or equivalent action (and preparations for it) because a person exercised rights under the Directive is prohibited.
quote: to prohibit the dismissal or termination of the contract of persons performing platform work, or equivalent action, and all preparations therefor, on the grounds that they have exercised the rights
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Protection from dismissal. Test: yes.

right: Right to request substantiated grounds for dismissal
description: A person who considers they were dismissed or had their contract terminated for exercising Directive rights can ask the platform for duly substantiated grounds in writing.
exercise: Request to the platform; written grounds without undue delay.
quote: may request the digital labour platform to provide duly substantiated grounds for the dismissal, the termination of the contract or any equivalent action
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Written grounds for dismissal on request. Test: yes.

right: Shift of burden of proof in dismissal cases
addressee: Member State courts; digital labour platform
description: Once the person establishes facts from which retaliatory dismissal may be presumed, the platform must prove the dismissal was based on other grounds.
exercise: Before a court or competent authority; Member States need not apply it in inquisitorial or criminal proceedings (Art. 23(4)-(5)).
quote: it shall be for the digital labour platform to prove that the dismissal, termination of contract or equivalent action was based on grounds other than those referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026).
tl_reason: Burden of proof rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with the data protection supervisory authority
description: Infringements of the algorithmic management and data protection rules (Arts 7-11) are enforced by GDPR supervisory authorities under GDPR Chapters VI-VIII, so persons can complain to them.
exercise: Complaint under GDPR Art. 77 procedures; GDPR Art. 83(5) fine ceiling applies.
quote: shall also be responsible for monitoring and enforcing the application of Articles 7 to 11 of this Directive as far as data-protection matters are concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law (transposition deadline 2 Dec 2026). Derived via GDPR Chapter VIII remedies.
tl_reason: Complaint to data protection authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Protection against intra-Union export bans and restrictions on cross-border services
description: Member States may not ban intra-Union exports or transit of crisis-relevant goods or services, nor restrict exports or cross-border services where this causes supply-chain disruption or shortages (Art. 21(c)).
exercise: Directly applicable prohibition; enforceable before national courts.
quote: bans on intra-Union export, or measures having equivalent effect, of crisis-relevant goods or services, or bans on the transit of crisis-relevant goods
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Prohibition of export bans; market access. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Non-discrimination in free movement based on nationality or company seat
rightholder: beneficiaries of the right to free movement (individuals and companies)
description: Emergency measures may not discriminate between free-movement beneficiaries based on nationality or, for companies, the location of their registered office, central administration or principal place of business.
quote: measures that discriminate between beneficiaries of the right to free movement under Union law based on nationality
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Non-discrimination in free movement. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to enter, exit and transit to reach the Member State of nationality or residence
rightholder: beneficiaries of the right to free movement
description: During an emergency, Member States may not deny the right to enter one's Member State of nationality or residence, to exit another Member State to travel there, or to transit to reach it.
quote: measures that deny beneficiaries of the right to free movement under Union law the following: the right to enter the territory of their Member State of nationality or residence
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Physical entry, exit and transit. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Freedom of business travel linked to crisis-relevant goods
rightholder: business travellers involved in crisis-relevant goods
description: Member States may not prohibit business travel linked to R&D, production, placing on the market, inspection or maintenance of crisis-relevant goods.
quote: measures that prohibit business travel linked to the research and development, production, placing on the market or related inspections and maintenance of crisis-relevant goods
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Business travel freedom. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Freedom to travel between Member States for imperative family reasons
rightholder: individuals travelling for imperative family reasons
description: Member States may not prohibit cross-border travel for imperative family reasons where such travel is permitted domestically.
quote: measures that prohibit travel between Member States for imperative family reasons, when such travel is permitted within the Member State introducing such a measure
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Travel for family reasons. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Freedom of cross-border workers and service providers to reach their workplace
rightholder: service providers, business representatives and workers
description: Member States may not impose travel restrictions preventing service providers, business representatives and workers from travelling between Member States to their place of activity or workplace where no such domestic restrictions exist.
quote: measures that impose travel restrictions on service providers, business representatives and workers, preventing them from travelling between Member States in order to access their place of activity
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Cross-border travel to workplace. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Freedom of movement of crisis-relevant workers and their equipment
rightholder: providers of crisis-relevant services, business representatives and workers in crisis-relevant production, civil protection workers
description: Member States may not prevent travel of crisis-relevant service providers, workers and civil protection workers, or transport of their equipment to their place of activity.
quote: the travel of providers of crisis-relevant services, business representatives and workers involved in the production of crisis-relevant goods
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Movement of crisis-relevant workers. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Priority processing of procedures for providers of crisis-relevant services
description: During an emergency, declaration, registration or authorisation procedures for providers of crisis-relevant services must be prioritised.
quote: Member States shall prioritise declaration, registration or authorisation procedures with regard to providers of crisis-relevant services.
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Priority administrative processing. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to assistance from a national single point of contact
rightholder: citizens, consumers, economic operators, workers and their representatives
description: A national single point of contact helps people obtain information on national free-movement restrictions and complete national crisis procedures and formalities.
exercise: Contact the national single point of contact.
quote: Each Member State shall operate a national single point of contact that shall provide citizens, consumers, economic operators and workers and their representatives with the following:
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Assistance from single point of contact; no technical channel required. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to information on how national crisis measures are interpreted and applied
rightholder: citizens, consumers, economic operators, workers and their representatives
addressee: national competent authorities (via single point of contact)
description: On request, people can receive from competent authorities, via the single point of contact, clear information (with step-by-step guidance where appropriate) on how national crisis measures are interpreted and applied.
exercise: Request via the single point of contact; remote and electronic access.
quote: to receive, at their request and via the relevant single point of contact, information from the competent authorities on the way in which the respective national crisis response measures
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Law requires electronic accessibility, but request and plain-language guidance are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to assistance from the Union-level single point of contact
rightholder: citizens, consumers, economic operators, workers and their representatives
description: The Commission's Union-level single point of contact helps people obtain information on EU crisis measures affecting free movement and complete Union-level crisis procedures.
exercise: Contact the Union-level single point of contact.
quote: provide citizens, consumers, economic operators, workers and their representatives with assistance in requesting and obtaining information as regards Union-level crisis response measures
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Assistance from Union contact point; plain. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to ask the Commission to modify an information request
rightholder: economic operators addressed by a mandatory information request
description: The implementing act for a mandatory information request must specify a period in which the economic operator can ask the Commission to modify the request.
exercise: Within the period specified in the implementing act.
quote: specify the period during which the economic operator can ask the Commission to modify the request.
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Request to modify information request. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to request an extension of the information-request deadline
rightholder: economic operators addressed by an individual information-request decision
description: Economic operators get a reasonable deadline of up to 20 working days and may request a one-time extension, which the Commission must answer within one working day.
exercise: Request no later than two days before the deadline expires.
quote: The economic operator may request a one-time extension to the time limit until two days prior to its expiration in the event that the gravity of the situation requires such extension.
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Extension request. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to contest an individual information-request decision before the Court of Justice
rightholder: economic operators addressed by an individual information-request decision
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Individual information-request decisions must inform the economic operator of the possibility of contesting the decision before the CJEU.
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: information on the possibility of contesting the decision before the Court of Justice of the European Union in line with relevant Union law;
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Action before CJEU. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to refuse an information request that would significantly disrupt operations
rightholder: economic operators addressed by an information request
description: An economic operator may refuse to supply requested information where processing the request could significantly disrupt its operations; the Commission may not disclose the refusal or its reasons.
exercise: Reasons must be given to the Commission.
quote: that economic operator may refuse to supply the requested information and shall provide the reasons for such refusal to the Commission
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Refusal of information request with reasons. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to erasure of supplied information and to be informed of it
description: The Commission must use supplied information only for its stated purpose, erase it once no longer necessary, and inform the economic operator of the erasure.
exercise: Notification without undue delay, unless archiving is required for transparency under national law.
quote: erase the information as soon as it is no longer necessary for the stated purpose and inform the economic operator
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Erasure of supplied business information and notice; holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to refuse a priority-rated request
rightholder: economic operators established in the Union
description: An economic operator addressed with a priority-rated request remains free to refuse it, and the request must say so explicitly; binding effect only follows express acceptance.
exercise: Express acceptance triggers an implementing act (Art. 29(4)).
quote: The Commission shall explicitly indicate in the priority-rated request that the economic operator remains free to refuse that request.
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Refusal of priority-rated request. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to a fair and reasonable price for accepted priority-rated requests
rightholder: economic operators that accepted a priority-rated request
description: Accepted priority-rated requests must be placed at a fair and reasonable price that adequately reflects the operator's opportunity costs.
quote: The priority-rated request made pursuant to paragraph 4 shall be placed at a fair and reasonable price adequately taking into account the economic operator’s opportunity costs
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Fair price; remuneration. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Exemption from contractual liability when complying with a priority-rated request
rightholder: economic operators subject to an accepted priority-rated request
description: An operator complying with an accepted priority-rated request is not liable for breaches of contracts governed by Member State law that are necessary to comply.
exercise: Conditions: breach necessary, implementing act complied with, acceptance not aimed solely at avoiding prior obligations.
quote: The economic operator subject to a priority-rated request pursuant to paragraph 4 shall not be liable for any breach of contractual obligation that is governed by the law of a Member State
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Exemption from contractual liability. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to judicial review of fines with unlimited jurisdiction
addressee: Court of Justice of the EU
description: Economic operators can challenge fines for non-compliance with accepted priority-rated requests before the CJEU, which may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions whereby the Commission has fixed a fine in accordance with Article 29(10).
notes: Only during an activated internal market emergency mode.
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Judicial review of fines. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right to be heard before the imposition of fines
description: Before a fine decision, the economic operator can comment on the Commission's preliminary findings and intended measures; the decision may rest only on objections it could comment on.
exercise: Written observations within a time limit of at least 21 days (Art. 33(2)).
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to Article 29(10), the Commission shall give the economic operator concerned the opportunity of being heard on:
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Right to be heard. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Right of access to the Commission's file
description: In fine proceedings the economic operator is entitled to access the Commission's file under negotiated disclosure, excluding confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Subject to protection of business secrets.
quote: The economic operator concerned shall be entitled to have access to the Commission’s file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Access to file. Test: yes.

act: Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA)
right: Access to a single digital portal to submit crisis declarations, registrations and authorisations
description: Citizens and businesses can find and submit crisis-related declaration, registration or authorisation forms through a dedicated single digital portal or website.
exercise: Online portal (to be set up by 29 May 2026 where no suitable tools exist).
quote: a dedicated single digital portal or website where citizens and businesses can find and submit declaration, registration or authorisation forms
entry_current_status: Adopted as the Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2747
tl_reason: Law requires a single digital portal for crisis forms, but declarations and their result are non-technical. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right of recipients to a plurality of editorially independent media content
description: Recipients of media services have a right to access a plurality of editorially independent media content, which Member States must respect and safeguard through framework conditions.
exercise: No specific procedure; Member States must put framework conditions in place in line with the Regulation.
quote: Member States shall respect the right of recipients of media services to have access to a plurality of editorially independent media content
notes: Framework right owed by Member States.
tl_reason: Framework right owed by Member States; no mechanism or technical ability.

right: Right of media service providers to exercise economic activities in the internal market
description: Media service providers may carry out their economic activities across the internal market without restrictions other than those allowed by Union law.
quote: Media service providers shall have the right to exercise their economic activities in the internal market without restrictions other than those allowed pursuant to Union law.
tl_reason: Internal market freedom of media providers; no technical element.

right: Right to editorial freedom and independence (non-interference)
addressee: Member States, including national regulatory authorities or bodies
description: Member States and their regulators must respect the editorial freedom of media service providers and must not interfere in or try to influence their editorial policies and decisions.
quote: Member States shall respect the effective editorial freedom and independence of media service providers in the exercise of their professional activities.
tl_reason: Editorial freedom against state interference; no technical element.

right: Protection of journalistic sources and confidential communications
rightholder: media service providers, their editorial staff and persons with a regular or professional relationship with them
description: Protection against being compelled to disclose sources, against detention, sanctions, search or surveillance aimed at identifying sources, and against intrusive spyware, save for strictly conditioned derogations subject to prior judicial or independent authorisation and regular review.
exercise: Derogations only if provided by law, justified case by case by an overriding public interest, proportionate and authorised by a judicial or independent authority (Art. 4(4)-(5)); measures regularly reviewed (Art. 4(6)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that journalistic sources and confidential communications are effectively protected.
notes: Art. 4(7) applies Directive 2016/680 safeguards (e.g. data subject's rights of information and access) to related processing.
tl_reason: Protection against compelled disclosure and spyware owed by states; holder operates no mechanism.

right: Right to effective judicial protection for breaches of source protection
rightholder: media service providers, their editorial staff and persons with a regular or professional relationship with them
description: Persons affected by breaches of the source-protection and surveillance safeguards can seek effective judicial protection, with assistance from an independent authority or body.
exercise: Court action under Art. 47 Charter; assistance from an independent authority or body, or else a self-regulatory body or mechanism.
quote: have a right to effective judicial protection, in line with Article 47 of the Charter, in cases regarding breaches of paragraphs 3 to 7 of this Article
tl_reason: Judicial protection; no technical element.

right: Right to a justified dismissal decision, prior notification and judicial review (public service media management)
rightholder: head of management or members of the management board of public service media providers
description: Early dismissal of public service media management must be duly justified on criteria laid down in advance, notified beforehand to the person concerned and open to judicial review.
exercise: Prior notification of the dismissal decision; judicial review of the decision.
quote: shall be subject to prior notification to the persons concerned and shall include the possibility of judicial review
tl_reason: Dismissal safeguards for public media management; no technical element.

right: Right to information on media ownership and state advertising revenue
description: Recipients can access up-to-date information on the provider's legal name and contact details, its direct, indirect and beneficial owners, and the annual state advertising funds and third-country public advertising revenue it receives.
exercise: Information must be easily and directly accessible to recipients.
quote: Media service providers shall make easily and directly accessible to the recipients of their services up-to-date information on:
notes: General information made accessible to all recipients, not individualised.
tl_reason: Ownership and funding information made accessible; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to declare media service provider status on very large online platforms
rightholder: media service providers (recipients of VLOP services)
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: Media service providers can use a dedicated VLOP functionality to declare their status, editorial independence and regulatory oversight, which triggers the procedural privileges in Art. 18(3)-(7).
exercise: Self-declaration through the VLOP functionality with contact details; VLOP may seek confirmation from the regulator where there is reasonable doubt.
quote: Providers of very large online platforms shall provide a functionality allowing recipients of their services to:
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: VLOP must provide a declaration functionality, but declaration and resulting privileges are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right to acknowledgement of and a decision on the media declaration
rightholder: media service providers that submitted a declaration
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: The VLOP must acknowledge receipt of the declaration, give a direct contact point and state without undue delay whether it accepts or rejects the declaration.
exercise: Acknowledgement plus VLOP contact details incl. email; acceptance or rejection without undue delay.
quote: Providers of very large online platforms shall, without undue delay, indicate whether they accept or reject declarations submitted pursuant to paragraph 1.
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: Acknowledgement and decision on a declaration are plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to a prior statement of reasons before suspension or visibility restriction
rightholder: media service providers that submitted a declaration
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: Before a VLOP's decision to suspend or restrict the visibility of declared media content for incompatibility with its terms and conditions takes effect, the media service provider must receive a statement of reasons, and is then informed of the final decision.
exercise: Statement of reasons under P2B Art. 4(1) and DSA Art. 17 before the decision takes effect; information on final decision without undue delay.
quote: communicate to the media service provider concerned a statement of reasons as referred to in Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 and Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
notes: Only VLOPs; not applicable to restrictions under DSA Arts 28, 34, 35, AVMSD Art. 28b or illegal-content obligations.
tl_reason: Statement of reasons per DSA Art. 17 explains moderation incl. automated means, but is plain language; digital object conflicts with test.

right: Right to reply before a suspension or visibility restriction takes effect
rightholder: media service providers that submitted a declaration
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: The media service provider can reply to the VLOP's statement of reasons before the envisaged suspension or restriction takes effect.
exercise: Reply within 24 hours of receiving the statement of reasons (shorter in a DSA Art. 36 crisis).
quote: give the media service provider the opportunity to reply to the statement of reasons referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph of this paragraph within 24 hours of receiving it
notes: Only VLOPs; same exclusions as Art. 18(4)(a).
tl_reason: Reply to a statement of reasons; plain, channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to priority handling of complaints and to representation
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: Complaints by media service providers under P2B Art. 11 or DSA Art. 20 must be processed and decided with priority, and the media service provider may be represented by a body in that process.
exercise: Internal complaint-handling system of the VLOP; representation by a body allowed.
quote: A media service provider may be represented by a body in the internal complaint-handling process referred to in those Articles.
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: Priority and representation in existing complaint systems; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a meaningful dialogue on repeated unjustified restrictions
rightholder: media service providers that submitted a declaration
addressee: providers of very large online platforms
description: Where a VLOP repeatedly restricts or suspends its content without sufficient grounds, the media service provider can require the VLOP to engage in good-faith dialogue to end and prevent unjustified restrictions.
exercise: Request to the VLOP; dialogue within a reasonable timeframe; outcome may be notified to the Board and the Commission.
quote: the provider of a very large online platform shall engage in a meaningful and effective dialogue with the media service provider, at its request, in good faith
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: Request for good-faith dialogue; no technical element.

right: Right to request a Board opinion on the outcome of the dialogue
rightholder: media service providers that submitted a declaration
description: The media service provider may ask the European Board for Media Services for an opinion, including recommended actions for the VLOP, on the outcome of the dialogue.
exercise: Request to the Board (see also Art. 13(1)(e)); Board informs the Commission of its opinion.
quote: The media service provider may request the Board to issue an opinion on the outcome of such a dialogue
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: Request for a Board opinion; procedural.

right: Right to mediation or out-of-court dispute settlement
addressee: providers of very large online platforms / mediators / certified out-of-court bodies
description: If a VLOP rejects or invalidates a media declaration, or no amicable solution is found in the dialogue, the media service provider can use P2B mediation or DSA out-of-court dispute settlement.
exercise: Mediation under P2B Art. 12 or out-of-court settlement under DSA Art. 21; outcome may be notified to the Board.
quote: the media service provider concerned may resort to mediation under Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 or to out-of-court dispute settlement under Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
notes: Only VLOPs.
tl_reason: Mediation or DSA out-of-court settlement, possibly online; plain procedure works. Test: yes.

right: Right to customise the media offering
addressee: manufacturers, developers and importers of devices and user interfaces
description: Users can easily change the configuration and default settings of devices and user interfaces that control access to audiovisual and audio media services to tailor the media offer to their preferences.
exercise: Via a functionality that devices and user interfaces must include, usable freely and easily at any time (Art. 20(2)).
quote: Users shall have a right to easily change the configuration, including default settings, of any device or user interface controlling or managing access to and the use of media services
notes: Does not affect national prominence measures under AVMSD Arts 7a and 7b.
tl_reason: Devices and interfaces must include a functionality to change configuration and defaults; exercised only in the interface. Test: no.

right: Right to visibility of the media service provider's visual identity on devices and interfaces
addressee: manufacturers, developers and importers of devices and user interfaces
description: Devices and user interfaces giving access to media services must display the visual identity of media service providers consistently and clearly to users.
quote: ensure that the visual identity of media service providers to whose services their devices and user interfaces give access is consistently and clearly visible to the users
tl_reason: Object is device UI display, fulfillable only technically, but protection is passive and holder is a media provider; ability and holder criteria fail.

right: Right to appeal national measures affecting the media service provider
rightholder: media service providers individually and directly concerned
addressee: independent appellate body (may be a court)
description: A media service provider individually and directly concerned by a regulatory or administrative measure liable to affect media pluralism or editorial independence can appeal it before an independent appellate body.
exercise: Appeal before an independent, expert appellate body, which may be a court.
quote: that concerns it individually and directly shall have the right to appeal that measure before an appellate body
tl_reason: Appeal before an appellate body; no technical element.

right: Right to request a Board opinion on a national measure
rightholder: media service providers individually and directly affected
description: A media service provider individually and directly affected by a national measure likely to significantly affect media service providers in the internal market can ask the Board to issue an opinion on it.
exercise: Duly justified and reasoned request to the Board (see also Art. 13(1)(f)); opinions made public.
quote: upon a duly justified and reasoned request of a media service provider that is individually and directly affected by such a measure, draw up an opinion on the measure
tl_reason: Request for a Board opinion; procedural.

right: Right to information on proprietary audience measurement methodology
rightholder: media service providers, advertisers and third parties authorised by them
addressee: providers of proprietary audience measurement systems
description: Media service providers and advertisers receive accurate, detailed and up-to-date information on the methodology used by proprietary audience measurement systems.
exercise: Provided without undue delay and free of charge, subject to trade secret protection.
quote: providers of proprietary audience measurement systems shall provide, without undue delay and free of charge, to media service providers, to advertisers and to third parties authorised
tl_reason: Object is measurement-system methodology, but information is plain and needs no mechanism; holder not the governed party.

right: Right to obtain own audience measurement results, including non-aggregated data
addressee: providers of proprietary audience measurement systems
description: A media service provider can request audience measurement results, including non-aggregated data, relating to its own media content and services.
exercise: Request to the provider of the proprietary audience measurement system; data protection rules apply.
quote: At the request of a media service provider, a provider of a proprietary audience measurement system shall provide it with information on audience measurement results, including non-aggregated data
tl_reason: Non-aggregated measurement data is a dataset, but format is unspecified and media providers are not the governed party; holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to transparent and non-discriminatory allocation of state advertising funds
rightholder: media service providers and providers of online platforms
description: Public funds for state advertising and supply or service contracts with media must be awarded on transparent, objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory criteria published in advance, through open procedures.
quote: shall be awarded in accordance with transparent, objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory criteria, made publicly available in advance by electronic and user-friendly means
notes: Does not affect public procurement or State aid rules.
tl_reason: Transparent allocation of state advertising; no technical element.

right: Right to pay with digital euro as legal tender
addressee: payee of a euro-denominated monetary debt
description: Digital euro must be accepted at full face value without surcharge and discharges the payer from the debt; payees may not refuse it.
exercise: Offline payments in the euro area and online payments to euro-area payees (Art. 8); exceptions for small businesses not accepting comparable digital payments, private individuals, good-faith temporary refusal and prior agreement (Art. 9).
quote: a payer shall be able to discharge himself from a payment obligation by tendering digital euro to the payee
notes: Proposal text; may change. Commission may add monetary-law exceptions by delegated act (Art. 11).
tl_reason: Paying in digital euro needs a wallet or card and acceptance infrastructure; the money itself is digital. Test: no.

right: Right not to be bound by non-negotiated terms excluding payment in digital euro
addressee: payee obliged to accept digital euro
description: Standard terms or commercial practices of payees that exclude digital euro payment are not binding on the payer.
quote: Such contractual terms or commercial practices shall not be binding on the payer.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Standard terms excluding digital euro are not binding; contract rule, nothing to operate.

right: Right to choose between cash and digital euro
description: Where both cash and digital euro must be accepted, the payer chooses which to use.
quote: the payer is entitled to choose the means of payment
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Choosing between cash and digital euro is a plain choice, but the digital option needs a wallet. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to fund and defund digital euro holdings at par at any time
description: Users can convert digital euro to and from bank money or cash, manually or automatically, at par.
exercise: At any time via non-digital-euro accounts; via cash where the provider offers cash services (Art. 13(3)); par convertibility (Arts 12(1), 13(5)); subject to ECB holding limits (Art. 16).
quote: shall enable digital euro users to manually or automatically fund or defund their digital euro payment accounts from or to non-digital euro payment account s, or euro banknotes and coins
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Funding and defunding digital euro holdings, manually or automatically, through the provider's technical functions. Test: no.

right: Right to link a digital euro account to a bank account for automatic overflow and top-up
description: Users can have amounts above the holding limit swept automatically to a linked account and pay amounts exceeding their digital euro holdings, using a linked account that may be held with another provider.
exercise: With the user's prior approval; one linked non-digital-euro account.
quote: Digital euro users shall be allowed to have that designated non-digital euro payment account with a different payment service provider than the one where a given digital euro payment account is held.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Linking a digital euro account to an account at another provider for automatic sweeps; interoperation across services. Test: no.

right: Right to hold one or several digital euro accounts with different providers
description: Users may hold one or more digital euro accounts with the same or different providers.
exercise: Holding limit allocated across accounts by the user (Art. 16(6)).
quote: Digital euro users may h ave one or several digital euro payment account s with the same or different payment service providers.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Holding digital euro accounts at several providers and allocating limits; accounts usable only through technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to basic digital euro services from one's bank on request
rightholder: natural persons residing in the euro area (clients)
description: Banks offering payment accounts must, on request of their clients, provide all basic digital euro payment services listed in Annex II.
exercise: Request to the credit institution.
quote: shall , upon request of the ir clients , provide those persons with all basic digital euro payment services as referred to in Annex II
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Request is plain, but the result is digital euro services usable only via wallet or card. Test: no.

right: Right of consumers without a bank account to a basic digital euro account
rightholder: consumers residing in the euro area without a non-digital euro account
description: Consumers without a bank account get access to a digital euro account with basic services on the terms of the Payment Accounts Directive's basic account rules.
exercise: Under Chapter IV of Directive 2014/92/EU (except Arts 17-18).
quote: on access to payment account with basic features shall apply, with the exception of Article s 17 and 18, to the access to digital euro account with basic services by consumers
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Basic digital euro account for the unbanked; request is plain but the account is usable only via wallet or card. Test: no.

right: Right to basic digital euro services from public entities or post offices
rightholder: natural persons residing in the euro area who do not hold or do not want a non-digital account; persons needing face-to-face support
addressee: public authorities or post office giro institutions designated by Member States
description: Member States must designate public bodies or post offices to provide basic digital euro services to people without (or not wanting) a bank account, and face-to-face support for persons with disabilities, limited digital skills or older persons.
quote: provid e basic digital euro payment services to natural persons referred to in Article 13( 1) (a) that do not hold or do not wish to hold a non-digital euro payment account
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Face-to-face distribution, but the result is a digital euro holding used only through a device or card. Test: no.

right: Right to digital inclusion support
rightholder: persons with disabilities, functional limitations or limited digital skills, and older persons
addressee: payment service providers distributing basic digital euro services
description: Providers must give dedicated assistance with onboarding to a digital euro account and using all basic services.
quote: shall provide digital inclusion support to persons with disabilities , functional limitations or limited digital skills
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Assistance is human and non-technical, but exists to onboard and operate a digital account. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to set one's offline holding limit
description: Users choose their offline holding limit anywhere between zero and the maximum, and decide how the overall limit is split across their accounts.
exercise: Allocation across multiple accounts specified by the user (Art. 16(6)).
quote: A digital euro user may set its offline holding limit at any amount between zero and the holding limit set in accordance with Article 37.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Offline holding limit is a setting the provider must offer within the digital euro service. Test: no.

right: Right to free basic digital euro services
rightholder: natural persons (euro-area residents, former residents, visitors)
description: Providers may not charge natural persons for the basic digital euro payment services listed in Annex II.
quote: payment services providers shall not charge fees to natural persons as referred to in Article 13(1) , points (a), (b) and (c)
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Fee ban for basic digital euro services; price rule.

right: Right of merchants to capped digital euro merchant service charges
description: Merchant service charges for digital euro payments may not exceed the lower of providers' relevant costs plus reasonable profit or fees for comparable digital means; merchants may not be charged for funding and defunding.
exercise: Merchant service charge is the only per-transaction charge (Art. 17(6)).
quote: Any merchant service charge or inter-PSP fee shall not exceed the lowest of the following two amounts
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Cap on merchant service charges; price rule for merchants.

right: Right to use digital euro without having to open another account or buy other products
description: Providers may not require users to have or open a non-digital-euro account or accept other products to get digital euro services.
quote: digital euro users shall not be required to h ave or open non-digital euro payment account s or accept other non-digital euro products
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Ban on tying digital euro to other accounts or products; nothing technical to operate.

right: Right to a joint digital euro account
description: Providers must allow a digital euro account to be used by more than one user.
exercise: Holding limit equals the sum of the users' individual limits (Art. 16(7)).
quote: Payment service providers shall allow the use of digital euro payment account by more than one digital euro users.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Provider must let several users operate one digital euro account from their devices. Test: no.

right: Right to make both online and offline digital euro payments
addressee: European Central Bank; payment service providers
description: Digital euro must be usable both online and offline from first issuance.
