quote: The digital euro shall be available for both online and offline digital euro payment transactions as of the first issuance of the digital euro
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Online and device-to-device offline digital euro payments; possible only through technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to convert between online and offline digital euro at par
description: Online and offline digital euro holdings are convertible at par into each other at the user's request.
exercise: On request.
quote: held online or offline, shall be convertible at par between each other, at the request of the digital euro user s
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Converting between online and offline holdings moves value onto a device. Test: no.

right: Right to be told whether a proximity payment will be online or offline
description: Before a proximity payment, payer and payee must be told whether it will be processed offline or online.
exercise: Before initiation.
quote: Before initiating a digital euro payment transaction in a proximity payment , the payee and the payer shall be informed of whether the digital euro payment transaction will be offline or online
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Indicator of online or offline processing in the payment interface concerns software behaviour, but is plain information a cashier could give. Test conflicts.

right: Right to use one's European Digital Identity Wallet for digital euro services
addressee: payment service providers distributing the digital euro
description: On request, users can rely on the functionalities of their EU Digital Identity Wallet when using digital euro services.
exercise: On request.
quote: On request by digital euro users, payment service providers distributing the digital euro shall ensure that those users can rely on the functionalities of their European Digital Identity Wallets
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Using the EU Digital Identity Wallet with digital euro services; interoperability between apps. Test: no.

right: Right to payment-services dispute resolution for digital euro disputes
addressee: payment service providers; competent authorities; ADR entities
description: Digital euro disputes (other than on lawfulness of personal data processing) are governed by PSD2, giving users its complaint, authority-complaint and ADR routes.
exercise: Via PSD2 Arts 99-102 (to be replaced by the PSR); ECB/NCBs may offer message-exchange mechanisms for PSPs (Art. 27(2)).
quote: Without prejudice to the disputes concerning the lawfulness of the processing of personal data, disputes shall be governed by Directive 2015/2366.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Cross-reference to PSD2.
tl_reason: Complaints and ADR under PSD2; ordinary means.

right: Right to bring representative actions for infringements of the Digital Euro Regulation
addressee: infringing traders; national courts or administrative authorities
description: The Representative Actions Directive applies to infringements of the Regulation that harm consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Under national rules transposing Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements of provisions of this Regulation that harm or may harm the collective interests of consumers.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Representative actions by qualified entities; judicial remedy.

right: Right to choose between the provider's and the ECB's digital euro app
addressee: payment service providers distributing the digital euro
description: Providers must let users choose between their own front-end service and the ECB-developed one.
quote: Payment service providers distributing the digital euro shall provide digital euro users with the choice of using the following digital front-end services
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Choice between provider's and ECB front-end apps; using the chosen app means installing and linking it. Test: no.

right: Right of providers to compensation for sanctions-screening failures of another provider
rightholder: payment service provider involved in a digital euro transaction
addressee: payment service provider that failed to carry out sanctions verifications
description: A provider penalised because another provider failed to screen its users against EU sanctions lists can claim compensation for the financial damage.
quote: shall compensate the financial damage caused to the other payment service provider resulting from penalties imposed on that other payment service provider
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Compensation between providers for screening failures; liability rule.

right: Right to switch digital euro accounts while keeping the account identifier
description: Users can move their digital euro account (holdings and/or payment information) to another provider, keeping the same account identifier; in emergencies the ECB/NCBs may authorise switching to a provider the user designates.
exercise: At the user's request; emergency switching where the provider is unavailable or lost data (Art. 31(2)).
quote: shall enable digital euro users at their request to switch the ir digital euro payment account s to other payment service providers while maintaining the same account identifier s
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Switching a digital euro account to another provider with the same identifier; result usable only technically. Test: no.

right: Right of front-end and EU Digital Identity Wallet providers to fair access to mobile device features
rightholder: providers of front-end services and of European Digital Identity Wallets
addressee: mobile device manufacturers and electronic communications service providers
description: Device makers and telecom providers must give effective interoperability with, and access to, the hardware and software features needed for online and offline digital euro payments (e.g. NFC) on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.
exercise: Strictly necessary, justified integrity measures allowed (Art. 33(2)).
quote: shall allow providers of front end services and providers of European Digital Identity Wallets effective interoperability with, and access for the purposes of interoperability to
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Access to device hardware and software features such as NFC is technical, but held by app providers, not the governed party. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to EU-based alternative dispute settlement on device access terms
rightholder: providers of front-end services and of European Digital Identity Wallets
addressee: mobile device manufacturers and electronic communications service providers
description: Published general access conditions must include an EU-based alternative dispute settlement mechanism, without prejudice to judicial redress.
exercise: Under the published general conditions; courts remain available.
quote: Such general conditions shall include a European Union - based alternative dispute settlement mechanism.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Dispute settlement on device access terms between firms; no technical element for users.

right: Right not to be directly identifiable by the ECB and national central banks
addressee: European Central Bank; national central banks; payment service providers
description: Personal data processed by the central banks must be segregated and pseudonymised so they cannot directly identify individual users; providers must ensure that data they pass on does not directly identify users (Art. 34(4)).
quote: This shall include the clear segregation of personal data to ensure that the European Central Bank and the national central banks cannot directly identify individual digital euro users
notes: Proposal text; may change. Privacy safeguard, not a request-based right.
tl_reason: Duty is technical (segregation, pseudonymisation), but the holder exercises nothing beyond checking a technical result. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to cash-like privacy for offline payments
addressee: payment service providers; European Central Bank; national central banks
description: Transaction data of offline digital euro payments may not be retained by providers or central banks; only funding and defunding data are kept for anti-money-laundering purposes.
exercise: Funding/defunding data retained under AML rules (Art. 37(3)-(4)).
quote: Transaction data shall not be retained by p ayment s ervice p roviders or by the European central banks and the national central banks
notes: Proposal text; may change. Privacy safeguard, not a request-based right.
tl_reason: Non-retention of offline transaction data is a technical design duty, but the holder exercises nothing. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right of access to one's own financial data in real time
description: On electronic request, financial institutions must make the customer's data on loans, savings, investments, crypto-assets, pensions, non-life insurance and credit assessments available to the customer without delay, free of charge, continuously and in real time.
exercise: Electronic request to the data holder.
quote: The data holder shall, upon request from a customer submitted by electronic means, make the data listed in Article 2(1) available to the customer without undue delay, free of charge
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Electronic request; financial data made available continuously in real time, a dataset the holder must handle. Test: no.

right: Right to have one's financial data shared with a third-party data user
description: On the customer's electronic request, the data holder must share the customer's data with an eligible data user, continuously and in real time, for the purposes the customer permitted.
exercise: Electronic request; data user must be an authorised financial institution or FISP (Art. 6(1)); sharing under a data sharing scheme (Art. 9); any compensation is paid by the data user, not the customer (Art. 5(2)).
quote: make available to a data user the customer data listed in Article 2(1) for the purposes for which the customer has granted permission to the data user
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Real-time sharing of financial data with a chosen data user through scheme interfaces. Test: no.

right: Right of data holders to compensation for making data available under a scheme
description: A data holder may claim compensation from the data user for sharing customer data, but only under a financial data sharing scheme's model or a delegated act.
exercise: Within the scheme's compensation model (Art. 10(1)(h)) or delegated act (Art. 11).
quote: A data holder may claim compensation from a data user for making customer data available pursuant to paragraph 1 only if
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Compensation of data holders by data users; commercial rule.

right: Right to withdraw permission given to a data user
description: The customer can withdraw a data-sharing permission; where processing is needed for a contract, withdrawal follows the contractual obligations.
exercise: Directly or via the permission dashboard (Art. 8).
quote: A customer may withdraw the permission it has granted to a data user.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Withdrawal of a data-sharing permission via dashboard or directly by plain notice; object is a digital data flow. Test conflicts.

right: Right to a permission dashboard to monitor, withdraw and re-establish data-sharing permissions
description: Data holders must provide an easy-to-find dashboard showing each permission (data user, account/product, purpose, data categories, validity), letting the customer withdraw and re-establish permissions, with a 2-year record of withdrawn or expired permissions.
exercise: Via the data holder's user interface; updated in real time (Art. 8(4)).
quote: A d ata holder shall provide the customer with a permission dashboard to monitor and manage the permissions a customer has provided to data users.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Permission dashboard the data holder must provide in its interface; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right of customer organisations and consumer associations to be members of data sharing schemes
description: Financial data sharing schemes must include customer organisations and consumer associations among their members.
quote: customer organi s ations and consumer associations
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Membership of associations in data sharing schemes; governance right of organisations.

right: Right of SME data users to cost-based compensation only
rightholder: micro, small or medium-sized data users
addressee: data holders / financial data sharing schemes
description: Where the data user is an SME, compensation may not exceed the costs directly related to making the data available.
quote: any compensation agreed shall not exceed the costs directly related to making the data available to the data recipient and which are attributable to the request
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Cost-based compensation for SME data users; price rule.

right: Right to independent dispute resolution within data sharing schemes
rightholder: scheme members (data holders and data users) and membership applicants
description: Each scheme must provide an independent, impartial, transparent and effective dispute resolution system for disputes among members and on membership.
exercise: Meets Directive 2013/11/EU quality requirements.
quote: a financial data sharing scheme shall provide for an i ndependent, impartial , transparent and effective dispute resolution system to resolve disputes among scheme members and membership issues
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Dispute resolution among scheme members; no technical element.

right: Right of data holders and users to join data sharing schemes on equal terms
description: Schemes must be open at any time to new members on the same terms as existing ones, based on objective criteria and equal treatment (Art. 10(1)(b)-(c)).
quote: Membership in financial data sharing schemes shall remain open to new members on the same terms and conditions as those for existing members at any time.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Open scheme membership on equal terms; market access.

right: Right to a timely, reasoned decision on an authorisation application
description: Applicants must be told within 3 months whether authorisation is granted, with reasons if refused.
exercise: 3 months from receipt of the (complete) application.
quote: the competent authority shall inform the applicant whether the authorisation is granted or refused
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Reasoned decision on an authorisation application; administrative procedure.

right: Right to reasons for withdrawal of authorisation
description: Withdrawal of a FISP's authorisation must be reasoned and communicated to those concerned.
exercise: Withdrawal only on the listed grounds.
quote: The competent authority shall give reasons for any withdrawal of an authorisation and shall inform those concerned accordingly.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Reasons for withdrawal of authorisation; administrative procedure.

right: Right to contest competent authority decisions before the courts
rightholder: persons subject to competent authority decisions
description: Decisions of competent authorities under the Regulation, and failures to act, can be challenged in court.
exercise: Also covers failure to act (Art. 24(2)).
quote: Decisions taken by the competent authorities pursuant to this Regulation, may be contested before the courts.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Judicial review of supervisory decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to justified and communicated supervisory measures
description: Measures involving penalties or restrictions on cross-border provision must be properly justified and communicated to the FISP.
quote: shall be properly justified and communicated to the financial information service provider concerned
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Supervisory measures must be justified and communicated; administrative procedure.

right: Right to information on charges for cash withdrawals in shops before the cash is provided
addressee: retailer providing cash without a purchase
description: When a shop provides cash on request without a purchase, the user must be told of any charges before the cash is handed over.
exercise: Before the cash is provided.
quote: The payment service user shall be provided with information on any possible charges for this service before the requested cash is provided
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Charges disclosed before cash is handed over in a shop; no technical element.

right: Right to disclosure of charges and exchange rate before currency conversion at ATM or point of sale
addressee: party offering the currency conversion service (ATM operator, merchant/payee)
description: Where currency conversion is offered at an ATM, at the point of sale or by the payee, all charges and the exchange rate must be disclosed, and the payer must be able to agree to the conversion on that basis.
exercise: Before initiation; payer given the possibility to agree (Art. 5(3)).
quote: the party offering the currency conversion service to the payer shall disclose to the payer all charges and the exchange rate to be used for converting the payment transaction
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Charges and exchange rate shown on ATM or terminal before conversion; plain disclosure, agreement needs no technical skill. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told of surcharges or reductions before paying, and to pay only disclosed charges
addressee: payee; payment service provider; other party involved
description: Charges or reductions for using a payment instrument must be disclosed before initiation, and the payer only has to pay charges whose full amount was made known in advance.
exercise: Prior to initiation.
quote: The payer shall only be obliged to pay for the charges referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 if their full amount was made known prior to the initiation of the payment transaction.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Disclosure of surcharges and liability only for disclosed charges; price rule, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on cash withdrawal charges before and after withdrawal
addressee: providers of cash withdrawal services (e.g. independent ATM deployers)
description: Cash withdrawal providers must show any charges before the withdrawal and again on receipt of the cash.
exercise: Before withdrawal and on completion.
quote: shall provide or make available to their customers information on any charges before the customer carries out the withdrawal as well as upon receipt of the cash when the transaction is completed
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Charges shown on the ATM before withdrawal and on completion; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive required information free of charge
description: Providers may not charge for the information required under Title II.
exercise: Charges only for additional or more frequent information or other means requested by the user; reasonable and cost-based (Art. 8(2)-(3)).
quote: shall not charge payment service user s for providing information under this Title.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Ban on charging for required information; price rule.

right: Right to pre-contractual information for single payment transactions
description: Before a single payment contract, the user must have the Art. 13 information (identifier needed, maximum execution time, estimated time for transfers leaving the EU, charges, exchange rate, estimated currency conversion mark-up, ADR procedures), on paper or durable medium on request.
exercise: Before contract; immediately after execution if concluded at a distance (Art. 12(2)).
quote: At the payment service user’s request, the payment service provider shall provide the information and conditions on paper or on another durable medium.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to identification and contact details of a payment initiation service provider before initiation
description: Before initiation, a PISP must give its name, head office and agent/branch address, contact details and the competent authority's contact details.
exercise: Prior to initiation.
quote: payment initiation service providers shall, prior to initiation, provide the payer with, or make available to the payer clear and comprehensive information on all of the following
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Provider identity and contact details before initiation, usually on screen; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to confirmation and transaction details after placement via a payment initiation service
description: Immediately after initiation the PISP must confirm successful placement and give a reference, the amount and any PISP charges.
exercise: Immediately after initiation.
quote: the payment initiation service provider shall, immediately after initiation, provide or make available to the payer and, where applicable, to the payee all of the following data
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Confirmation, reference and charges after initiation; plain data delivered electronically. Test: yes.

right: Right to information after receipt of a payment order (single payment)
description: Immediately after receipt the payer must get a reference and information unambiguously identifying the payee (incl. commercial trade name), the amount, charges, exchange rate and date of receipt.
exercise: Immediately after receipt of the payment order.
quote: Immediately after receipt of the payment order, the payer’s payment service provider shall provide the payer with or make available to the payer
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Transaction information after receipt of the order; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payee to information after execution (single payment)
description: The payee must receive a reference, the amount, charges, exchange rate and credit value date immediately after execution.
exercise: Immediately after execution.
quote: Immediately after the execution of the payment transaction, the payee’s payment service provider shall provide the payee with, or make available to the payee
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Payee transaction information after execution; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information before a framework contract
description: In good time before signing a framework contract, the user must receive the Art. 20 information on paper or durable medium, including ATM withdrawal charges, currency conversion mark-ups, liability for fraud and verification failures, refunds, termination and ADR.
exercise: In good time before being bound; immediately after conclusion if at a distance (Art. 19(2)).
quote: In good time before the payment service user is bound by any framework contract or offer, the payment service provider shall provide the payment service user on paper or on another durable medium
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Framework-contract information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive the framework contract terms on request at any time
description: During the contract the user can ask for the contract terms and Art. 20 information on paper or durable medium.
exercise: On request, at any time.
quote: At any time during the contractual relationship the payment service user shall have a right to receive, on request, the contractual terms of the framework contract
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Contract terms on request on paper or durable medium; plain request and result. Test: yes.

right: Right to advance notice of changes to the framework contract and to accept or reject them
description: Proposed changes must be notified at least 2 months before they apply, and the user can accept or reject them.
exercise: Notice at least 2 months ahead on paper or durable medium.
quote: The payment service user can either accept or reject the changes before the date of their proposed date of entry into force.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Change notice on paper or durable medium; acceptance or rejection by plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate free of charge when rejecting proposed contract changes
description: A user who rejects the proposed changes may terminate free of charge with effect at any time before the changes apply.
exercise: Before the date the changes would have applied.
quote: the payment service user has the right to terminate the framework contract free of charge and with effect at any time until the date when the changes would have applied
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Free termination when rejecting changes; contract right.

right: Right to terminate the framework contract at any time
description: The user may terminate at any time with at most 1 month's agreed notice; free of charge after 6 months, and bundled technical services are subject to the same termination fee rules.
exercise: Notice of at most 1 month; any fee in the first 6 months must be appropriate and cost-based (Art. 23(2)).
quote: The payment service user may terminate the framework contract at any time, unless the parties have agreed on a period of notice. Such a period shall not exceed 1 month.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Member States may provide more favourable termination rules (Art. 23(6)). Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Termination of the framework contract at any time; contract right, notice by any means.

right: Right to at least 2 months' notice of termination by the provider
description: The provider can terminate an open-ended framework contract only if agreed and with at least 2 months' notice.
quote: the payment service provider may terminate a framework contract concluded for an indefinite period by giving at least 2 months’ notice
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Minimum notice period for termination by the provider; contract protection.

right: Right to pay regular charges only pro rata and to a refund of prepaid charges on termination
description: Regular charges are payable only up to termination; prepaid charges are reimbursed proportionally.
exercise: On termination.
quote: Charges for payment services levied on a regular basis shall be payable by the payment service user only proportionally up to the termination of the contract.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Pro-rata charges and refund of prepaid charges; monetary contract right.

right: Right to information on execution time and charges before an individual payment, on request
description: Before a payment under a framework contract the payer can ask for the maximum execution time and the charges, with a breakdown.
exercise: On request for the specific transaction.
quote: a payment service provider shall, at the payer’s request for this specific payment transaction, provide explicit information on all of the following
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Execution time and charges on request; plain request and answer. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payer to information on each individual payment transaction
description: After each debit the payer must receive a reference, information unambiguously identifying the payee (incl. commercial trade name), amount, charges or interest, exchange rate and value date.
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: the payer’s payment service provider shall provide the payer, without undue delay and in the same way as laid down in Article 19 (1), with all of the following information
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Post-debit transaction information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free monthly statement on request
description: The framework contract must let the payer require the transaction information at least monthly, free of charge, in a storable form.
exercise: On request; Member States may require monthly paper statements (Art. 25(3)).
quote: the payer may require the information referred to in paragraph 1 to be provided or made available periodically, at least once a month, free of charge
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Monthly statement in storable form, paper or electronic; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payee to information on each individual payment transaction
description: After execution the payee must receive a reference identifying the transaction and payer, the amount, charges, exchange rate and credit value date.
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: the payee’s payment service provider shall provide the payee without undue delay in the same way as laid down in Article 19 (1) with all of the following information
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out of Title II (Art. 4(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Payee transaction information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be charged for information and corrective or preventive measures
description: Providers may not charge for Title III information obligations or corrective and preventive measures, except for refusal, revocation and recovery where agreed and cost-based.
quote: The payment service provider shall not charge the payment service user for fulfilment of its information obligations or corrective and preventive measures under this Title
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Ban on charging for information and corrective measures; price rule.

right: Right not to be surcharged for regulated card payments, credit transfers and direct debits
description: Payees may not surcharge payments with cards whose interchange fees are regulated, or credit transfers (incl. instant) and direct debits within the Union.
exercise: Member States may extend the ban to other instruments (Art. 28(4)).
quote: The payee shall not request charges for the use of payment instruments for which interchange fees are regulated under Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2015/751 and for credit transfers
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Surcharge ban for regulated cards, transfers and direct debits; price rule.

right: Payee's freedom to surcharge, offer reductions or steer payers for other instruments
description: For instruments not covered by the surcharging ban, a merchant's provider may not stop it from charging, discounting or steering, with charges capped at direct costs.
quote: the payment service provider shall not prevent the payee from requesting from the payer a charge, offering him a reduction or otherwise steering the payer towards the use of a given payment instrument
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Merchant freedom to surcharge, discount or steer; commercial freedom.

right: Right to redeem electronic money at par value at any time
description: E-money holders can redeem their e-money at any time at par value, in whole or in part; redemption conditions and any fees must be stated before the contract.
exercise: On request; fees only if contractually stated, in the cases of Art. 30(4), and cost-based; non-consumer acceptors subject to contract (Art. 30(7)).
quote: Upon request by the holder of the electronic money, the issuer of the electronic money shall redeem, at any moment and at par value, the monetary value of the electronic money held.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Redemption of e-money at par on request; plain request, result is money. Test: yes.

right: Right of payment service providers to objective, risk-based admission to payment systems with reasons for refusal
rightholder: authorised or registered payment service provider (legal person)
description: Payment system operators must have objective, non-discriminatory, transparent and proportionate published access rules, may refuse an applicant only for risks to the system, and must give written full reasons for refusal.
exercise: Written decision; full reasons; national oversight authority enforces (Art. 31(7)).
quote: A payment system operator shall only refuse participation to an applicant payment service provider where the applicant poses risks to the system
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Risk-based admission to payment systems with reasons; market access for providers.

right: Right to request indirect participation in a payment system on equal terms
rightholder: authorised or registered payment service provider
description: A participant that lets one non-participant PSP pass transfer orders through a system must give other PSPs the same possibility on request and give full reasons for any rejection.
exercise: Request to the participant; full reasons for rejection.
quote: shall, when requested, give the same possibility to other authorised or registered payment service providers in an objective, proportionate, transparent and non-discriminatory manner
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Indirect participation in a payment system on request; market access for providers.

right: Right of payment institutions to a bank account, refused or closed only on listed grounds with specific reasons
rightholder: payment institution, its agents or distributors, applicant for a payment institution licence
description: Banks may refuse or close accounts of payment institutions only on listed grounds (AML concerns, breach of contract, insufficient information, excessive risk, disproportionate compliance cost), and must notify a specific, reasoned decision.
exercise: Notification with risk-specific motivation (Art. 32(3)).
quote: A credit institution shall only refuse to open or shall only close a payment account for a payment institution for its agents or distributors or for an applicant for a license as a payment institution
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Bank accounts for payment institutions; market access, no technical element.

right: Right to appeal a bank's refusal or closure of a payment account to the competent authority
rightholder: payment institution, its agents or distributors, applicant for a payment institution licence
description: A payment institution denied an account or whose account is closed can appeal to a competent authority.
exercise: Appeal to the competent authority.
quote: which is the subject of a negative decision by a credit institution on access or of a decision on closure from payment accounts services may appeal to a competent authority
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Appeal to the authority against account refusal; administrative procedure.

right: Right to use a payment initiation service
description: Providers may not prevent users from using third-party payment initiation services on any online-accessible payment account; the bank must treat PIS orders as if placed directly (Art. 40).
exercise: All online-accessible accounts; based on the user's permission (Art. 49(2)).
quote: Payment service providers shall not prevent payment service users from making use of a payment initiation service provider to obtain payment initiation services
notes: Proposal text; may change. Article titled 'Rights of payment service users'.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Use of third-party payment initiation software on online accounts; bank must not prevent interface access. Test: no.

right: Right to use an account information service
description: Providers may not prevent users from using account information services on any online-accessible payment account; AIS data requests must be treated as the user's own (Art. 41).
exercise: All online-accessible accounts; based on the user's permission (Art. 49(2)).
quote: Payment service providers shall not prevent p ayment service users from making use of account information services
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Use of third-party account information software over the bank's interface; possible only technically. Test: no.

right: Right of AIS and PIS providers to access accounts without a contract with the bank
rightholder: account information and payment initiation service providers
addressee: account servicing payment service providers; any party
description: Open-banking access may not be made conditional on a contract with the bank, and must remain possible outside any multilateral contractual arrangement (Art. 34(2)).
quote: The provision of account information services and payment initiation services shall not be conditioned by any party on the existence of a contractual relationship to that end
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Contract-free interface access to accounts is technical, but held by providers, not the governed party. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right of AIS and PIS providers to interface documentation, advance notice of changes and testing facilities
rightholder: authorised (or applicant) payment initiation and account information service providers
description: Banks must provide technical documentation of their dedicated interface free and without delay on request, announce changes at least 3 months ahead (Art. 35(4)), offer a testing facility (Art. 35(6)) and explain errors (Art. 35(7)).
exercise: On request, free of charge.
quote: available, at no charge and without delay , upon request by authorised payment initiation service providers, account information service providers
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Interface documentation, change notice and testing facility are purely technical, but held by providers. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right of AIS and PIS providers to data access parity with the bank's customer interface
rightholder: account information and payment initiation service providers
description: The dedicated interface must perform as well as the customer interface and give AISPs and PISPs at least the same account and transaction information as the user sees directly (excluding sensitive payment data).
quote: shall provide account information services providers with at least the same information from designated payment accounts and associated payment transactions made available to the payment service user
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Data parity between dedicated and customer interface is technical, but held by providers. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right of AIS and PIS providers to request use of the customer interface when the dedicated interface is down
rightholder: payment initiation and account information service providers
addressee: competent authority; account servicing payment service provider
description: If the dedicated interface is unavailable and no effective alternative is offered, AISPs/PISPs may ask the competent authority to allow access through the customer interface, and may use it pending the decision.
exercise: Request with evidence to the competent authority; decision without undue delay; interim access (Art. 38(5)).
quote: payment initiation service provider s or account information service provider s may request their competent authority, providing all necessary information and evidence
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Fallback use of the customer interface is technical, but held by providers via an authority request. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to be informed when the bank denies a third-party provider access to the account
description: If the bank denies an AISP or PISP access for unauthorised or fraudulent access, it must inform the user and give reasons, where possible beforehand.
exercise: At the latest immediately after denial, unless security reasons or law prevent it.
quote: the account servicing payment service provider shall inform the payment services user that access to the payment account is denied and provide the reasons therefor
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Reasons for denying the user's chosen third-party software access (digital object), but the notice is plain language. Test conflicts.

right: Right to a permission dashboard to monitor, withdraw and re-establish open-banking access
addressee: account servicing payment service provider (with AISPs/PISPs)
description: Banks must offer an easy-to-find dashboard showing each permission given to AISPs/PISPs (provider, account, purpose, validity, data categories), letting the user withdraw and re-establish access, with a 2-year record of withdrawn or expired permissions.
exercise: Via the bank's user interface; updated in real time (Art. 43(4)).
quote: The account servicing payment service provider shall provide the payment service user with a dashboard , integrated into its user interface, to monitor and manage the permissions
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Permission dashboard integrated into the bank's interface; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right to open-banking access free of prohibited obstacles
rightholder: payment initiation and account information service providers and their users
description: Banks may not obstruct PIS/AIS, e.g. by requiring manual IBAN entry, extra permission checks or registrations, limiting payments to the beneficiary list or domestic accounts, or adding authentication steps.
exercise: Competent authorities must ensure removal of obstacles (Art. 48).
quote: Account servicing payment service providers shall ensure that their dedicated interface does not create obstacles to the provision of payment initiation an d account information services.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Bank's dedicated interface must not obstruct third-party services the user chose; object is interface behaviour. Test: no.

right: Right to withdraw permission for payments or for third-party account access
description: The user can withdraw permission to execute a payment, a series of payments, or AIS/PIS access to the account at any time; later transactions become unauthorised.
exercise: At any time (subject to irrevocability, Art. 66).
quote: to access a payment account for the purpose of payment initiation services or account information services may be withdrawn by the pay ment service user at any time
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Withdrawal of payment or third-party access permission; possible via dashboard or plain notice, object partly digital. Test conflicts.

right: Right to verification of the payee's name against the IBAN before a credit transfer
addressee: payer's payment service provider (with payee's provider)
description: Before authorising a credit transfer, the payer must be told, free of charge, whether the payee's name and identifier match and the degree of any discrepancy; the payer can still proceed.
exercise: Free of charge, before authorisation (Art. 50(2)); not required where the payer did not input the details (Art. 50(7)); excludes euro instant credit transfers covered by the IPR (Art. 50(8)).
quote: the payment service provider of the payer shall notify the payer of any such discrepancy detected and shall inform the payer of the degree of that discrepancy
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 24 months after entry into force (Art. 112).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Automated name and IBAN matching in the payment flow, but the user only reads a plain match notice. Test conflicts with digital object.

right: Right to opt out of (and back into) the payee verification service
description: Users can opt out of name/IBAN verification and opt back in; they must be told how, and warned of the risk of misdirected funds (Art. 50(5)).
exercise: By the means the provider must communicate.
quote: Payment service providers shall ensure that payment service users have the right to opt out from being offered the service referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 24 months after entry into force (Art. 112). Opting out removes Art. 57 protection.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Opt-out from and back into an automated verification feature the provider must offer. Test: no.

right: Right that agreed spending limits are not unilaterally increased
description: Providers may not unilaterally raise spending limits agreed with the user for a payment instrument.
quote: Payment service providers shall not unilaterally increase the spending limits agreed with their payment service users.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Agreed spending limits not raised unilaterally; contract rule.

right: Right to be informed of the blocking of a payment instrument and the reasons
description: If the provider blocks an instrument it must inform the payer with reasons, where possible beforehand and at the latest immediately afterwards.
exercise: Unless security reasons or law prevent it.
quote: the payment service provider shall inform the payer of the blocking of the payment instrument and the reasons for it in an agreed manner
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Notice of blocking and reasons in an agreed manner; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to unblocking or replacement of a blocked payment instrument
description: Once the reasons for blocking cease, the provider must unblock or replace the instrument.
exercise: User may request unblocking via means available at all times (Art. 53(1)(c)).
quote: The payment service provider shall unblock the payment instrument or replace it with a new payment instrument once the reasons for blocking no longer exist.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Unblocking or replacement requested via provider channels, including phone; result needs no technical skill. Test: yes.

right: Right to report loss, theft or misuse at any time, free of charge, and to obtain proof of the report
addressee: payment service provider issuing the instrument
description: Issuers must provide means at all times to notify loss, theft or misuse or request unblocking, free of charge (only replacement costs), block further use, and on request give proof of the notification for 18 months.
exercise: On request for the proof (Art. 53(1)(f)).
quote: the payment service provider shall provide the payment service user upon its request with the means to prove, for 18 months after notification, that the payment service user made such a notification
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Loss notification by any means at all times; proof on request. Technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Protection from the risk of sending payment instruments and security credentials
addressee: payment service provider issuing the instrument
description: The issuer bears the risk of sending a card or credentials to the user.
quote: The payment service provider shall bear the risk of sending a payment instrument or any personalised security credentials relating to it to the payment service user.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Risk allocation for sending cards and credentials; liability rule.

right: Right to rectification of unauthorised, incorrectly executed or fraud-affected authorised transactions
addressee: payment service provider (account servicing PSP where a PISP is involved)
description: A user who notifies in time can obtain rectification of unauthorised or incorrectly executed transactions and of authorised transfers covered by Arts 57 and 59.
exercise: Notify without undue delay, at the latest 13 months after the debit date; limit lifted if the provider failed to give Title II information; with PIS, claim from the bank (Art. 54(2)).
quote: The payment service provider shall only rectify any unauthorised , incorrectly executed payment transaction or authorised payment transaction where the payment service user notifies
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may agree different time limits (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Rectification after timely notification; contract remedy, notification by any means.

right: Burden of proof on the provider when a user disputes a transaction
addressee: payment service provider (incl. payment initiation service provider)
description: The provider must prove the transaction was authorised, recorded and not affected by technical failure; use of the instrument alone is not sufficient proof of authorisation, fraud or gross negligence.
quote: the burden shall be on the payment service provider to prove that the payment transaction was authorised, accurately recorded, entered in the accounts and not affected by a technical breakdown
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Burden-of-proof rule in payment disputes; procedural, holder operates nothing.

right: Right to an immediate refund of unauthorised payment transactions
addressee: payer's payment service provider (account servicing PSP where PIS used)
description: The provider must refund an unauthorised transaction and restore the account with original value date by the end of the next business day; if it suspects payer fraud it must, within 10 business days, refund or justify refusal and name the bodies the payer can turn to.
exercise: After notification (Art. 54); 10-business-day decision where fraud suspected (Art. 56(2)); ASPSP refunds PIS-initiated transactions (Art. 56(4)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider shall refund the payer the amount of the unauthorised payment transaction immediately, and in any event no later than by the end of the following business day
notes: Proposal text; may change. Failure to respect the refund period is sanctionable (Art. 97(1)(e)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund of unauthorised transactions; monetary remedy.

right: Right to a refund where the provider failed to warn of a name/IBAN mismatch
addressee: payer's payment service provider (payee's provider if at fault)
description: The payer bears no loss on an authorised credit transfer if its provider failed to notify a detected name/identifier discrepancy as required by Art. 50(1).
exercise: Provider refunds the full amount or justifies refusal and names complaint/ADR bodies within 10 business days (Art. 57(2)); burden of proof on providers (Art. 57(4)); not if payer acted fraudulently or opted out (Art. 57(5)).
quote: The payer shall not bear any financial losses for any authorised credit transfer where the payment service provider of the payer failed, in breach of Article 5 0 (1), to notify the payer
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 24 months after entry into force (Art. 112). Excludes euro instant credit transfers covered by the IPR (Art. 57(6)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund where a name and IBAN mismatch was not notified; monetary remedy.

right: Right to compensation from technical service providers and payment schemes for failure to support strong customer authentication
rightholder: payee; payee's or payer's payment service provider
addressee: technical service providers and payment scheme operators
description: Technical service providers and payment scheme operators are liable for financial damage caused to payees or providers by failing to provide the services needed to apply strong customer authentication.
exercise: Within the remit of the contractual relationship.
quote: shall be liable for any financial damage caused to the payee, to the payment service provider of the payee or of the payer for their failure, within the remit of their contractual relationship
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Liability of technical service providers to payees and providers; compensation rule.

right: Right to a refund for bank-impersonation (spoofing) fraud
description: A consumer manipulated by a fraudster posing as an employee of their bank (using its name, e-mail or phone number) into authorising payments is entitled to a full refund.
exercise: Report to the police and notify the provider without delay; provider refunds or, if it suspects fraud or gross negligence, justifies refusal and names complaint/ADR bodies within 10 business days (Art. 59(2)); burden of proof on the provider (Art. 59(4)).
quote: shall refund the consumer the full amount of the fraudulent authorised payment transaction under the condition that the consumer has, without any delay, reported the fraud to the police
notes: Proposal text; may change. Excluded where the consumer acted fraudulently or with gross negligence (Art. 59(3)). Member States/providers may grant more favourable refund rights (Art. 107).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund for bank-impersonation fraud after reporting; monetary remedy.

right: Liability cap of EUR 50 for lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instruments
description: The payer bears at most EUR 50 of losses from a lost, stolen or misappropriated instrument, and nothing if the loss was undetectable or caused by the provider's staff; unlimited only for fraud or intentional/grossly negligent breach.
quote: the payer may be obliged to bear the losses relating to any unauthorised payment transactions, up to a maximum of EUR 50
notes: Proposal text; may change. Authorities or providers may reduce liability further. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: EUR 50 liability cap; monetary rule.

right: No liability where strong customer authentication was not applied
description: If the payer's provider fails to require strong customer authentication, or either provider applies an SCA exemption, the payer bears no loss unless it acted fraudulently.
quote: the payer shall not bear any financial losses unless the payer has acted fraudulently. The same shall apply where either the payment service provider of the payer or of the payee applies an exemption
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: No liability where strong authentication was not applied; liability rule.

right: No liability for use after notification or where no notification means were provided
description: The payer bears no loss from use of a lost or stolen instrument after notifying it, or if the provider offered no means to notify at all times, unless the payer acted fraudulently.
quote: The payer shall not bear any financial consequences resulting from use of the lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instrument after notification
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: No liability after notification; liability rule.

right: Right to have card funds blocked only with permission for the precise amount, proportionately, and released immediately
description: For card payments of unknown final amount, funds may be blocked only with the payer's permission for the precise amount, in proportion to the expected amount, and must be released immediately once the exact amount is known.
exercise: Release immediately after receipt of the exact amount (Art. 61(4)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider may only block funds on the payer’s payment account if the payer has given his or her permission to that precise amount of funds to be blocked
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Permission for the precise blocked amount, given at terminal or checkout; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund of authorised payee-initiated transactions that exceed reasonable expectations
description: The payer can get a full refund of an executed payee-initiated payment if the exact amount was not specified and it exceeded what the payer could reasonably expect.
exercise: Request within 8 weeks of debit (Art. 63(1)); refund or justified refusal with complaint/ADR bodies within 10 business days (Art. 63(2)); excludable by contract in Art. 62(3) cases.
quote: A payer shall be entitled to a refund from the payment service provider of an authorised payment transaction which was initiated by the payer through a payee and which has already been executed
notes: Proposal text; may change. Payer bears burden of proving the conditions on request. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund of payee-initiated transactions on request; monetary remedy.

right: Unconditional right to a refund of payee-initiated transactions, including direct debits
description: For authorised payee-initiated transactions, including SEPA direct debits, the payer has an unconditional refund right.
exercise: Within 8 weeks of debit; the provider may not refuse (Art. 63).
quote: the payer shall have an unconditional right to a refund within the time limits laid down in Article 63 of this Regulation
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Unconditional refund of payee-initiated transactions; monetary remedy.

right: Right to be notified of the refusal of a payment order, with reasons and how to correct errors
description: If a provider refuses to execute or initiate a payment it must notify the refusal, if possible the reasons, and how to correct factual mistakes.
exercise: At the earliest opportunity and within execution periods (Art. 69); fee only for objectively justified refusals if agreed.
quote: shall notify the refusal and, if possible, the reasons for that refusal and the procedure for correcting any factual mistakes that led to the refusal
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Notice of refusal with reasons and correction procedure; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to execution of authorised payments meeting the contract conditions
addressee: payer's account servicing payment service provider
description: Where all framework contract conditions are met, the bank may not refuse an authorised payment, however placed (directly, via PISP or by payee).
exercise: Unless prohibited by Union or national law.
quote: the payer’s account servicing payment service provider shall not refuse to execute an authorised payment transaction
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Bank may not refuse authorised payments; service obligation, nothing technical for the holder.

right: Right to revoke a direct debit until the end of the business day before debiting
description: For direct debits, the payer can revoke up to the end of the business day before the agreed debit day, without prejudice to refund rights.
exercise: By end of the preceding business day.
quote: the payer may revoke the payment order at the latest by the end of the business day preceding the day agreed for debiting the funds
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Revocation of a direct debit online or by plain notice; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to revoke a future-dated payment order
description: Where execution was agreed for a future day, the user can revoke up to the end of the preceding business day.
exercise: By end of the preceding business day.
quote: the payment service user may revoke a payment order at the latest by the end of the business day preceding the agreed day
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Revocation of a future-dated order online or by plain notice; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to have the full amount transferred without deductions
addressee: payer's and payee's payment service providers and intermediaries
description: Providers and intermediaries must transfer the full amount without deducting charges; if other charges are deducted, the relevant provider must make sure the payee receives the full amount.
exercise: Payee may agree that its own provider deducts its charges, shown separately (Art. 67(2)).
quote: shall transfer the full amount of the payment transaction and shall refrain from deducting charges from the amount transferred
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Full amount transferred without deductions; monetary rule.

right: Right to execution within one business day
description: For in-scope payments the amount must reach the payee's provider by the end of the next business day after receipt (one more day for paper orders).
exercise: Longer agreed periods for other intra-EU transactions max. 4 business days (Art. 68(2)).
quote: the amount of the payment transaction will be credited to the payee’s payment service provider’s account by the end of the following business day
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Execution time limit; service standard.

right: Right of consumers to immediate availability of cash placed on their payment account
description: Cash a consumer pays into their account in the account currency must be made available and value dated immediately.
quote: the payment service provider shall ensure that the amount is made available and value dated immediately after receipt of the funds
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Immediate availability of deposited cash; monetary rule.

right: Right to correct value dating and immediate availability of received funds
addressee: payee's and payer's payment service providers
description: Funds must be value dated no later than the day the payee's provider is credited and be at the payee's disposal immediately; the payer's debit value date may not precede the actual debit.
exercise: Not at the parties' disposal (Art. 68(2)).
quote: the amount of the payment transaction is at the payee’s disposal immediately after that amount is credited to the payee’s payment service provider’s account
notes: Proposal text; may change.
