entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Value dating and availability of funds; monetary rule.

right: Right to recovery assistance and information where an incorrect unique identifier was used
addressee: payer's payment service provider (with cooperation of payee's provider)
description: The provider must make reasonable efforts to recover funds sent to a wrong identifier and, if that fails, give the payer on written request all information needed to bring a legal claim.
exercise: Written request; recovery charge only if agreed (Art. 74(4)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider shall provide to the payer, upon written request, all information available to the payer’s payment service provider and relevant to the payer
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Recovery efforts and information on written request for a legal claim; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund for non-executed or defective payer-initiated transactions
description: The payer's provider is liable for correct execution and must immediately refund a non-executed or defective transaction and restore the account, unless it proves the payee's provider received the funds.
exercise: Immediately; value date no later than the debit date; subject to Art. 54 notification.
quote: it shall immediately refund to the payer the amount of the non-executed or defective payment transaction
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund for non-executed or defective transactions; monetary remedy.

right: Right to have a non-executed or defective transaction traced free of charge
description: Regardless of liability, the provider must on request try immediately to trace a failed transaction and report the outcome, without charge.
exercise: On request.
quote: on request and without charging the payer, make immediate efforts to trace the payment transaction and notify the payer of the outcome
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Tracing on request with outcome notified; plain request and answer. Test: yes.

right: Payee's right to correct transmission and handling of payee-initiated transactions
description: The payee's provider is liable to the payee for correct transmission of payee-initiated orders and for making funds available with correct value date; otherwise the payer's provider is liable to the payer.
exercise: Immediate re-transmission; correct value dating.
quote: be liable to the payee for correct transmission of the payment order to the payment service provider of the payer in accordance with Article 69 (3)
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Payee's provider liable for transmitting payee-initiated orders; liability rule.

right: Right to compensation for charges and interest caused by non-execution or defective execution
description: Providers are liable to users for charges they are responsible for and interest incurred because of non-execution or defective or late execution.
quote: shall be liable to their respective payment service users for any charges for which they are responsible, and for any interest to which the payment service user is subject
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Compensation for charges and interest; monetary remedy.

right: Right to a refund from the bank for failed payments placed through a payment initiation service
description: If a PIS-placed payment is not executed or is defective, the bank must refund the payer and restore the account; the PISP compensates the bank if at fault (Art. 76(2)).
exercise: Subject to Art. 54 notification.
quote: refund to the payer the amount of the non-executed or defective payment transaction and, where applicable, restore the debited payment account
notes: Proposal text; may change. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 27(1)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Refund by the bank for failed PIS payments; monetary remedy.

right: Right of recourse against the provider or intermediary responsible
addressee: other payment service provider or intermediary
description: A provider that has paid under Arts 56, 57, 59, 75 or 76 can recover from the provider or intermediary to which liability is attributable, including for failure to apply strong customer authentication; banks may claim from liable PISPs (Arts 56(5), 76(2)).
quote: that payment service provider or intermediary shall compensate the first payment service provider for any losses incurred or sums paid under Articles
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Recourse between providers; liability rule.

right: Right not to lose one's account or onboarding because of fraud-data sharing
description: Sharing of fraud-related data between providers may not lead to termination of the customer's contract or affect their onboarding by another provider.
quote: shall not lead to termination of the contractual relationship with the customer by the payment service provider or affect their future on-boarding by another payment service provider
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Fraud-data sharing may not cost the customer the account; contract protection, nothing to operate.

right: Right to fraud alerts and guidance on avoiding and reporting fraud
description: Providers must alert customers to new forms of payment fraud, explain how to recognise and avoid fraud, and tell them where to report it and get information quickly.
exercise: Via all appropriate means, considering vulnerable customers.
quote: Payment service providers shall alert their customers via all appropriate means and media when new forms of payment fraud emerge
notes: Proposal text; may change. General customer communications rather than individual notices.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: General fraud alerts and guidance via all appropriate media; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to an accessible means of strong customer authentication not dependent on a smartphone
rightholder: customers, including persons with disabilities, older persons, persons with low digital skills or without digital access
description: Every customer must have at least one authentication method adapted to their situation; SCA may not depend on a single method or on owning a smartphone.
quote: shall not make the performance of strong customer authentication depend , explicitly or implicitly, on the possession of a smartphone
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Strong authentication is inherently technical; provider must offer a method not tied to a smartphone, which the holder still operates. Test: no.

right: Right to complain to the competent authority
rightholder: payment service users and other interested parties, including consumer associations
description: Users and interested parties can complain to competent authorities about alleged infringements of the Regulation by providers.
exercise: Reply informs of ADR (Art. 90(2)); without prejudice to court proceedings.
quote: Member States shall set up procedures which allow payment service users and other interested parties including consumer associations, to submit complaints to the competent authorities
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Complaint to the competent authority by ordinary means.

right: Right to have complaints answered by the provider within 15 business days
description: Providers must run complaint procedures on rights under Titles II and III and reply on paper or durable medium, addressing all points, within 15 business days.
exercise: Holding reply in exceptional cases; final reply within 35 business days.
quote: Such a reply shall address all points raised, within an adequate timeframe and at the latest within 15 business days of receipt of the complaint.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Internal complaint answered on paper or durable medium; plain request and reply. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed about a competent ADR entity
description: Providers must name at least one competent ADR entity on their website, mobile app, at branches and in the general terms and conditions.
exercise: Information on how to access the ADR entity (Art. 94(4)).
quote: The payment service provider shall inform the payment service user about at least one ADR entity which is competent to deal with disputes concerning the rights and obligations under Titles II and III.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: ADR information on website, app, branches and terms; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to out-of-court dispute resolution (ADR)
addressee: Member State / ADR entities; payment service providers must participate
description: Independent, impartial ADR procedures must be available for disputes between users and providers under Titles II and III, and apply to providers.
exercise: Directive 2013/11/EU quality requirements; cross-border cooperation (Art. 95(2)).
quote: Member States shall establish adequate, independent, impartial, transparent and effective ADR procedures for the settlement of disputes between payment service users and payment service providers
notes: Proposal text; may change. Member States may exclude non-consumers (Art. 27(2)).
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Out-of-court dispute resolution; no technical element.

right: Right to contest competent authority decisions before the courts
rightholder: persons subject to competent authority decisions (e.g. payment service providers)
description: Decisions of competent authorities under the Regulation, and failures to act, can be challenged in court.
exercise: Also covers failure to act (Art. 100(2)).
quote: decisions taken by the competent authorities pursuant to this Regulation shall be contest able before the courts
notes: Proposal text; may change.
entry_current_status: Provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position); rights below are from the Commission proposal
source_legal_status: Pending proposal (provisional agreement Nov 2025; final text differs)
tl_reason: Judicial review of supervisory decisions, mainly by providers; no technical element.

right: Right to advance notice of network migrations affecting end-user devices
addressee: providers of public electronic communications networks and publicly available electronic communications services
description: Be informed at least two years in advance, with a migration roadmap, where a move to other network technologies may discontinue services on devices currently in use.
quote: shall inform national competent authorities and end-users at least 2 years in advance , by providing a roadmap reflecting the migration process
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Advance notice and roadmap of network migration from provider; plain information usable without technical means. Test: yes.

right: Freedom to provide electronic communications networks and services
rightholder: providers of public electronic communications services and networks
description: Provide electronic communications networks and services subject only to the general authorisation conditions; Member States may restrict this freedom only on public policy, security or health grounds.
exercise: Conditions exhaustively listed in Art. 9(4); restrictions must be reasoned and notified to the Commission.
quote: Member States may limit the freedom to provide electronic communications networks and services only for the reasons set out in Article 52(1) TFEU on grounds of public policy
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Freedom to provide networks; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to a Single Passport general authorisation
rightholder: providers of electronic communications networks or services
addressee: national regulatory authority of the Member State of notification
description: Notify once to the NRA of one Member State and, without any prior administrative decision, operate in one or several Member States under the general authorisation.
exercise: Notification on BEREC template; NRA confirms within one week, including applicable conditions in each Member State; existing providers may re-notify (Art. 10(9)).
quote: Once the notification is confirmed, the provider may exercise the rights derived from the general authorisation and start the activity
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: General authorisation by notification; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to use frequencies free from harmful interference
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum
description: Use assigned frequencies free from harmful interference.
exercise: Subject to National Frequency Allocation Plans and international agreements.
quote: Holders of rights of use for radio spectrum shall have the right to use their frequencies free from harmful interference
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Spectrum use free from interference; operator right. Test: yes.

right: Right to request RSPB good offices on cross-border interference
rightholder: holder of a right of use for radio spectrum
description: Ask the RSPB to use its good offices to resolve unresolved cross-border coordination or harmful interference between Member States.
exercise: RSPB may issue an opinion proposing a coordinated solution.
quote: any national competent authority or any holder of a right of use for radio spectrum may request the RSPB to use its good offices to resolve the issue
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request for RSPB good offices. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a Commission decision on unresolved cross-border interference
rightholder: holder of a right of use for radio spectrum
description: Where a cross-border interference issue between Member States remains unresolved 12 months after the RSPB request, ask the Commission to resolve it by implementing act.
exercise: After 12 months from the Art. 14(3) request.
quote: the Commission shall, at the request of a national competent authority from any affected Member State or holder of a right of use for radio spectrum, or on its own initiative, take a decision
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request for Commission decision. Test: yes.

right: Right to technology neutrality in spectrum use
rightholder: providers of electronic communications networks or services using radio spectrum
description: Use any type of technology in spectrum declared available for electronic communications services.
exercise: Restrictions only where necessary and proportionate on the grounds listed in Art. 16(1).
quote: Any type of technology may be used to provide electronic communications networks or services within the radio spectrum declared available for electronic communications services
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Technology neutrality for providers; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to service neutrality in spectrum use
rightholder: providers of electronic communications services using radio spectrum
description: Provide any type of electronic communications service in spectrum declared available for electronic communications services.
exercise: Restrictions only to meet ITU Radio Regulations or on the general-interest grounds listed in Art. 16(2).
quote: Any type of electronic communications service may be provided in the radio spectrum declared available for electronic communications services in the National Frequency Allocation Plan
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Service neutrality for providers; market access. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of an extended spectrum authorisation deadline
description: Ask the national authority to review an extension of the deadline for authorising harmonised wireless broadband spectrum.
quote: shall review the extension referred to in the first subparagraph at least every two years and upon request from a prospective radio spectrum user or the Commission
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request review of authorisation deadline. Test: yes.

right: Right to request harmonisation of a frequency band
description: Submit a reasoned request to the Commission to consider harmonising conditions for the availability or efficient use of a frequency band, and receive a reasoned response.
exercise: Commission holds a public consultation and refers to RSPB and/or Radio Spectrum Committee; reasoned response within a reasonable deadline; request and response published.
quote: Any interested party may submit a reasoned request to the Commission to consider the harmonisation of conditions for the availability and/or efficient use of a specific frequency band
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Reasoned request for band harmonisation. Test: yes.

right: Right to be consulted and informed on conditions attached to individual spectrum rights
description: Be consulted and informed in a timely and transparent way about conditions to be attached to individual rights of use, and receive the compliance criteria in advance.
exercise: Before conditions are imposed.
quote: Competent authorities shall consult and inform interested parties , in a timely and transparent manner, about the conditions to be attached to individual rights of use
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Consultation on spectrum conditions. Test: yes.

right: Right to request common multi-country spectrum authorisation conditions
rightholder: prospective users of radio spectrum in two or several Member States
addressee: national competent authorities of the Member States concerned
description: Ask the national authorities of several Member States to jointly establish common authorisation conditions, with RSPB assistance, to reduce deployment cost or environmental impact.
exercise: Authorities inform the Commission of the request.
quote: Prospective users of radio spectrum in two or several Member States , for public and non-public electronic communication s networks, may request national competent authorities
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request common authorisation conditions. Test: yes.

right: Right to a minimum 40-year duration of limited harmonised wireless broadband spectrum rights
rightholder: holders of individual rights of use for harmonised wireless broadband spectrum
description: Where such rights are granted for a limited duration, use the spectrum for at least 40 years.
exercise: Rights are in principle unlimited (Art. 24(1)) and revocable only on Art. 25(2) grounds or with five years' notice (Art. 24(2)); shorter durations only in Art. 24(5) cases.
quote: holders of those rights of use shall have the right to use radio spectrum for a period of at least 40 years.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Minimum duration of spectrum rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to automatic renewal of harmonised spectrum rights
rightholder: holder of a right of use of harmonised radio spectrum
description: Have a limited-duration right of use of harmonised spectrum automatically renewed for a similar duration and on similar conditions.
exercise: On request of the holder; the authority may refuse automatic renewal only by decision at least five years before expiry on Art. 25(2) grounds after public consultation (Art. 25(3)).
quote: Any right of use of harmonised radio spectrum subject to limited duration shall be automatically renewed for a similar duration and with similar conditions upon request by its holder.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Renewal of spectrum rights on request. Test: yes.

right: Right to transfer or lease spectrum rights of use
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum
description: Transfer or lease rights of use for radio spectrum to others.
exercise: Notify intention and effective date to the authority; refusal only for clear risk to competition or serious doubts on the new user, or blocking on resilience, security, defence or public-order grounds (Art. 26(3)); excludes general-interest broadcasting and free-of-charge spectrum.
quote: shall have the right to transfer or lease their rights of use in conformity with this Article and subject to compliance with competition law
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Transfer or lease of spectrum rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to request shared use of radio spectrum
rightholder: any third party interested in using a part of the radio spectrum
addressee: national competent authority / holders of rights of use
description: Express interest to the national authority in using part of an assigned band in a specific territory or period, triggering a sharing assessment.
exercise: Holders may refuse only by demonstrating actual or planned use making sharing infeasible; authority applies the Art. 188 procedure mutatis mutandis.
quote: Any third party interested in using a part of the radio spectrum in a specific territory or period of time may express its interest to the national competent authority.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Expressing interest in shared spectrum use. Test: yes.

right: Right to refuse shared use of assigned spectrum
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum
addressee: national competent authority / requesting third parties
description: Refuse shared use where the holder demonstrates current or planned use that makes sharing technically infeasible.
exercise: Holder must commit to its plans; non-compliance triggers Art. 196.
quote: Holders of rights of use for radio spectrum shall have the right to refuse shared use of radio spectrum where they demonstrate that they are using the radio spectrum
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Refusal of shared use. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to the spectrum-sharing database
rightholder: any prospective user of radio spectrum
description: Directly access the ODN's dynamic geolocation database of spectrum usage opportunities.
exercise: Subject to privacy, business confidentiality and national-security limits (Art. 28(3)).
quote: The database shall be directly accessible to any prospective user of radio spectrum.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Direct access to ODN dynamic geolocation database; object is a dataset reachable only technically. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to pay spectrum fees in yearly instalments and only once spectrum is available
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum
description: Pay spectrum fees only when the spectrum is actually available for use, with the option to pay in yearly instalments.
quote: Any payment of any fees shall be applied only whe re radio spectrum is actually available for use and the possibility shall be given for those fees to be paid in yearly instalments.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Fee payment terms. Test: yes.

right: Right to reimbursement of spectrum fees against fulfilled commitments
rightholder: holder of a right of use for radio spectrum
description: Obtain reimbursement of annual or one-off fees upon fulfilling pre-determined commitments (e.g. coverage).
exercise: On request; possibility and rate announced in advance of selection, assignment, renewal or review.
quote: Annual or one-off fees shall, upon request, be reimbursed against the fulfilment of pre- determined commitments by the holder of a right of use for radio spectrum.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Fee reimbursement. Test: yes.

right: Right to be granted individual rights of use for radio spectrum
rightholder: any undertaking able to comply with the conditions
description: Obtain individual spectrum rights upon request through open, transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate procedures.
exercise: Application demonstrating ability to comply; no discrimination against wholesale and associated-facility operators (Art. 30(2)); decision within six weeks, up to eight months in a selection procedure (Art. 30(8)).
quote: grant individual rights of use for radio spectrum under Article 21 upon request and following open, transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate procedures, set in advance, to any undertaking
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Grant of spectrum rights on request. Test: yes.

right: Right to express views on limited spectrum selection procedures
rightholder: all interested parties, including users and consumers
description: Comment on any aspect of a procedure limiting the number of spectrum rights, including selection criteria, and have the views taken into account.
exercise: Within a period of at least 30 days.
quote: National c ompetent authorities shall give all interested parties, including users and consumers, the opportunity to express their views on any aspect of the procedure
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Comment on selection procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to request review of a limitation on the number of spectrum rights
description: Ask the authority to review a limitation on the number of rights of use, which may lead to additional rights being granted.
exercise: Reasonable request.
quote: any limitation at regular intervals or at the reasonable request of affected undertakings
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request review of limitation. Test: yes.

right: Right of providers to open their networks via RLANs
rightholder: providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services
description: Allow other providers or the public to access their networks through Wi-Fi/RLANs.
exercise: Subject to general authorisation conditions and the end-user's prior informed agreement where the RLAN is at the end-user's premises.
quote: Providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services have the right to allow access to their networks to other providers
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Provider freedom to open networks via RLANs. Test: yes.

right: Right of end-users to consent before their home RLAN is opened to others
addressee: providers of public electronic communications networks or services
description: Have a provider obtain the end-user's prior informed agreement before opening an RLAN located at the end-user's premises to other providers or the public.
quote: subject to compliance with the applicable general authorisation conditions and the prior informed agreement of the end-user, where the RLAN is located at the end-user’s premises.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Object is the user's own home RLAN configuration, but prior agreement can be given plainly by contract. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to access third-party RLANs of one's choice
addressee: providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services
description: Access Wi-Fi/RLANs of their choice provided by third parties, and allow other end-users to access networks through RLANs, without unilateral restriction by their provider.
quote: providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services shall not unilaterally restrict or prevent end-users from
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Provider must permit connecting to third-party Wi-Fi; holder operates own device across networks. Test: no.

right: Right to share one's RLAN with other end-users
description: Allow other end-users access to their RLAN, reciprocally or otherwise, including via third-party aggregation initiatives.
exercise: Non-commercial provision is exempt from general authorisation and end-user-rights obligations (Art. 33(1)).
quote: End-users may allow access, reciprocally or otherwise, to their RLANs by other end-users
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Sharing one's RLAN requires configuring own equipment; provider must permit. Test: no.

right: Right of access to public-authority infrastructure for small-area wireless access points
addressee: national, regional or local public authorities controlling physical infrastructure
description: Access street furniture and other public-authority infrastructure suitable to host small cells or connect them to a backbone network.
exercise: Reasonable requests granted on fair, reasonable, transparent and non-discriminatory terms published at a single information point; subject to the Gigabit Infrastructure Act.
quote: operators shall have the right to access any physical infrastructure controlled by national, regional or local public authorities which is technically suitable to host small-area wireless
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Access to public street furniture. Test: yes.

right: Right to provide satellite networks and services EU-wide under a Union general authorisation
rightholder: providers of satellite networks and satellite communications services
description: Provide satellite networks and services in the Union or several Member States on the basis of a notification to the Commission, without any other national authorisation, enjoying the general-authorisation rights in all Member States (Art. 38(4)).
exercise: Notification to the Commission (assisted by the ODN); subject only to conditions set by implementing act.
quote: Providers shall submit a notification to the Commission and shall not need to obtain any explicit decision or authorisation or any other administrative act from other competent authorities.
applies_from: 12 months after entry into force (proposed, Art. 210(3)(a))
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Union general authorisation for satellite providers. Test: yes.

right: Right to be granted a Union authorisation for satellite spectrum
rightholder: any undertaking applying for a Union authorisation
description: Obtain a single Union authorisation to use radio spectrum for satellite communications where the Art. 39 conditions are met, conferring the right to provide services and use spectrum throughout the Union (Art. 41(1)).
exercise: Application to the Commission (Art. 40(1)-(2)); RSPB opinion within 10 working days; selection procedure under Annex VI where numbers are limited.
quote: The Commission shall adopt an implementing act grant ing the Union authorisation where the applicant compl ies with conditions set out in Article 39
applies_from: 12 months after entry into force (proposed, Art. 210(3)(a))
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Union satellite spectrum authorisation. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of Commission findings of non-compliance
description: Be informed of the Commission's findings before corrective measures, fines or withdrawal of a Union satellite authorisation.
quote: Where the Commission finds that a holder of a Union authorisation does not comply with any condition laid down in Article 38 or Article 39 it shall inform that operator of its findings.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Informed of findings. Test: yes.

right: Right to judicial review of Commission fines on satellite operators
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Challenge Commission fines or periodic penalty payments before the Court of Justice, which may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Fines capped at 5% of worldwide turnover.
quote: The Court of Justice shall have unlimited jurisdiction within the meaning of Article 229 TFEU to review decisions whereby the Commission has fixed a fine or periodic penalty payments
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Judicial review of fines. Test: yes.

right: Right of terrestrial right holders to consent to shared satellite use
rightholder: primary holder of the terrestrial right of use
addressee: Commission / national competent authorities / satellite operators
description: Shared use of its spectrum by satellite systems is only possible with the agreement and under the responsibility of the primary terrestrial holder.
quote: Shared use of radio spectrum between terrestrial and satellite systems shall only be possible with the agreement and under the responsibility of the primary holder of the terrestrial right of use
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Consent of terrestrial holder to shared use. Test: yes.

right: Right of non-telecom undertakings to obtain numbering resources
rightholder: undertakings other than providers of electronic communications networks or services
description: Obtain rights of use for national numbers for the provision of specific services (e.g. IoT/M2M).
exercise: On request; must demonstrate ability to manage the numbers; may be suspended if exhaustion risk is shown.
quote: shall also grant rights of use for numbering resources from the national numbering plans for the provision of specific services to undertakings other than providers
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Obtaining numbering resources. Test: yes.

right: Right to be granted rights of use for numbering resources
rightholder: any undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services under a general authorisation
description: Obtain individual rights of use for numbers through open, objective, transparent and non-discriminatory procedures.
exercise: On request; decision within three weeks for numbers allocated for specific purposes, extendable by three weeks for numbers of exceptional economic value (Art. 49(3)-(4)).
quote: national regulatory authorities shall grant such rights, upon request, to any undertaking for the provision of electronic communications networks or services covered by a general authorisation
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Grant of numbering rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to reach all numbers and services in the Union
addressee: providers of number-based electronic communications services
description: Be able to call non-geographic numbers, all numbers in the Union (including UIFN) and pan-European numbers.
exercise: Where economically feasible, unless the called party has restricted access from certain areas for commercial reasons.
quote: providers of number - based electronic communications services shall take all necessary steps to ensure that the originating parties are able to access all of the following
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Reaching numbers is ordinary calling. Test: yes (a phone call works without technical skill). Consistency pass.

right: Right to information about the copper switch-off
rightholder: end-users affected by the copper switch-off
description: Be informed clearly, timely and accessibly of the switch-off timing, necessary changes to service or terminal equipment, and available alternative services.
quote: Member States shall ensure that end-users affected by the copper switch-off are informed clearly, in a timely and accessible manner about the following
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Member State information on copper switch-off; plain information, no channel required. Test: yes.

right: Right to continuity of essential copper-based services
rightholder: end-users relying on essential copper-based services
description: Have services supporting essential copper-based services (e.g. alarms, lifts) kept running or migrated to functionally equivalent alternatives.
exercise: Member States also adopt affordability and switching safeguards (Art. 59(3)-(5)).
quote: Operators shall take the necessary technical and commercial measures to ensure the continued operation of such services or their migration to functionally equivalent alternatives.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Operator duty to keep essential services running or migrate; holder operates nothing. Test: yes.

right: Right to a timely, transparent decision on rights of way
rightholder: undertakings authorised to provide electronic communications networks applying for rights to install facilities
description: Have applications for rights to install facilities on, over or under public or private property decided through simple, transparent, non-discriminatory procedures within six months.
exercise: Except expropriation; conditions must be transparent and non-discriminatory.
quote: in any event make its decision within six months of the application, except in the case of expropriation
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Rights-of-way decision deadline. Test: yes.

right: Right to negotiate access and interconnection agreements
description: Negotiate technical and commercial access or interconnection arrangements with undertakings in the same or other Member States, without needing authorisation where not operating there.
quote: Undertakings in the same Member State or in different Member States shall have the right to negotiate between themselves agreements on technical and commercial arrangements for access
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Negotiation of access agreements. Test: yes.

right: Right to interconnection negotiations with public network operators
addressee: operators of public electronic communications networks
description: Request interconnection negotiations, which public network operators are obliged to conduct, to ensure provision and interoperability of services across the Union.
exercise: Terms must be consistent with NRA-imposed obligations.
quote: Operators of public electronic communications networks shall have a right and, when requested by other undertakings so authorised in accordance with Article 9, an obligation to negotiate
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Interconnection negotiations. Test: yes.

right: Right to confidentiality of information exchanged in access negotiations
rightholder: undertakings supplying information in access or interconnection negotiations
description: Have information supplied during access or interconnection negotiations used only for its intended purpose and kept confidential, including from the recipient's other departments, subsidiaries or partners.
quote: shall use that information solely for the purpose for which it was supplied and respect at all times the confidentiality of information transmitted or stored
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Confidentiality of negotiation information. Test: yes.

right: Right to request symmetric access to in-building wiring
description: Ask the NRA to impose obligations to grant access to in-building wiring, cables and associated facilities up to the first concentration or distribution point.
exercise: Reasonable request; NRA discretion; where replication is economically inefficient or physically impracticable.
quote: national regulatory authorities may, upon reasonable request, impose obligations to grant access to wiring and cables and associated facilities inside buildings
notes: Proposal text; may change; NRA discretion
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request for in-building wiring access. Test: yes.

right: Right to be connected to the fibre network on request in copper switch-off areas
rightholder: users (households passed by the FTTH network)
addressee: FTTH network provider designated by the NRA
description: Have one's household connected to a fibre-to-the-home network that passes it, in areas where copper switch-off is mandated.
exercise: Request to the provider; any additional connection fee must be fair and reasonable and may be capped by the NRA (Art. 71(3)).
quote: the obligation to connect, upon user’s request, households passed by its fibre network
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Physical fibre connection on request; supply right. Test: yes.

right: Right of residents to have fibre deployed inside multi-dwelling buildings
rightholder: any resident of a multi-dwelling unit
addressee: owner or administrator of the multi-dwelling unit
description: Require the building owner or administrator to allow deployment of fibre wiring and associated facilities inside the building.
exercise: In copper switch-off areas; fulfilled once one provider has deployed; other providers get access via Arts. 68-69.
quote: the owner or the administrator of such multi-dwelling unit shall allow such deployment at the request of any resident of the multi-dwelling unit.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Fibre deployment in building; property/physical. Test: yes.

right: Right to request a BEREC analysis of transnational demand
description: Submit a reasoned, evidenced request asking BEREC to analyse transnational end-user demand.
exercise: BEREC decides whether there is a serious demand problem to address.
quote: BEREC may also conduct such analysis where it receives a reasoned request from market participants providing sufficient supporting evidence
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Request BEREC analysis. Test: yes.

right: Right of SMP undertakings to offer commitments
rightholder: undertakings designated as having significant market power
description: Offer commitments on access and/or co-investment that the NRA must consider and may make binding instead of or alongside imposed remedies.
exercise: NRA must inform of this possibility (Art. 83(1)); market test; preliminary conclusions communicated and offer may be revised; co-investment commitments binding for at least seven years.
quote: Undertakings designated as having significant market power may offer to the national regulatory authority commitments regarding conditions for access, co-investment, or both
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Offering commitments. Test: yes.

right: Right of co-investors and access seekers to comment on SMP commitments
description: Give views on whether offered commitments comply with the applicable conditions and propose changes during the NRA's market test.
exercise: Via the NRA's public consultation.
quote: Potential co-investors or access seekers may provide views on the compliance of the commitments offered with the conditions provided
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Comments in market test. Test: yes.

right: Right to affordable adequate internet access and voice communications (universal service)
description: Have access at a fixed location to an affordable, adequate internet access service and voice communications services.
exercise: Bandwidth defined by each Member State with BEREC guidance (Art. 87(2)).
quote: All consumers in the Union shall be entitled to have access to an affordable and adequate internet access service and to voice communications services
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Universal service: affordable access supply; no mechanism the holder operates. Test: yes.

right: Right of eligible consumers to conclude a social-tariff contract
rightholder: consumers with low income or special social needs entitled to tariff options or packages
addressee: providers of adequate internet access service and voice communications services
description: Conclude a contract for the affordable tariff options or packages, limited to voice communications if the consumer so requests.
exercise: Where the Member State requires tariff options/packages, which all providers must offer.
quote: Consumers entitled to the tariff options or packages referred to in the first subparagraph of this paragraph shall have a right to conclude a contract with a provider
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Social-tariff contract; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Support for consumers with disabilities to access terminal equipment and services
description: Receive support so that terminal equipment and services enhancing equivalent access (e.g. total conversation, relay services) are available and affordable.
exercise: As appropriate, under national measures.
quote: Member States shall provide support, as appropriate, to consumers with disabilities and take other specific measures where appropriate
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Support for affordable equipment; funding measure. Test: yes.

right: Right to have reasonable requests for fixed-location access met (universal service availability)
rightholder: consumers, microenterprises, small enterprises and not-for-profit organisations
addressee: Member States / designated universal service providers
description: Have reasonable requests for an adequate internet access service and voice communications at a fixed location met where the market does not provide them.
exercise: Only where the Member State imposes universal service obligations after other public policy tools failed.
quote: to ensure that all reasonable requests by consumers, microenterprises, small enterprises and not-for-profit organisations for accessing those services in the relevant parts of their territory are met
notes: Proposal text; may change; Conditional on Member State imposing universal service obligations
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Reasonable request for connection met; supply right. Test: yes.

right: Right not to pay for unnecessary facilities under universal service
description: Not be required to pay for facilities or services that are not necessary or not required for the universal service requested.
quote: the eligible end-user is not obliged to pay for facilities or services which are not necessary or not required for the service requested
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Not paying for unnecessary facilities; contract terms. Test: yes.

right: Right to expenditure-control facilities for universal service consumers
rightholder: consumers benefiting from affordability measures under Art. 88
description: Use facilities to monitor and control spending: selective call/SMS barring, pre-payment, phased connection fees, warning before disconnection for non-payment, tariff advice, free alerts on unusual consumption, and deactivation of third-party billing.
quote: shall offer the following specific facilities and services to consumers benefiting from measures pursuant to Article 88 , as applicable, in order that consumers can monitor and control expenditure
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Mixed facilities: call barring, alerts, third-party billing deactivation are service settings; pre-payment, phased fees, tariff advice are plain. Mechanism partly required.

right: Right to open internet access
description: Access and distribute information and content, use and provide applications and services, and use terminal equipment of their choice via their internet access service.
exercise: Contracts and commercial practices may not limit this right (Art. 93(2)); complaints to the provider (Art. 188(3)); NRA enforcement (Art. 94).
quote: End-users shall have the right to access and distribute information and content, use and provide applications and services, and use terminal equipment of their choice
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Use applications and terminal equipment of choice over internet access; provider must permit. Test: no.

right: Right to equal treatment of internet traffic
description: Have all traffic treated equally, without blocking, throttling or discrimination of content, applications or services beyond reasonable traffic management.
exercise: Exceptions only for legal compliance, network security, or congestion management.
quote: Providers of internet access services shall treat all traffic equally, when providing internet access services, without discrimination, restriction or interference
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Object is network traffic treatment; enjoyed only by using the service and checked technically. Test: no.

right: Freedom to offer specialised (optimised) services
rightholder: providers of electronic communications to the public and providers of content, applications and services
description: Offer services other than internet access that are optimised for specific content, applications or services where needed for a specific quality level.
exercise: Only with sufficient network capacity; not as a substitute for, or to the detriment of, internet access services.
quote: and providers of content, applications and services shall be free to offer services other than internet access services which are optimised for specific content, applications or services
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Freedom to offer specialised services. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information
addressee: providers of internet access services or publicly available interpersonal communications services
description: Receive the Annex III information on a durable medium (or downloadable document) before being bound by a contract.
exercise: Accessible format on request for end-users with disabilities; becomes an integral part of the contract (Art. 95(3)); also for microenterprises and not-for-profits unless waived (Art. 99).
quote: Before a consumer is bound by a contract or any corresponding offer, and in addition to requirements pursuant to Directive 2011/83/EU, providers of internet access services
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on durable medium or download; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to a contract summary
addressee: providers of internet access services or publicly available interpersonal communications services
description: Receive a concise, easily readable contract summary free of charge before being bound by the contract.
exercise: Using the Commission template; if technically impossible beforehand, without undue delay afterwards and before being bound.
quote: provide the contract summary free of charge to consumers, before the consumer is bound by the contract or any corresponding offer, including distance contracts
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Contract summary; plain document, may be delivered online. Test: yes.

right: Right to monitor and control usage and costs
addressee: providers of time- or volume-billed internet access or interpersonal communications services
description: Use a facility to monitor consumption and costs and be notified before a tariff-plan limit is reached and when a service is fully consumed.
quote: providers shall notify consumers before any consumption limit, included in their tariff plan, is reached and when a service included in their tariff plan is fully consumed
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Provider must offer a facility to monitor usage and alerts, but consumption figures are plain and could come by bill. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to free basic itemised bills
description: Receive basic itemised bills free of charge to verify charges and monitor usage and expenditure.
exercise: Premium-number supplier identity shown unless the consumer asks otherwise; free calls (e.g. helplines) need not appear.
quote: shall offer the basic level of itemised bills , where applicable, to consumers free of charge
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Itemised bill; plain document on paper or online. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive non-itemised bills
description: Choose to receive bills that are not itemised.
quote: Consumers shall have the right to receive non-itemised bills.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Choice of non-itemised bills; plain billing option. Test: yes.

right: Maximum 24-month contractual commitment period
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (other than NI-ICS and M2M transmission)
description: Not be bound to a commitment period longer than 24 months.
exercise: Separate instalment contracts solely for deploying a physical connection are excepted but may not include terminal equipment or block other rights.
quote: shall not mandate a commitment period longer than 24 months
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Maximum contract duration; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate after automatic prolongation
addressee: providers of electronic communications services (other than NI-ICS and M2M transmission)
description: After automatic prolongation of a fixed-term contract, terminate at any time with at most one month's notice and without costs other than for service during notice.
quote: consumers are entitled, after such prolongation, to terminate the contract at any time with a maximum one-month notice period and without incurring any costs
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Termination after prolongation; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to notice before automatic prolongation and best-tariff advice
description: Be told prominently, in time and on a durable medium of the end of the commitment and how to terminate, and receive best-tariff advice.
exercise: Before the contract is automatically prolonged.
quote: Before the contract is automatically prolonged, providers shall inform the consumers in a prominent and timely manner and on a durable medium, of the end of the contractual commitment
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Notice on durable medium and tariff advice; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate upon changes to contractual conditions
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services (other than NI-ICS)
description: Terminate the contract without further costs when the provider proposes changes to the contractual conditions.
exercise: Provider must notify at least one month in advance on a durable medium and inform of the right; exercisable within one month after notification; not for changes exclusively beneficial, purely administrative or imposed by law.
quote: Consumers shall have the right to terminate their contract without incurring any further costs upon notice of changes in the contractual conditions proposed by the provider
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Termination on contract changes; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Remedies for performance discrepancies, including free termination
description: Invoke national-law remedies, including free-of-charge termination, for significant continuous or recurring discrepancies between actual and contracted performance.
exercise: For internet access, discrepancies in speed or other QoS established by the BEREC monitoring mechanism certified by the NRA are deemed non-conformity.
quote: shall be considered to be a basis for triggering the remedies available to the consumer in accordance with national law, including the right to terminate the contract free of cost
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Non-conformity established via certified QoS monitoring mechanism (technical measurement), but remedy and termination are plain. Mechanism vs result conflict.

right: Limit on compensation payable on early termination
description: When terminating early under a legal right, owe no compensation except for retained subsidised terminal equipment, capped at its pro rata value or the remaining fees, whichever is smaller.
quote: no compensation shall be due by the consumer other than for retained subsidised terminal equipment
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Limit on termination compensation. Test: yes.

right: Right to free unlocking of terminal equipment
description: Have any SIM/network lock on retained terminal equipment lifted free of charge.
exercise: At the latest upon payment of any compensation due.
quote: The provider shall lift any condition on the use of that terminal equipment on other networks free of charge at the latest upon payment of the compensation.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: SIM/network lock is software; lifting it and using device on other networks needs technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to terminate the whole bundle
addressee: providers of bundles including internet access or number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Where entitled to terminate any element of a bundle for lack of conformity or failure to supply, terminate the contract for all elements of the bundle.
exercise: Arts. 95(2), 96(1), 97 and 100(1) apply to all elements of such bundles (Art. 98(1)).
quote: the consumer has the right to terminate the contract with respect to all elements of the bundle
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Termination of bundle; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Protection against contract extension through add-on subscriptions
addressee: providers of internet access or number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Subscribing to additional services or equipment does not extend the original contract duration unless the consumer expressly agrees.
quote: shall not extend the original duration of the contract to which such services or terminal equipment are added, unless the consumer expressly agrees otherwise
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: No contract extension through add-ons. Test: yes.

right: Extension of contract rights to microenterprises, SMEs and not-for-profit organisations
rightholder: end-users that are microenterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises or not-for-profit organisations
description: Benefit from the consumer rights on information, contract duration, bundles, termination after prolongation or contract changes, and early-termination compensation limits.
exercise: Unless explicitly waived; Arts. 95, 97(1), 98(1), 98(3) for microenterprises and not-for-profits; Arts. 97(2), 97(3), 97(5) also for SMEs.
quote: Article 95, Article 97(1), Article 98(1) and Article 98(3) shall also apply to end-users that are microenterprises or not-for-profit organisations, unless they have explicitly agreed to waive
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Extension of contract rights to small businesses. Test: yes.

right: Right to seamless switching of internet access provider
addressee: transferring and receiving providers of internet access services
description: Switch internet access provider with adequate information, continuity of service, activation on the agreed date and no more than one working day without service.
exercise: Receiving provider leads the process (Art. 100(6)); contract with the old provider ends automatically.
quote: The transferring provider shall continue to provide its internet access service on the same terms until the receiving provider activates its internet access service.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Switching provider is a supply-contract right; providers handle technical continuity. Test: yes.

right: Right to number portability
rightholder: end-users with numbers from the national numbering plan
description: Keep their telephone number when changing provider.
exercise: On request; geographic numbers at a specific location, non-geographic anywhere; not between fixed and mobile; no direct charges (Art. 100(4)); activation within one working day of the agreed date, reactivation if porting fails (Art. 100(5)).
quote: shall have the right to retain their numbers, upon request, independently of the undertaking providing the service
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Number (technical identifier) is ported between networks, but holder only makes a plain request; providers do the technical work. Object vs ability conflict.

right: Right to port a number after contract termination
description: Port the number to the same or another provider for at least one month after the contract ends.
exercise: Unless renounced by the end-user.
quote: the end-user shall have the right to port a number from the national numbering plan to the same or another provider for a minimum of one month after the date of termination
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Post-termination number porting; technical identifier moved, but plain request suffices. Object vs ability conflict.

right: Right not to be switched or ported without explicit consent
description: Not be switched to another provider or have the number ported without explicit consent (no slamming).
exercise: NRAs ensure end-users are informed and protected throughout the process.
quote: nor shall they port numbers or switch end-users without the end-users’ explicit consent
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Explicit consent to switching/porting is contractual consent; no mechanism to operate. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for switching and porting failures
description: Be compensated by providers for delays in or abuse of switching and porting, missed service and installation appointments, or other breaches of Art. 100.
exercise: Process detailed in BEREC guidelines and implemented by NRAs; Member States may keep or adopt compensation rules (Art. 100(7)).
quote: The guidelines shall also detail the compensation process of end-users by their providers in the case of delays in, or abuse of, porting and switching processes
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Compensation for porting failures. Test: yes.

right: Right to refund of remaining pre-paid credit on switching
description: Get remaining pre-paid credit refunded when switching provider.
exercise: On request; a fee only if provided in the contract and proportionate to actual costs.
quote: Transferring providers shall refund, upon request, any remaining credit to the consumers using pre-paid services.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Refund of pre-paid credit. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of a microenterprise exemption
addressee: microenterprises providing number-independent interpersonal communications services
description: Be told before concluding a contract that the microenterprise provider is exempt from the end-user rights Title.
quote: Before concluding a contract, a microenterprise benefiting from such an exemption shall inform end-users of the exemption under the first paragraph.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Plain pre-contract notice of exemption from online provider. Test: yes.

right: Right to non-discrimination in access to networks and services
addressee: providers of electronic communications networks or services
description: Not be subjected to different requirements or general conditions of access to or use of networks or services unless justified under Union law.
quote: Providers of electronic communications networks or services shall not apply any different requirements or general conditions of access to, or use of, networks or services to end-users
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Non-discrimination in access conditions. Test: yes.

right: Right to free access to the 116000 missing-children hotline
addressee: providers of number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Call the 116000 missing-children hotline free of charge, including the visited country's service when travelling in the Union.
quote: Providers of number-based interpersonal communication s services shall ensure free of charge access for end-users, including end-users with disabilities, to the service operating a hotline
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Calling the hotline is an ordinary phone call. Test: yes (a phone call works without technical skill). Consistency pass.

right: Right to free access to emergency services (112)
addressee: providers of publicly available number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Reach emergency services free of charge, without any means of payment, via 112 and national emergency numbers, with caller location transmitted free of charge.
exercise: Also when travelling in the Union (Art. 106(3)); caller location free (Art. 106(6)); Member States may extend to number-independent services.
quote: Those emergency communication shall be provided free of charge and without having to use any means of payment, including by using the single European emergency number ‘112’
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Calling 112 is an ordinary phone call. Test: yes (a phone call works without technical skill). Consistency pass.

right: Right to contact emergency services via an EU Digital Identity Wallet-coupled app
description: Originate emergency communications through a mobile application coupled with the European Digital Identity Wallet.
quote: Member States sh all ensure that end-users can originate emergency communication by means of a mobile application coupled with the European D igital Identity W allet s
applies_from: no later than 24 months after adoption of the Art. 106(8) delegated act (proposed)
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Emergency communication through an app coupled with the EUDI Wallet; requires operating app and wallet. Test: no.

right: Right of end-users with disabilities to equivalent access to emergency services
addressee: providers of emergency communication / Member States
description: Access emergency services on an equivalent basis: two-way interactive, without pre-registration when travelling, free of charge, routed to a qualified PSAP, with equivalent caller location.
quote: shall ensure that access for end-users with disabilities to emergency services is available through emergency communication and is equivalent to that enjoyed by other end-users
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Equivalent access is provided by the service; the holder just calls. Test: yes (a phone call works without technical skill). Consistency pass.

right: Right to receive public warnings
addressee: providers of mobile number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Receive public warnings about imminent or developing major emergencies and disasters in the affected area.
exercise: Via technology mandated by the Member State; also via EUDI Wallet-coupled app one year after the implementing act (Art. 107(3)).
quote: Providers of mobile number-based interpersonal communications services shall transmit public warnings to the end-users concerned
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Public warnings transmitted to the user's phone; received only via device. Test: no.

right: Right to withhold calling line identification
addressee: providers of public networks, interpersonal communications or internet access services
description: Prevent display of one's number or originating identification on a per-call basis, simply and free of charge.
