exercise: Also for calls to third countries (Art. 108(5)); may be overridden for tracing malicious calls and for emergency calls (Art. 109).
quote: They shall ensure that the originating party is able, by using a simple means and free of charge, to prevent the presentation of calling line or originating identification
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Simple per-call means to withhold caller ID must exist in the service. Test: no.

right: Right to suppress incoming calling line identification
description: Prevent presentation of the caller's identification on incoming calls, simply and free of charge for reasonable use.
quote: the receiving party is able, by using a simple and free of charge means for reasonable use of this function, to prevent the presentation of the calling line identification
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Simple means to suppress incoming caller ID; a service function. Test: no.

right: Right to reject anonymous calls
description: Reject incoming voice calls where the caller has withheld identification, simply and free of charge.
quote: the receiving party is able, by using a simple and free of charge means, to reject incoming voice communications where the originating party has used its right provided for in paragraph 1
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Simple means to reject anonymous calls; a service function. Test: no.

right: Right to prevent connected line identification
description: Prevent the calling party from seeing the connected line identification, simply and free of charge.
exercise: Where connected line identification is offered.
quote: the receiving party is able , by using a simple and free of charge means, to prevent the presentation of the connected line identification
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Simple means to prevent connected line ID; a service function. Test: no.

right: Tracing of malicious or nuisance communications upon complaint
description: Have caller identification temporarily overridden so that malicious or nuisance communications can be traced.
exercise: Upon complaint to the authorities.
quote: to enable competent authorities or an end-user in tracing of malicious or nuisance communications upon complaint to the authorities
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Tracing overrides caller ID technically, but exercised by plain complaint to authorities with plain result. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to block calls from specific or anonymous numbers
addressee: providers of publicly available number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Block incoming calls from specific numbers or anonymous sources, free of charge.
exercise: On request; where technically feasible.
quote: to block, where technically feasible, incoming calls from specific numbers or from anonymous sources
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Call blocking is a network function the provider must offer; result exists only technically. Test: no.

right: Right to stop automatic call forwarding
addressee: providers of publicly available number-based interpersonal communications services
description: Stop automatic forwarding of calls by a third party to one's terminal equipment, free of charge.
exercise: On request.
quote: to stop automatic call forwarding by a third party to the end- user ’ s terminal equipment
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Stopping automatic call forwarding to own terminal; service setting. Test: no.

right: Right to caller identification for automated calls
addressee: interpersonal communications service providers offering automated calling systems
description: See the caller identification of automated calls and a number or identity on which the caller can be contacted.
quote: Providers of interpersonal communications services offering automated calling systems shall not prevent the right of the presentation of the calling line or originating identification
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Caller identification displayed on terminal for automated calls; digital output only. Test: no.

right: Right of end-users with disabilities to equivalent access and choice
addressee: providers of publicly available electronic communications services
description: Enjoy access to services and contractual information equivalent to the majority of end-users and the same choice of undertakings and services.
exercise: Requirements specified by competent authorities.
quote: have access to electronic communications services, including the related contractual information provided pursuant to Article 9 5 , equivalent to that enjoyed by the majority of end-users
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Equivalence/non-discrimination guarantee; no specific mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to return digital TV equipment free of charge on termination
description: Return provider-supplied digital TV equipment through a free and easy process when the contract ends.
exercise: Unless the provider shows the equipment is fully interoperable with other providers' services.
quote: upon termination of their contract, end-users shall have the possibility to return the digital television equipment through a free and easy process
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Physical return of equipment. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to documents of BEREC, the RSPB and the ODN
rightholder: any natural or legal person (under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001)
description: Request access to documents held by BEREC, the RSPB and the ODN.
exercise: Requests processed by the ODN under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
quote: shall apply to documents held by BEREC, the RSPB and the ODN
notes: Proposal text; may change; Applies Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Access to documents request; plain documents. Test: yes.

right: Right to confidential treatment of submitted information
rightholder: persons submitting information to BEREC, the RSPB or the ODN
description: Have information covered by a reasoned confidentiality request withheld from third parties.
exercise: Reasoned request for confidential treatment, in whole or in part.
quote: BEREC, the RSPB and the ODN shall not disclose to third parties information that they process or receive in relation to which a reasoned request for confidential treatment has been made
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Confidential treatment on reasoned request. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by the ODN
description: Obtain compensation for damage caused by the ODN's departments or staff in the performance of their duties.
exercise: Non-contractual liability under general principles common to Member States' laws; Court of Justice has jurisdiction (Art. 175(4)).
quote: the ODN shall, in accordance with the general principles common to the laws of the Member States, make good any damage caused by its departments or by its staff in the performance of their duties
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Non-contractual liability claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasoned, proportionate information requests
description: Receive only reasoned and proportionate information requests and be told the specific purpose for which the information will be used.
exercise: Reporting on general authorisation and rights of use no more than once a year (Art. 181(7)).
quote: they shall inform them of the specific purpose for which th e information is to be used
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Proportionate information requests. Test: yes.

right: Right to comment on draft regulatory measures
addressee: national regulatory and other competent authorities
description: Comment on draft measures with significant market impact during a public consultation.
exercise: At least 30 days; consultations accessible via a single information point and results published (Art. 184(3)-(4)).
quote: they shall give interested parties the opportunity to comment on the draft measure within a reasonable period
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Consultations accessible via single information point; comments plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of end-users and consumers to be consulted on end-user rights
rightholder: end-users, in particular consumers and end-users with disabilities; manufacturers; undertakings
description: Have views taken into account on issues relating to end-user and consumer rights, including equivalent access for persons with disabilities.
exercise: Via a consultation mechanism accessible for end-users with disabilities (Art. 185(2)).
quote: shall take account of the views of end-users, in particular consumers and end-users with disabilities, manufacturers and undertakings that provide electronic communications networks or services
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Consultation mechanism on end-user rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to out-of-court dispute resolution
rightholder: consumers (and, where within the body's mandate, microenterprises and small enterprises)
addressee: ADR entity (NRA, other competent authority or independent body)
description: Bring contract-related disputes with providers under Arts. 95-98 and 100 to an alternative dispute resolution entity.
exercise: ADR entity listed under Directive 2013/11/EU; cross-border disputes coordinated between bodies (Art. 188(2)).
quote: shall be listed as an alternative dispute resolution entity in accordance with Article 20(2) of Directive 2013/11/EU with a view to resolving disputes between providers and consumers
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Out-of-court dispute resolution. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to the internet access provider
rightholder: end-users (open internet); consumers, microenterprises and not-for-profit organisations (Annex III Section 5 rights)
description: Use transparent, simple and efficient complaint procedures on open-internet rights and on speed/quality-of-service information rights.
quote: Providers of internet access services shall put in place transparent, simple and efficient procedures to address complaints of end-users relating to the rights and obligations laid down in Article 9 3
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Complaint procedure at provider, no technical form required; plain complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right to binding NRA resolution of disputes between undertakings
rightholder: providers of public electronic communications networks or services, access/interconnection beneficiaries, providers of associated facilities
description: Obtain a binding NRA decision resolving a dispute over obligations under the Regulation.
exercise: At the request of either party; within four months; full statement of reasons (Art. 189(3)); court action not precluded (Art. 189(4)).
quote: the national regulatory authority concerned shall, at the request of either party, issue a binding decision to resolve the dispute in the shortest possible time-frame
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Binding NRA dispute resolution. Test: yes.

right: Right to refer cross-border disputes to national regulatory authorities
rightholder: any party (undertakings in different Member States)
description: Refer a dispute with an undertaking in another Member State to the NRAs concerned, with a BEREC opinion where trade is affected.
exercise: BEREC opinion within four months; interim measures possible at a party's request in urgent cases (Art. 190(4)); court action not precluded (Art. 190(6)).
quote: Any party may refer the dispute to the national regulatory authority or authorities concerned.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Cross-border dispute referral. Test: yes.

right: Right to request voluntary conciliation on ecosystem cooperation
rightholder: providers of electronic communications networks or other undertakings active in the electronic communications or closely related sectors
description: Request an NRA-convened conciliatory meeting with another network provider or undertaking (e.g. content provider) on technical and commercial arrangements.
exercise: BEREC opinion within two months; meeting within three months of the request; written account within one month after the meeting (Art. 192(2)-(3)).
quote: national regulatory authorities shall offer a conciliatory meeting between two providers of electronic communications networks or between such a provider and another undertaking
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Conciliation meeting. Test: yes.

right: Right to notice and comment before amendment of rights and authorisations
rightholder: holders of rights or of the general authorisation and other interested parties, including users and consumers
description: Be notified in advance of intended amendments to rights, conditions and procedures and express views on them.
exercise: At least four weeks except in exceptional circumstances; not for minor amendments agreed with the holder; restriction or withdrawal without consent also requires consultation (Art. 195(4)).
quote: Holders of the rights or the general authorisation and other interested parties, including users and consumers, shall be given sufficient time to express their views on the proposed amendments.
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Notice and comment on amendments. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for spectrum migration or reallocation costs
rightholder: holders of rights of use for radio spectrum assigned for a specific duration
description: Be compensated for the direct cost of migration or reallocation when spectrum rights are restricted or withdrawn.
exercise: In accordance with national law, unless provided otherwise at grant; rights may not be restricted or withdrawn before expiry except as justified (Art. 195(1)).
quote: the holders of the rights shall have the right to be compensated appropriately for the direct cost of migration or reallocation of radio spectrum in accordance with national law
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Compensation for migration costs. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before compliance measures
addressee: national regulatory and other competent authorities
description: Be notified of findings of non-compliance and state views within a reasonable time before measures are taken.
exercise: Measures and reasons communicated without delay with a reasonable compliance period (Art. 196(4)); opportunity to state views also for interim measures (Art. 196(11)).
quote: it shall notify the undertaking of those findings and give the undertaking the opportunity to state its views, within a reasonable time limit
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Right to be heard. Test: yes.

right: Right of appeal against decisions of competent authorities
rightholder: any user or undertaking affected by a decision of a competent authority
description: Appeal decisions of national regulatory or other competent authorities to an independent appeal body.
exercise: Decision stands pending appeal unless interim measures granted; non-judicial bodies give written reasons and are subject to court review.
quote: Any user or undertaking providing electronic communications networks or services or associated facilities who is affected by a decision of a competent authority shall have the right of appeal
notes: Proposal text; may change
entry_current_status: Proposed as the Digital Networks Act, COM(2026) 16, 2026/0013(COD), awaiting committee decision
tl_reason: Appeal against regulator decisions. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free digital travel credential with one's passport on request
rightholder: applicants for passports/travel documents (Member State nationals)
description: On request, passports issued by Member States to their nationals must be accompanied by a free, wallet-compatible digital travel credential without fingerprints.
exercise: Request at application; free of charge.
quote: Upon request from the applicant, passports and travel documents issued by Member States to their own nationals shall be accompanied by a digital travel credential
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 12 months after the implementing act on technical specifications (Art. 20).
tl_reason: Result is a wallet-compatible digital travel credential usable only through technical means. Test: no.

right: Right of EU citizens to create a digital travel credential via the EU Digital Travel application
rightholder: persons enjoying the right of free movement under Union law
description: Holders of compliant passports or ID cards can use the EU Digital Travel application to create a single- or multiple-use digital travel credential.
exercise: After facial-image matching and chip verification (Art. 4(5)); voluntary.
quote: may use the EU Digital Travel application to create a digital travel credential based on that travel document for single or multiple use
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Creating a credential in the app via chip reading and face matching; purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to store a digital travel credential in the European Digital Identity Wallet
description: The application must allow storage of a multiple-use digital travel credential in the European Digital Identity Wallet.
quote: shall provide for the possibility to store a d igital travel credential for multiple use in the European Digital Identity Wallet
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: App must allow storing the credential in the EU Digital Identity Wallet; operated across apps. Test: no.

right: Right of third-country nationals to create a digital travel credential
rightholder: third-country nationals holding a travel document with a storage medium
description: Third-country nationals with chip-enabled travel documents can create a digital travel credential via the application.
exercise: Subject to availability of valid certificates to check authenticity.
quote: use the EU Digital Travel application to create a digital travel credential for single or multiple use
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Creating a credential in the app via chip reading; purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to consent before stakeholders access the passport chip
rightholder: person to whom the passport or travel document has been issued
description: Stakeholders involved in external border crossing may access the passport's storage medium (except fingerprints) only with the holder's consent.
quote: with the consent of the person to whom the passport or travel document has been issued
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Object is chip data read by machine, but consent can be given by plain means. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to voluntary, consent-based use of the application and credentials
description: Using the application and creating or using digital travel credentials is voluntary and based on the traveller's consent.
quote: the creation and use of digital travel credentials by persons enjoying the right of free movement under Union law and third-country nationals shall be voluntary and based on their consent
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Consent-based use of a technical app, but the right's core is voluntariness, which needs nothing technical. Criteria conflict.

right: Right to revoke consent to processing in the application at any time
rightholder: users of the EU Digital Travel application
description: Users can revoke their consent to the processing of their personal data in the application at any time.
exercise: At any time.
quote: Users of the EU Digital Travel application shall be able to revoke their consent to process their personal data on the EU Digital Travel application at any time.
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Consent revocable within the app at any time; a single in-app choice. Test: no.

right: Right of EU citizens to use the application for advance border checks
rightholder: persons enjoying the right of free movement holding a digital travel credential
description: EU citizens with a digital travel credential may submit travel data in advance via the application so that border checks are carried out up to 36 hours before crossing.
quote: Persons enjoying the right of free movement under Union law who are in possession of a digital travel credential may use the EU Digital Travel application for the purposes of advance border checks
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Advance border checks by submitting credential data through the app. Test: no.

right: Right of third-country nationals to use the application for advance clearance
rightholder: third-country nationals, including those registered in the EES
description: Third-country nationals may use the application to have entry conditions verified in advance (advance clearance).
quote: Third-country nationals, including those subject to registration in the EES, may use the EU Digital Travel application for the purposes of advance clearance
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Advance clearance by submitting data through the app. Test: no.

act: Digital Travel Credentials based on ID cards Regulation (proposal)
right: Right to a digital travel credential with a new identity card on request
rightholder: person applying for an identity card (Union citizen)
description: On request, an identity card issued by a Member State must be accompanied by a free, wallet-compatible digital travel credential without fingerprints (Art. 2(4)).
exercise: Request at application; free of charge.
quote: Upon request from the person having applied for an identity card , identity cards issued by Member States shall be accompanied by a digital travel credential
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 12 months after the technical specifications enter into force (Art. 8).
tl_reason: Result is a wallet-compatible digital travel credential usable only technically. Test: no.

act: Digital Travel Credentials based on ID cards Regulation (proposal)
right: Right of existing identity card holders to obtain a digital travel credential
rightholder: holder of a compliant identity card
addressee: Member State that issued the card
description: Holders of compliant ID cards can request that the issuing Member State issue them a free digital travel credential.
exercise: Request to the issuing Member State; free of charge.
quote: the Member State having issued the identity card shall issue a digital travel credential
notes: Proposal text; may change. Applies 12 months after the technical specifications enter into force (Art. 8).
tl_reason: Result is a digital travel credential usable only technically. Test: no.

act: Digital Travel Credentials based on ID cards Regulation (proposal)
right: Right to remotely create a digital travel credential from one's identity card
rightholder: holder of a compliant identity card
description: Member States must offer card holders the possibility to create a digital travel credential remotely through the EU Digital Travel application, with access to the necessary parts of the card chip.
exercise: After chip authenticity check and facial-image matching; from the date set by implementing act (Art. 2(6)).
quote: Holders shall be allowed to access the parts of the storage medium of identity cards that are necessary for the purpose of creating a digital travel credential
notes: Proposal text; may change.
tl_reason: Remote creation via the app with access to the card chip; purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right of transport operators to fair, non-exclusive agreements and FRAND remuneration
addressee: B2C MDMS providers with significant market presence; B2B MDMS providers
description: When contracting with transport operators, designated B2C platforms and B2B distribution systems must protect operators' commercially sensitive data, may not impose unfair conditions or exclusivity clauses, and must set remuneration on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory criteria.
exercise: Complaint to the national enforcement body (Art. 14(3)).
quote: not attach any unfair conditions or exclusivity clauses to the commercial agreement
notes: Proposal text; may change. Only providers designated as having significant market presence (Art. 4) for B2C; SMEs exempt (Art. 2(3)).
tl_reason: Fair contract terms and FRAND remuneration; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right of transport operators to equal treatment by B2B MDMS providers
description: B2B distribution systems may not reserve loading or processing procedures for certain operators, must give all participating operators the same information on changes, and must separate their facilities from any operator's inventory and marketing.
exercise: Complaint to the national enforcement body (Art. 14(3)).
quote: provide the same information to all participating transport operators about changes to their distribution facilities, loading procedures and processing procedures
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Concerns loading and processing procedures of distribution systems, but enforced by plain complaint. Object vs test conflict.

right: Protection of business users against lock-in and unfair conditions in B2B MDMS agreements
description: Agreements with B2B distribution systems may not stop business users from using other similar systems, impose unnecessary extra conditions or specific equipment/software, or include other unfair conditions.
exercise: Complaint to the national enforcement body (Art. 14(1)).
quote: hinder or prevent a business user from subscribing to or using effectively any other similar system
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Provider must permit use of other systems and own equipment/software; exercising means operating across systems. Test: no.

right: Right of small-enterprise business users to terminate B2B MDMS agreements
rightholder: business user that is a small enterprise
description: Small business users may terminate their agreement with a B2B distribution system at any time after the first year, paying at most the directly related administrative costs.
exercise: Written notice of no more than three months.
quote: it may terminate its commercial agreement with a B2B MDMS provider any time after the first year of that agreement
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Termination by written notice. Test: yes.

right: Right of transport operators to neutral, non-discriminatory display and ranking
description: Platforms must load operators' data with equal care and rank products neutrally using the listed criteria, not based on the operator's identity unless the user asks.
exercise: Complaint to the national enforcement body (Art. 14(3)).
quote: to rank the transport products and combinations of transport products on a non-discriminatory basis to all transport operators
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Concerns neutral ranking by software, but enforced by plain complaint. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to see final prices
description: When transport products are displayed, users must always see the final price including all unavoidable charges, taxes and booking fees; flights by carriers under an EU operating ban must be flagged (Art. 7(12)).
exercise: Shown in search results; air fares per Art. 23 Reg (EC) 1008/2008.
quote: B2C MDMS providers and B2B MDMS providers shall always present final prices to end users or business users when displaying transport products or a combination of transport products
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Final price shown in search results; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose and combine ranking criteria, including emissions
description: Users can rank results by price, travel time, greenhouse gas or CO2-equivalent emissions, departure time, connections or accessibility, and combine these in any order; ranking by emissions must always be offered.
exercise: Via the search interface; other criteria on explicit request (Art. 7(10)); always available emissions ranking (Art. 7(7)).
quote: B2C MDMS providers and B2B MDMS providers shall enable end users and business users to use or combine any of the criteria listed in paragraph 5, points (a) to (g), in any order
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Interface must let users choose and combine ranking criteria; the right is the option itself. Test: no.

right: Right of code-share operators to have products displayed under their own code
description: Although each product is shown only once per search, each of the two code-share operators can ask for the product to be displayed as its own service under its own carrier code.
exercise: Request to the MDMS provider; with more than two code-share partners, the operating carrier identifies the two.
quote: each of the two code-share transport operators shall be allowed to ask for the relevant transport products to be displayed as their own service
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Concerns display in search interface, but exercised by plain request. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to see paid-prominence rankings only on request
description: Paid prominence may not be a default ranking criterion and is shown only if the end user requests it, with offers labelled 'choice of' or 'sponsored content' and the effect of payment explained.
exercise: Opt-in by the end user.
quote: Such ‘paid prominence’ shall not be one of the default ranking criteria and shall only be available upon request by the end user.
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Paid-prominence ranking only via user opt-in in interface; right is the default setting. Test: no.

right: Right of transport operators to equal access to marketing, booking and sales data
rightholder: transport operator with a commercial agreement
description: Marketing, booking or sales data given to one operator must be made available in time to all operators with an agreement, and on request must cover all operators and business users.
exercise: Request to the MDMS provider; anonymised and aggregated data only; may not be used to identify and influence users' choices (Art. 8(2)).
quote: it shall also be made available in a timely manner to all transport operators with whom that provider has concluded a commercial agreement
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Aggregated sales data may be dataset or plain report; request-based, result only sometimes digital. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of business users to consent before being identified in shared data
rightholder: business user established in the Union
description: Data generated by a business user's use of a B2B distribution system may not identify it, to operators or other parties, unless it agrees the conditions of use with the provider.
exercise: Agreement with the B2B MDMS provider; billing settlement excepted.
quote: it shall not identify the business user unless that business user agrees on the conditions for making appropriate use of that data with the B2B MDMS provider
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Object is usage data, but consent is given by contractual agreement. Object vs exercise conflict.

right: Right to emissions information on transport products
description: Platforms must show clear, accessible greenhouse gas or CO2-equivalent emissions information for transport products where the operator provides it, and say which parts of a journey lack such data.
exercise: Displayed with search results; products lacking data ranked last when sorting by emissions (Art. 9(3)).
quote: transparent and accessible information on the GHG emissions or CO 2 equivalent emissions
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Emissions information shown with results; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of MDMS providers and business users to lodge a complaint with the national enforcement body
rightholder: B2C MDMS providers, B2B MDMS providers and business users
description: Platform providers and business users can complain to the national enforcement body about breaches of the Regulation or unfair or discriminatory treatment.
exercise: Body of the Member State of establishment; non-EU parties per Art. 14(4); fallback any Member State (Art. 14(5)); refused if a complaint between the same parties is pending elsewhere or a court remedy was sought (Art. 14(7)).
quote: B2C MDMS providers, B2B MDMS providers or business users shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging a breach of this Regulation with the national enforcement body
notes: Proposal text; may change. End users (consumers) are not given a complaint right in Art. 14.
tl_reason: Complaint to enforcement body. Test: yes.

right: Right of transport operators to lodge a complaint with the national enforcement body
description: Transport operators can complain about breaches of the Regulation or unfair or discriminatory treatment.
exercise: Body of the Member State that granted the operating licence; third-country-licensed operators per Art. 14(4).
quote: Transport operators shall have the right to lodge complaints alleging a breach of this Regulation with the national enforcement body
notes: Proposal text; may change
tl_reason: Complaint to enforcement body. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit a consumer dispute to a quality ADR entity
description: Consumers can submit domestic and cross-border contractual disputes with EU traders to an ADR entity meeting the Directive's quality requirements, online or offline, free of charge or for a nominal fee.
exercise: Complaint via the ADR entity's website or offline (Art. 5(2)); free or nominal fee (Art. 8(c)); no lawyer needed (Art. 8(b)); outcome within 90 days of the complete file (Art. 8(e)); entities may refuse on listed grounds, e.g. no prior contact with the trader, or a filing deadline of at least one year (Art. 5(4)); trader participation voluntary unless national law makes it mandatory.
quote: disputes covered by this Directive and which involve a trader established on their respective territories can be submitted to an ADR entity
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Amended by Dir (EU) 2025/2647 from 20 September 2028.
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: ADR complaint online or offline; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to a reasoned explanation when an ADR entity refuses to deal with a dispute
rightholder: parties to the dispute (consumer and trader)
description: If an ADR entity declines a dispute under its procedural rules, both parties receive a reasoned explanation of the grounds.
exercise: Within three weeks of receipt of the complaint file.
quote: that ADR entity shall provide both parties with a reasoned explanation of the grounds for not considering the dispute within three weeks of receiving the complaint file
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Reasoned explanation of refusal; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to object to an ADR adjudicator with a conflict of interest
description: If circumstances affecting the independence or impartiality of the person in charge arise, that person is replaced or steps down; failing that, the parties are informed and the person may continue only if they do not object.
exercise: Object after being informed of the circumstances and the right to object.
quote: the natural person concerned is allowed to continue to conduct the ADR procedure only if the parties have not objected after they have been informed of the circumstances and their right to object
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Objection to conflicted adjudicator; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to independent advice and representation in ADR
description: Parties can use ADR without a lawyer but keep the right to independent advice or to be represented or assisted by a third party at any stage.
exercise: Parties must be informed of this (Art. 9(1)(b)).
quote: the procedure shall not deprive the parties of their right to independent advice or to be represented or assisted by a third party at any stage of the procedure
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Advice and representation in ADR; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard and to comment on the other party's submissions
description: Parties can express their views within a reasonable period, receive the other party's arguments, evidence and documents and any expert statements, and comment on them.
exercise: Within a reasonable period set by the ADR entity.
quote: the parties have the possibility, within a reasonable period of time, of expressing their point of view
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Right to be heard in ADR. Test: yes.

right: Right to a written, reasoned ADR outcome
description: Parties are notified of the outcome in writing or on a durable medium together with a statement of the grounds.
exercise: At the end of the procedure.
quote: the parties are notified of the outcome of the ADR procedure in writing or on a durable medium, and are given a statement of the grounds on which the outcome is based.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Written reasoned outcome. Test: yes.

right: Right to withdraw from the ADR procedure at any stage
rightholder: parties to the dispute (only the consumer where trader participation is mandatory)
description: In ADR procedures proposing a solution, parties can withdraw at any stage if dissatisfied with how the procedure is run, and must be told of this right beforehand.
exercise: Notify the ADR entity; information given before the procedure starts.
quote: The parties have the possibility of withdrawing from the procedure at any stage if they are dissatisfied with the performance or the operation of the procedure.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Withdrawal from ADR by notice. Test: yes.

right: Right to freely accept or reject a proposed solution, after information and reflection time
description: Before agreeing to a proposed solution, parties are told they may refuse it, that court action remains possible, that the result may differ from a court ruling, and what legal effect acceptance has, and they get a reasonable reflection period.
exercise: Information and reflection period before consent (Art. 9(2)(b)-(d)); where acceptance binds the trader by law, applies only to the consumer (Art. 9(3)).
quote: they have the choice as to whether or not to agree to or follow the proposed solution
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Free acceptance of proposed solution. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be bound by pre-dispute ADR clauses that exclude the courts
description: An agreement made before a dispute arises to submit complaints to ADR does not bind the consumer if it would deprive them of the right to go to court.
exercise: Invoked against the trader; consumer keeps access to courts.
quote: an agreement between a consumer and a trader to submit complaints to an ADR entity is not binding on the consumer if it was concluded before the dispute has materialised
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Pre-dispute ADR clause not binding. Test: yes.

right: Right to be bound by an imposed ADR solution only after informed, specific acceptance
rightholder: parties to the dispute (trader acceptance not required where national law binds traders)
description: An ADR solution imposed on the parties is binding only if they were told in advance it would be binding and specifically accepted this.
exercise: Prior information and specific acceptance.
quote: the solution imposed may be binding on the parties only if they were informed of its binding nature in advance and specifically accepted this
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Binding only after specific acceptance. Test: yes.

right: Right to keep mandatory consumer protection in imposed ADR solutions
description: An ADR solution imposed on the consumer may not deprive them of the protection of non-derogable provisions of the law of their habitual residence (or the law applicable under Rome I / the Rome Convention).
exercise: Applies to ADR procedures imposing a solution.
quote: the solution imposed shall not result in the consumer being deprived of the protection afforded to him by the provisions that cannot be derogated from by agreement
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Mandatory consumer protection preserved. Test: yes.

right: Right to go to court after non-binding ADR despite expiry of limitation periods
description: Parties who used a non-binding ADR procedure are not barred from court proceedings because limitation or prescription periods expired during the ADR procedure.
exercise: Invoked before national courts.
quote: are not subsequently prevented from initiating judicial proceedings in relation to that dispute as a result of the expiry of limitation or prescription periods during the ADR procedure
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Limitation periods suspended. Test: yes.

right: Right to ADR information when a complaint to the trader is not resolved
description: If a complaint made directly to the trader cannot be settled, the trader must tell the consumer which ADR entity covers it (with website) and whether it will use it.
exercise: On paper or another durable medium; traders committed or obliged to use ADR must also show this on their website and in general terms (Art. 13(1)-(2)).
quote: the trader provides the consumer with the information referred to in paragraph 1, specifying whether he will make use of the relevant ADR entities to settle the dispute
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: ADR information on paper or durable medium. Test: yes.

right: Right to assistance in accessing ADR for cross-border disputes
addressee: European Consumer Centres, consumer organisations or other designated bodies
description: Consumers with cross-border disputes can get help to reach the competent ADR entity in another Member State.
exercise: Contact the body designated under Art. 14(2), usually the national European Consumer Centre.
quote: consumers can obtain assistance to access the ADR entity operating in another Member State which is competent to deal with their cross-border dispute
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Replaced by ADR contact points under Dir (EU) 2025/2647 from 20 September 2028.
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Assistance from consumer centre. Test: yes.

right: Right to ADR for disputes with third-country traders
rightholder: consumer resident in a Member State
description: Consumers can bring disputes with non-EU traders that direct activities to their Member State before a quality ADR entity, on a joint request with the trader; any choice of law cannot strip mandatory protections of the consumer's country of residence.
exercise: Joint request by consumer and third-country trader; Member States may require agreement on the applicable law and the trader's commitment to the procedural rules and fees.
quote: ensure that those disputes can be submitted to an ADR entity which complies with the requirements set out in this Directive, following a joint request by the consumer and the third-country trader
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: ADR for third-country disputes, filed online or offline. Test: yes.

right: Right to choose digital or non-digital ADR
description: Consumers can choose whether to file complaints and documents and to take part in ADR in a digital or non-digital format; online filing must be traceable and digital tools accessible and inclusive.
exercise: Choice made by the consumer when filing (Art. 5(2)(a)-(c)).
quote: enable consumers to choose whether to submit complaints and other supporting documents and to access ADR in a digital or a non-digital format
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Right guarantees a non-digital route; technology optional. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed in advance of automated decision-making in ADR
description: Where automated means are used in ADR decision-making, the parties are told in advance, clearly and accessibly.
exercise: Before the procedure.
quote: inform the parties in advance, in a clear, comprehensible and easily accessible way about their use
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Notice of automated decision-making in ADR; object digital, notice plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to human review of an ADR outcome reached with automated means
description: Where automated means are used, the parties can ask for the ADR outcome to be reviewed by a qualified, independent natural person of the ADR entity.
exercise: Request to the ADR entity; parties must be informed of this right (Art. 5(2)(e)).
quote: ensure that the parties have the right to request that the outcome of the ADR procedure be reviewed by a natural person from the ADR entity meeting the requirements of Article 6(1)
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Human review of automated ADR outcome; plain request, plain result. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed of the bundling of cases
description: If an ADR entity bundles similar cases, the consumer concerned must be informed.
exercise: Member States may set additional bundling conditions.
quote: the consumer concerned is informed of the bundling
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Information on bundling of cases. Test: yes.

right: Right to have the trader invited to ADR and to a timely answer
description: Once an ADR entity accepts a consumer complaint it must invite the trader (Art. 5(8)); EU traders must say within 20 working days (max 30 in complex cases) whether they will take part, and the consumer is told of any extension and of closure if the trader does not reply.
exercise: Duty to reply does not apply where participation is mandatory, outcomes can be reached without the trader, or the trader is contractually committed to ADR; consequences of silence set by national law.
quote: The trader shall reply to the ADR entity within a reasonable period, which shall not exceed 20 working days.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Trader invitation and reply deadline. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit a complaint to the competent European Consumer Centre via the online entry point
addressee: Commission (Single Digital Gateway entry point); European Consumer Centres Network
description: Through the online consumer entry point, consumers can submit a complaint to the competent centre of the European Consumer Centres Network, replacing the former route via the ODR platform.
exercise: Online via the Single Digital Gateway entry point; the competent centre depends on the parties involved.
quote: submit a complaint to the competent centre of the European Consumer Centres Network, depending on the parties involved.
notes: Lead-in wording of Art. 5 of Dir (EU) 2019/2161 is not reproduced in this file; ODR platform discontinued by Reg (EU) 2024/3228.
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Complaint routed through online Single Digital Gateway entry point, but complaint and result are non-technical. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right of package travellers to information on complaint handling and ADR
description: The package travel contract or its confirmation must state the in-house complaint procedures, ADR mechanisms and, where applicable, the ADR entity covering the trader.
exercise: Included in the package travel contract or confirmation.
quote: information on available in-house complaint handling procedures and on alternative dispute resolution (“ADR”) mechanisms pursuant to Directive 2013/11/EU
notes: Amends the Package Travel Directive; previous text referred to the ODR platform. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Complaint and ADR information in contract. Test: yes.

right: Right to ADR information when a complaint to the trader is not resolved
description: Where a complaint made directly to the trader could not be resolved, the trader must give the consumer the information on the ADR entity or entities covering it.
exercise: Also on the trader's website (clear and prominent) and in general terms and conditions (Art. 13(2) as replaced).
quote: the trader is required to provide the consumer with the information referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: ADR information from trader; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to assistance from an ADR contact point in cross-border disputes
addressee: ADR contact point (European Consumer Centre or other designated body)
description: Consumers and traders in cross-border disputes can get help from a national ADR contact point to reach the competent ADR entity, including help filing the complaint, machine translation, information on rights and procedures, and pointers to other redress.
exercise: On request; consumers use the contact point of their residence, traders that of their establishment (Art. 14(3)); Member States may extend help to domestic disputes (Art. 14(5)).
quote: consumers and traders are able to obtain assistance to facilitate their access to the ADR entity or entities competent to deal with their cross-border dispute
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Consumer rights: adapting ADR to digital markets
tl_reason: Assistance from ADR contact point; plain help. Test: yes.

right: Right to interest for late payment in transactions between undertakings
description: A creditor that has performed and is not paid on time is entitled to late-payment interest without needing to send a reminder, unless the debtor is not responsible for the delay.
exercise: Interest runs from the day after the contractual due date or, absent one, 30 days after receipt of invoice or goods (Art. 3(3)); statutory rate is the reference rate plus at least 8 points (Art. 2(6)); payment terms over 60 days and acceptance periods over 30 days only if expressly agreed and not grossly unfair (Art. 3(4)-(5)).
quote: the creditor is entitled to interest for late payment without the necessity of a reminder
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Would be repealed by the proposed Late Payment Regulation.
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Late-payment interest; money claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to statutory interest when a public authority pays late
description: When a public authority pays late, the creditor is entitled to statutory interest without a reminder; public payment periods are capped at 30 days (60 in specified cases).
exercise: Payment period 30 days from invoice/goods (Art. 4(3)); up to 60 days for certain public undertakings and healthcare entities (Art. 4(4)) or if expressly agreed and objectively justified (Art. 4(6)); invoice receipt date not subject to agreement.
quote: the creditor is entitled upon expiry of the period defined in paragraphs 3, 4 or 6 to statutory interest for late payment, without the necessity of a reminder
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Statutory interest from public authority; money claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to a fixed EUR 40 compensation for recovery costs
description: Whenever late-payment interest becomes payable, the creditor is entitled to at least a fixed EUR 40 for its own recovery costs.
exercise: Payable without a reminder (Art. 6(2)).
quote: the creditor is entitled to obtain from the debtor, as a minimum, a fixed sum of EUR 40
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Fixed recovery compensation. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasonable compensation for recovery costs exceeding EUR 40
description: In addition to the fixed sum, the creditor can claim reasonable compensation for higher recovery costs caused by late payment, such as lawyer or debt-collection fees.
exercise: Claim against the debtor.
quote: be entitled to obtain reasonable compensation from the debtor for any recovery costs exceeding that fixed sum
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Recovery cost compensation. Test: yes.

right: Right to challenge grossly unfair payment terms and practices
description: Terms or practices on payment dates, interest or recovery compensation that are grossly unfair to the creditor are unenforceable or give rise to a damages claim.
exercise: Terms excluding interest are grossly unfair (Art. 7(2)); terms excluding recovery compensation are presumed grossly unfair (Art. 7(3)).
quote: is either unenforceable or gives rise to a claim for damages if it is grossly unfair to the creditor
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Challenge to unfair payment terms. Test: yes.

right: Right of business organisations to take action against grossly unfair payment terms
rightholder: organisations officially recognised as representing undertakings or with a legitimate interest in representing them
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Representative business organisations can go to court or administrative bodies to stop the continued use of grossly unfair payment terms or practices.
exercise: According to national law.
quote: organisations with a legitimate interest in representing undertakings may take action according to the applicable national law before the courts
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Action by business organisations. Test: yes.

right: Right to retain title until full payment
description: Where expressly agreed before delivery, the seller keeps title to the goods until they are fully paid for.
exercise: Subject to the national law designated by private international law; Member States may regulate down payments (Art. 9(2)).
quote: the seller retains title to goods until they are fully paid for if a retention of title clause has been expressly agreed between the buyer and the seller before the delivery of the goods
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Retention of title; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain an enforceable title for unchallenged claims within 90 days
addressee: Member State courts or competent authorities
description: For undisputed debts, creditors can obtain an enforceable title, including by expedited procedure and regardless of amount, normally within 90 days of filing.
exercise: Same conditions for all EU-established creditors (Art. 10(2)); periods for service and creditor-caused delays excluded (Art. 10(3)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that an enforceable title can be obtained, including through an expedited procedure and irrespective of the amount of the debt, normally within 90 calendar days
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Enforceable title procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to payment within a maximum of 30 days
description: In B2B and public-authority-to-business transactions, the payment period may not exceed 30 calendar days from receipt of the invoice, provided the goods or services were received.
exercise: Contrary terms are null and void (Art. 9(1)(a)); acceptance or verification procedures max 30 days and only where strictly necessary (Art. 3(2)-(3)).
quote: In commercial transactions, the payment period shall not exceed 30 calendar days
notes: Proposal text; may change. Regulation would be directly applicable; consumer transactions excluded (Art. 1(3)(a)).
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Maximum payment period; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to automatic, non-waivable interest for late payment
description: In case of late payment the debtor owes interest automatically, without a reminder, unless not responsible for the delay; the creditor cannot waive it.
exercise: Conditions in Art. 5(2); runs from the later of invoice or goods receipt until payment (Art. 5(6)-(7)); rate is the reference rate plus 8 points (Art. 6); applies to overdue instalments (Art. 7); non-waivable (Art. 5(3)).
quote: In case of late payment, the debtor shall be liable to pay interest for late payment, except where the debtor is not responsible for the payment delay.
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Automatic late-payment interest. Test: yes.

right: Right to information needed for invoice acceptance
description: The debtor must give the creditor all information needed for its invoice to be accepted and processed as soon as received.
exercise: Provided by the debtor; invoice receipt date cannot be set by contract (Art. 5(4)).
quote: The debtor shall provide all relevant information to the creditor to ensure that the creditor’s invoice or equivalent request for payment is accepted and processed by the debtor
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Information for invoice acceptance; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to a flat EUR 50 compensation for recovery costs per transaction
description: When late-payment interest is due, the creditor automatically receives a flat EUR 50 per commercial transaction for its own recovery costs.
exercise: Without a reminder (Art. 8(2)); cannot be waived (Art. 8(3)).
quote: a flat fee compensation for recovery costs shall be automatically due by the debtor to the creditor and shall amount to a fixed sum of EUR 50
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Flat recovery compensation. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasonable compensation for recovery costs exceeding the flat fee
description: The creditor can also claim reasonable compensation for recovery costs above the flat fee caused by late payment.
exercise: Claim against the debtor; other compensation rights unaffected (Art. 8(5)).
quote: the creditor shall be entitled to obtain reasonable compensation from the debtor for any recovery costs exceeding that flat fee compensation
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Recovery cost compensation. Test: yes.

right: Right to have unfair payment terms and practices treated as null and void
description: Terms and practices exceeding the maximum payment period, excluding or limiting interest or recovery compensation, extending verification beyond 30 days, or deliberately delaying invoicing are null and void.
exercise: Invoked before courts or enforcement authorities.
quote: The following contractual terms and practices shall be null and void
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Void unfair payment terms. Test: yes.

right: Right of creditor organisations to take action against void terms and practices
rightholder: organisations officially recognised as representing creditors or with a legitimate interest in representing undertakings
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Representative organisations can bring proceedings to end the use of null and void payment terms and practices.
exercise: Before courts or competent administrative bodies.
quote: the possibility for an organisation officially recognised as representing creditors or organisations with a legitimate interest in representing undertaking s to take act ion before the courts
notes: Proposal text; may change. Quote reproduces spacing errors in the source text.
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Action by creditor organisations. Test: yes.

right: Right to retain title until full payment
description: Where expressly agreed before delivery, the creditor keeps title to the goods until fully paid.
exercise: Requires express prior agreement.
quote: A creditor shall retain title to goods until they are fully paid for if a retention of title has been expressly agreed between the debtor and the creditor before the delivery of the goods.
notes: Proposal text; may change. Heading appears as 'Article 1 0' in the source file.
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Retention of title; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain an enforceable title for undisputed claims within 90 days
description: Creditors obtain an enforceable title for undisputed debts, including by expedited procedure and regardless of amount, within 90 calendar days of filing.
exercise: Service periods and creditor-caused delays excluded (Art. 12(2)).
quote: Creditors shall obtain an enforceable title, including through an expedited procedure and irrespective of the amount of debt, within 90 calendar days
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Enforceable title procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of creditors to complain to the late-payment enforcement authority
description: Creditors can complain about late payment to the enforcement authority of their own Member State or of the debtor's, which can order payment of interest and compensation.
exercise: Authority may investigate and order interest or compensation (Art. 14(1)(d)) and require the debtor to stop the practice (Art. 15(7)).
quote: Creditors may address complaints either to the enforcement authority of the Member State in which the y are established
notes: Proposal text; may change. Quote reproduces spacing error ('the y') in the source text.
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Complaint to enforcement authority. Test: yes.

right: Right of creditor organisations to submit complaints on behalf of members
rightholder: organisations officially recognised as representing creditors or with a legitimate interest in representing undertakings
description: Representative organisations can complain to the enforcement authority at the request of members who consider themselves affected by an infringement.
exercise: At the request of one or more members (or members of member organisations).
quote: organisations with a legitimate interest in representing undertakings shall have the right to submit a complaint to the enforcement authorities referred to in Article 13
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Complaint by organisations. Test: yes.

right: Right of complainants to confidentiality of their identity
description: On request, the enforcement authority must protect the complainant's identity and any information the complainant flags as confidential.
exercise: Request by the complainant identifying the confidential information.
quote: the enforcement authority shall take the necessary measures for the appropriate protection of the identity of the complainant
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Confidentiality of complainant identity. Test: yes.

right: Right of complainants to be informed of the follow-up and of reasons for not acting
description: The authority must tell the complainant within a reasonable time how it will follow up the complaint and, if it decides not to act, why.
exercise: Within a reasonable period after receipt (Art. 15(4)-(5)).
quote: shall inform the complainant within a reasonable period of time after the receipt of the complaint of how it intends to follow up on the complaint
notes: Proposal text; may change
table_entry: Revision of the late payments Directive
entry_current_status: Proposed as Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD), pending at Council; Directive 2011/7/EU still in force
tl_reason: Information on complaint follow-up. Test: yes.
